We perform a rigorous spectral analysis of the intrinsic $B$-mode power spectrum $P_{BB}$ in the limit of a large horizon and at leading order in the slow-roll approximation. This analysis requires a clear definition of the polarized $B$-mode spectrum on the whole probed angular scale range, which is lacking in the current literature. We introduce a new parametrization that is both well-defined and suitable for performing the slow-roll approximation. By means of this parametrization, we show that the amplitude of $P_{BB}$ is given by the usual expression in terms of the scalar tilt $n_S$, but with a spectral index $n_S^{(B)}$ different from the scalar one $n_S$. We evaluate the corresponding running of the $B$-mode spectral index, and provide a simple fitting function that depends on the two standard slow-roll parameters $\epsilon$ and $\eta$ and on a single extra parameter $\beta_B$ that governs the running. We show that the running of the $B$-mode spectral index is constrained by the Planck satellite, even though $P_{BB}$ itself is too small to be detectable yet. We also show that a detection of gravitational waves with an r.m.s. amplitude of $1$ would lead to a significant improvement of the constraint, and we quantify the effect of neglecting the running.

The work reported in this article presents a high-order, stable, and
efficient Gegenbauer pseudospectral method to solve numerically a wide variety
of mathematical models. The proposed numerical scheme exploits the stability
and the well-conditioning of the numerical integration operators to produce
well-conditioned systems of algebraic equations, which can be solved easily
using standard algebraic system solvers. The core of the work lies in the
derivation of novel and stable Gegenbauer quadratures based on the stable
barycentric representation of Lagrange interpolating polynomials and the
explicit barycentric weights for the Gegenbauer-Gauss (GG) points. A rigorous
error and convergence analysis of the proposed quadratures is presented along
with a detailed set of pseudocodes for the established computational
algorithms. The proposed numerical scheme leads to a reduction in the
computational cost and time complexity required for computing the numerical
quadrature while sharing the same exponential order of accuracy achieved by
Elgindy and Smith-Miles (2013). The bulk of the work includes three numerical
test examples to assess the efficiency and accuracy of the numerical scheme.
The present method provides a strong addition to the arsenal of numerical
pseudospectral methods, and can be extended to solve a wide range of problems
arising in numerous applications.

Ultracold neutron (UCN) detectors are crucial tools in various fields of research, including particle physics, materials science, and nuclear medicine. However, current UCN detectors suffer from limited efficiency and spatial resolution due to their simple design, which consists of a single layer of converter material.

In this work, we present a novel approach to UCN detection that utilizes a multilayer surface detector. By stacking multiple layers of different materials with varying neutron interaction cross-sections, we enhance the detection efficiency and improve the spatial resolution. The additional layers also allow for better discrimination between UCNs and background particles, leading to improved signal-to-noise ratio.

The proposed detector design consists of alternating layers of boron carbide (B4C) and graphite, which provide efficient conversion of UCNs into charged particles. The B4C layers have high thermal conductivity, ensuring fast heat dissipation and reducing the risk of thermal neutron absorption. In contrast, the graphite layers have low atomic number, minimizing the probability of UCN absorption.

We simulate the performance of our multilayer surface detector using Monte Carlo simulations and compare it to traditional single-layer detectors. Our results show an increase in detection efficiency by up to 50% and an improvement in spatial resolution by a factor of 2-3. We also experimentally validate our design using a prototype detector at a UCN source.

Our findings demonstrate the potential of multilayer surface detectors for enhancing UCN detection capabilities. This technology can be applied in various areas, such as fundamental neutron physics experiments, neutron scattering and imaging applications, and medical treatments involving UCNs.

The Lennox Bridge, Glenbrook is a heritage-listed road bridge that carries the Mitchell's Pass across Brookside Creek (also known as Lapstone Creek), located at Glenbrook, in the City of Blue Mountains local government area of New South Wales, Australia. The bridge was designed by David Lennox and built from 1832 to 1833 by James Randall and other convicts. It is also known as Lennox Bridge or The Horseshoe Bridge. The property is owned by Blue Mountains City Council. It was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999. The first road up the eastern slopes of the Blue Mountains, built by William Cox (1814–15), was in Governor Macquarie's words "pretty steep and sharp" and was found to be subject to serious washways. This road was superseded in 1824 by what was known as the Bathurst Road (now Old Bathurst Road). It avoided watercourses, but its grade was very steep and this rendered it hazardous to travellers. When Major Thomas Mitchell was appointed as Surveyor General in 1828, one of the first matters to which he turned his attention was the improvement of the Great Western Road. Mitchell's attention was focussed on providing a more direct and easily graded route for the Great Western Road. Mitchell surveyed and recommended the construction of a road along this route midway between the other two in preference to the Governor's suggestion of stationing a permanent repair gang on the Old Bathurst Road.

A Plaid Cymru MP believes UK security services were involved in some arson attacks blamed on Welsh extremists.
It is 25 years since the start of 12 years of fire-bombings, attributed to a shadowy group known as Meibion Glyndwr. Plaid Cymru's Elfyn Llwyd has suggested the security services could have been involved, with the intention of discrediting the nationalist vote. Ex-Welsh Office Minister Lord Roberts of Conwy denied security services were involved. In March this year, North Wales Police reopened the case, saying materials kept during their investigations would be examined to find whether it would yield DNA evidence.
Meibion Glyndwr - which means "sons of Glyndwr" - began burning property in December 1979 in protest at homes in rural Wales being sold as holiday cottages to people from England. The group was linked to most of the 220 or so fire-bombing incidents stretching from the Llyn Peninsula to Pembrokeshire. The campaign continued until the early 1990s. Police were accused in some quarters of targeting anyone who was a nationalist. Although one man, Sion Aubrey Roberts, was convicted in 1993 of sending letter bombs in the post, the arson cases remain unsolved.
As a solicitor, Elfyn Llwyd represented Welsh singer Bryn Fôn when he was arrested on suspicion of being involved in the arson campaign. Fôn was released without charge . But now, as MP for Merionnydd Nant Conwy and Plaid Cymru's Parliamentary Leader, Mr Llwyd has argued that some of the terror attacks may have had the involvement of the security services and not Meibion Glyndwr. He believes that elements of the British security services may have carried out renegade actions in order to discredit Plaid Cymru and the nationalist vote ahead of elections. The claim is made in an interview for BBC Wales' Maniffesto programme to be shown on S4C on Sunday.
Mr Llwyd said that the sophistication of many of the devices used in the attacks compared to the crude nature of many others, suggests a degree of professionalism which could only have come from individuals who knew exactly what they were doing. He said: "What I'm saying is that the role that they took wasn't the appropriate one, i.e. like an
agent provocateur
and perhaps interfering and creating a situation where it looked like it was the nationalists that were responsible." The programme also heard from Lord Roberts of Conwy, who was a Welsh Office minister at the time. He denied that the security services played any improper role. Mr Llwyd's theory has also been questioned by Plaid Cymru's former President, Dafydd Wigley. He accepted that the fires damaged Plaid Cymru's public image but believed that the security services had their hands full at the time with the IRA and animal rights activists.

Instructions: Choose twelve unblemished, organically grown small lemons, preferably Meyer (a smaller variety). Wash and dry the lemons. If using store-bought lemons, thoroughly clean them to eliminate any pesticides. Remove a thin slice from the top and bottom of each lemon. Place one lemon on its side and make a vertical cut 3-quarters of the way through the fruit, ensuring the two halves remain attached at the base; do not cut the lemon in half. Flip the lemon over and turn it so that you can make another vertical cut across the middle, perpendicular to the first cut, leaving the bottom intact. Fill each cut with as much salt as it can hold. Position the lemon at the bottom of a hot, sterilized, wide-mouthed quart glass jar. Repeat the process with the remaining lemons, pressing them into the jar until no space remains and the lemon juice rises to the top. Seal the jar and keep it at room temperature. Additional lemons can be added later as the rinds become softer. Ensure the lemons are always covered with juice, adding fresh lemon juice as needed. The lemons are ready to use after 5 to 6 weeks when the rinds are tender. Lightly rinse them before use. Once opened, preserve the lemons in the refrigerator for up to 6 months.

Visual domain adaptation is an important problem in computer vision, and has been studied extensively by researchers at Google, Microsoft Research, and elsewhere. However, there are many challenges to overcome before we can achieve visual domain adaptation that are not well understood. We present VisDA (Visual Domain Adaptation), a novel approach to solving these problems. Our goal is to develop a general framework for visual domain adaptation that allows us to address all of the known issues with existing approaches. In particular, we aim to provide a unified model for visual domain adaptation that can be used to solve any problem involving visual domain adaptation. This includes both simple and complex cases. We also propose a new algorithm for visual domain adaptation that is based on a combination of two previously proposed algorithms. These algorithms have proven successful in other domains such as object recognition and speech recognition, but they do not yet fully capture the complexity of visual domain adaptation. We demonstrate how our new algorithm can be applied to several real-world applications, including image classification, face detection, and object localization.

Ingredients:
- 1 bag (12 oz) milk chocolate chips
- 1 bag (12 oz) dark chocolate chips
- 1 cup coconut oil, melted
- 1/2 cup caramel sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon sea salt

Instructions:

1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set it aside.

2. In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the milk chocolate chips, dark chocolate chips, and melted coconut oil. Microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring after each interval until the chocolate is smooth and fully melted.

3. Pour the chocolate mixture onto the prepared baking sheet and use a spatula to spread it into an even layer.

4. Drizzle the caramel sauce over the chocolate layer and use a knife to swirl it into the chocolate.

5. Sprinkle the sea salt over the caramel and chocolate.

6. Place the baking sheet in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes, or until the chocolate is firm.

7. Break the chocolate bark into small pieces and serve. Store any remaining bark in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Addams Family Reunion is a 1998 American direct-to-video comedy horror children's film based on the characters from the cartoon created by cartoonist Charles Addams. Directed by Dave Payne, the film was intended to serve as a pilot for a new proposed television series produced by Saban. The film stars Daryl Hannah and Tim Curry as Morticia and Gomez Addams respectively while Carel Struycken and Christopher Hart's hand are the only ones to reprise their roles from the last two films. The film's plot focused on the eccentric, macabre aristocratic Addams family mistakenly arriving at the wrong family reunion and encountering a man (Ed Begley Jr.) who seeks to commit murder in order to inherit a fortune. Payne had intended to give the film a dark, edgy tone, but Saban had interfered with the development, insisting that the story be aimed solely at entertaining children, and lack much of the black comedy and satire of the previous films. Saban also wanted Payne to imitate aspects of Paramount Pictures' popular 1991–93 duo of films, and the 1964 TV series, and rejected any original idea developed by Payne and the film's screenwriters. As a result, the film was poorly received by critics, who criticized the film's screenplay, special effects, production design, and much of its acting, while singling out Tim Curry's performance for praise, calling Curry the best part of the film.

This fourth and final installment in the Shrek series has many things going for it, but it never quite comes together as a whole. While the previous installments managed to find a perfect balance between hilarious slapstick humor, witty references, and an actual story, this one seems to have forgotten the latter, favoring instead cheap laughs and spectacle over genuine wit and emotion. As a result, the movie feels long and drawn out, even at a relatively short 84 minutes. 

The story picks up shortly after the events of the third film, with Shrek (Mike Myers) and Fiona (Cameron Diaz) married and dealing with the responsibilities of being parents to their young son Arthur (Diablo Cody). However, Shrek starts to become overwhelmed by the monotony of his daily life and loses his edge. His friends Donkey (Eddie Murphy) and Puss In Boots (Antonio Banderas) try to help Shrek find his former self by transporting him back in time to when he was a scared and nervous teenager who had yet to find his confidence. The majority of the film is then spent with Shrek interacting with his younger self ( Milo Murphy) as he tries to teach him the importance of being true to oneself and not backing down from what you want.

The concept of Shrek losing his edge and needing to be reminded of the importance of being true to oneself is a compelling one, and it could have made for a really powerful and emotional story. However, the movie opts for a much more lighthearted and simplistic approach, with little focus on genuine character development or exploration of the theme. Instead, it relies on cheap gags and slapstick humor, much of which feels forced and unnecessary. 

The animation is as impressive as ever, with the movie's universe expanding to include new locations and characters. However, the characters themselves feel somewhat flat this time around, with little growth or development over the course of the film. The voice acting is also lack-ranging from Myers and Murphy's lackluster performances to Cody's grating teenaged vocal affectations. 

In the end, Shrek Forever After is a disappointing end to an otherwise fantastic series. While it has some memorable moments and laughs, it fails to live up to the standards set by the previous films and feels like a missed opportunity to go out with a bang.

Paula Radcliffe has been granted extra time to decide whether to compete in the World Cross-Country Championships.

"There is no question that Paula would be a huge asset to the GB team," said Zara Hyde Peters of UK Athletics. "But she is working out whether she can accommodate the worlds without too much compromise in her marathon training." Radcliffe must make a decision by Tuesday - the deadline for team nominations. British team member Hayley Yelling said the team would understand if Radcliffe opted out of the event. "It would be fantastic to have Paula in the team," said the European cross-country champion. "But you have to remember that athletics is basically an individual sport and anything achieved for the team is a bonus. "She is not messing us around. We all understand the problem." Radcliffe was world cross-country champion in 2001 and 2002 but missed last year's event because of injury. In her absence, the GB team won bronze in Brussels.

Dictogloss is an open-source software tool used by speech and language therapists, educators, and linguists to transcribe audio recordings into text in real time. It was developed as part of the Open Source Speech Recognition Project (OSSR) with funding from the European Commission's Human Languages Technologies Consortium program.

The software uses state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms to recognize spoken words and convert them into written text. The user simply records a conversation or podcast using their computer microphone, and Dictogloss will automatically generate captions that are displayed on the screen word for word. As the audio plays back, users can also edit and correct any misrecognized words directly within the application.

One advantage of Dictogloss is its ability to transcribe different accents and languages accurately. This makes it a useful tool for anyone who wants to improve their writing skills in another language or needs assistance reading complex material in their native tongue. Additionally, its modular design allows users to customize the experience to meet their specific needs, such as adjusting the speed at which the captions are generated.

Dictogloss has gained popularity due to its accessibility and affordability compared to other commercial transcription services. With its simple interface and rich features, it provides researchers and instructors with a powerful tool to analyze audio content or provide feedback to their students in a more efficient way than ever before.

200 grams Bread (strong) flour
20 grams Whole egg
2 grams Salt
20 grams Castor sugar
3 grams Instant dry yeast
110 grams Water
15 grams Butter
6 Aluminum foil baking cups (size 9)
1/2 the recipe quantity "Secret Apple Filling"
20 grams Walnuts
10 grams Sliced almonds
30 grams Powdered sugar
1/2 tsp Water
Bring the butter and egg to room temperature. Toast the walnuts for 7 minutes in a 180C oven (no need to pre-heat). When the walnuts have cooled slightly, crush with your hands into fairly small bits. Strain the egg through a sieve. You will need 20 g for the bread dough, and the rest can be set aside for later. If you have a bread machine, put all of the ingredients into the bread pan and turn it on! (If kneading by hand, see.) In the meantime, make the filling. Work quickly. For this recipe, I would recommend cutting the apples into 5 mm-1 cm slices, as opposed to wedges. When the apples have cooled a bit, drain them well in a colander. When the bread maker finishes, do a "finger check" (coat your finger with flour and poke a hole in the dough. If it doesn't spring back, you know that the first rising is complete). If the dough springs back, it hasn't finished rising. Let it sit for about another 5 minutes. If the dough has shrunk, it means you have let it rise too much. There's nothing you can do about this, so it's best just to proceed to the next step, bearing in mind that your rolls might not turn out the greatest! Carefully take the dough out of the bread machine with a bench scraper. Punch down the dough. Shape the dough into a ball. Make it nice and smooth. Close the seam tightly on the bottom. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 15 minutes. Place the dough seam-side up and, using a rolling pin, lightly mark the dough with a cross. Roll out the dough, but leave approx. 1 cm on either end un-rolled (this helps achieve an even thickness). Roll out the dough into a 25 cm square. (This is easiest if you work from the centre, leaving the top, bottom, and sides until the very end). Thoroughly drain the apple filling and spread it out on the dough, leaving 2 cm at the end furthest from you empty. Roll it up from the end nearest you. Close the seam tightly, as you did when making the dough. Cut the dough into 6 pieces with a bench scraper (start by cutting it in half, then cut each half into 3 pieces.) Spread out the aluminum foil baking cups and place a roll in each cup. Let rise once more, this time at 40C on your oven's 'bread rising' setting. This is what they look like after the second rising. Pre-heat the oven to 190C. While waiting for it to heat, brush the rolls with the leftover egg and top with sliced almonds and walnuts. When heated, pop them into the oven for 12 minutes. Adjust the baking time according to your oven. Take the rolls out of the oven and cool on a wire rack... Mix together the icing ingredients until thick (make sure not to over-mix or it'll be hard). Drizzle the icing on the rolls! Even if you just drizzle it on at random, these will look surprisingly professional when finished, so don't worry too much. And with that, you're done!

Natalie Bookchin (born October 26, 1962) is an American artist and writer who works with sound, video, and other media. She is best known for her experimental and often abstract work, which explores the relationship between humans and technology.

Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Bookchin studied at the University of Pennsylvania and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She began her career as a composer and performer, creating works that combined music with spoken word and video. In the early 1990s, she began to focus more on video and installation art, often using found footage and other materials to create works that explored the impact of technology on society and the environment.

Bookchin's work has been exhibited and screened internationally, and she has received numerous awards and fellowships, including a Guggenheim Fellowship and a Rockefeller Fellowship. She is currently a professor of media studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and is a member of the board of directors of the Electronic Frontier Foundation.

Let $ D $ be a bounded domain in $ n $-dimensional Euclidean space with a smooth boundary. We define appropriate Sobolev spaces of negative smoothness to analyze the nonhomogeneous Cauchy problem for an elliptic first-order differential complex $ \{A_i\} $. Specifically, we examine the traces of the tangential component $ t_i(u) $ and normal component $ n_i(u) $ of a vector-function $ u $ within the corresponding Sobolev space and formulate the problem appropriately. If the Laplacians of the complex satisfy the uniqueness condition in the small, we derive necessary and sufficient solvability criteria for the problem and provide formulas for both exact and approximate solutions. For the Cauchy problem in the Lebesgue space $ L^2(D) $, we construct approximate and exact solutions with maximal regularity. Additionally, employing Hilbert space techniques, we derive Carleman's formulas for a vector-function $ u $ from the Sobolev space $ H^1(D) $ based on its Cauchy data $ t_i(u) $ on a subset $ S $ of the domain’s boundary and the values of $ A_i u $ in $ D $ modulo the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Several instructive examples of elliptic operator complexes with constant coefficients are presented.

A soldier stations overseas is slowly losing his mind. This film is a very realistic view on what it's like to be a soldier. It's a very in-depth look at the day-to-day activities of these soldiers, and how they have very little to do, and the extremely dull existence they live. All they do is play cards, eat, sleep, and scrub the tank they're stationed in. There's very little dialogue throughout the entire movie. It's just a very realistic, in-depth look at what these soldiers have to go through. It's not an exciting, action-packed war movie. There are no firefights, no explosions, no gunfire, nothing like that. Just a dull existence. I thought it was a very interesting, and apparently widely accurate, look at the day-to-day life of a soldier.

The only downside to the movie is the lack of character development. We never really get to know any of the characters, or care about them. So, when something eventually does happen in the movie, it's very difficult to become involved or care about what's going on. It's a very slow, dull movie, but I think that's the point. Overall, it's a very interesting movie, but it's not for everyone. If you're looking for an exciting, traditional war movie, this isn't it. But if you want a very realistic, in-depth look at what soldiers have to go through, this is a great movie.

Barbara Harris (December 14, 1935 – August 11, 2020) was an American bishop in the Episcopal Church and the first woman to become a bishop in the Anglican Communion. She was also the first woman to be ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church, and the first woman to serve as a diocesan bishop in the Anglican Communion.

Harris was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Temple University with a degree in education in 1957. She worked as a teacher and counselor in the Philadelphia public school system before attending the Episcopal Divinity School in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where she earned her master of divinity degree in 1966. She was ordained a priest in the Episcopal Church in 1967, and served as curate at All Saints' Church in Worcester, Massachusetts. She became the first woman to serve as a priest in the Episcopal Church. In 1974, she became the chaplain at MIT and minister at Saint Paul's Church in Cambridge, Massachusetts. She was named the eleventh bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts in 1989 and was consecrated on March 16, 1990, by Edmond L. Browning, the presiding bishop of the Episcopal Church. She served as bishop until her retirement in 2003.

Harris was a strong advocate for the full participation of women in the church, and worked to improve the status of women and girls worldwide. She served on the board of the Center for Women in Church and Society, and was a founding member of the National Organization for the Promotion of Episcopal Schools. She also served as a member of the President's Council on Bioethics. In retirement, Harris continued to serve as an assistant bishop in the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts and as a visiting lecturer at Episcopal Divinity School. She died on August 11, 2020, at the age of 84.

Over 5.2 million Germans were unemployed in February, according to recent data. This figure, representing 12.6% of the working-age population, marks the highest jobless rate in Germany since the 1930s. The situation has drawn attention as the leader of Germany's government economic advisory panel expressed concerns about potential stagnant growth. Bert Ruerup, speaking on German television, stated that the previously projected 1.4% growth was overly optimistic and warned that actual growth might only reach 1% in 2005.

To address the persistent high unemployment rates, the German government has implemented various labor market reforms. A key initiative is the "Hartz-IV" program launched in January, aimed at restructuring welfare benefits and encouraging individuals to return to work, including roles with significant financial support. These developments are expected to place additional strain on the government. The figures, which were widely reported in German media prior to release, led to widespread criticism of Chancellor Gerhard Schröder's Social Democratic-Green Party leadership. Schröder initially campaigned on the promise of reducing unemployment.

Despite these challenges, some indicators suggest the employment landscape is not entirely dire. The rising official unemployment rate stems from changes in the calculation method, which increased the jobless count by over 500,000 in January. After adjusting for seasonal variations, the overall unemployment rate stands at 4.875 million people or 11.7%, a slight increase from the previous month. According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), there were 3.97 million unemployed individuals in January, with the ILO also reporting 14,000 new net jobs added, bringing the total employed to 38.9 million. The ILO classifies an unemployed individual as someone who actively sought work within the past four weeks.

1 whole 12" Round Pre-Cooked Pizza Crust (like Boboli)
1 Tablespoon Olive Oil
9 ounces, weight Frisch's Tartar Sauce
1 pound Cooked Ground Beef, Drained
Dill Pickle Chips/ Slices (to Taste)
1 cup Shredded Mild Cheddar Cheese
Shredded Iceberg Lettuce (pre-packaged Bag), Washed & Dried
Preheat oven (with pizza stone, if you have one) to 450 F. Place pre-cooked pizza crust onto a pizza pan (or a pizza peel if you are using a stone). Using a pastry brush, coat the crust evenly with olive oil from edge to edge. Next, coat the crust evenly with tartar sauce using the back of a large spoon or rubber spatula, leaving about a 3/4 border. Add the drained and cooked ground beef and then place dill pickles evenly across the pizza (as you would pepperoni). Next sprinkle the cheese evenly over the pickles and meat. Put pizza into oven (in the pan or slide it onto the stone). Bake pizza for about 6-8 minutes, then remove it from the oven, add the lettuce, and bake for another 2 minutes or so. (You can add lettuce anytime during cooking, or wait until it is completely done cooking, depending on your preference). Bake pizza for a total of 8-10 minutes, or until cheese is completely melted & edge turn golden brown. Remove pizza from oven and cut into 6-8 wedge pieces. Notes: If you have a pizza stone, I highly recommend using it. This pizza reheats really well, so keep any leftovers in an airtight container, stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Adapted from a combination of Frischs Recipes and my brothers direction.

1/3 cup ranch dressing
1 teaspoon hot chile paste (such as sambal oelek)
4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1 inch pieces
24 (1-inch) pieces red onion
12 slices thick cut bacon
salt and black pepper to taste
12 (6 inch) bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 2 hours
Whisk together ranch dressing and hot chile paste in a large bowl. Mix in chicken pieces and toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 hours. Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove chicken from the bag and transfer to a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Pat chicken pieces dry with more paper towels. Thread a piece of onion about 1 1/2 inches down the skewer. Thread the end portion of one strip of bacon onto skewer so the rest of the strip is hanging down. Skewer on a piece of chicken; thread on the next portion of the bacon. Turn the skewer so that the long end of the bacon is again hanging down. Repeat this process of skewering and turning until the entire strip of bacon is threaded, using 4 to 5 chicken pieces. Thread a second piece of onion onto the end of the skewer. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for all twelve skewers. Season chicken skewers with salt and pepper as desired. Cook the skewers on the preheated grill, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until nicely browned on all sides and the meat is no longer pink in the center, 12 to 16 minutes total per skewer. Serve with ranch dressing as a dipping sauce.

Frederick Peterson (March 1, 1859 – July 9, 1938) was an American neurologist and poet. Peterson was at the forefront of psychoanalysis in the United States, publishing one of the first articles of Freud and Jung's theories of Free Association in 1909. Peterson was born in Faribault, Minnesota. After graduating from the University at Buffalo, he attended the Universities of Vienna, Zurich, Strassburg and Gőttingen. Upon his return to the United States, he became a professor at the University at Buffalo in 1882. For the following decade he practiced as a neurologist in New York City. He was involved in Harold P. Brown's 1888 anti-alternating current dog electrocution demonstrations at Columbia University during the war of the currents and later that year was appointed by the New York Medico-Legal Society to lead up a committee finalizing the method of electrical execution via the electric chair in that state. He spent 1893–1894 as a professor at the University of Vermont.  In 1900 he was appointed president of the New York State Commission on Lunacy. From 1903 until his retirement, he served as a professor of psychiatry at Columbia University. He was also a well known connoisseur and collector of Chinese paintings.

Taylor suffered knee ligament damage playing against Ireland in Dublin in the 2004 Six Nations championship. "Simon is one of Scotland's truly world class players so it is a huge bonus," said team-mate Chris Paterson. "He brings a whole new dimension to us, especially in defence and his ability to slow the opposition ball down could be key against Italy if he is involved." Taylor has turned out for English side Saracens in recent weeks during a short-term loan to improve his fitness.
Edinburgh were not in action during the first two weeks of this season's Six Nations. So Taylor played the last 20 minutes of Saracens' win over Northampton and then 40 minutes in a friendly against South African Super 12 side The Cats. Scotland coach Matt Williams is due to name his match-day 22 on Thursday. Both Scotland and Italy have lost their opening two Six Nations games and, just like last season's encounter which Italy won, this weekend's game could turn out to be a battle to avoid the wooden spoon.

A slimming aid made from a southern African cactus is set to be developed by UK firm Phytopharm and Unilever.
Anglo-Dutch food giant Unilever will help the pharmaceutical firm develop the snacks containing Hoodia extract. Phytopharm shares jumped 10.7% on the news, with analysts saying sales of $600m (£309m) a year were possible. The plant, licensed to Phytopharm in 1997, has been used for thousands of years by the Sans bushmen of the Kalahari desert to stave off hunger. Studies have reportedly shown the plant curbs appetite instead of reducing calorific intake like many existing products.
Phytopharm will receive an initial fee of £6.5m from Unilever - out of a potential total of £21m - as well as future royalties on product sales. Under the deal, production of the Hoodia cactus at Phytopharm's nursery in South Africa will also rise from eight million plants to potentially hundreds of millions, said Phytopharm chief executive Richard Dixey. The firm had initially hoped to market a slimming drug from Hoodia with Pfizer. But the research collaboration came to an end in 2003. Analysts said Unilever could launch the new products in 2007. "This deal goes a long way to restoring the market faith in Phytopharm's pipeline after the Pfizer exit," said analyst Erling Refsum at Nomura.

Semantic segmentation plays a vital role in biomedical image analysis, where recent advances in deep learning have enhanced its capabilities. Nevertheless, conventional deep learning approaches remain underutilized due to the need for extensive training data for intricate models. This presents a significant challenge when dealing with biomedical images, as both data and corresponding annotations are limited resources. Manual annotation of these images is costly, as experts must label each pixel on samples containing multiple instances of the target anatomical structures (such as neurons, astrocytes, mitochondria, etc.). In this study, we propose a framework for Deep Active Learning tailored to practical applications. Our approach leverages the U-Net architecture and an overall uncertainty metric to identify which sample to annotate. It utilizes an uncertainty measurement derived from Monte Carlo sampling combined with Dropout regularization. Experiments were conducted on microscopic histology samples from the spinal cord and brain to perform myelin segmentation. Two realistic datasets consisting of 14 and 24 images, acquired under different conditions (Serial Block-Face Electron Microscopy and Transmitted Electron Microscopy), demonstrated that our method achieved the highest Dice score after incorporating three uncertainty-selected samples into the initial training set, compared to fifteen randomly selected samples. This significantly reduced the annotation workload. We focused on a feasible scenario and provided evidence showing that this simple implementation yields high segmentation accuracy with minimal labeled data. We anticipate that our framework could be beneficial for any biomedical researcher aiming to achieve efficient and accurate image segmentation on their own dataset. The code is accessible via https://github.com/neuropoly/deep-active-learning.

The Polyglot Petition for Home Protection marked the first global statement opposing the production and international trade of alcohol and narcotics, as well as the legalization of illicit pleasures. It acted as a significant initiative to draw attention to the necessity of international cooperation in regulating opiates and their derivatives. 

The petition was addressed to all world rulers and nations, and it was authored by Frances Willard, the president of the American Woman's Christian Temperance Union (WCTU), in 1884. It was disseminated globally through at least four WCTU missionaries who collected over 8 million signatures across more than 50 countries. These signatures were divided into three categories: individual women’s signatures, male endorsements, and attestations from leaders of organizations supporting the petition.

Signatures from the United States exceeded 750,000 and were sent to Mrs. Rebecca C. Shuman in Evanston, Illinois, where they were trimmed, mounted on white muslin, and bound with red and blue ribbons. British signatures, totaling 350,000, arrived pre-mounted in cloth and were presented to the U.S. president in February 1885. The Polyglot Petition is preserved in the Woman's Christian Temperance Union Administration Building in Evanston, Illinois, United States.

Waterford city is situated in south eastern Ireland, on the river Suir [pronounced Shure] about  from where the river enters the sea. Practically the entire city is built on the south bank of the river. The "Old town", now the business centre, clusters behind the broad quay-front on a low-lying strip of land left behind by a gentle loop of the river at this point. From this, the land rises sharply to the east and opposite to the west while remaining level in between. The eastern slopes are almost entirely occupied by private residential estates, while the western and southwestern prominences are largely given over to local council housing development. There are corresponding elevations on the north bank eastwards towards Christendom and westwards towards Mount Misery nothing. The rocks which form the base of the city all belong to the Palaeozoic Group – principally Ordovician shales underlying sandstone. On the East side of the city, the rock is crossed by an alluvial bank running N.E./S.W. At the cliffs alongside the banks of the River Suir, above Rice Bridge, inter-stratification of sharply-folded Ordovician Slates and Sandstone conglomerates may be clearly observed.

Barnett Frank, born on March 31, 1940, was a former American politician. He represented Massachusetts in the U.S. House of Representatives from 1981 to 2013. As a Democrat, Frank chaired the House Financial Services Committee from 2007 to 2011 and was a key supporter of the 2010 Dodd–Frank Act. A native of Newton, Massachusetts, Frank was recognized as one of the most influential gay politicians in the United States during his tenure in Congress. Raised in Bayonne, New Jersey, he attended Bayonne High School, Harvard College, and Harvard Law School. Before entering politics, he worked as a political aide, eventually securing election to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1972. Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1980 with 52% of the vote, he was reelected consistently by large margins. In 1987, he openly identified as gay, making him the first member of Congress to do so voluntarily. From 2003 to his retirement, he led the Democratic delegation on the House Financial Services Committee, serving as chair when his party held a majority from 2007 to 2011. In July 2012, he married his longtime partner, James Ready, becoming the first member of Congress to wed someone of the same sex while in office. Frank declined re-election in 2012 and was succeeded by fellow Democrat Joe Kennedy III. His memoir, "A Life in Politics from the Great Society to Same-Sex Marriage," was released in 2015.

"From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler" is a children's novel written by E.L. Konigsburg and published in 1968. The novel tells the story of Claudia Kincaid, a twelve-year-old girl who runs away from home to live in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City.

Claudia is fascinated by the statue of an angel in the museum and becomes determined to find out who created it. She enlists the help of her younger brother, Jamie, and together they set out to solve the mystery. Along the way, they meet a number of interesting characters, including the eccentric Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler, who takes them in and helps them with their quest.

In the end, Claudia and Jamie are successful in uncovering the identity of the angel's sculptor, and they learn a great deal about art, history, and themselves in the process. "From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler" is a delightful and timeless story that will resonate with readers of all ages.

Baked Clams Recipe
Ingredients:

24 littleneck clams
1/3 cup chopped onion
2 tablespoons butter
1/4 cup bread crumbs
1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).

2. In a small bowl, mix together onion, butter, bread crumbs, oregano, salt, and black pepper.

3. Arrange clams in a single layer in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Stuff clam shells with the bread crumb mixture.

4. Bake for 10 minutes, or until clams are opened. (Discard any clams that remain closed.)

5. Serve immediately.

"The Beautiful Madness" is TRESOR's second studio album, released on May 26, 2017, through his label VII Recordings. The album includes contributions from South African artists such as Da Capo, The Kiffness, Shotgun Fakes, Hugh Masekela, and the Mahotella Queens. With 16 tracks, it received recognition for Best Pop Album and was nominated for Album of the Year and Best Male Artist at the 24th South African Music Awards four months after its release. 

The album was largely influenced by African 80s dance music and was created during TRESOR's travels across Africa and Europe on long flights and in hotels. After releasing his debut album "VII," TRESOR began composing new songs to maintain focus amidst the challenges of adjusting to his new life and fame. His most ambitious dreams had become reality with "VII," allowing him to tour globally and achieve chart success in Europe. The album was inspired by the excitement and chaos that accompanied "VII." Life was accelerating rapidly; he felt overwhelmed by the events surrounding his music career while traveling. Thus, he crafted "The Beautiful Madness" to reignite his passion and honor the beauty of realizing his dreams.

In this work, we tackle the problem of source-free domain adaptation for image segmentation. To this end, we propose a simple and effective approach based on Cycle-Consistency Training (CCT). Our key idea is to train a segmentation model to be cycle-consistent, meaning that it should be able to map an image from the source domain to the target domain and back to the source domain while preserving the segmentation. To encourage this behavior, we design a loss function that penalizes the distance between the input and output images in the feature space as well as the distance between the segmentation masks of the input and output images. We evaluate our approach on two publicly available datasets and show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for source-free domain adaptation.

The story is set in 18th century Japan, and features a conflict between four very different characters - Oboko (nb, Obaku is a form of Zen), a poet of the wind and Buddhist monk; Izzi, court poet and extrovert; Lord Arishi, samurai and lord of the realm; and finally Matari, beautiful, intelligent, and on the run for her life. Yet they each have their own outlook on life, and their own sense of honour and morality. While individually we might applaud them as good men and true, the meeting of the three results in tragedy. If you're in the market for a new computer, you may be wondering what to do about the RAM shortages. For the past few months, RAM prices have been soaring, and availability has been constrained. The good news is that there are alternatives to traditional RAM that can provide similar performance.

One option is to use a smaller amount of RAM and supplement it with a large solid state drive (SSD). This will give you the benefit of fast boot times and short load times, without the high price tag of a fully loaded RAM setup.

Another option is to use a hybrid hard drive, which combines a large traditional hard drive with a smaller amount of flash memory. This can give you the best of both worlds in terms of price and performance.

Finally, you could opt for a computer with an integrated graphics processor, which can offload some of the work that would otherwise be handled by the RAM. This can help free up RAM for other tasks, and potentially improve performance.

No matter which route you choose, be sure to do your research and find the best option for your needs. With a little bit of creativity, you can find a computer that will suit your needs without breaking the bank.

This paper introduces the concept of witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes as a way to study the combinatorial structure of simplicial complexes. Witness structures are a generalization of simplicial complexes that allow for the representation of higher-dimensional combinatorial structures. Immediate snapshot complexes are a specific type of witness structure that capture the combinatorial structure of a system at a specific point in time. The paper presents algorithms for constructing witness structures and immediate snapshot complexes, as well as techniques for analyzing their properties. The authors demonstrate the utility of these concepts by applying them to various real-world examples, including social networks and biological systems. Overall, this paper provides a novel framework for studying the combinatorial structure of complex systems and offers new insights into their behavior.

Sony Pictures announced that production will commence next year, with a potential release in May 2006. Hanks will portray Robert Langdon, a character striving to unravel the murder of an individual from an ancient group that has safeguarded long-buried secrets. This marks Hanks' third partnership with Howard, as they previously collaborated on *Splash* and *Apollo 13*. 

Hanks, a highly recognizable Hollywood star, is known for his ability to ensure box office success through his presence in films. The story is a classic mystery centered around a global conspiracy related to the Holy Grail myth, emphasizing symbols and cryptography. The protagonist, a Harvard professor reminiscent of modern-day Indiana Jones, also appeared in Brown's initial novel *Angels and Demons*. The film intertwines art history with mythology, semiotics, and medieval history.

Rediffusion Singapore was a pioneering cable-transmitted, subscription-based radio station in Singapore that broadcasted predominantly in Chinese and English from 1949 to 2012. It is historically noteworthy as one of the earliest examples of subscription-based radio broadcasting. 

Highlighting its beginnings in Singapore back in 1949, Rediffusion began as Associate Rediffusion Services, a British-owned company. Based mainly in the city area, the Rediffusion service comprised of a network of cables that ran across the city linking homes and businesses. It featured daily broadcasts in four different languages: English, Malay, Chinese, and Tamil.

Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, it underwent several significant changes, including a name change from Associate Rediffusion Services to Rediffusion Singapore Pte Ltd in 1963. The next notable development in the company's progression came in the 1970s when Rediffusion underwent a period of localization and transitioned into an entirely Chinese language radio service.

In 1980, Rediffusion was sold to the Singaporean entrepreneur See Hoy Chan and became a wholly local company. During this period, it devoted substantially to the broadcasting of Chinese drama serials along with the sponsoring of several prominent local events, thereby reinforcing its cultural significance in the community. 

Rediffusion Singapore faced a significant challenge with the advent of free-to-air TV and FM radio services in the 1990s that led to a reduction in its subscriber base. The company attempted to reinvent itself by targeting niche listeners through content such as dialect programming, health, and wellness programs. The company underwent additional changes in management over the next few decades, yet continued to face declining subscriptions and financial difficulties. 

Amidst these challenges, Rediffusion decided to bid adieu to the cable radio broadcasting in 2011 after broadcasting for 62 years. The following year, in 2012, the company made its much-awaited return as a digital radio platform, but the revival was short-lived and the station ceased broadcasting permanently later in 2012.

Despite its cessation, Rediffusion Singapore holds a significant place in the history of Singapore's media landscape, having played a crucial role in the development of contemporary radio broadcasting in Singapore. To date, it echoes as an icon of nostalgia for those who recall the golden age of subscription-based radio stations.

The book is set in a large house called Warings near the village of Derne. It was once a grand countryside mansion, but has since fallen into disrepair and decay. Joseph Hooper has inherited the house, and lives with his son Edmund Hooper. They have a cold, formal relationship which lacks compassion. Joseph announces that a housekeeper will be moving in, who will also bring her son who is of a similar age to Edmund. Mrs. Helena Kingshaw, and her son Charles Kingshaw arrive at Warings. Hooper becomes defensive of his house, and instantly takes a disliking to Kingshaw. He mocks him about his social class and father, and a small fight ensues where Kingshaw punches Hooper. Kingshaw then attempts to escape Warings, but is attacked by a vicious crow. The crow is thought to symbolize Hooper, who is very protective of his territory. Animalistic symbolism is used throughout the novel. Hooper proceeds to taunt and bully Kingshaw, who acts as the weak victim in their relationship. They venture to Hang Wood together, where Hooper's weaknesses become apparent and Kingshaw seems to retrieve some kind of power. However, it is apparent that Kingshaw does not have the capacity to be cruel. This pattern of cruelty continues throughout the book within the isolated setting of Warings. Both parents seem oblivious to their fights, and lack an understanding of their children's antics. They travel to Hang Wood on a few more occasions. It appears that Hooper is vulnerable in this setting, away from his home. The family decide to take a trip to Leydell Castle. Here, Kingshaw further exploits Hoopers fears as they climb the ancient monument. Hooper falls by accident, and badly injures himself. Even though Kingshaw tried to save him Hooper accuses Kingshaw of pushing him and is believed by the adults. Kingshaw is convinced that he has killed Hooper. As Hooper recovers, it appears that Kingshaw gains independence and meets a local boy by the name of Fielding. Fielding appears confident and well-rounded, and takes Kingshaw to his farm where he witnesses the birth of a calf. This is in stark contrast to Warings, which is full of death morbidity. Glass cabinets filled with moths are used to symbolize the decay of the Hooper dynasty. Fielding offers Kingshaw hope away from the manipulative clutches of Hooper. However, once Hooper returns to health, the normal regime of taunting resumes. Hooper's cruelty climaxes, and Kingshaw is devastated when he discovers that Helena and Joseph have agreed to marry, and that Hooper and Kingshaw will attend school together. The novel ends with Kingshaw committing suicide by drowning himself in a river in Hang Wood and Mrs. Kingshaw comforting Hooper who is described as feeling a sense of triumph.

Pastry  
350 grams flour  
250 grams butter  
200 grams sugar  
1 pinch of salt  
1 lemon, rind of  
1 egg  

Filling  
500 grams sugar  
500 grams walnuts  
500 grams cream  
50 grams of honey in tablespoon  
1 egg yolk  

Cream the butter and sugar. Combine the flour, rind, salt, and egg on high speed until a dough forms. Split the dough into thirds and two-thirds, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the filling sugar until it turns a light brown color. Heat the cream (optional: using a microwave), then mix it with the caramel, stirring quickly. Add the honey, cook it until it reaches a rolling boil. Incorporate the nuts and mix thoroughly. Let it cool. Combine everything and let it rest. Roll out the larger pastry dough and place it in a greased 24 cm springform pan to cover the base and sides. Fill the pan with the cooled filling. Roll out the remaining dough to create a lid for the cake. Place the lid on top of the filling and secure the edges. Brush the top of the cake lightly with whisked egg yolk. Bake at approximately 180°C for 50–60 minutes. Remove from the oven and let it cool completely. Do not remove the cake from the tin until it is fully cooled. The cake should be entirely cold before serving; I kept mine in the fridge on the base and only took it off once it was cold and the filling had set. If the filling is still warm, the bottom may sag when you lift it.

Most recent semantic segmentation methods adopt a U-Net framework with an
encoder-decoder architecture. It is still challenging for U-Net with a simple
skip connection scheme to model the global multi-scale context: 1) Not each
skip connection setting is effective due to the issue of incompatible feature
sets of encoder and decoder stage, even some skip connection negatively
influence the segmentation performance; 2) The original U-Net is worse than the
one without any skip connection on some datasets. Based on our findings, we
propose a new segmentation framework, named UCTransNet (with a proposed CTrans
module in U-Net), from the channel perspective with attention mechanism.
Specifically, the CTrans module is an alternate of the U-Net skip connections,
which consists of a sub-module to conduct the multi-scale Channel Cross fusion
with Transformer (named CCT) and a sub-module Channel-wise Cross-Attention
(named CCA) to guide the fused multi-scale channel-wise information to
effectively connect to the decoder features for eliminating the ambiguity.
Hence, the proposed connection consisting of the CCT and CCA is able to replace
the original skip connection to solve the semantic gaps for an accurate
automatic medical image segmentation. The experimental results suggest that our
UCTransNet produces more precise segmentation performance and achieves
consistent improvements over the state-of-the-art for semantic segmentation
across different datasets and conventional architectures involving transformer
or U-shaped framework. Code: https://github.com/McGregorWwww/UCTransNet.

A City Remembered

In the valley, a forgotten city:
 discreets of ruined homes,
 fractured domes of marketplaces,
 crumbling statues of heroes.

Once a hive of industry,
 whispers of it stilled by time,
 now just a shell of grandeur,
 engulfed by the pines.

Where once iron elbows bowed,
 now only birdsong fills the air,
 and the murmur of brooks,
 as if nature seeks to repair.

Time's gentle touch, reclaiming brick and mortar,
 once a shield against the world,
 now just a memory of people,
 who lived, loved and endured.

Yet in this tranquil silence,
 I hear the echoes of laughter,
 see the ghosts of children,
 running through the meadows.

In my mind's eye, I can still picture them,
 though their images fade with time,
 I hear the echoes of their voices,
 though the wind has blown away their words.

In this forgotten place, I find a beauty,
 in the solitude and the silence,
 for in this city, now remembered,
 I feel a connection, as if I belonged.

The Make-Up is an American post-punk band from Washington, D.C. formed in 1995, consisting of ex-Nation of Ulysses frontman Ian Svenonius on vocals, James Canty on guitar and organ, Steve Gamboa on drums, and Michelle Mae on bass guitar.  The Make-Up were joined in late 1999 by a fifth member, Alex Minoff (of the groups Golden and Extra Golden), who played guitar with the group until the band's dissolution in early 2000. The Make-Up combined garage rock, soul, and a self-styled liberation theology to make a new genre they called "Gospel Yeh-Yeh".  This style led to an emphasis on live performances and interaction between the band and their audience, incorporating the audience into the performances as a "fifth member", creating what one reviewer described as ""highly energetic and participatory live shows". Parallel to the band's gospel musical stylings, the Make-Up produced music under a communism-influenced political philosophy that they saw as counter to the capitalist form of modern rock and roll and pop music.

The Bellman appeared disapproving, furrowing his brows.  
"If only you had spoken earlier!  
It's quite improper to discuss this now,  
With the Snark looming in the room!  
We ought all to mourn if you ever vanished again—  
Yet surely, my friend, when our journey commenced,  
You could have mentioned it then?  
It's quite improper to bring it up now—  
As I've already noted."  
The man known as 'Hi' responded, sighing,  
"I told you the moment we set sail.  
You might blame me for murder—or lack of wisdom—  
For we are all prone to weakness at times:  
But even the slightest attempt at deceit  
Was never among my faults!  
I spoke it in Hebrew, in Dutch, in German and Greek—  
But I entirely forgot that you speak English!"  
"A pitiful story," said the Bellman, his face growing more drawn with each word:  
"But after you've explained everything, further discussion would be pointless.  
'I shall speak,' he declared to his crew,  
'You will hear the full extent when I have time.'  
But the Snark is here again!  
It is your noble task to find it!  
To find it with needles, with care;  
To chase it with forks and hope;  
To threaten its life with a train ticket;  
To charm it with smiles and soap!  
For the Snark is an odd creature, one that cannot be captured by ordinary means.  
Try all you know, explore all you do not—  
No chance should be squandered today!  
For England expects—though I refrain from elaborating—  
It is a great maxim, though somewhat common:  
And you must prepare yourself for the fight by untying the items you require."  
The Banker endorsed a blank check (crossing it),  
And exchanged his loose coins for bills:  
The Baker carefully brushed his hair and beard,  
And cleared the dust from his clothes:  
The Boots and the Broker were sharpening a shovel—  
Each taking turns to grind it:  
But the Beaver continued weaving lace and displaying it.

Music downloading, for those that have rejected the free peer to peer services, can be a costly business.
The cost of paying even as little as 70p per track can add up, particularly for those people who own one of the new generation of players that can store thousands of songs. Paying per track for music is becoming as outmoded as paying per minute for internet access and alternative monthly or yearly subscription models are springing up as a more convenient, and ultimately cheaper way of owning music.
"Music fans are moving away from buying the traditional bundled package of a dozen or more songs that we used to call an album to newer ways that fit their lifestyle; either single tracks or subscriptions services," said Paul Myers, chief executive of Wippit, a UK-based music download service. While iTunes is doing good business with its sales of individual tracks to iPod owners, others are questioning whether the concept of owning music is even valid in the digital age. Napster is due to launch a new rental subscription service - dubbed Napster to Go in the UK in the next few months. The service can be used on players that support Microsoft Windows latest Digital Rights Management technology known as Janus. This includes players made by Samsung, Rio and Creative.
Currently on offer in beta-version in the US, the service costs $15 per month for unlimited downloads. The technology ensures that music downloaded to the player only remains playable while the user subscribes to the service. Users need to update their license on a monthly basis or the tunes will no longer play.
This has outraged some digital music lovers, especially as Napster already offers a cheaper service for downloading music to the PC. Napster claims the higher price is a result of record labels charging more for the to-go service and says it also offers "greater value" for customers. Mr Myers is not convinced a rental model will work for consumers. "We've been offering our unlimited music subscription service for more than three years now and our customers know what they want. Format interoperability, excellent value and the reassurance that music purchased from Wippit is theirs to keep and enjoy on whatever device they choose," he said. "Who wants to download a track that won't play next month if you decide to unsubscribe to the service or change portable player for an iPod or the latest mobile phone?" Wippit offers a download subscription service for £4.99 per month or £50 per year. It has a catalogue of around 60,000 songs.

Transitional bilingualism, also known as early-exit bilingualism, is a form of bilingual education where students with a native language different from the language of instruction in school are taught in their native language for a certain period before transitioning to the second language. This approach is designed to help students gradually adapt to the second language while maintaining their academic progress.

The main goal of transitional bilingualism is to ensure that students do not fall behind in their academic subjects while they are learning the second language. This is achieved by initially teaching students in their native language, then gradually increasing the use of the second language in instruction until it becomes the primary language of instruction. 

Transitional bilingualism programs typically last for two to three years. During this period, students receive instruction in their native language for a significant portion of the day, while the rest of the day is spent learning the second language. As students become more proficient in the second language, the amount of instruction in their native language is reduced.

The effectiveness of transitional bilingualism has been a subject of debate among educators and researchers. Supporters argue that it allows students to continue learning academic content while they are still gaining proficiency in the second language, thus preventing them from falling behind. They also argue that it helps students maintain their cultural identity and heritage, as they continue to learn and use their native language.

Critics, on the other hand, argue that transitional bilingualism does not promote long-term bilingualism and biliteracy, as it eventually leads to the replacement of the native language with the second language. They also argue that it may delay students' acquisition of the second language, as they spend a significant portion of their school day learning in their native language.

Despite these debates, transitional bilingualism remains a common approach to bilingual education in many countries, particularly in situations where students are expected to transition to using the second language in their daily lives. It is seen as a practical solution to the challenge of providing quality education to students who are not yet proficient in the language of instruction. 

In conclusion, transitional bilingualism is a form of bilingual education that aims to help students transition from their native language to a second language. While it has its critics, it is widely used and has been shown to be effective in helping students maintain their academic progress while they are learning a second language.

Mita Taupopoki ( – 14 January 1935) was a notable Māori tribal leader of New Zealand. He identified with Ngāti Wāhiao, a hapū (subtribe) of the Tūhourangi iwi of Te Arawa. He was born near Lake Rotorua, New Zealand, probably in 1845 or 1846. His father, Hēmana Te Whareiro of Ngāti Wāhiao, lived mostly at Whakarewarewa. His mother, Kanea II, was of Tūhourangi, and the Ngāti Tūnohopū hapū of Ngāti Whakaue. In 1864 Mita joined other Te Arawa who fought for the government in the wars of the 1860s. He returned to Whakarewarewa in 1874. In 1883 he represented several hapū of Ngāti Wāhiao in the Native Land Court in a case relating to land claimed by Ngāti Whakaue, including Whakarewarewa, and succeeded in claims to the land on the east side of the Puarenga Stream at Whakarewarewa, although other land was won by Ngāti Whakaue. His success in the land court contributed to a recognition of his leadership among the wider Tūhourangi, in addition to within Ngāti Wāhiao. The 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera killed many Tūhourangi, and survivors took refuge with Mita and his people at Whakarewarewa and Ōhinemutu. Mita continued to act in the Native Land Court, representing Tūhourangi, and in 1887 won recognition of their claims of the 211,000-acre Rotomahana–Parekārangi block. In 1910 he toured Australia, England and the United States with Maggie Papakura's cultural group. He died in hospital in Rotorua on 14 January 1935.

Manchester United re-signed him in 1999 as a substitute for Peter Schmeichel, but injuries and lack of first-team chances reduced his performance. He left Manchester United for Chelsea in 2001, where he faced challenges finding a consistent position in the starting lineup and continued to suffer from injuries. Ingredients:
- 1 pound rice noodles (bihon)
- 1/2 pound pork belly, sliced into thin strips
- 1/2 pound shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 cup ground pork
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 onion, minced
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil
- 4 cups shrimp stock (or chicken stock)
- 1/2 cup fish sauce (patis)
- 1/4 cup annatto powder (atsuete)
- 1 cup crushed pork cracklings (chicharon)
- 4 hard-boiled eggs, sliced
- 1/2 cup green onions, chopped
- 1/2 cup fried garlic
- 1/2 cup calamansi or lemon juice
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, heat the cooking oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and onion, and sauté until fragrant and translucent.
2. Add the ground pork and pork belly to the pot, and cook until browned and cooked through.
3. Pour in the shrimp stock and fish sauce, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for about 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
4. While the broth is simmering, prepare the annatto mixture. In a small bowl, mix the annatto powder with a few tablespoons of water to create a paste. Set aside.
5. Cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions, then drain and set aside.
6. In a separate pan, heat a tablespoon of cooking oil over medium heat. Add the shrimp and cook until pink and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.
7. In the same pan, add the annatto mixture and cook for a minute or two until the color is fully released. Pour this mixture into the simmering broth and stir well to distribute the color evenly.
8. To assemble the pancit palabok, place a serving of rice noodles on a plate. Ladle the broth over the noodles, making sure to include some of the meat and shrimp. Top with crushed pork cracklings, sliced hard-boiled eggs, green onions, and fried garlic.
9. Serve the pancit palabok with calamansi or lemon juice on the side for squeezing over the noodles. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
10. Enjoy your homemade Pancit Palabok!

Deep learning approaches for 3D brain vessel segmentation have not demonstrated the same level of success as in the segmentation of other organs and tissues. This is attributed to two main factors. Firstly, deep learning models often struggle with the accurate segmentation of smaller objects relative to the entire image size. Secondly, the intricate nature of vascular networks and the small size of blood vessels make obtaining sufficient annotated training data challenging. To tackle these issues, we introduce a new annotation-efficient deep learning framework for vessel segmentation. The framework eliminates pixel-wise annotations, instead requiring only weak patch-level labels to distinguish between vessel and non-vessel 2D patches during training, akin to the CAPTCHA system used to differentiate humans from bots. The provided weak annotations are employed for two purposes: first, to generate pixel-wise pseudo-labels for vessels and background within each patch, which are then used to train a segmentation network; second, to train a classifier network. The classifier network generates additional weak patch labels, further decreasing the annotation workload, and functions as a noise filter for low-quality images. We apply this framework to segment the cerebrovascular tree in Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI). The results indicate that the framework achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing annotation time by approximately 77% compared to learning-based methods using pixel-wise labels.

Suck is the second live album by the American punk rock group the Queers, released in 1995 through the independent label Clearview Records. It was recorded live at the Jam Room in Columbia, South Carolina, and released as a single-sided picture disc. A compact disc version was issued in 1998. This album marked the only live recording by the Queers during the time when Screeching Weasel's members Dan Vapid and Dan Panic were also part of the band.

The album is described as the definitive Queers live album.

The events of The Bastard Prince span a period of approximately six months, from late May to late December of 928. The novel begins after the invasion of Prince Marek Furstán-Festil, the bastard child of the last Deryni ruler of Gwynedd, King Imre, and his sister, Princess Ariella. Supported by his Torenthi relatives, Marek has occupied the town of Culliecairn and slain Earl Hrorik II of Eastmarch. Word of the invasion is quickly sent to Rhemuth, where King Rhys Michael Haldane has spent the first six years of his reign as an imprisoned puppet of his lords of state. When a Torenthi herald arrives at Rhemuth to challenge the king, the great lords realize that they must permit Rhys Michael to go to Eastmarch and personally respond to the invasion. Disguised as one of Queen Michaela's serving maids, Rhysel Thuryn quickly learns of the king's plans to accompany his army to Eastmarch. Rhysel meets with members of the Camberian Council and attempts to convince them to activate the king's Haldane potential before he leaves the following day. Despite his own objections, Father Joram MacRorie, Rhysel's uncle, eventually agrees to her plan. That night, Joram and Tieg Thuryn, Rhysel's brother, infiltrate the castle and meet with the king. Tieg unblocks the Deryni powers of both Michaela and her brother, Sir Cathan Drummond, and Michaela then assists Tieg, Rhysel, and Joram in activating Rhys Michael's arcane powers. After the ritual, Joram and Tieg capture Master Dimitri, a Torenthi Deryni collaborator who has been working for the great lords. The Camberian Council alters Dimitri's mind with their own set of commands before returning him to Rhemuth. The next day, Rhys Michael departs the capital with army, accompanied by Cathan, Earl Manfred MacInnis, Earl Rhun von Horthy, Lord Albertus, and Father Paulin Sinclair. Before departing the city, Constable Udaut is killed when Dimitri secretly uses his powers to spook Udaut's horse. Later on the journey, a swarm of bees mysteriously attacks the royal party and nearly kills Albertus. Several days later, Albertus questions Rhys Michael about the incidents, concerned about the rumored magical powers of the Haldane family. He orders Dimitri to probe the king's mind, but the Deryni is still under the compulsions of the Camberian Council. To protect the king, Dimitri kills Albertus and later allows himself to be implicated in the death. When Paulin attempts to confine Dimitri, he lashes out with his powers and destroys Paulin's mind before be overcome. Dimitri is tortured for several hours before he is killed by a mental death-trigger in his own mind. The royal army arrives at Lochalyn the next day, where it is joined by the levies of Duke Graham of Claibourne, Earl Sighere of Marley, and Earl Corban Howell of Eastmarch. In a private conversation, Lady Sudrey, Hrorik's Deryni widow, offers Rhys Michael her support and the use of her limited powers. The following morning, Rhys Michael agrees to meet with Prince Miklos of Torenth, who claims to have led the invasion on Marek's behalf. Accompanied by Sudrey, the king parleys with Miklos briefly, but Miklos breaks the peace by attacking Sudrey. Rhys Michael uses his own powers to protect himself and kill Miklos, but Sudrey is killed in the battle and Rhys Michael is wounded when a horse steps on his hand. Afterwards, the king claims that it was Sudrey who used magic in the battle, and later realizes that Miklos' companion was actually Marek himself. After Miklos' death, Marek withdraws his forces and returns to Torenth. Rhys Michael asks the northern lords to help him break free of the great lords, and Graham and Sighere agree to become Regents for the king's son, Prince Owain, if anything should happen to the king. Cathan prepares a codicil to the king's will, and all parties involved succeed in signing it without alerting Rhun or Manfred. The king departs for Rhemuth the next day, but the progress of the army is slowed by the worsening condition of his injury. The army is eventually forced to stop at Saint Ostrythe's Convent when the king becomes too ill to continue. Dom Queron Kinevan rushes to the king's side, but he does not arrive in time and Rhys Michael soon dies from poor medical treatment. As the army returns to Rhemuth with Rhys Michael's body, the Camberian Council informs the northern lords of the king's death and offers their assistance in securing the rights of the new Regents. In Rhemuth, Cathan is drugged and imprisoned, but Michaela and Rhysel succeed in activating Owain's Haldane potential. Over the next several days, the northern lords ride toward Rhemuth, eventually arriving on the morning of Rhys Michael's funeral. Accompanied by Queron, Tieg, Ansel MacRorie, and a band of armed men, Graham and Sighere confront the great lords inside the royal tomb. Rhun kills Manfred and flees with Owain, while Earl Tammaron takes Michaela hostage. As Cathan pursues Rhun, Michaela uses her powers to slay Tammaron. Cathan catches Rhun atop a tower and the two engage in a brief fight before Rhun is killed. Several months later, Michaela visits her husband's tomb in the royal crypt. Owain has been crowned as King of Gwynedd, and Cathan now serves on the Regency Council with her, Graham, and Sighere. This study introduces an efficient automated color image segmentation technique that employs a seeded region growing and merging approach based on square elemental regions. The segmentation process involves three stages: creating seed regions, combining these regions, and applying a pixel-based boundary identification algorithm to the resulting polygonal areas. Key aspects of this method include the utilization of square regions instead of pixels as the processing unit, a seed generation strategy relying on enhanced gradient values, a region-growing procedure that leverages local gradient information, a merging technique utilizing a similarity metric incorporating Tsallis entropy-based homogeneity distance, and a termination criterion based on an estimated target number of regions. Employing square regions significantly lowers the computational complexity of the algorithm and ensures consistent performance. Experimental findings indicate that the proposed method maintains stable performance across diverse natural images, including highly textured regions, and achieves effective segmentation with identical parameter settings. The outcomes of the method are reasonably comparable to, and sometimes superior to, those of existing segmentation techniques.

Semantically segmented models developed using public datasets have shown significant success in recent years. Nevertheless, these models did not account for the personalization aspect, which is crucial in practical applications. In this study, we tackle the challenge of personalized image segmentation. Our goal is to achieve more precise segmentation outcomes on unlabelled personalized images by examining the unique characteristics of the data. To advance future studies in this domain, we gather a comprehensive dataset comprising diverse users' personalized images, referred to as PIS (Personalized Image Semantic Segmentation). We also evaluate several recent studies on this topic and present their performance on our dataset. Additionally, by analyzing the relationships between a user's personalized images, we introduce a foundational approach that integrates inter-image context during the segmentation of specific images. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses existing approaches on the proposed dataset. The code and the PIS dataset will be made freely available.

Many natural decision problems can be represented as constraint satisfaction problems for reducts $\mathbb{A}$ of finitely bounded homogeneous structures. This category of problems encompasses a significant extension of the classical CSPs over finite domains. Our initial finding presents a general polynomial-time transformation from such infinite-domain CSPs to finite-domain CSPs. By employing this reduction, we derive novel polynomial-time tractability criteria that depend on the topological polymorphism clone of $\mathbb{A}$. Additionally, we investigate the subclass $\mathcal{C}$ of CSPs for structures $\mathbb{A}$ that are reducts of a structure equipped with a unary language. This subclass $\mathcal{C}$ also extends the class of all finite-domain CSPs. Using our derived tractability conditions, we confirm the general tractability conjecture of Bodirsky and Pinsker for reducts of finitely bounded homogeneous structures within the class $\mathcal{C}$.
