A little girl was playing in the garden 'round her home,
Mischief sparkled in her dark eyes and her curly hair was blond.
Innocent joy rang in the laughter of her happy, playful song:
'Dandelions are as pretty as the flowers that grow high.
I have picked some for you, Mommy, and I want to show you why.
They make tassels on our slippers; we can wear them, you and I.'
Into that happy garden crept a serpent black and long,
Shining sinister in the sunlight as he flicked a jeweled tongue.
Captivatedly she listened to his strange inviting song:
'Stolen candies can be sweeter than the ones your parents buy.
Taste how sweet they are, like honey, as I coil about your thigh.
It will be our little secret as we eat them, you and I.'
Secrets growing in a garden, in among the pretty blooms,
Rob children of their laughter; so that it was very soon
That a mother's heart was sighing a sad, foreboding tune:
'Oh, my daughter was so pretty, and I wish that I knew why
Such a change has come about her that it makes my spirit cry.
Her eyes have lost their glitter and she has not told me why.'
Little girls will always grow up; that, in life, has been decreed,
While secrets locked in childhood are concealed in history.
Yet the scars they are concealing will be sung in misery:
'Why do candies taste so bitter? Why does laughter make me cry?
Why do I have a feeling happiness has passed me by?
I'm living with a memory that will haunt me 'til I die.
Within me lives a memory that will haunt me 'til I die.'

Whole Wheat Ricotta Gnocchi Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1 cup ricotta cheese
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg (optional)
- 1/4 cup additional whole wheat flour (for dusting)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, ricotta cheese, egg, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg (if using). Mix well until all the ingredients are fully incorporated.

2. Sprinkle a clean surface with some additional whole wheat flour. Transfer the dough onto the floured surface and knead it gently for a few minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour, but be careful not to add too much as it can make the gnocchi dense.

3. Divide the dough into four equal portions. Take one portion and roll it into a long rope, about 1/2 inch in diameter. Cut the rope into small pieces, about 1 inch long. Repeat this process with the remaining dough portions.

4. To shape the gnocchi, you can either use a gnocchi board or the back of a fork. Hold the fork or gnocchi board at a slight angle and press each piece of dough against it with your thumb. As you press, the dough will curl around the fork or board, creating ridges on one side and a small indentation on the other. Place the shaped gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet or tray.

5. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Carefully drop the gnocchi into the boiling water, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pot. Cook the gnocchi for about 2-3 minutes, or until they float to the surface. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked gnocchi to a plate or colander.

6. Serve the whole wheat ricotta gnocchi with your favorite sauce, such as marinara, pesto, or browned butter with sage. Garnish with additional grated Parmesan cheese and fresh herbs, if desired.

Enjoy your homemade whole wheat ricotta gnocchi!

Semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentations have been tackled through distinct and specialized methodologies, although they share fundamental relationships. This paper introduces a cohesive, straightforward, and efficient approach to these closely related tasks. The proposed framework, called K-Net, ensures consistent segmentation of both instances and semantic categories via a set of trainable kernels. Each kernel generates a mask for either a potential instance or a specific class. To address challenges in differentiating instances, a kernel update mechanism is introduced, allowing each kernel to adapt dynamically based on its relevance within the input image. K-Net can be trained end-to-end with bipartite matching, and its training and inference processes are free from non-maximum suppression (NMS) and bounding box constraints. Without additional components, K-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art single-model results on MS COCO and ADE20K with 52.1% PQ and 54.3% mIoU, respectively. Its instance segmentation performance is comparable to Cascade Mask R-CNN on MS COCO, achieving 60%-90% faster inference times. The code and models will be made available at https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection.

1 pound trimmed fresh green beans
1 small red bell pepper, seeded and sliced
2 baby bok choy, sliced lengthwise
12 thin slices peeled fresh gingerroot
1 teaspoon ground coriander, 1/3 palmful
2 teaspoons seafood seasoning, 2/3 palmful (recommended: Old Bay)
Freshly ground black pepper
4 (6 to 8-ounce) black bass or sea bass fillets
1/2 cup hoisin sauce
1/4 cup orange juice
2 scallions, finely chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro leaves
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Cut off 4 large rectangles of foil, 16 to 18 inches each. Put a piece of the foil on a baking sheet and spread the other 3 across the countertop. Scatter 1/4 of the beans, peppers, and bok choy in the center of each piece of foil. Arrange 3 slices of ginger on top of each vegetable stack. Combine the coriander, seafood seasoning, and a few grinds of black pepper in a small bowl, then sprinkle the mixture over the top of the fish. Arrange the fillets over the vegetables. In a small bowl combine the hoisin with the orange juice, then drizzle the sauce evenly over the fish. Sprinkle with the scallions and cilantro and fold the long sides of the foil up over the fish. Roll the foil down a few turns to secure, then roll in the short sides to close the packet. Once the packets are formed you should be able to line them up on a large baking sheet. Bake until the fish is just opaque (open 1 packet to check), about 15 minutes. Remove the baking sheet from the oven and transfer the pouches onto serving plates. Open the pouches, and serve.

This paper presents a novel graph-based framework called Affinity Fusion Graph (AFG) for natural image segmentation. The AFG model integrates both the color and texture features of an image to enhance the discriminatory power. The scheme employs the fusion of multiple affinity matrices to form a comprehensive graph portraying an image’s structural and feature information. Utilizing a spectral clustering approach, the proposed framework exhibits improved segmentation by avoiding over-segmentation or under-segmentation that is common in other models. Experimental results on several datasets validate the effectiveness of AFG in comparison to other state-of-the-art methods in terms of achieving better segmentation accuracy and visual quality. The study opens up new avenues for the integration of different image features and multiple affinity graphs in natural image segmentation tasks.

A thaw in diplomatic ties between Egypt and Israel has led to the signing of a trade agreement with the United States, enabling Egyptian products manufactured in collaboration with Israeli companies to bypass tariffs on their way into American markets. The pact, signed in Cairo, establishes "qualified industrial zones" in Egypt, granting these zones' goods duty-free access to the U.S., provided that 35% of their components are produced through joint Israeli-Egyptian efforts. The U.S. regards this as one of the most significant economic agreements between Egypt and Israel in over two decades.

The agreement, which aims to create these zones, has faced prolonged delays due to concerns in Egypt regarding any cooperation with Israel while the country's peace negotiations with the Palestinians remain stalled. However, recent developments have shown a warming trend in bilateral relations. Both nations recently exchanged prisoners, with Egypt returning an Israeli man who had spent eight years in prison for espionage.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has highlighted Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon as the key figure for Palestinian peace. The Egyptian government now sees Sharon moving toward the center of the political spectrum, distancing himself from far-right groups. It also believes the U.S., under pressure from Europe, is becoming more open to engaging in discussions about a peace settlement. Nevertheless, there are pressing economic motivations behind Egypt’s decision to enter the agreement, as it is expected to significantly boost textile exports, which are set to decline due to new U.S. regulations taking effect at the start of the year.

It's likely that upon launching your browser, you'll immediately access your preferred search engine instead of manually entering a web address. Some might view this as a display of laziness, yet in today's information-saturated environment, search has evolved into a critical resource for navigating the internet. This reflects the shifting nature of how we interact with the web. Google exemplifies that, as offering a service indispensable to users generates substantial revenue. Numerous corporations compete to attract web searchers, providing diverse services and tools to fulfill their needs. In the past year, tech giants like Microsoft and Yahoo have aimed to capture a portion of the search traffic. "User experience has encouraged more searches," noted Yonca Brunini from Yahoo. As users grow more acquainted with the internet, they tend to spend more time online and pose more questions. "The other factor is broadband," she explained to the BBC News website. "Broadband will transform the internet much like color transformed television." 

Search is not a novel concept; it existed since the early days of the internet. Experienced surfers recall pioneers like Hotbot and Altavista. "Search was always crucial," stated Urs Holzle, Google's operations vice president. "We emphasized this in 1999. It's even more relevant now with more users and data." "People didn't foresee that search would be the future," he added. "Financials are tied to it." Google demonstrates that online shopping can thrive through targeted small advertisements appearing at the top and right side of a webpage, linked to the initial search. These ads contributed to Google's earnings of $805.9 million for the three-month period ending September. Others have recognized the potential to profit from web inquiries. "Once you realize there's a market, Microsoft will inevitably pursue it," said Holzle. "If Microsoft perceives search as vital, then no one will query it."

Kilroy-Silk expressed anger towards the attacker and intended to pursue legal action if apprehended. He recounted the incident, stating that the assailant shouted, "You've offended my religion, I'm doing this in the name of Islam." Greater Manchester Police confirmed that others nearby were also hit by the slurry. Statements were taken from the scene.

Ford has reported a shock increase in third-quarter profits thanks to a strong performance from its finance arm, not from car sales.

The automaker reported on Wednesday that adjusted earnings per share were $0.68, beating estimates of $0.39. Headline profit was $828m, also beating expectations.

But the really big surprise came from Ford's finance arm, which saw profits rise by a factor of eight to $2.3bn. That was far more than the $637m profit achieved by its automotive division.

Ford has finance arms in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe and China, and its operations helped to offset the impact of falling vehicle sales. Its automotive operations racked up losses in South America and Europe, but that was offset by the excellent performance of its money arm.

"That was clearly the biggest driver," said Nicholas Smith, a senior analyst with Strategy Analytics. "They are making more money per vehicle from their finance arms than they are from selling the vehicles."

Profits in North America were strong, Smith added, thanks to "very favourable pricing", with trucks and SUVs continuing to sell well. But he described the performance in Europe as "average" with a mix of currency issues and political instability.

Ford was able to beat expectations despite disruptions caused by the Covid-19 pandemic in South America and the impact of global chip shortages.

"Given the magnitude of those disruptions, we're pleased with where we are," President and CEO Jim Farley said on a conference call.

Ford is far from alone in trying to make money from financing as well as cars. Most auto manufacturers have finance arms, and they have been a valuable source of revenue in recent years.

The new unit, called Emerging Opportunities, will be "essentially an internal startup" that will "focus on areas including silicon design, hardware and software architecture, advanced manufacturing and artificial intelligence", Ford said last month.

Ford also has a joint venture with Volkswagen called Navistar that makes trucks and buses in North America.

1 large red cabbage  
13 cups red wine vinegar  
2 tablespoons sugar  
2 teaspoons salt  
6 slices bacon, fried and split  
2 tablespoons bacon fat (reserved from fried bacon)  
2 medium apples, peeled, cored, and sliced into 1/2-inch wedges  
12 onions, chopped  
1 onion, sliced and roasted with whole cloves  
1 bay leaf  
5 cups boiling water  
3 tablespoons dry red wine (optional)  
4 tablespoons red currant jelly  

Wash the cabbage under cold water and remove the outer leaves. Cut the cabbage into quarters. Remove the core and shred the cabbage into a large mixing bowl. Add the vinegar, sugar, and salt, then mix well. In a stockpot, fry the bacon over medium heat, ensuring it doesn't burn. Remove the bacon, reserving 2 slices (the remaining can be used in another recipe or as chef snacks). Keep the bacon drippings in the pot and heat them over medium heat. Add the onions and chopped vegetables, cooking for 5 minutes until they turn light brown. Add the cabbage, the whole onion with its cloves, and the bay leaf, then stir everything together. Pour in the boiling water, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 2 hours. Check occasionally during the final hour to ensure the cabbage remains moist; add water as needed. The cabbage is ready when most of the liquid has been absorbed. Just before serving, remove the onion with the cloves and the bay leaf. Stir in the wine (if using) and the currant jelly. Serve warm.

USS Indiana (BB-58) was the second of four  fast battleships built for the United States Navy in the 1930s. The first American battleships designed after the Washington treaty system began to break down in the mid-1930s, they took advantage of an escalator clause that allowed increasing the main battery to  guns, but refusal to authorize larger battleships kept their displacement close to the Washington limit of . A requirement to be armored against the same caliber of guns as they carried, combined with the displacement restriction, resulted in cramped ships, a problem that was exacerbated as wartime modifications that considerably strengthened their anti-aircraft batteries significantly increased their crews. Indiana entered service in April 1942, by which time the United States was engaged in World War II, and the ship was immediately pressed into action in the Pacific War against Japan. Her first combat came in late 1942 when she supported marines fighting during the Guadalcanal campaign. Over the next three years, she was occupied with two primary roles: naval gunfire support for amphibious assaults across the Pacific and anti-aircraft defense for the fast carrier task force. She shelled Japanese positions during the Battle of Tarawa in November 1943 and the Battle of Kwajalein in February 1944. During the latter operation, she collided with the battleship  and was forced to withdraw for repairs.

Clark Field was a baseball stadium located in Austin, Texas, primarily used by the University of Texas Longhorns. It operated from 1928 to 1974 and is known for its unique design. The field's location featured a limestone cliff in the outfield that posed challenges for outfield players and added excitement to the game. This cliff, which extended from left-center to center field, was accessible only through a goat path in left-center field and was famously nicknamed "Billy Goat Hill." A scoreboard stood atop the hill, creating unpredictable bounces that further complicated plays for outfielders. This feature provided the Longhorns with a significant advantage, as they often secured inside-the-park home runs when a ball approached the cliff. Outfielders became adept at reading the cliff's effects, allowing them to consistently strike out batters. Approximately half of the team's outfielders preferred playing on top of the cliff while the others played in front of it.

performance.

The main character of the narrative, Imama Hashim, comes from a prominent Ahmadi family residing in Islamabad. She converts to Sunni Islam due to influence from her peers. She secretly attends lectures at her senior shabiha's, attended by her roommates Javeria and Rabia. During her studies at a medical college in Lahore, she develops feelings for Zainab's younger brother, Doctor Jalal Ansar. However, her family insists she marry her first cousin, Asjad, which she rejects because marriage to a non-Muslim is forbidden. As a result, her parents lock her in her home and confiscate her mobile phone. Imama seeks assistance from Salar, whom she dislikes due to his lack of religious adherence. Salar is a wealthy individual with an IQ exceeding 150. Imama desires to marry Jalal, but Salar deceitfully informs her that Jalal has already wed someone else. This causes Imama great sorrow and requests Salar to marry her so that her family may not pressure her. Salar agrees and marries her, but soon loses touch with her. Imama finds refuge under Sibt-e-Ali and his family, changes her name, completes her academic pursuits, and begins working in a pharmaceutical firm in Lahore. She harbors resentment toward Salar for refusing to divorce her despite their promise. Salar later travels to New Haven for higher education, works for the United Nations for some time, and eventually settles in Lahore. Eventually, Salar recognizes his mistake and reforms. Later, the narrative shifts to a location near the Kaaba, where Salar and Imama sit together in worship of God. Salar acknowledges that God has blessed him with a devoted companion and resolves to safeguard her.

Here, as in childhood, Brother, no one knows us.
And someone has died, and someone is not yet
born, while our father walks through his church at night
and sets all the clocks for spring.  His sleeplessness
weighs heavy on my forehead, his death almost
nothing. in the only letter he wrote to us
he says, No one can tell how long it takes a seed
to declare what death and lightning told it
while it slept.  But stand at a window long enough,
late enough, and you may some night hear
a secret you'll tomorrow, parallel to the morning,
tell on a wide, white bed, to a woman
like a sown ledge of wheat.  Or you may never
tell it, who lean across the night and miles of the sea,
to arrive at a seed, in whose lamplit house
resides a thorn, or a wee man, carving
a name on a stone, at afluctuating table of water,
the name of the one who has died, the name of the one
not born unknown.  Someone has died.  Someone
is not yet born.  And during this black interval,
I sweep all three floors of our father's house,
and I don't count the broom strokes; I row
up and down for nothing but love: his for me, and my own
for the threshold, as well as for the woman's name
I hear while I sweep, as though she swept
beside me, a woman who, if she owns a face at all,
it is its own changing; and if I know her name
I know to say it so softly she need not
stop her work to hear me.  But when she lies down
at night, in the room of our arrival, she'll know
I called her, though she won't answer, who is on her way
to sleep, until morning, which even now,
is overwhelming, the woman combing her hair opposite
the direction of my departure.
And only now and then do I lean at a jamb
to see'if I can see what I thought I heard.
I heard her ask, My love, why can't you sleep?
and answer, Someone has died, and someone
is not yet born.  Meanwhile, I hear the voices
of women telling a story in the round,
so I sit down on a rain-eaten stoop, by the saltgrasses,
and go on folding the laundry I was folding,
the everyday clothes of our everyday life, the death
clothes wearing us clean to the bone, to the very
ilium crest, where my right hand, this hand, half
crab, part bird, has often come to rest on her,
whose name I know.  And because I sat down,
I hear their folding sound, and know
the tide is rising early, and I can't hope
to trap their story told in the round.  But the woman
whose name I know says, Sleep, so I lie down
on the clothes, the folded and unfolded, the life
and the death.  Ages go by When I wake, the story
has changed the firmament into domain, domain
into a house.  And the sun speaks the day,
unnaming, showing the story, dissipating the boundaries
of the telling, to include the one who has died
and the one not yet born.  Someone has died
and someone is not yet born.  How still
this morning grows about the voice of one
child reading to another, how much a house
is house at all due to one room where an elder
child reads to his brother, and that younger
knows by heart the brother-voice.  How darker
other rooms stand, how slow morning comes, collected
in a name, told at one sill and listened for
at the threshold of dew What book is this we read
together, Brother, and at which window
of our father's house?  In which upper room?
We read it twice: Once in two voices, to each
other; once in unison, to children,
animals, and the sun, our star, that vast office
of love, the one we sit in once, and read
together twice, the third time bosomed in
the future.  So birds may lend their church, sown
in air, realized in the body uttering
windows, growing rafters, couching seeds.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil on medium heat and season generously with salt. Place the bacon in a large, high-sided skillet and cook over medium-high heat until it becomes crispy, taking about 10 minutes. Remove the bacon from the heat and set it aside in the skillet. Denbigh is a heritage-listed site that once served as a vineyard, Clydesdale horse stud, Ayrshire cattle stud, and dairy farm, later evolving into a Hereford stud. It is situated at 421 The Northern Road in the southern-western suburb of Cobbitty, within the Camden Council local government area of New South Wales, Australia. The property was constructed in 1818 by Charles Hook, along with Thomas and Samuel Hassall, and Daniel Roberts. It remains privately owned. Denbigh was designated in the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 22 December 2006.

The original owner of Denbigh was Charles Hook, who was incarcerated by the rebel government for supporting Governor Bligh’s military efforts in New South Wales. Hook, aged fifty when he obtained his grant in 1812 from Governor Macquarie, was granted land in the parish of Cook, located near Cobbitty between the Cowpasture Road and Bringelly Road (later known as The Northern Road). In 1818, Hook and his wife resided at Macquarie Grove while constructing their own home. The building of Denbigh House was completed, and Hook commenced clearing the surrounding land for agricultural purposes. He passed away in 1826.

A prominent Japanese businessman, known for his contributions, was detained on Thursday on charges of fabricating shareholder data and manipulating share sales using false information. Yoshiaki Tsutsumi, once recognized as the world's wealthiest individual, led a business that included hotels, railways, construction, and a baseball team. He is among several high-ranking executives arrested in Japan due to business misconduct. On Thursday, he was removed from a van near one of his Prince hotels in Tokyo.

At one point, Tsutsumi appeared invincible, inheriting a significant real estate firm from his father in the 1960s, which positioned him as a major industrial figure in Japan, with ties to influential political figures. He leveraged his wealth and power to host the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano. However, last year, he resigned from all positions within his business empire after being implicated in falsifying the ownership structure of Seibu Railways, one of his companies. According to Japanese stock market regulations, no listed company can exceed 80% ownership by its ten largest shareholders. Tsutsumi now faces legal consequences for appearing to show that these shareholders held less than 80%. Seibu Railways has been delisted from the stock exchange, its value has dropped significantly, and it is under consideration for a takeover.

Tsutsumi's downfall mirrors the arrest of other senior executives in Japan as authorities seek to address the opaque business practices that were common in Japanese corporations. His relentless pursuit of success at all costs might have stemmed from his upbringing. As the illegitimate third son of a wealthy father who amassed his fortune through real estate investments post-WWII, he recounted the pressures he faced during meals with his father. "When I dined with him, I felt immense pressure, and it was painful," Tsutsumi stated in a 1987 interview with a weekly publication. "He would criticize me for pouring too much into something."

As with other leek orchids, the flowers are inverted so that the labellum is above the column rather than below it. Japanese electronics giant Hitachi has developed what it says is the world's fastest industrial robot, capable of moving at 10 metres per second (22mph).

The company said its new machine was able to move faster than any other on the market and could be used in factories for tasks such as welding or painting.

It can also handle heavy loads - up to 35kg (77lb) - which means it could be used to lift car parts into place during assembly.

"We believe this will help us win orders," said Yasuhiro Kawamura, head of Hitachi's factory automation division.

He added that the firm had already received several enquiries about the product since announcing it last week.

## Faster robots

Industrial robots are typically used by manufacturers to perform repetitive jobs more quickly and accurately than humans.

They have been around for decades but their speed has increased significantly over time.

In 2014, Japanese firm Fanuc launched an industrial robot called CR-35iA/L that could travel at speeds of up to nine metres per second.

But Hitachi claims its latest model, known as HS16iD/85, is even quicker. It can reach top speeds of 10 metres per second when carrying light objects weighing less than one kilogramme (two pounds), according to the BBC's Tokyo correspondent Rupert Wingfield-Hayes.

However, he adds that the robot slows down considerably if it needs to carry heavier items. For example, it takes just under two seconds to accelerate from zero to five metres per hour while holding something weighing 35kg.

Mr Kawamura told Reuters that the robot would cost between $90,000-$100,000 (£65,000-£72,000). He expects sales to start next year.

It allows soldiers to practice against moving targets from close range, in a safe, virtual battlefield.

Mita Taupopoki (– 14 January 1935) was a prominent Māori tribal leader from New Zealand. He belonged to the Ngāti Wāhiao hapū, a subtribe of the Tūhourangi iwi of Te Arawa. Born near Lake Rotorua, New Zealand, he was likely born around 1845 or 1846. His father, Hēmana Te Whareiro of Ngāti Wāhiao, resided mainly at Whakarewarewa. His mother, Kanea II, was of Tūhourangi descent, and her family included the Ngāti Tūnohopū hapū of Ngāti Whakaue. In 1864, Mita joined other Te Arawa individuals in participating in the wars of the 1860s. He returned to Whakarewarewa in 1874. In 1883, he represented various Ngāti Wāhiao hapū in the Native Land Court, addressing land disputes involving Ngāti Whakaue, including Whakarewarewa, and successfully secured claims to land on the eastern side of the Puarenga Stream at Whakarewarewa, despite other lands being won by Ngāti Whakaue. His achievements in the land court earned him recognition both within the broader Tūhourangi community and within Ngāti Wāhiao. In 1886, the eruption of Mount Tarawera resulted in the deaths of many Tūhourangi, and survivors sought refuge with Mita and his people at Whakarewarewa and Ōhinemutu. Mita continued to represent Tūhourangi in the Native Land Court until 1887, when he gained acknowledgment of their claims over the 211,000-acre Rotomahana–Parekārangi block. In 1910, he traveled to Australia, England, and the United States with Maggie Papakura's cultural group. He passed away in a hospital in Rotorua on 14 January 1935.

Computer giant Microsoft has launched a pilot scheme to replace counterfeit versions of Windows XP with legal ones.
The first-time initiative is restricted to the UK and to users with pre-installed copies of the operating system in PCs bought before November. Until December Microsoft said software can be sent to it for analysis if there are doubts about its legitimacy. The company aims to detect illegal traders and turn users of fake versions of Windows into legitimate ones.
The Windows XP Counterfeit Project will mean that software that is found to be counterfeit will be replaced for free, subject to certain conditions, until the end of the year. It is the first time Microsoft has launched a counterfeit product replacement scheme in the world, the company told the BBC News website. In June, the software giant said that the major security update to Windows XP, Service Pack 2, would not work with the most widely pirated versions of its operating system. The upgrade closed security loopholes in XP and added features that made it easier to keep machines safe from viruses and other types of malicious computer code.
The US company invited anyone who had suspicions about their version of Windows XP to submit it for testing as soon as possible. The procedure consists of a series of computer checks, collating documents, and filling out a witness statement. "This is a great opportunity for users to confirm the authenticity of Windows XP software whilst helping gather vital information about illegal traders", said Alex Hilton, licence compliance manager at Microsoft. The scheme has also been welcomed by the technology and commerce industry. "It is important that users ensure that they are legally licensed to avoid the risks of purchasing and using counterfeit products", said David Frost, director general of the British Chambers of Commerce. The plan would enable Microsoft to gather intelligence about illegal traders in a prompt way, which would allow it to take action against software pirates. Microsoft said it would evaluate the results of the UK programme before setting up similar schemes in other countries.

Supervised semantic segmentation typically assumes that the test data belongs to the same data domain as the training data. However, in practical applications, a domain mismatch between the training data and the unseen data can result in a notable performance decline. Accurately labeling pixels in images across different domains is often time-consuming and effort-intensive, particularly for histopathology images. In this paper, we introduce a dual adaptive pyramid network (DAPNET) designed for histopathological gland segmentation, enabling adaptation between different staining domains. We address the domain adaptation challenge at two levels: first, at the image level, considering variations in image color and style; second, at the feature level, tackling spatial inconsistencies between domains. These components are implemented as domain classifiers with adversarial training. Our method is evaluated on two gland segmentation datasets stained with H&E and DAB-H. Extensive experiments and an ablation study confirm the effectiveness of our approach in the context of domain-adaptive segmentation. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Deep convolutional neural networks have demonstrated exceptional effectiveness in medical image segmentation. A common challenge in training supervised deep learning models is the scarcity of labeled data, which is both time-intensive and costly to acquire. This paper introduces a novel uncertainty-guided semi-supervised learning framework based on a student-teacher architecture, aimed at enhancing the training of segmentation networks using a limited number of labeled samples alongside a vast dataset of unlabeled images. Initially, a teacher segmentation model is trained on labeled data using Bayesian deep learning techniques. The resulting model generates soft segmentation labels and uncertainty maps for the unlabeled dataset. Subsequently, the student model is refined by incorporating these softly segmented samples and leveraging the pixel-wise confidence of segmentation quality derived from the uncertainty estimates provided by the teacher model through a newly developed loss function. Experimental evaluations on a retinal layer segmentation task indicate that the proposed method outperforms the fully supervised approach and achieves results comparable to those of an expert annotator. The introduced semi-supervised segmentation framework represents a significant advancement and is applicable for biomedical image segmentation across diverse imaging modalities, particularly in scenarios where annotated medical images are scarce.

Dividing and categorizing similar elements is crucial for image segmentation and clustering tasks. In these scenarios, a common aim is to cluster similar items or pixels in image processing. Additionally, groups should be distinct from other clusters and potentially sizable. These objectives are frequently integrated into a ratio optimization framework. Examples include the normalized cut problem and the ratio regions problem. Here, we present the first polynomial-time algorithms that solve these problems optimally. These methods are both efficient and combinatorial, contrasting with heuristic strategies employed in image segmentation research, which transform the problems into nonlinear optimization models and solve them using spectral techniques. Such approaches often fail to yield optimal solutions and are computationally intensive. The algorithms utilize a minimum $s,t$-cut method on a related graph, resulting in the optimal solution for the respective ratio problem along with sequences of nested solutions based on varying weights of the numerator and denominator objectives. Part II presents an extension of these findings to bi-criteria and multi-criteria objective functions.

Deep learning has shown remarkable success as a robust classification method and has also advanced in semantic segmentation. Consequently, many researchers think that deep learning is currently the most effective technique for pixel-level image segmentation. Can deep learning attain the same level of pixel-level accuracy as conventional image segmentation approaches by transforming object features into a nonlinear function? This paper provides a concise overview of the performance of deep learning in image classification and segmentation. While deep learning achieves high accuracy in classifying limited categories in global vision competitions, its segmentation accuracy in these competitions is approximately 80%. In contrast, image segmentation accuracy in biomedical challenges reaches nearly 95%. The significant disparity in results raises questions: why such a large gap exists? Are the reported accuracies verifiable or exaggerated due to the fact that competitor methods are assessed based solely on submitted results rather than on replicating them through code submission? To address this, we will analyze the underlying mechanisms of deep learning. Ultimately, we compare the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning models with a threshold selection method using quantitative analysis. Experimental findings indicate that the threshold selection approach can achieve substantially higher accuracy than deep learning methods in image segmentation.

So how do you change the world in today’s world, with its fragmented media landscape, with democratizing technologies, with dramatic changes in how we interact with each other, and with a culture evolving at neck-breaking speeds? In a large mixing bowl combine the butter and sugars until light and fluffy. Add the molasses, egg and vanilla. Gently mix until incorporated. To My Dear Sister Mrs. C. P. On Her Nuptial

Why do you, my dear Sister, now disclose
A bosom where all softly bowed before?
Why doth your cheek with gladness overflow,
And raise a glance too gay for woe?

'Tis Nature, stern mistress of our fate,
Commands the heart to love, and stamps it true:
With thrills of sweet emotion you are moved,
And must obey her mighty law.

In vain you offer to my searching eye
Your placid brow and cheek of roseate hue;
In vain you seek to still my anxious fear,
And whisper of a joy too great to bear.

I see you tremble; I behold your heart
 tumultuously beating as you start;
And through a sea of troubled emotions wide
I see love dawning in your timid eye.

You are about to be united in ties
Of holy wedlock, close and indissoluble;
And with a breast brimming with anguish deep
I see you leaving sisterly love's sunny steep.

Oh, do not fancy that I question thy choice,
Or that I doubt the worth of the one thou didst choose;
I but behold in thee a woman thro' and thro',
And own thee trembling, trembling at love's pow'r.

In the calm strength of that eternal love
I see thee standing, none may overthrow;
Nor evil tongue his subtle venom spray
On thee, dear sister, as thou wilt pass away.

I kiss thee as thou layest trembling there,
And bless thy choice, as I bid thee farewell;
And when in after time thou resemblest me
Call up a smile, thinking of thy sister.

According to elastic collisions, the linear momentum of a fast neutron can be determined using at most two consecutive recoil ion tracks along with the position of the third collision, referred to as "two and half" tracks. If the time interval between the first two tracks is also measured, the total number of tracks can be reduced to "one and a half." The angular and magnitude resolutions are constrained by ion range straggling, which limits them to approximately 10%. Multi-wire proportional chambers and light-field imaging are considered for fast neutron tracking. In both methods, single-charge or single-photon detection sensitivity is necessary. Light-field imaging avoids charge diffusion-induced image blur, yet the scarcity of available photons may pose a challenge. $^1$H, $^2$H, and $^3$He could serve as candidates for the initial design of fast neutron trackers employing light-field imaging.

Belief systems can be seen as poems. They shape our waking hours and dreams, our feelings, instincts, breathing, and natural gestures into a singular form of thought: poetry. Truth isn't revealed until it is expressed through words, and what is true is only partially captured within them. A poem, when contrasted with a structured religion, may resemble a single, brief moment of a soldier's life—dying and living—yet this is but a minor faith. True devotion is the expansive poem found in continuous recitation; much like any poem, it must remain infinite and whole, with twists that provoke questions such as "Why did the poet choose that?" You cannot pray a falsehood, Huckleberry Finn says; you also cannot compose one. It is the same mirror: fluid and shifting, we refer to it as poetry, yet fixed and central, we label it religion, and God is the poetry contained within any religion, not confined. Caught as in a mirror that draws itself, being present in the world as poetry is in the poem, a principle against its enclosure. There will always be religion nearby while there is poetry or its absence. Both exist and fluctuate, like the flight of these birds—crested pigeons and rosellas—whose wings are closed, then open, and once more closed.

Additive modifications of bialgebras, as defined by Wirth, refer to deformations of the multiplication operation within the bialgebra that satisfy specific conditions related to the coalgebra structure and continuity. Two key issues regarding these deformations are addressed: the development of a cohomology theory using a modified version of Hochschild cohomology, and the characterization of trivial deformations—those generated by coboundaries. In the initial segment of this paper, the primary finding involves identifying the trivial deformations, which are those arising from coboundaries. Starting from a Hopf algebra, it is anticipated that the deformed multiplications will exhibit an analogous property to the antipode, termed the deformed antipodes. We demonstrate that such deformed antipodes always exist, examine their characteristics, provide a method for calculating them based on the deformation and the original Hopf algebra's antipode, and in the cocommutative scenario, show that every deformation decomposes into a trivial component and a component featuring constant antipodes.

This paper proposes a novel approach to multi-target tracking in the presence of superpositional measurements using labeled random finite sets (RFS). The proposed method, called particle multi-target tracker (PMTT), combines the strengths of particle filtering and RFS to handle the challenges of multi-target tracking in the presence of measurement uncertainty and clutter.

The PMTT algorithm first represents the set of targets as an RFS, where each element of the set is associated with a label representing the target state. At each time step, the algorithm performs a prediction step, where the state of each target is propagated using a dynamics model, and a update step, where the measurement is processed using a likelihood function. The likelihood function is defined over the RFS, and it takes into account theLabel Random Finite Sets (RFS) to handle the superpositional measurements.

The authors evaluate the performance of the PMTT algorithm using a set of simulation experiments, and compare it with the traditional methods such as the Kalman filter and the particle filter. The results show that the PMTT algorithm outperforms the traditional methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, especially in the presence of high clutter levels and non-linear dynamics.

The main contribution of this paper is the introduction of a novel algorithm for multi-target tracking that can handle superpositional measurements using labeled RFS. The proposed algorithm combines the benefits of particle filtering and RFS, and provides a more robust and accurate solution to the problem of multi-target tracking in various applications such as radar, sonar, and computer vision.

The paper is organized as follows: The next section provides a brief overview of the related work in the field of multi-target tracking and the use of RFS. The section after that presents the mathematical formulation of the problem and the proposed algorithm. The results and discussion are presented in the following section, and the conclusion and future work are presented in the last section.

This paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of multi-target tracking and will be of interest to researchers and practitioners working in this area. The proposed algorithm has the potential to be applied in a variety of applications such as air traffic control

3/4 cup beer
1/2 cup Dijon mustard
7 tablespoons honey
1/3 cup olive oil
1 tablespoon dried rosemary
3 -4 tablespoons chopped fresh garlic
1 small onion, sliced
1/2 cup whipping cream, unwhippped
salt and pepper
2 -3 lbs boneless pork loin roast
In a small bowl whisk together beer, Dijon mustard, honey, olive oil, rosemary, fresh garlic and onions. Place the pork roast in a heavy-duty zip-lock plastic bag. Pour the marinade into the plastic bag and seal; turn a couple of times to coat well with marinade. Place the bag into a large bowl and refrigerate overnight (turning occasionally to coat roast). Set oven to 425 degrees. Place the roast onto a rack and place in a roasting pan; RESERVE MARINADE. Season roast with salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes at 425 degrees (to create a seared crust). Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees and continue to roast until a meat thermometer reads 150 degrees, about 1-1/2 hours (might take more or less time). Let stand 15 minutes, then remove to a slicing board (do not slice as yet). Strain the reserved beer/mustard marinade into a medium saucepan, and add in the whipping cream; simmer until it is reduced slightly (about 15-20 minutes). Season with salt and pepper. Slice the pork roast and arrange on a large platter. Drizzle some sauce over the slices, and pass the remaining sauce.

In an interview with the BBC, the former adviser disclosed that despite the ongoing debate over the country's exit from the EU, commonly known as Brexit, the longstanding fiscal rule remains a central tenet of UK economic policy.

The government has been under intense pressure to relax the rule in light of the ongoing economic uncertainty, with some arguing that it should be scrapped altogether. However, the former aide insisted that the principle remains a key foundation of the UK's economic strategy.

We generalize Ebert's Hat Problem for three persons and three colors. All
players guess simultaneously the color of their own hat observing only the hat
colors of the other players. It is also allowed for each player to pass: no
color is guessed. The team wins if at least one player guesses his or her hat
color correct and none of the players has an incorrect guess. This paper
studies Ebert's hat problem, where the probabilities of the colors may be
different (asymmetric case). Our goal is to maximize the probability of winning
the game and to describe winning strategies. In this paper we use the notion of
an adequate set. The construction of adequate sets is independent of underlying
probabilities and we can use this fact in the analysis of the asymmetric case.
Another point of interest is the fact that computational complexity using
adequate sets is much less than using standard methods.

The Korea Bank Group said on Thursday it plans to sell a majority stake in its credit card division to a group of Chinese investors. If successful, the sale to Jilin Cement Group and two affiliated companies will be the largest corporate acquisition in South Korea.

The new shareholders will maintain the Bank of Korea's 100% ownership and influence over the credit card business. The new partners will invest up to a total of 10 billion won ($8.8 million U.S.) in the business, which primarily serves Chinese clients.

The deal is part of Seoul and Beijing's efforts to boost investment in South Korean businesses and promote South Korea's image abroad. It comes about a week after China launched a diplomatic mission in Seoul as part of a plan to bolster cross-border trade and boost relations as Seoul heads into a round of high-profile bilateral and regional summits.

In a separate announcement, Seoul's government said it plans to sell an investment fund with $14.2 billion of assets managed by Saehan International Ltd. It said on Thursday that the fund, which was set up in the mid-1980s, will be set up to buy foreign assets and return them to South Korea if the terms of the deals are agreed with Chinese investors.

Separately on Thursday, Seoul said it would launch the world's largest free trade zone in Ulsan in August. The zone will have 1.8 million square kilometers, or about a fifth of South Korea, and will stretch along South Korea's eastern seaboard from the northern port in Busan to the southern port in Busan.

Actor Hugh Grant has been cast as the lead role in a new Broadway production of Harold Pinter's Betrayal, it was announced on Tuesday.

The 57-year-old will make his debut on the Great White Way opposite Rachel Weisz and Rafe Spall.

Grant said he had long wanted to work with director Mike Nichols - who directed him in Notting Hill (1999) - but that this would be their first time working together since then.

Betrayal tells the story of an adulterous love triangle between three friends over a period of six years.

It premiered at London's National Theatre in 1978 before transferring to New York where it won two Tony Awards for best play and best direction.

Pinter wrote the script after reading about the affair between novelist Graham Greene and actress Catherine Walston.

In a statement, Grant said: "I have always loved Harold Pinter's plays and I am thrilled to be doing one of my favourites."

He added: "Mike Nichols is a genius and I can't wait to start rehearsals."

Nichols said: "Hugh Grant is a wonderful actor and we are all looking forward to working with him again."

Weisz, who is married to Grant, previously appeared alongside her husband in the film adaptation of Woody Allen's Match Point (2005).

She also played the title character in the 2006 movie version of Pinter's The Deep Blue Sea.

"The Sound of Music is a story about love, hope and courage, and these are values that we need more than ever in today's world," he said.

"I am looking forward to bringing this classic musical to the city where it all began."

The Sound of Music will run at the Salzburg Festival from July 20 to August 30, 2018.

T-Mobile confirmed that the U.S. Secret Service is examining whether the hacker accessed photographs taken by T-Mobile subscribers using their smartphones. In the high dimensional regression analysis when the number of predictors is
much larger than the sample size, an important question is to select the
important variable which are relevant to the response variable of interest.
Variable selection and the multiple testing are both tools to address this
issue. However, there is little discussion on the connection of these two
areas. When the signal strength is strong enough such that the selection
consistency is achievable, it seems to be unnecessary to control the false
discovery rate. In this paper, we consider the regime where the signals are
both rare and weak such that the selection consistency is not achievable and
propose a method which controls the false discovery rate asymptotically. It is
theoretically shown that the false non-discovery rate of the proposed method
converges to zero at the optimal rate. Numerical results are provided to
demonstrate the advantage of the proposed method.

Image segmentation is a fundamental problem in medical image analysis. In
recent years, deep neural networks achieve impressive performances on many
medical image segmentation tasks by supervised learning on large manually
annotated data. However, expert annotations on big medical datasets are
tedious, expensive or sometimes unavailable. Weakly supervised learning could
reduce the effort for annotation but still required certain amounts of
expertise. Recently, deep learning shows a potential to produce more accurate
predictions than the original erroneous labels. Inspired by this, we introduce
a very weakly supervised learning method, for cystic lesion detection and
segmentation in lung CT images, without any manual annotation. Our method works
in a self-learning manner, where segmentation generated in previous steps
(first by unsupervised segmentation then by neural networks) is used as ground
truth for the next level of network learning. Experiments on a cystic lung
lesion dataset show that the deep learning could perform better than the
initial unsupervised annotation, and progressively improve itself after
self-learning.

Legal actions targeting websites that facilitate the exchange of pirated films have prompted the creation of a system potentially more difficult to dismantle. One such website, responsible for the success of the BitTorrent file-sharing model, is developing its own software to avoid the issues of previous programs. A beta version of the new Exeem software will be released in late January. However, concerns persist regarding the effectiveness of this new network in ensuring that transferred files are genuine copies. 

In December, major film studios initiated a legal effort against websites utilizing BitTorrent to distribute pirated movies. This campaign succeeded due to how BitTorrent is structured, relying on "trackers" that direct users to individuals willing to share specific files. Closing down sites that hosted these trackers significantly disrupted the BitTorrent network. One such site, suprnova.org, played a key role in boosting BitTorrent's popularity by verifying that trackers pointed to the correct content.

The individual behind suprnova.org, known as Sloncek, is now preparing to launch a new file-sharing platform called Exeem. In an interview with Novastream web radio, Sloncek explained that Exeem would integrate features from both BitTorrent and Kazaa. Similar to BitTorrent, Exeem will use trackers to guide users to the desired files. Unlike Kazaa, these trackers will be managed by all participants rather than a central authority. This decentralized approach, according to Sloncek, should reduce vulnerability to legal measures aimed at curbing piracy.

Exeem has been developed for several months and is currently undergoing testing with a small group of users. An initial public version is expected before February. Currently, only a Windows version of the software is in development, with no plans for a Linux version.

Image-to-image translation is a long-established and a difficult problem in
computer vision. In this paper we propose an adversarial based model for
image-to-image translation. The regular deep neural-network based methods
perform the task of image-to-image translation by comparing gram matrices and
using image segmentation which requires human intervention. Our generative
adversarial network based model works on a conditional probability approach.
This approach makes the image translation independent of any local, global and
content or style features. In our approach we use a bidirectional
reconstruction model appended with the affine transform factor that helps in
conserving the content and photorealism as compared to other models. The
advantage of using such an approach is that the image-to-image translation is
semi-supervised, independant of image segmentation and inherits the properties
of generative adversarial networks tending to produce realistic. This method
has proven to produce better results than Multimodal Unsupervised
Image-to-image translation.

Flexible grid optical networks allow a better exploitation of fiber capacity,
by enabling a denser frequency allocation. A tighter channel spacing, however,
requires narrower filters, which increase linear intersymbol interference
(ISI), and may dramatically reduce system reach. Commercial coherent receivers
are based on symbol by symbol detectors, which are quite sensitive to ISI. In
this context, Nyquist spacing is considered as the ultimate limit to
wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) packing.
  In this paper, we show that by introducing a limited-complexity trellis
processing at the receiver, either the reach of Nyquist WDM flexi-grid networks
can be significantly extended, or a denser-than-Nyquist channel packing (i.e.,
a higher spectral efficiency (SE)) is possible at equal reach. By adopting
well-known information-theoretic techniques, we design a limited-complexity
trellis processing and quantify its SE gain in flexi-grid architectures where
wavelength selective switches over a frequency grid of 12.5GHz are employed.

Germany's unemployment rate exceeded the threshold of five million last month. On Wednesday, the German Federal Labour Agency reported that the number of jobless individuals reached 5.037 million in January, bringing the unemployment rate up to 12.1%. A government minister stated that the figure is indeed over five million, according to ZDF public television. This level of unemployment has not been seen in Germany since the 1930s. 

The increase in the unemployment numbers can be attributed to changes in how the data is collected. However, these figures are concerning for the government. An economist noted that the figures represent the worst situation seen in the post-war era and could negatively impact the recent popularity gains of the Social Democratic Party (SPD) and potentially affect their electoral prospects in Schleswig-Holstein and North Rhine-Westphalia.

accuracy. Finally, we compare our results with winning solutions of SpaceNet 2
competition for real satellite multispectral images of Vegas, Paris, Shanghai

US car firms General Motors (GM) and Ford have been forced to cut production in the face of falling car sales.
US sales at GM sank 12.7% in February compared to a year ago while Ford sales dropped 3% as foreign rivals took a bigger share of the market. Meanwhile, Asian carmakers fared well - Toyota sales jumped 11% while rival Nissan notched up a 10% increase. Overall. sales across the industry also fell to 1.25 million vehicles from 1.27 million a year earlier.
GM and Ford blamed high fuel prices for low sales of big trucks and gas-guzzling sports utility vehicles (SUVs) - the vehicles that provide the biggest profits.
GM added that US truck sales fell 9% in February while car business tumbled 17%, however it did acknowledge that some new products - such as the Pontiac G6 and Chevrolet Cobalt - had put in solid performances. "The calendar year is starting off slower than expected, both for GM and the industry," said Mark LaNeve, GM's vice president for North American sales, service and marketing. The slump in sales prompted the group to cut production in North America by 3% - it has already reduced output by around 9% in the face of growing stockpiles. Meanwhile, Ford which posted its ninth consecutive drop in monthly US sales, said it was cutting first-quarter North American production by another 10,000 vehicles, or 1.2%. Chrysler, the US unit of Germany's DaimlerChrysler, was the only Detroit based automaker to boast an increase in market share during the month - with sales rising 8%.
But America's loss was its foreign rivals' gain as they continued to nibble away at the US market. While Japan's top car maker Toyota and Nissan saw sales accelerate, even the smaller Suzuki Motor Corp snapped up a more business with sales improving 17.6% on a year ago. In 2003, the firm launched an ambitious plan to triple US sales by 2007 as it seeks to become a bigger player in the Asian assault on the US market. Korea's Hyundai was another big gainer, turning in a 19% surge in February sales. Toyota put its rise in sales down to strong results for its redesigned Avalon sedan and a 120% surge in sales of its gas-electric Prius hybrid mid-size sedan as petrol-price conscious consumers looked to vehicles that were cheaper to run. "As gas prices continue their upward march, fuel efficiency catches the public eye," Jim Press, vice president and chief operating officer of Toyota's US sales arm, said in a statement.

Mark Ellingson (1905 – 1993) was the 5th president of the Rochester Institute of Technology, succeeding John A. Randall, from 1936 – 1969. He rose from a teacher at the institute to the presidency, which he held for longer than anyone before or since, and in many ways he brought the institute into its modern form. During Dr. Ellingson's lengthy tenure in office from 1936 to 1969, enrollment in day and evening classes rose from 2,250 to 16,000. He also oversaw a major expansion of the RIT endowment; a 1937 merger with the Empire School of Printing; the 1944 renaming to "Rochester Institute of Technology" (formerly, Rochester Athenaeum and Mechanics Institute); the planning, construction, and 1968 transfer to the current campus in Henrietta.  He also spearheaded the drive to have RIT selected as the location for the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, which admitted its first students in 1968. The tallest building on the Henrietta campus, a residence hall nicknamed "Tower A", is named for Ellingson.

The concept of transforming a matrix into its dual or conjugate form is a fundamental tool in linear algebra and has numerous applications in various fields such as physics, engineering, computer science, and statistics. However, the traditional methods for performing these transformations are often tedious and prone to errors. In this paper, we present two new methods, called the Perfect NOT Transformation (PNT) and the Conjugate Transformation (CT), which significantly simplify the process of computing the dual and conjugate forms of matrices.

The PNT is based on the idea of subtracting the identity matrix from a given matrix, followed by an elementary row operation. This simple method can be applied to any square matrix, regardless of its size, and produces a compact representation of the matrix that is easy to work with. We demonstrate how the PNT can be used to efficiently compute the inverse, transpose, and determinant of a matrix, making it an essential tool for linear algebra computations.

The CT is based on the concept of similarity transformation, which states that two matrices are similar if they have the same eigenvalues. By applying a series of similarity transformations to a given matrix, we can easily obtain its conjugate form. We show how the CT can be used to quickly compute the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of a matrix,which has important implications for many applications in physics, engineering,and data analysis.

Our experimental results demonstrate that both the PNT and CT outperform existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. We also compare the performance of our methods with state-of-the art software libraries such as MATLAB and NumPy, showing that they offer significant improvements over current practices. Finally,we discuss potential applications and future directions for research involving these techniques .

Caracas, Venezuela - The Venezuelan government has identified thousands of idle farmlands across the country that could potentially be used to increase food production and alleviate the ongoing food crisis in the nation.

According to Agriculture Minister Luis Carlos Diaz, these unused lands have the potential to produce crops such as rice, corn, beans, and potatoes which are currently in short supply due to the economic crisis facing the South American nation.

The minister stated that this initiative is part of President Nicolas Maduro's plan to boost agricultural output and reduce dependence on imports. He added that the government will provide technical assistance, seeds, fertilizers, and machinery to farmers who wish to cultivate these plots.

However, some experts have expressed skepticism over whether this plan can truly address the root causes of Venezuela's food shortage problem, which includes an economy in shambles, hyperinflation, and widespread corruption.

Despite these concerns, the government remains optimistic about the potential impact of this program and hopes that it will help improve the lives of millions of Venezuelans struggling with hunger and malnutrition.

In this paper, we explore the potential contributions of non-contact atomic force microscopy (ncAFM) to the measurement of the Casimir force, a fundamental interaction between objects that arises from quantum fluctuations in vacuum. The Casimir force has important implications for various fields such as nanotechnology and materials science, yet its precise measurement remains challenging due to the fragile nature of the interaction. Conventional methods rely on indirect techniques, which can be limited by thermal noise or sample damage. Non-contact AFM offers an attractive alternative for directly measuring the Casimir force with high sensitivity and spatial resolution. Our study demonstrates the capabilities of ncAFM in probing the Casimir force between various surfaces, including dielectric and metallic samples. We discuss the theoretical framework for interpreting the experimental data and highlight the advantages of ncAFM over conventional techniques. Our results open up new opportunities for investigating the Casimir effect at the nanoscale and pave the way for novel applications in surface engineering and material design.
