Mountview House is a heritage-listed detached house at 37 Leichhardt Street, Spring Hill, City of Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. It was originally built in the 1860s with a new wing added in 1882 designed by Andrea Stombuco. It was added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 13 May 2004. History 
The earliest section of Mountview House, a two-storeyed stone residence, is believed to have been erected in the 1860s for Brisbane foreman carpenter Daniel McNaught. A two-storeyed brick wing designed by architect Andrea Stombuco was added in 1882, when the house was converted into a preparatory school for boys. This part of Spring Hill was surveyed officially into suburban allotments in 1856, but was soon subdivided for closer residential settlement by speculative landowners. Along with Kangaroo Point and Petrie Terrace, Spring Hill was among the earliest of Brisbane's dormitory suburbs, attracting wealthier residents to the high land along the ridges, and the less affluent to the hollows in between: Hanly's Hollow (between Wickham Terrace and Leichhardt Street), Spring Hollow (between Leichhardt Street and Gregory Terrace), and York's Hollow (to the north of Gregory Terrace - an area occupied by a number of brick-makers in the 1850s and 1860s, now Victoria Park).

A 3D surface, defined by an elevation function on a 2D grid, combined with non-spatial features at each pixel, presents a challenge where the goal is to categorize pixels into connected groups based on both non-spatial attributes and surface characteristics. This task holds significant applications in hydrology, planetary science, and biochemistry, yet it faces unique difficulties. One key issue is that the boundaries of class segments align with surface contours in the topological space, irrespective of their actual shapes and orientations. Additionally, the topological structure varies across different spatial scales due to differing surface resolutions. Current deep learning approaches for image segmentation, which rely heavily on convolution and pooling operations, often fail to address this. To overcome this, we introduce a contour tree skeleton, a polytree that captures how surface contours evolve at various elevation levels. We then develop a graph neural network based on the contour tree's hierarchical structure to model topological relationships at varying spatial scales. Experiments using real-world hydrological data demonstrate that our method achieves higher classification accuracy compared to existing baselines.

Each character brings unique perspectives and stories to the table - from pursuing spiritual enlightenment, seeking fulfillment in life, grappling with loneliness, to dealing with personal demons.

Over the course of several meals together, Sarah learns valuable lessons about compassion, perspective, mindfulness, and living a purposeful life. She also finds herself confronted by past regrets and realizes the power of forgiving oneself. Ultimately, through these encounters with strangers turned friends, Sarah begins to see her own journey in a new light, and gains clarity on what matters most.

As the characters part ways, they reconnect on a deeper level and continue to inspire each other. The Ambedkar cartoon is an issue that rocked the Parliament of India on 11 May 2012. Both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha were adjourned on that day due to the ruckus created by the opposing parties. The issue was taken up by Thirumavalavan, an MP from the state of Tamil Nadu. He put the issue to parliament (Lok Sabha), but was at first denied permission to speak about it. He then showed a copy of the controversial cartoon that allegedly insulted the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.  In the cartoon, the former Prime Minister of India (Congress), Jawaharlal Nehru, holds a whip and along with Ambedkar is driving a snail, which represents the Indian Constitution. The Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes considered the cartoon to be insulting. The book it appeared in was published by NCERT under the guidance of the Ministry of Human Resources in 2006 under the UPA government headed by Sonia Gandhi (Indian National Congress). Later the HRD Minister Kapil Sibal apologised to the nation with regards to the cartoon. NCERT was also asked to remove the cartoon from their textbooks.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art
performance in many different 2D medical image analysis tasks. In clinical
practice, however, a large part of the medical imaging data available is in 3D.
This has motivated the development of 3D CNNs for volumetric image segmentation
in order to benefit from more spatial context. Due to GPU memory restrictions
caused by moving to fully 3D, state-of-the-art methods depend on
subvolume/patch processing and the size of the input patch is usually small,
limiting the incorporation of larger context information for a better
performance. In this paper, we propose a novel Holistic Decomposition
Convolution (HDC), for an effective and efficient semantic segmentation of
volumetric images. HDC consists of a periodic down-shuffling operation followed
by a conventional 3D convolution. HDC has the advantage of significantly
reducing the size of the data for sub-sequential processing while using all the
information available in the input irrespective of the down-shuffling factors.
Results obtained from comprehensive experiments conducted on hip T1 MR images
and intervertebral disc T2 MR images demonstrate the efficacy of the present
approach.

Throughout the novel, Tempest remains oblivious to the fact that Lucio is actually the embodiment of the Devil. As his wealth grows, so does his suffering. Ultimately, when confronted with the truth about his companion, he rejects evil and leaves society with no money but a renewed sense of spiritual purity. While the storyline centers on Tempest's downfall and redemption, he is essentially a minor figure compared to Lucio. Both the title and much of the novel's philosophical themes revolve around the intense desire of Satan to attain salvation. The book significantly contributes to the Faustian genre by introducing the idea that, apart from all others, Satan genuinely believes in the Gospel, yet is prohibited from receiving it.

Keannekeuk (c. 1790–1852), referred to as the "Kickapoo Prophet," was a medicine man and spiritual leader of the Vermilion band of the Kickapoo nation. He resided in East Central Illinois near the Vermilion River throughout his life. One account suggests his name means "the son of the drunkard." At a young age, he killed his uncle in a fit of intoxication and was exiled from his tribe. He traveled between frontier towns in Indiana and Illinois, seeking sustenance, until a Catholic priest took him in to teach him Christianity. Keannekeuk chose to abandon alcohol and started preaching to encourage others to do the same. His people welcomed him back, and by 1816, at around twenty-five years old, he had become a prominent leader of the Vermilion band. Soon after, alcohol consumption among his followers decreased significantly, and his community became more united and efficient. From 1833 until his death in 1852, he guided a group of followers who believed in nonviolence, peaceful resistance to relocation, abstaining from alcohol, and meditating. He advocated for moderate, nonviolent engagement with American expansion and a stable agricultural lifestyle. These ideas caused him and his followers to face ridicule and isolation from other Kickapoo groups. His community’s religious stance reflected some aspects of Christian evangelism and attracted several Potawatomi converts over time. He passed away on the reservation in Kansas in 1852.

1/3 cup dried minced onions  
1/3 cup water  
1 package (1/4 ounce) active dry yeast  
2 tablespoons warm water (110° to 115°)  
1 cup warm 2% milk (110° to 115°)  
1/4 cup toasted wheat germ  
1 tablespoon canola oil  
1 tablespoon honey  
1 teaspoon garlic powder  
3/4 teaspoon salt  
3 to 3-1/4 cups all-purpose flour  
2 tablespoons melted butter  
1 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese  
Freshly chopped parsley, optional  

In a small bowl, mix onions and water. Let sit 10 minutes or until softened. In another small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water. In a large bowl, combine milk, wheat germ, oil, honey, garlic powder, salt, onion mixture, yeast mixture, and 1-1/2 cups of flour; mix on medium speed until smooth. Add enough remaining flour to create a stiff dough (the dough will be sticky). Transfer the dough to a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, approximately 6-8 minutes. Place the dough in a greased bowl, turn it once to coat the top, and cover with plastic wrap. Allow it to rise in a warm place until double in size, about 1 hour. Press the dough down, then transfer it to a lightly floured surface. Divide into 20 balls and shape them. Place the balls in a greased container, cover with a kitchen towel, and let rise until nearly doubled, about 45 minutes. Preheat the oven to 375°F. Bake for 15-18 minutes or until slightly golden. Brush the rolls with butter and sprinkle with cheese. Continue baking for 5-7 minutes longer until the cheese is melted and the rolls are golden. If desired, garnish with parsley. Serve warm.

Characterising tractable fragments of the constraint satisfaction problem
(CSP) is an important challenge in theoretical computer science and artificial
intelligence. Forbidding patterns (generic sub-instances) provides a means of
defining CSP fragments which are neither exclusively language-based nor
exclusively structure-based. It is known that the class of binary CSP instances
in which the broken-triangle pattern (BTP) does not occur, a class which
includes all tree-structured instances, are decided by arc consistency (AC), a
ubiquitous reduction operation in constraint solvers. We provide a
characterisation of simple partially-ordered forbidden patterns which have this
AC-solvability property. It turns out that BTP is just one of five such
AC-solvable patterns. The four other patterns allow us to exhibit new tractable
classes.

Two threads in the knot—  
By the Great Grey Water.  
Two hands to touch, two hearts to touch;

Fair passage to the other

His sins, like ours, still on him,  
God rest his soul! Five oceans roll  
Their long weight all upon him.  
O God! thy Great Grey Water!  
But I am still, and you are still,  
And here our chance has flung us;  
True comrades we, but…there were three

Soft lights and beakers beaded,  
Then out again and on again,  
Unminded and unheeded,  
Across the Great Grey Water.

Detecting tumors in biomedical images is an extensive task for healthcare professionals and often involves inaccuracies. Consequently, researchers have introduced algorithmic approaches employing diverse mathematical methodologies, including statistical analysis, variational techniques, and machine learning. This study introduces a semi-automated approach for segmenting 2D CT scans of the liver into three categories: healthy, vascular, and tumor tissues, utilizing graph cuts. A new feature vector is constructed by incorporating 59 intensity values from time series data and introducing a streamlined perimeter cost component within the energy function. Data and perimeter terms are normalized to accelerate the graph-cut process without requiring optimization of the scaling factor $\lambda$. Instead of a training phase, predefined tissue means are calculated from regions identified by experienced radiologists. The proposed technique is computationally straightforward and demonstrated on a clinical dataset comprising 10 tumors, achieving a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.77 and a mean volume overlap error (VOE) of 36.7%. The average time required per slice was 1.25 minutes.

New rules on marriage for foreign nationals living in the UK are coming into force.
From Tuesday, most non-EU citizens will need Home Office approval to marry. The Home Office says the new rules are aimed at reducing the number of sham marriages, of which there are estimated to be up to 15,000 a year. But immigrants' group the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants (JCWI) says the rules breach human rights law and it may mount a legal challenge. When the changes were unveiled last year, immigration minister Des Browne said: "Our aim is to avoid unnecessary disruption of genuine marriages, while providing firm controls to prevent abuse." Under the previous regulations anybody wishing to get married in the UK only had to produce evidence they had been resident in the country for a week and give 15 days notice of the wedding at the local register office.
But from Tuesday all non-EU nationals, apart from citizens of Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Iceland or Norway, intending to wed in the UK must either obtain a visa allowing them to get married before they enter the country or apply for a Home Office 'certificate of marriage approval'. To get a certificate, costing £135, applicants will have to send proof that they have a legal right to be in the UK. Those without a settled status, such as asylum seekers awaiting a decision on their application, will have no right to marry in the UK.
Once they have the necessary documentation, those subject to immigration controls wishing to get married in England or Wales must register their intention to marry at one of 76 specially-designated register offices. They can, however, marry at the register office or church of their choice. Rhian Beynon of the JCWI said the new rules were "not proportionate" and "discriminatory".
"These rules means in some cases the Home Secretary is going to be a marriage registrar of last resort. "We're currently taking a legal opinion on this. We'll be looking for people whose right to marry is breached and we'll be looking at taking a case on this to the Human Rights Court," Ms Beynon said. The new rules have also been called into question by the parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights. In a report published last July the cross-party committee stated there was a "significant risk" the new procedures were incompatible with the right to marry because they introduced restrictions which were "disproportionate". The committee believed the new laws might be incompatible with the Human Rights Act on the grounds of religion, belief and nationality, the report added.
Over the last year immigration service operations against marriages of convenience have been stepped up resulting in a growing number of convictions. In January 25 people who took part in a sham marriage network based in Leicester were jailed for a total of 35 years. And last November Samuel Amoah, a Belgian national who set up two sham weddings for couples who wanted to remain in the UK, was jailed for three years. Several other cases are currently going through the courts. The role of registrars who under the Asylum and Immigration Act 1999 were obliged to report suspected sham marriages to the Home Office, has been key in many prosecutions. Registrars' spokesman, Mark Rimmer, said they welcomed the new marriage regulations and believed they would be an significant deterrent. "They will effectively remove most of the blatant cases. Certainly those who are illegals in this country, of which we had quite a few, will no longer be getting married," Mr Rimmer said. Mr Rimmer, the service director for registrations of marriages at Brent Council in north-west London, said he did not consider the new law to be an infringement of civil liberties. "It may be seen to be far more draconian than it has been but certainly it's still not as difficult to marry in the UK than it is to marry, for example, in Holland, Germany or France. "I think it's a proportionate response by government to what was a very large problem," Mr Rimmer said.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Cover a rolled-out chicken thigh with some cling film and flatten it slightly by pressing until the width of the chicken matches the length of the sausage. Place a rasher or slice of bacon or pancetta on a copping board—use the back of a knife to widen streaky bacon if needed. Place the roulades on a tray or oven-safe dish and bake for 20–30 minutes until golden and juices run clear. Remove and let rest for 5–10 minutes. Cut each roulade into 1 cm slices and serve.

Ingredients:

* 1 package of puff pastry, thawed
* 2-3 apples, peeled and sliced
* 1/4 cup brown sugar
* 2 tbsp granulated sugar
* 1 tsp cinnamon
* 1/4 cup raisins
* 1/4 cup chopped walnuts (optional)
* 1 egg, beaten (for brushing pastry)
* Powdered sugar, for dusting

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix together the brown sugar, granulated sugar, and cinnamon.
3. Add the sliced apples to the bowl and toss until they are evenly coated with the sugar mixture.
4. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
5. Spoon the apple mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
6. Sprinkle the raisins and chopped walnuts (if using) over the top of the apple mixture.
7. Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling, pressing the edges to seal. Use a fork to crimp the edges and create a decorative pattern.
8. Brush the top of the strudel with the beaten egg and cut a few small slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
9. Place the strudel on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown.
10. Dust with powdered sugar before serving warm. Enjoy!

Note: You can also add a drizzle of honey or maple syrup over the top of the strudel before baking for an extra touch of sweetness.

This paper presents an expanded version of the Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) graphical interface. It is a sketch-based interface developed for the Android platform, designed to simplify and make the LTL control interface more accessible to non-expert users. By defining specific areas of interest, the interface enables quick creation of plans that meet advanced LTL objectives. Users can further personalize these plans by drawing reference trajectories. Once the custom paths are established, the interface generates a plan that harmonizes both the customized paths and the LTL specifications. Experimental results are also provided using the implemented interface.

The soaring cost of oil has hit global economic growth, although world's major economies should weather the storm of price rises, according to the OECD.
In its latest bi-annual report, the OECD cut its growth predictions for the world's main industrialised regions. US growth would reach 4.4% in 2004, but fall to 3.3% next year from a previous estimate of 3.7%, the OECD said. However, the Paris-based economics think tank said it believed the global economy could still regain momentum.
Forecasts for Japanese growth were also scaled back to 4.0% from 4.4% this year and 2.1% from 2.8% in 2005. But the outlook was worst for the 12-member eurozone bloc, with already sluggish growth forecasts slipping to 1.8% from 2.0% this year and 1.9% from 2.4% in 2005, the OECD said. Overall, the report forecast total growth of 3.6% in 2004 for the 30 member countries of the OECD, slipping to 2.9% next year before recovering to 3.1% in 2006. "There are nonetheless good reasons to believe that despite recent oil price turbulence the world economy will regain momentum in a not-too-distant future," said Jean-Philippe Cotis, the OECD's chief economist. The price of crude is about 50% higher than it was at the start of 2004, but down on the record high of $55.67 set in late October.
A dip in oil prices and improving jobs prospects would improve consumer confidence and spending, the OECD said. "The oil shock is not enormous by historical standards - we have seen worse in the seventies. If the oil price does not rise any further, then we think the shock can be absorbed within the next few quarters," Vincent Koen, a senior economist with the OECD, told the BBC's World Business Report. "The recovery that was underway, and has been interrupted a bit by the oil shock this year, would then regain momentum in the course of 2005." China's booming economy and a "spectacular comeback" in Japan - albeit one that has faltered in recent months - would help world economic recovery, the OECD said. "Supported by strong balance sheets and high profits, the recovery of business investment should continue in North America and start in earnest in Europe," it added. However, the report warned: "It remains to be seen whether continental Europe will play a strong supportive role through a marked upswing of final domestic demand." The OECD highlighted current depressed household expenditure in Germany and the eurozone's over-reliance on export-led growth.

Akiem Jamar Hicks, born on November 16, 1989, is an American football defensive end who plays for the Chicago Bears in the National Football League (NFL). Hicks attended Sacramento City College and the University of Regina before his college career. Unable to transfer to another football program, he worked at a DirecTV call center in Colorado Springs while exploring his future. Hicks received an offer to play for the Toronto Argonauts in the Canadian Football League but chose to pursue further education and continue his college football career with the Regina Rams of the Canada West Universities Athletic Association. After his first season at Regina, he was drafted by the Omaha Nighthawks of the United Football League, but opted to remain in college. In this paper, a new approach for sign language recognition system using image segmentation is presented. The proposed method utilizes a topological derivative based approach combined with an isotropic filter to segment the sign language images. The isotropic filter is used to enhance the image quality and remove noise, while the topological derivative is used to identify the boundaries of the sign language gestures. The segmentation results are then used as input for a sign language recognition system, which can accurately recognize and interpret different sign language gestures. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Health Secretary Alan Milburn has defended his decision to launch an advertising campaign featuring posters showing graphic images of smoking-related illnesses, saying it is necessary to shock people into quitting.
The controversial posters show rotting teeth, cancerous lungs and amputated limbs in an effort to discourage smokers from lighting up. Critics have argued that they are too gruesome but Mr Milburn insists that tough measures are needed to reduce Britain's high smoking rates.
"We know these images can be disturbing," he said, "but we also know that sometimes it takes something shocking to make people take notice."
According to government figures, around 80% of lung cancer cases and 90% of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) cases could be prevented if everyone quit smoking. The new ad campaign forms part of a £20 million initiative aimed at encouraging more people to give up cigarettes.
Mr Milburn acknowledged that some individuals may find the imagery offensive but stressed that ultimately the aim was to save lives. "I understand why some people might think this approach goes too far," he added, "But when you consider what smoking does to your health – and worse still, the impact on those closest to you - I believe there is no such thing as going too far when it comes to protecting people's wellbeing."

A prescription cannabis drug made by UK biotech firm GW Pharmaceuticals is set to be approved in Canada.
The drug is used to treat the central nervous system and alleviate the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS). A few weeks ago, shares in GW Pharma lost a third of their value after UK regulators said they wanted more evidence about the drug's benefits. But now Canadian authorities have said the Sativex drug will be considered for approval.
Approximately 50,000 people in Canada have been diagnosed with MS and 85,000 people are suffering from the condition in the UK. Many patients already smoke cannabis to relieve their symptoms.
Now, GW Pharma's Sativex mouth spray could be legally available to MS sufferers in Canada within the next few months. This will be the first time a cannabis-based drug has been approved anywhere in the world, representing a landmark for GW Pharma and for patients with MS. Final approval in Canada should now be little more than a formality, analysts said, and the company expects full approval for Sativex early in 2005. "We are delighted to receive this qualifying notice from Health Canada and look forward to receiving regulatory approval for Sativex in Canada in the early part of 2005," said GW Pharma executive chairman Dr Geoffrey Guy.
The UK government granted GW Pharma a licence to grow the cannabis plant for medical research purposes. Satifex consists of a cannabis extract containing tetrahydrocannabinol and cannabidiol, a cocktail that has also proved effective in treating patients with arthritis. Thousands of plants are grown at a secret location somewhere in the English countryside. Despite hopes of regulatory approval last year, a series of delays has put back Sativex's launch in the UK. The latest news sent shares in GW Pharma up 8.5p, or 8.1%, to 113.5p.

The Japanese government has forecast that the country's economic growth will slow to 1.6% in the next fiscal year starting in April 2005.
While it predicts this fall from the current 2.1% level, it said it was making progress on ending deflation. The figures were given by economics minister Heizo Takenaka who said the economy would grow by 2% in 2006/07. He said the consumer price index (CPI) would rise 0.1% in the next fiscal year, the first gain since 2000/01. "We are attempting to make real economic conditions better and to overcome deflation. To ease the problem the Bank of Japan has regularly flooded the money market with excess cash to keep short term interest rates at 0% in an attempt to spur economic activity.

The successful application of deep learning in biomedical image segmentation has highlighted domain shift as a crucial and difficult issue, as disparities between domains can significantly impair model effectiveness when applied to unseen data with varied characteristics. To tackle this challenge, we introduce a new unsupervised domain adaptation framework aimed at transferring models trained on the labeled source domain to the unlabeled target domain for cross-modal biomedical image segmentation. Our methodology comprises two core components: a conditional domain discriminator (CDD), which extends conditional domain adversarial networks to handle complex cross-modal biomedical images effectively and reliably, and a category-focused prototype aligner (CCPA), derived from graph-induced prototype alignment mechanisms used in cross-domain object detection. The CCPA enables the extraction of precise instance-level features through a detailed prototype representation and addresses class imbalance by employing an entropy-based loss function. Experimental results on a publicly available benchmark for cardiac substructure segmentation show that our approach notably enhances performance on the target domain.

Ralf had left for the Viking ship that Peer's father constructed. When Hilde's younger siblings are kidnapped during a blizzard, Peer and Hilde venture into the mountain's tunnels to rescue them. At the story's peak, during a troll feast where the troll king raises the mountain on four red pillars, Peer faces a choice between fleeing alone or remaining forever under the mountain with Hilde. Meanwhile, Ralf returns from his journey and, alongside his crew and neighbors, enters the troll banquet hall. A confrontation ensues. 2 10-inch flour tortillas  
2 teaspoons canola oil  
1/2 teaspoon salt, divided  
1/2 teaspoon sesame seeds  
5 1/2 lbs fresh tuna  
1/4 teaspoon black pepper  
1/4 teaspoon ground cumin  
1 cup shredded low-fat cheddar cheese  
1/2 cup plain nonfat yogurt  
2 teaspoons lime juice  
8 cups mixed salad greens  
1 (7 ounce) jar roasted bell peppers, drained and cut into strips  
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray. Brush the tortillas on both sides with the oil, then cut them into 1/4-by-3-inch strips. Toss the strips with 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and the sesame seeds. Place the strips on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping once, until crisp and slightly golden. Meanwhile, season the tuna with the remaining salt, pepper, and cumin. Grease a broiling pan or griddle, heat it, and cook the tuna on both sides for about 3 minutes per side, depending on desired doneness. Allow the tuna to rest for 2 to 3 minutes before slicing into 1/4-inch-thick pieces. Mix the cheese, yogurt, and lime juice in a bowl. Combine the tuna with the lettuce, roasted pepper strips, and the dressing. Divide the salad among four dinner plates and garnish with the toasted tortilla croutons (or the crispy tortilla chips if using alternative option).

He returned to Romania and founded a series of companies, including a pharmaceutical company, a construction company, and an investment company.

In 2012, Gruia was elected to the Romanian Senate as a member of the Democratic Liberal Party. He served as the party's leader from 2014 to 2015 and has been the president of the National Liberal Party since 2021.

Gruia has also been involved in charitable work, founding the Gruia Family Foundation in 2009. The foundation works to improve the education and health care of Romanian children.

Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 medium beets, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 4 cups arugula, washed and dried
- 1/2 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 1/4 cup chopped walnuts
- 1/4 cup thinly sliced red onion

For the blue cheese dressing:
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup crumbled blue cheese
- 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Toss the beets with olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
3. Spread the beets out on a baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
4. In a large bowl, combine the roasted beets, arugula, blue cheese, walnuts, and red onion.
5. To make the blue cheese dressing, whisk together mayonnaise, blue cheese, apple cider vinegar, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until smooth.
6. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to combine.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy your delicious and healthy Salad of Roasted Beets and Arugula with Blue Cheese Dressing!

Incorporating multi-scale features in fully convolutional neural networks
(FCNs) has been a key element to achieving state-of-the-art performance on
semantic image segmentation. One common way to extract multi-scale features is
to feed multiple resized input images to a shared deep network and then merge
the resulting features for pixelwise classification. In this work, we propose
an attention mechanism that learns to softly weight the multi-scale features at
each pixel location. We adapt a state-of-the-art semantic image segmentation
model, which we jointly train with multi-scale input images and the attention
model. The proposed attention model not only outperforms average- and
max-pooling, but allows us to diagnostically visualize the importance of
features at different positions and scales. Moreover, we show that adding extra
supervision to the output at each scale is essential to achieving excellent
performance when merging multi-scale features. We demonstrate the effectiveness
of our model with extensive experiments on three challenging datasets,
including PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012 and a subset of MS-COCO 2014.

The leader of the technology-focused Nasdaq stock index intends to offer shares to the public and list itself on the exchange it manages. According to a registration statement submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission, Nasdaq Stock Market aims to generate $100 million (approximately £52 million) by selling these shares. Some analysts believe this represents another phase toward a complete public offering. However, Nasdaq, a prominent figure in the 1990s technology revolution, has previously discouraged such proposals.

Nasdaq initially conducted private share sales in 2000 and 2001. It officially became publicly traded in 2002 when its shares began trading on the OTC Bulletin Board, a platform that lists stocks that trade infrequently. Nasdaq will not profit from the sale but will provide returns to investors who participated in the private placements, according to the filings. The exchange primarily consists of shares in technology companies and other enterprises with significant growth potential. It served as a powerful emblem of the 1990s internet and telecommunications boom, but declined sharply after the bubble burst. A resurgence in the financial health of major technology companies like Intel and dot-com survivors such as Amazon has contributed to a revival of Nasdaq's fortunes.

All ye good people, afar and near,
To my request pray lend an ear;
I advise you all without delay to go
And see the Fair Maid's House - it is a rare show.
Some of the chairs there are very grand,
They have been cut and carved by a skilful hand;
And kings, perchance, if fhe truth were told,
Have sat on them in days of old.
King James the First of Scotland was murdered there,
And his cries for mercy rent the air.
But the Highland robbers only laughed at him,
And murdered him in the dungeon and thought if no sin.
Then there's an ancient shrine upstairs,
Where the Monks and Saints said their prayers,
To the Holy Virgin, be it told;
And the house, it is said, is six hundred years old.
The old cruisie lamps are there to be seen,
Which let the monks see to write from their sheen,
Arld if the walls could speak, they could tell a fearful tale,
Which would make the people's cheeks turn pale.
Then there's an old claymore dug up from Culloden Moor,
Which in its time shed innocent blood, I am sure,
If not at Culloden Moor, some other place,
Which no doubt the truth of it history might trace.
The interior of the house is magnificent to be seen,
And the wood panelling, I'm sure, would please the Queen;
And the old fire-place, with its big fire,
Is all that visitors could desire.
Then there's a ring in a big stone near by the door,
Where gentlemen tethered their horses in days of yore;
And on the staircase door there's a firling pin
For making a rattling noise when anyone wanted in.
The mistress of the house is very kind,
A more affable woman would be herd to find;
And to visitors she is very good,
And well versed in history, be it understood.

There are many examples in biological domains where there is insufficient information to estimate the uncertainty associated with a single observation, such as the mean or standard deviation of an observational dataset. This makes it hard for these datasets to be used on their own, and most researchers would rather obtain statistics of the entire dataset than simply the average values. There has been, however, some recent work which addresses this problem by using knowledge of the variance associated with different observations [1]. We present a framework for training hierarchical models to approximate certain aspects or facets of the true structure of a dataset. By defining the extent over which the model will estimate individual variability, the strength of its approximations and how much additional data must be provided before a given approximation can yield new information about the real structure of the raw data, we have gained experimental success at estimating the uncertainties associated with arbitrary features. Our analysis also demonstrates that the algorithm can improve upon known robustness bounds while substantially reducing training time and thus increasing accuracy.


[1] S. Wang, P. E. Cukierman, D. Dutta, J. M. Chan, S.-P. Chung, G. R. Veenstra and A. I. Hinton, Sparse Learning through Partition Tables, Neural Computation Letters (2015) 6(1): 933–939

Let $ G $ be a bridgeless cubic graph. Consider a list of $ k $ 1-factors of $ G $. Let $ E_i $ denote the set of edges present in exactly $ i $ members of the $ k $ 1-factors. Define $ \mu_k(G) $ as the minimum value of $ |E_0| $ over all such lists of $ k $ 1-factors of $ G $. If $ G $ is not 3-edge-colorable, then $ \mu_3(G) \geq 3 $. It is shown in [E. Steffen, 1-factor and cycle covers of cubic graphs, J. Graph Theory 78(3) (2015) 195–206] that if $ \mu_3(G) \neq 0 $, then $ 2 \mu_3(G) $ serves as an upper bound for the girth of $ G $. We demonstrate that $ \mu_3(G) $ also bounds the oddness $ \omega(G) $ of $ G $. We establish that $ \omega(G) \leq \frac{2}{3} \mu_3(G) $. If $ \mu_3(G) = \frac{2}{3} \mu_3(G) $, then every $ \mu_3(G) $-core possesses a specific structure. These cores are referred to as Petersen cores. We show that for any given oddness, there exists a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph $ G $ with $ \omega(G) = \frac{2}{3} \mu_3(G) $. However, the difference between $ \omega(G) $ and $ \frac{2}{3} \mu_3(G) $ can be arbitrarily large. This holds even when the oddness is fixed. Moreover, for every integer $ k \geq 3 $, there exists a bridgeless cubic graph $ G $ such that $ \mu_3(G) = k $.

1 large whole chicken (About 5 1/2 pounds)
8 medium cloves garlic, crushed
3 medium onions, halved
2 lemons, halved
1 1/2 pounds assorted fingerling potatoes
1/4 cup assorted chopped herbs (rosemary, thyme, parsley, or sage)
Olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Preheat oven to 425°. Rinse chicken well and pat dry, remove bag of giblets and discard or save for another use. Trim excess fat from opening of chicken cavity if necessary. Arrange halved onions in center of 9X13 inch pyrex dish to act as a base for chicken to sit on. Place chicken on top of onions. Squeeze halved lemon onto chicken body and legs, then place lemons in chicken cavity, repeat with all halved lemons. Place crushed garlic in cavity as well then tie chicken legs together with kitchen twine. Season chicken liberally with salt and cracked black pepper. Wash fingerling potatoes and slice largest fingerlings in half lengthwise. Toss potatoes with olive oil, half the chopped herbs and season with salt and pepper. Place in roasting baking dish around chicken. Roast until temperature taken in the thickest part of breast registers 150°F and thighs registers at least 165°F, about an hour. Remove from oven and allow chicken to rest for 15 minutes. Remove potatoes and toss with remaining chopped herbs. Carve chicken and serve immediately.

Controversial new EU rules for the patenting of computer-based inventions have been put on hold due to a last minute intervention from Poland.
Poland - a large and therefore crucial EU member - has requested more time to consider the issue, especially as it relates to the patenting of software. Critics say the law would favour large companies over small, innovative ones. They say it could have massive ramifications for developments such as open source software.
Polish ministers want to see the phrasing of the text of the Directive on the Patentability of Computer-Implemented Inventions changed so that it excludes the patenting of software. The planned law has ignited angry debate about whether the EU should allow the patenting of computer programs and internet business methods as currently happens in the US. So, for instance, US-based Amazon.com holds a patent on 'one-click shopping'. Critics claim the law, which the EU says is needed to harmonise with the US, is little more than a law on ideas. "Patent rights, it is claimed, protect inventors but in this case it is exclusively the interests of the big companies that are protected," Eva Lichtenberg, a Austrian Green member of the European Parliament said in a statement. "Smaller, innovative firms cannot afford the patenting and legal costs that the directive would inflict on them," she added. The European Parliament has already clashed with the European Union on the issue and there have been accusations that the process to decide the issue has been undemocratic. The directive has been subject to several previous delays.

The novel begins with Tarzan's day-to-day life in the African jungle, where he spends his time swinging through the trees, hunting for food, and protecting his animal friends. However, his peaceful existence is shattered when he comes across a race of minuscule warriors known as the Ant Men. 

Intrigued by these tiny beings with their intricate society, Tarzan decides to investigate further and discovers that they are at war with a neighboring tribe, the Waziri. Determined to assist the Ant Men, Tarzan offers his assistance and the strength of his superior physique. 

As the story progresses, Tarzan finds himself immersed in the complex politics and battles between the Ant Men and the Waziri, showcasing his leadership and strategic skills. Along the way, he learns more about their customs, traditions, and their reverence for the giant ants that inhabit their underground realm. 

With his unwavering loyalty, Tarzan forms valuable alliances and becomes a pivotal figure in the war between the Ant Men and the Waziri. As he fights alongside them, Tarzan begins to question his own identity and where he truly belongs. Is he more human or animal? Can he bridge the gap between his jungle upbringing and the civilized world?

Throughout the novel, Tarzan faces numerous challenges, from hostile wildlife to fierce warriors, and even the treacherous terrain of the underground ant kingdom. With his strength, intelligence, and resourcefulness, Tarzan must overcome these obstacles to help the Ant Men protect their land and defeat their enemy.

Tarzan and the Ant Men is a thrilling and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the balance between civilization and the wild. Burroughs' vivid storytelling and his ability to transport readers into the heart of the jungle make this novel a captivating read for both fans of the Tarzan series and new readers alike.

We propose an improved workflow for unsupervised multiphase image segmentation. Our method consists of four steps: (1) construction of an initial multiphase segmentation, (2) identification of oversegmentation artifacts, (3) correction of oversegmentation artifacts, and (4) refinement of the segmentation. We evaluate our method on two publicly available datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that our method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

In high-dimensional regression analysis, when the number of predictors exceeds the sample size, a key challenge is identifying relevant variables that influence the response of interest. Both variable selection and multiple testing techniques aim to tackle this problem. However, the relationship between these areas remains underexplored. If the signal is sufficiently strong to achieve selection consistency, controlling the false discovery rate may become unnecessary. This study focuses on a scenario where signals are both rare and weak, making selection consistency unachievable, and proposes a method that asymptotically controls the false discovery rate. Theoretical analysis shows that the false non-discovery rate of the proposed approach converges to zero at the optimal rate. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Rediffusion Singapore was a cable television provider in Singapore. It was previously a subsidiary of Rediffusion Industries, which originated from Radio Rediffusion, the first radio broadcaster in Singapore.

Radio Rediffusion began broadcasting in June 1949 and continued for 35 years until September 1984. At its peak, it reached 900,000 listeners, unparalleled by any other local radio station. However, with the emergence of television, Radio Rediffusion began to decline in popularity. On September 1, 1984, the radio station broadcast its last signal, thus ending its era.

In November 1989, Rediffusion acquired a 20-year franchise to operate a cable television service in Singapore. Installation works began in March 1990, and the service was launched on June 11, 1990, costing subscribers S$15.20 per month. In 1997, it increased its coverage area from 85 to 98 percent of Singapore, with an additional 84,000 homes able to receive the service. In March 1998, Rediffusion accelerated its expansion program to reach all households by end 1999.

On May 1, 2001, Singapore's then Minister for Information and the Arts Lee Yock Suan announced that the franchise for the cable television service would not be renewed, and that it would expire on August 31, 2001. The service would be replaced by StarHub CableTV, which began on December 29, 2001. In 2002, Rediffusion's cable television business was sold to Singapore Cable Vision (SCV), a subsidiary of StarHub.

On April 1, 2003, SCV merged with Singapore Digital Media Pte Ltd (SDM), a subsidiary of StarHub, and became StarHub Cable TV.

Place in a pan with a roasting rack and roast at 400 degrees for 40 min, so which the meat can brown. Turn down the oven to 325 degrees and roast for an additional 40 to 50 min or possibly till the meat thermometer registers 140 degrees. For Medium Lamb: Follow the above instructions but cook a bit longer so the thermometer registers 145 to 150 degrees. Remove the meat from the oven and allow it to sit 1/2 hour before slicing. It will continue to cook during this time. In the meantime, prepare the sauce. This recipe serves 4 to 6. Comments: This dish is from Louis' Basque Corner in Reno. The Basque sheepherders came to this Nevada area generations ago and they brought their recipes with them. Louis and Lorraine Erreguible have kept up the Basque boarding house tradition of dining and the place is just terrific.

A writer named Fernando returns to Medellín after a 30-year absence. He discovers the city now known as Colombia's "capital of hate." Fernando meets Alexis, a 16-year-old male prostitute and hitman—known as a "Medellín child"—with whom he develops a deep affection. However, their love is destined to end in tragedy. Alexis has no need for justification to kill; he acts like an Angel of Death, targeting anyone who disrupts his plans. Fernando and Alexis share an intense passion as they traverse from church to church, murder to murder. Alexis imparts the secrets and symbolism of the dangerous world of Medellín's drug cartel, while the author recounts his own childhood memories in a Medellín that feels unfamiliar. When Alexis is ultimately killed by two teenagers on a motorcycle, Fernando seeks out his killer. He identifies Wilmar, another young man with striking similarities to Alexis—not just physically, but also in behavior. Attempting to live a life with Wilmar, Fernando learns he is in a relationship with the killer of Alexis. However, he cannot kill him because Wilmar confesses that Alexis murdered his brother. Fernando suggests to Wilmar that they leave the country, and the boy agrees. Yet, when he arrives at his home to bid farewell to his mother, he is also killed. Fernando ends up alone in the heart of a city where love appears impossible.

Guy Fawkes was an Englishman who, along with twelve fellow conspirators, was part of the Gunpowder Plot, a failed attempt to blow up the British Houses of Parliament and assassinate King James I. The plot was discovered on November 4, 1605, and Fawkes was arrested while attempting to escape. He was tried, found guilty of high treason, and sentenced to be hanged, drawn, and quartered. However, he was spared from this gruesome punishment due to the intercession of the King, who ordered that he should merely be hanged and then decapitated.

Fawkes has become synonymous with the term "Guy Fawkes Night," which is celebrated annually on November 5 in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and other parts of the world. The celebrations usually involve burning effigies of Fawkes, fireworks, and bonfires.

Fawkes was born in 1570 in York, England. He was educated at Leeds Grammar School and studied at the University of Cambridge. He later fought for the Spanish in their war against the Dutch and, upon returning to England, became involved in the Gunpowder Plot.

The Gunpowder Plot was masterminded by Robert Catesby, who believed that the English Catholic population was being unfairly persecuted by the Protestant King James I. Catesby and his co-conspirators planned to blow up the Houses of Parliament during a session of the English Parliament, assassinate the King and his advisers, and install a Catholic monarch on the English throne.

Despite the failure of the Gunpowder Plot, Fawkes became a symbol of the dangers of political extremism and the importance of parliamentary democracy. His image is often used in political cartoons and other works of art to represent the peril of tyranny and the resilience of freedom.

For the guided collages, we first train a coalitional game model to segment an image into a set of regions, each of which is then replaced by a corresponding image retrieved from a large database. For the unguided collages, we train a recurrent neural network to generate a set of region proposals using the query image as context, and then retrieve images for each of the proposed regions.
