The cast is undoubtedly the highlight of the movie, with standout performances from Jay Baruchel, Seth Rogen, and James Franco. The chemistry between the actors is palpable, and their banter and interactions are some of the funniest moments in the film.

Overall, I'd recommend "This Is the End" to fans of stoner comedies and apocalyptic humor. It's not perfect, but it's a fun and entertaining ride that's worth taking. Just be prepared for some unevenness and a few missed opportunities for laughs.

We present a technique that enables automatic segmentation of images into semantically relevant areas without requiring human intervention. The identified regions are consistent across various images and align with manually defined semantic categories on certain datasets. When semantic regions are challenging to define and label, our approach remains effective in identifying coherent and consistent semantic classes. In this study, we employ a pre-trained StyleGAN2~\cite{karras2020analyzing} generative model, leveraging clustering in its feature space to uncover semantic classes. Following class discovery, a synthetic dataset comprising generated images and their corresponding segmentation masks can be constructed. Subsequently, a segmentation model is trained on this synthetic data and demonstrates capability to generalize to real-world images. Furthermore, by utilizing CLIP~\cite{radford2021learning}, we leverage natural language prompts to identify specific semantic classes. Our methodology is evaluated on publicly accessible datasets and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Cardinal Vincent Nichols, the leader of the Catholic Church in England and Wales, has criticised the cost of the Iraq war, saying that it has had a "devastating impact" on the country and its people.

Speaking at a conference in London, Cardinal Nichols said that the war, which was launched in 2003 by the US and UK, had caused "enormous suffering" and had led to the displacement of millions of people.

He added that the cost of the war had been "enormous", and had diverted attention and resources away from other important issues such as poverty and inequality.

The cardinal's comments come as the UK government is facing criticism over its decision to join the US in the invasion of Iraq, which was based on false claims that Saddam Hussein's regime had weapons of mass destruction.

The war, which lasted for several years, has been widely criticised for its human rights abuses and its failure to achieve its stated objectives.

Cardinal Nichols said that the Church had a duty to speak out against injustice and to work for peace and reconciliation, and called on governments to prioritise the needs of their citizens over military intervention.

On 25 October 1946, Popper, then at the London School of Economics, was invited to deliver a paper titled "Are There Philosophical Problems?" at a gathering of the Moral Sciences Club, led by Wittgenstein. They engaged in intense debate regarding whether philosophical issues were substantive or merely linguistic conundrums—Wittgenstein advocating for the latter. During the discussion, Wittgenstein emphasized his points using a fireplace poker, gesturing with it as the argument intensified. When confronted with a request to provide an example of a moral rule, Popper later recalled responding with "Not to threaten visiting lecturers with pokers," prompting Wittgenstein to throw down the poker and leave the room. *Wittgenstein's Poker* compiles and analyzes the various interpretations of the argument, along with examining the backgrounds and careers of Popper, Wittgenstein, and Bertrand Russell, who attended the meeting. The book traces three narrative strands, all revolving around the 1946 Cambridge dispute: one explores the precise events and the differing accounts from witnesses; another presents a comparative biography of the philosophers, highlighting their origins in Vienna and their divergent paths to fame; and the third examines the philosophical implications of the conflict and its impact on early 20th-century debates about the nature of language.

Boosting involves creating a single precise predictor by merging multiple less accurate weak predictors linearly. Structured learning has been widely applied in computer vision recently. Drawing inspiration from structured support vector machines (SSVM), this paper introduces a novel boosting algorithm tailored for structured output prediction, termed StructBoost. StructBoost enables nonlinear structured learning by integrating a collection of weak structured predictors. Similar to SSVM, which extends SVM, StructBoost generalizes traditional boosting methods like AdaBoost or LPBoost to structured learning. The optimization challenge in StructBoost is more complex due to its potential for exponentially large variables and constraints. In contrast, SSVM typically features an exponential number of constraints and employs a cutting-plane approach. To efficiently solve StructBoost, we develop an equivalent 1-slack formulation and employ a blend of cutting planes and column generation techniques. Our results demonstrate the broad applicability and effectiveness of StructBoost across various tasks, including optimizing tree loss for hierarchical multi-class classification, refining the Pascal overlap criterion for robust visual tracking, and estimating conditional random field parameters for image segmentation.

Orleanna Price introduces the opening chapter of five out of the novel's seven parts. The story then shifts between the four daughters, with a particular emphasis on the voice of the most assertive, Leah. As the girls grow older, they gradually adapt to African village life, the harshness of their father Nathan's misogyny, and the political unrest in The Congo during the 1960s. Due to the perspective of the developing daughters, the portrayal of the Congolese villagers evolves. Initially, they seem like foolish savages, but as the girls mature, these villagers become complex individuals living within a rich and intricate cultural environment. Nathan's failure to engage with this new world causes his family's hospitality to wane, yet he refuses to depart. It is only after several hardships, including the loss of one daughter, that the women decide to leave Nathan Price. The survivors follow divergent paths in their lives, and the novel concludes at the time of Mobutu Sese Seko's death in the 1990s. Rachel, the oldest, marries Axelroot at sixteen and later becomes the owner of a luxury hotel near Brazzaville. Leah marries Anatole, has four sons, and stays in the impoverished Congo. Adah returns to the United States with her mother Orleanna, attends college, and later pursues medical studies. She undergoes a long experimental procedure that enables her to walk again and begins speaking. Orleanna returns to living on the Georgian coast, enjoying Adah's occasional visits.

This proud ship is the Morning Star,
She is built of solid oak beams.
A smell of varnish and fresh boiled tar,
With brass that in sunshine gleams.
Her masts and rigging tell of ancient skills,
Sails unfurled awaiting a breeze.
Bellowing canvas at long last fills,
And her bows plough furrows in the seas.
A darkening sky a foreboding of storms,
With a hush distressing the soul.
Saint Anselm plays with fire, and forms,
Rain and thunder engulfing the whole.
Waves break over those bows of oak,
Men shudder and fight for a hold.
Many a prayer for calm was spoke,
Tall tales of despair were told.
Three days and nights, seas kept at bay,
Then calm and a time for sleep.
Sail makers repairs took many a day,
They were saved from that yawning deep.
The Morning Star is outward bound,
Chile is the course we've set,
Pass we not Cape Horn, safe and sound,
Those fathoms will be our yet.
Clear skies indeed with nary a cloud,
Heat and sickness is our lot.
Gazing at mast's that stand so proud,
Eyes blinded by a sun so hot.
This Maiden Voyage of the Morning Star,
An opus of men's iron will.
Shall we reach that land so far,
Lying here becalmed and still.
Sea-way has come at long last,
A movement, A ripple of sales.
Taking us on to the icy blast,
Of the Horns most fearsome gales.
We are past the Horn, No dreaded storm,
With sea as calm as a pond.
The Morning Star, is much in form.
For together we have forged a bond.
Homeward bound, cargo is filled,
Hearts beat higher with hope.
Loved one's waiting, need is stilled,
Hands blistered by the pull on rope.
Gliding into port sails are trimmed,
Shouts of command are heard
The memories of hardships strangely dimmed,
As Morning Star is likened to a bird.

Santee St. John is a reporter for NewsReal, a shock site for which he records video via a virtual “interface” allowing viewers to actually experience his recordings on the World Wide Web. He is sent to record a massacre of indigenous people being attacked at Chiapas, Mexico without warning by landowners working for capitalist corporations. However, due to a business deal with Mexico’s government, NewsReal decides not to show the story, prompting Santee to take a sabbatical. While on sabbatical, he meets Margaret Mayfield, a rebel Zapatista with whom he is swayed to travel with and, eventually, fall in love with and decide to fight against the capitalist elite. St. John and Mayfield decide to join a group called Intrepid Explorers, working for the corporations, in order to find a strong group of Zapatistas to join. They are met by an individual claiming to be Subcomandante Marcos, the first revolutionary to use cyberspace, who helped Santee and Margaret establish a plan: to give the rebel victims of the capitalists’ massacres interfaces, which will allow the entire world to experience their sufferings via the World Wide Web by actually taking on all sense perceptions of that person through a completely realistic virtual reality simulator. Margaret Mayfield went on her part of the mission with Webster Webfoot, who used to be one of the most highly rated internet stars but became a “webkicker” and now tries to avoid using an interface whenever possible. However, once there, she is told that Santee is dead and that the funeral will be held the very next day; she and Webster travel to Chiapas, where the funeral is to be held, and discover that Santee is not actually dead, but that someone has faked his demise. Margaret abandons Webster, leaving him some cash for travel, and travels with a hotel owner named Zack Hayman who seems to have an inside connection with the conspirators. In Chiapas, Margaret discovers that Santee left her a personalized interface, which cannot be activated until Santee is actually present. At the same time, Webster’s girlfriend on the internet, Starchilde or “Starr” for short, discovers through her work on a space station that there exists oil on Mars, which means that biological extraterrestrial life must have existed on the planet at some point, as well as that Mexican rebels are being shipped to Mars in order to harvest the oil. Back on Earth, Zack, the hotel manager whom Margaret is with, discovered that the rebels are being sent to Mars in part so that the rich landowners can take their land without resistance. Santee and Margaret believed that they were setting up the victims with interfaces so that they would be able to show their sufferings to others outside of Mexico, but in fact the interfaces were going to make them think that they were receiving messages from Santee, while they were actually going to be tricked to going to Mars as slave labor. On the ship near Mars, Starr discovers that the slaves are to be sent to Mars in order to live there for a time and scout out any biological hazards or chemical hazards. Starr meets an intelligent AI, called Alice Irene, who serves as a literal deus ex machine. Starr convinces Alice Irene to join the cause of the rebels by having her examine the entire Internet and come to her own conclusions about the corruption of the current capitalist regime. Starr was given control of the ship, and the Zapatistas took control with the assistance of Alice Irene. The revolutionaries were given the option to stay on Earth or go to Mars, but as a form of utopian paradise rather than as slave labor. Santee St. John and Margaret Mayfield chose to stay on earth, while the remaining main characters chose life on Mars.

John Samuel Rowell (1837-1915) was a Canadian businessman and politician.

Rowell was born in Fredericton, New Brunswick, the son of John Rowell and Jane Ann McLean. He was educated in Fredericton and at the University of New Brunswick. In 1856, he went to Saint John, New Brunswick, where he was employed as a clerk in a hardware store. He later became a partner in the firm. In 1868, he married Elizabeth Ann McLean. Rowell served as mayor of Saint John from 1874 to 1875. He was also a director of the New Brunswick Railway and the Saint John Harbour Commission. He was elected to the House of Commons of Canada for the riding of Saint John City in an 1878 by-election, and was reelected in 1882 and 1887. A Liberal, he served as Postmaster General from 1887 to 1888. He was defeated in the 1888 election. Rowell died in Saint John in 1915.

Crude oil prices rebounded above $47 per barrel on Thursday following an increase in global demand projections by an energy regulatory body. The International Energy Agency (IEA) cautioned that OPEC's crude oil demand in the first quarter would exceed supply. The IEA revised its 2005 oil demand growth forecast by 80,000 barrels daily to 84 million barrels daily. US light crude increased by $1.64 to $47.10, while Brent crude in London climbed by $1.32 to $44.45. The Paris-based IEA noted that the price rise was attributed to heightened demand from China and other Asian markets. The recent surge in crude prices followed gains on Wednesday, driven by significant drops in U.S. crude inventories after a cold winter in North America. The U.S. Department of Energy reported that crude stockpiles fell by 1 million barrels to 294.3 million barrels. Additionally, ongoing challenges faced by the struggling Russian oil company Yukos have led the IEA to adjust its production estimates for Russia, a key non-OPEC supplier. "I believe prices are starting to establish a new range, with levels between $40 and $50," stated energy analyst Orin Middleton of Barclays Capital.

He must find new ways to interact with his family and friends, adapt to his changing surroundings, and learn how to control his emotions before they trigger another bout of shrinkage. Along the way, he meets other people like him, forming a support group that helps him cope with his unique situation.

But just when things seem to be looking up, our hero's life takes a dangerous turn. A group of ruthless scientists, aware of his condition, kidnap him in an attempt to exploit his abilities for their own gain. Our hero must use all his wits and resourcefulness to escape and take down his captors.

In the end, our protagonist emerges stronger and more resilient than ever before. With the help of his support system and newfound confidence, he embraces his role as a symbol of hope for others facing similar challenges. The trial of Bernie Ebbers, former chief executive of bankrupt US phone company WorldCom, has started in New York with the selection of the jury.
Mr Ebbers, 63, is accused of being the mastermind behind an $11bn (£6bn) accounting fraud that eventually saw the firm collapse in July 2002. His indictment includes charges of securities fraud, conspiracy and filing false reports with regulators. If found guilty, Mr Ebbers could face a substantial jail sentence. He has firmly declared his innocence.
Under Mr Ebbers' leadership, WorldCom emerged from Mississippi obscurity to become a $160bn telecoms giant and the darling of late 1990s investors. Yet as competition intensified and the telecoms boom petered out, WorldCom found itself under growing financial stress. When WorldCom finally collapsed, shareholders lost about $180bn and 20,000 workers lost their jobs. Mr Ebbers' trial, which is expected to last two months, is the latest in a series of attempts by US prosecutors to pursue senior executives for fraud. It will coincide with the retrial of former Tyco International chief Dennis Kozlowski and his top lieutenant, accused of looting the industrial conglomerate to the tune of $600m. Trail preparations are also preparing for former executives of shamed US energy firm Enron.

The owners of embattled Russian oil giant Yukos are to ask the buyer of its former production unit to pay back a $900m (£479m) loan.
State-owned Rosneft bought the Yugansk unit for $9.3bn in a sale forced by Russia to part settle a $27.5bn tax claim against Yukos. Yukos' owner Menatep Group says it will ask Rosneft to repay a loan that Yugansk had secured on its assets. Rosneft already faces a similar $540m repayment demand from foreign banks. Legal experts said Rosneft's purchase of Yugansk would include such obligations. "The pledged assets are with Rosneft, so it will have to pay real money to the creditors to avoid seizure of Yugansk assets," said Moscow-based US lawyer Jamie Firestone, who is not connected to the case. Menatep Group's managing director Tim Osborne told the Reuters news agency: "If they default, we will fight them where the rule of law exists under the international arbitration clauses of the credit."
Rosneft officials were unavailable for comment. But the company has said it intends to take action against Menatep to recover some of the tax claims and debts owed by Yugansk. Yukos had filed for bankruptcy protection in a US court in an attempt to prevent the forced sale of its main production arm. The sale went ahead in December and Yugansk was sold to a little-known shell company which in turn was bought by Rosneft. Yukos claims its downfall was punishment for the political ambitions of its founder Mikhail Khodorkovsky and has vowed to sue any participant in the sale.

1 pint strawberry
1 (12 ounce) bag chocolate chips
8 ounces cream cheese
1 tablespoon powdered sugar
1 tablespoon milk
sliced almonds (optional)
Wash the strawberries. Then, slice the bottom point off the strawberry, so that it can stand up straight. Next, pluck the stem off. Using a paring knife or strawberry huller, scoop out the top to make room for the cheesecake. This is the most important step...dry off the strawberries individually with paper towels. If the strawberries are wet, the chocolate will not stick. Melt the chocolate in a double broiler or microwave. (Note: if using a microwave, only melt it in 20-second increments to make sure it doesn't burn). I use Ghirardelli 60% Cacao Bittersweet Chocolate Chips. Line a cookie sheet (that will fit in your freezer) with waxed paper or a Silpat. Dip the bottom half of each strawberry into the melted chocolate and place on the lined pan. Once the pan is full, place it in the freezer for about 5 minutes or until the chocolate has hardened. While the chocolate is cooling, make the cheesecake filling. In a small bowl, beat together the cream cheese, powdered sugar and milk, until smooth. If it seems too thick, add a splash more milk. Spoon the cheesecake mixture into a piping bag with a star tip. If you don't have a piping bag, scoop it into a large Ziploc bag and snip off the corner. Remove the strawberries from the freezer and pipe in the cheesecake filling. Top with a slivered almond and serve or refrigerate until ready to serve.

With the recent development in multimedia technologies, identifying visual attention regions has become a significant challenge in image processing. The widespread use of diverse terminal devices in the context of multimedia technology provides ample opportunities for improving image visualization. Among various methodologies, feature-based image extraction has gained prominence in the field of image processing. Image segmentation involves dividing an image into distinct regions based on certain properties like gray level, texture, or color. This process, along with subsequent extraction, forms the initial stage and critical aspect of object recognition, scene understanding, and image analysis. The application of this technique spans across mobile devices, industrial quality control, medical equipment, robotic navigation, geophysics, and military uses. The accuracy of final outcomes heavily relies on the quality of preprocessing steps. Often, obtaining spurious-free preprocessing data necessitates extensive computational and mathematical efforts. We introduce a novel, feature-based fuzzy rule-guided method that operates without external interference during execution. Experimental findings indicate that this approach offers superior efficiency compared to existing techniques discussed in the literature. To validate the effectiveness of our method against competitors, we utilize metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR).

Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered weak and weary,  
Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore—    
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,   
As of someone gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door—. 
"'Tis some visitor," I muttered, "'tapper at my window lent;     
Only this and nothing more." 

Ah distinctly I remember it was in the bleak December;      
And each separate dying ember writhed upon the floor.   
Eagerly I wished the morrow ; - vainly had I sought to borrow       
From my books surcease of sorrow — sadness measured out her hours         
 
To an early grave or two removed from all human dwellings          
 
 But little thought they stumbling over me that ever again           

 Would be masterless their chosen dwelling place forlorn        


 As dreaming on things happy long past far off voices seem            

 
 To whisper unto one another low sounds like distant thunder                



 While I struggled through decades dark as dreams where hope is never born               




 Suddenly there burst into bloom before mine eyes once more

In his malodorous brain what slugs and mire,
Lanthorned in his oblique eyes, guttering burned!
His body lodged a rat where men nursed souls.
The world flashed grape-green eyes of a foiled cat
To him. On fragments of an old shrunk power,
On shy and maimed, on women wrung awry,
He lay, a bullying hulk, to crush them more.
But when one, fearless, turned and clawed like bronze,
Cringing was easy to blunt these stern paws,
And he would weigh the heavier on those after.
Who rests in God's mean flattery now? Your wealth
Is but his cunning to make death more hard.
Your iron sinews take more pain in breaking.
And he has made the market for your beauty
Too poor to buy, although you die to sell.
Only that he has never heard of sleep;
And when the cats come out the rats are sly.
Here we are safe till he slinks in at dawn
But he has gnawed a fibre from strange roots,
And in the morning some pale wonder ceases.
Things are not strange and strange things are forgetful.
Ah! if the day were arid, somehow lost
Out of us, but it is as hair of us,
And only in the hush no wind stirs it.
And in the light vague trouble lifts and breathes,
And restlessness still shadows the lost ways.
The fingers shut on voices that pass through,
Where blind farewells are taken easily ....
Ah! this miasma of a rotting God!

John D. Goldman, born on August 18, 1949, is an American businessman and philanthropist based in San Francisco, California. He belongs to the Haas family through his mother. 

Goldman was born to a Jewish family on August 18, 1949, in San Francisco, the son of Rhoda (née Haas) and Richard Goldman. He is the second eldest of four children: Richard Goldman (who passed away in 1989), Douglas E. Goldman, and Susan R. Gelman. His grandfather was Walter A. Haas, the former president and chairman of Levi Strauss & Co; his great-grandfather was Abraham Haas, the founder of Hellman-Haas Grocery (which later became Smart & Final); and his great-great-grandfather was Simon Koshland, who once held the title of one of the largest wool merchants in the United States. He grew up in the Presidio Heights neighborhood of San Francisco. In 1967, he graduated from Lick-Wilmerding High School. He earned a B.A. from Swarthmore College and an M.B.A. from Stanford University in 1975. Following his education, he worked at the Office of the Legislative Analyst for California. In 1978, he was appointed as the state’s assistant secretary of transportation under Governor Jerry Brown. In 1981, he acquired a chain of children's clothing stores called Jamboree, but the business collapsed. In 1986, he joined Richard N. Goldman and Company (later Goldman Insurance Services), which was established by his father. In 1991, he became president, and in 2002, the family sold the company. After his mother's death in 1998, he served as a trustee of the Richard and Rhoda Goldman Fund.

The dough should be soft but not sticky. Dust with flour if dough is too sticky to handle. Divide the dough into four equal pcs and roll each piece to create a 12-inch-long loaf. Place on a parchment-lined cookie sheet, spacing loaves 3 inches apart. Bake 20 to 25 min, or possibly till golden. Remove cookie sheet from the oven. Using two metal spatulas, carefully lift the loaves off the cookie sheet and onto a wire cooling rack. Cold. Place cooled loaves on a cutting board. Remove cookie sheet from the oven. Cold toasted biscotti on a wire cooling rack. Store in an airtight container. This recipe yields 48 cookies. The Endeavour Leadership Program, formerly Endeavour Scholarships and Fellowships, formerly Endeavour Awards, was an internationally competitive, merit-based scholarship programme that formed part of the Australian Government's $1.4 billion Australian initiative. The programme brought leading researchers, executives and students to Australia to undertake short or long term study, research and professional development in a broad range of disciplines, and enabled Australians to do the same abroad. It aimed at developing linkages between involved nations. The Endeavour Awards were established as part of the 2003 International Education Package Engaging the World Through Education.

The Australian Scholarships, a $1.4 billion Australian Government initiative, brings under the one umbrella the scholarship programmes managed by the federal government and AusAID. Over the five years from July 2006, Australian Scholarships have doubled the number of Australian Government funded scholarships available in the Asia-Pacific region.

Acquiring comprehensive and varied representations is essential for enhancing the performance of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). In this study, we explore how incorporating privileged information can boost the intrinsic diversity of a single CNN model, enabling it to acquire more effective representations and improve its generalization capabilities. As such, we introduce a new group orthogonal convolutional neural network (GoCNN), which leverages provided privileged information to uncover untangled representations within each layer and significantly enhance representation diversity. We apply this approach to image classification, using image segmentation annotations as privileged information during training. Experimental results on two widely recognized datasets—ImageNet and PASCAL VOC—validate the superior generalization capability of our proposed GoCNN model. Specifically, on the ImageNet dataset, GoCNN achieves a 1.2% improvement over the state-of-the-art ResNet-152 model when only 10% of the training images are utilized as privileged information, demonstrating the efficacy of GoCNN in harnessing available privileged knowledge to train improved CNNs.

Claphamomnibus's ship lands at Gaul, and he unleashes the secret weapon: female legionaries (strongly resembling amazons). Claphamomnibus's reasoning for the forming of this strange unit is that because of the Gaul warriors' code of chivalry, they cannot fight women and thus could be easily defeated. Asterix, while scouting the Romans, learns of the arrival of Claphamomnibus and his female legionnaries and is sent as an ambassador to warn the village women of the threat (they worriedly send clothes to their husbands via Asterix and Obelix, in case it gets cold at night in the forest). Bravura tries to meet the women as an ambassador, claiming that since they are all women, they are sisters. The Roman sentry pounds her and Claphamomnibus insults her. Asterix watches it all; he also sees her slapping Clapharmomnibus which gives the Gaul hero a new perspective about the lady bard. Asterix approaches Bravura with a plan to get rid of this new problem. Part of his plan is to have Cacofonix sing songs in the forest, causing it to rain and scaring off all animals such as rabbits and snakes (and in one scene even a dragon). This scares the female Roman scout parties, causing them to retreat many times. (Humorously Asterix' departure to talk to Bravura was misinterpreted by the men, who by their passed comments assumed he was proposing marriage.) The rest of the plan involves the women of the village setting up a mall with the latest styles and accessories from Lutetia, and thus when the Roman women arrive to attack the supposedly undefended village they immediately become absorbed in shopping. In the meantime, the men of the village take out the fortified camps filled with male legionaries; Obelix is even allowed to destroy one of the camps single-handedly, as acknowledgment that he has not been much involved with the storyline until that point. Finally, Cacofonix sings once again as the Roman women leave the village with their shopping, and the terrified women (along with the dragon) flee Gaul on their ship with Claphamomnibus left behind. The story ends with the Gauls in a good mood, and there seems to be a good mood in Rome as well, for Julius Caesar is the laughing stock of his nation for having had to hire women to defeat the Gauls, and, on top of this, it is again a failure. Bravura and Asterix settle their original angst and develop a regard for one other.

The middle-levels graph $M_k$ ($0<k\in\mathbb{Z}$) has a dihedral quotient
pseudograph $R_k$ whose vertices are the $k$-edge ordered trees $T$, each $T$
encoded as a $(2k+1)$-string $F(T)$ formed via $\rightarrow$DFS by: {\bf(i)}
($\leftarrow$BFS-assigned) Kierstead-Trotter lexical colors $0,\ldots,k$ for
the descending nodes; {\bf(ii)} asterisks $*$ for the $k$ ascending edges. Two
ways of corresponding a restricted-growth $k$-string $\alpha$ to each $T$
exist, namely one Stanley's way and a novel way that assigns $F(T)$ to $\alpha$
via nested substring-swaps. These swaps permit to sort $V(R_k)$ as an ordered
tree that allows a lexical visualization of $M_k$ as well as the Hamilton
cycles of $M_k$ constructed by P. Gregor, T. M\"utze and J. Nummenpalo.

Shares of Irish oil company Petrel Resources have dropped over 50% following a report that the company did not secure a contract in Iraq. According to Reuters, Iraq's Oil Ministry has assigned the first post-war oilfield contracts to a Canadian and a Turkish company. By 17:00 GMT, Petrel's stock price fell from 97p ($1.87) to 44p ($0.85). Petrel stated it has not received any confirmation or denial from Iraqi authorities regarding the report.

Iraq is set to award contracts for three projects worth $500 million (£258.5 million). Turkey's Everasia is reported to have secured a contract to develop the Khurmala Dome field in the northern part of the country. A Canadian entity, IOG, is said to have won the contract to manage the Himrin field. Ironhorse Oil and Gas has denied being the subject of the report. These two projects aim to increase production at the Khurmala field to 100,000 barrels per day and enhance output at the Himrin field. The winning companies are expected to construct new flow lines and gas separation facilities. The contract for the Suba-Luhais field has not yet been announced as Iraq's Oil Ministry is reviewing proposals. If the cabinet approves the ministry's selection, this would mark the first time Iraq has signed a deal with a foreign oil company. Iraq continues to strive to boost its production capacity to align with levels observed in the 1980s prior to the Iranian conflict. Oil officials anticipate doubling Iraq's output by the end of the decade.

Cynthia Johnston Turner is a conductor and clinician in the United States, Latin America, Europe and Canada. She was appointed Dean of the Faculty of Music at Wilfrid Laurier University in July 2021. Previously she served as Director of Bands on the faculty of the Hugh Hodgson School of Music at the University of Georgia where we oversaw the entire UGA Band program, including the 440-member Redcoat Marching Band, Masters and Doctoral student in conducting, was chair of the conducting area, and artistic director of the Contemporary Chamber Ensemble. She formerly served on the faculty of Cornell University, where she directed the Wind Ensemble, Wind Symphony and chamber winds. Turner is a guest conductor and clinician in Canada, United States, and abroad. A Canadian, Turner completed her Bachelor of Music and Bachelor of Education degrees at Queen's University and her Master of Music in music education and conducting at the University of Victoria. Touring with her ensembles inspired her master's thesis on the musical and personal transformations that occur on tours, and her D.M.A. thesis at the Eastman School of Music centered on Dialogues and Entertainments by William Kraft. At Eastman, she was the recipient of the Eastman Graduate Teaching Award in conducting. She was nominated for the Canadian Prime Minister's Leadership in Teaching Award and received the National Leadership in Education Award (Readers Digest Foundation), the Excellence in Education Award (Ontario Secondary School Teachers Federation), and the Marion Drysdale Leadership Among Women Teachers Award (also from OSSTF).

Black trees beneath an orange sky,  
Trees swayed by the wind with great force,  
Trembling like a violent wave on the road,  
Shaking with the weight of desolation,  
Twisting like rivers, like eerie spells  
Of molten metal cast upon snow. Below,  
The iron ice bit like a whip,  
Cutting through my torn footwear,  
And every breath was filled with icy sleet.  
The land was thick with snow,  
Steely and cruel, gleaming faintly,  
As pale ridges of obsidian.  
Yet I pressed forward—fire and ice,  
One in the raging hunger of desire.  
A quiet longing, for distant lands,  
For verdant fields in summer’s light,  
For burning wood, for walls, for eyes—  
For wine, for ancient, sweet discourse,  
A golden sphere in fountain's dance,  
And memories lost, now forever apart.  
(Oh, god, I tread upon them,  
And they stay, etched with unspoken pain,  
Loved lips and faces now estranged,  
Once close, now broken, in anguish—  
A part of me, in torment, in pain.)  
Lethe does not belong to any soul,  
Nor will any remember it in hell.  
There were blossoms, mugs, radiant,  
Old Italian blades—glances of flame,  
Sparking, soaring, reaching upward,  
Into the clear, boundless blue,  
Until two hearts became one,  
Flame, flesh, and yet the same!  
As if all springs were channeled into  
One single droplet of dew!  
But only the most thought of warmth,  
A deep yearning for heat...  
Hot white sand, where the body rests,  
Sun-dried grass, a nest within,  
Fires, countless, tossing golden plumes  
Upward, and the red core in coals,  
Crushing as they split into sparks,  
Snapping kindling, bursting sticks,  
Fallen like jackstraws—green and blue,  
The devilish flames of driftwood,  
Heavy, fierce, and smoky heaps—  
Still burning, full of hate and heat.  
And then the image of his face,  
All theirs, came like a blade—  
Three times to the heart—

Mathew McConaughey is Brandon Lane, a former football star recruited by Walter Abraham (Al Pacino), the head of a sports consulting firm to help them set the line for their sports betting business. Lane's ability to predict the outcome of games quickly turns him into a golden boy, but it soon becomes apparent that he's bitten off more than he can chew when his abilities start to falter.

Two for the Money is a forgettable, generic thriller that doesn't really offer anything new. The film does have some entertaining moments and the first half of the movie is actually pretty exciting to watch. But, the second half is really slow and very tedious. It just drags on and on and for no reason either. It could have been a nice 90 minute movie but the story is stretched out into a two hour film. Luckily, Al Pacino is in the movie and he keeps the film exciting. He gives a good, over the top performance and he pretty much raises the film up to mediocrity. Personally, sports betting isn't that interesting to me but Al Pacino makes it interesting. He can turn a bad script into an okay movie which is what he does with the film. Let's be honest, the script is not very good and the direction is weak. It's so obvious where things are going which is not surprising because this is the same guy that made Taking Lives.

Al Pacino is playing mentor to Matthew McConaughey and their chemistry together isn't very strong. McConaughey is a pretty weak actor and he can't keep up with Pacino. The lead role should have gone to someone else. Rene Russo is okay as Pacino's wife. She gives a decent performance but she was a little too bland to truly stand out. Another thing about the film that people may not like is that every character is unlikable. It's hard to care for these characters because they are either pretty mean or bland. It didn't really bother me because I watched the film to be entertained and I did get some entertainment value from the movie. In the end, if you like Al Pacino then you should give the film a shot, if you don't then just skip it. Rating 6/10

Much like the easily frightened deer, a horse is naturally prone to fear. Over millennia as prey, it has developed an instinct to flee. It is clear that courage and fear often go together. In 2011, Tonk, a stallion, was deserving of a medal. He refused to leave despite a grizzly bear appearing suddenly and chasing a young boy. His rider, Erin Bolster, who had no weapon or holster, stood her ground and shouted, "I will not stand by and let this boy die!" The horse, towering at 18 hands, remained steadfast even as other horses fled. Three times, they charged the bear, staring into its terrifying eyes until it retreated. Afterward, Tonk could not shake the tremors, having come dangerously close to breaking. The sight of those menacing jaws and sharp claws left him shaken, his coat soaked with sweat. Thus, the bravest animal I know is similar to a nervous doe—this white Percheron draft horse, named Tonk. David Letterman introduced them on his show, bringing smiles and relief to the world.

Built from great constellations and long forgotten rivers
I give you my restless poems without regret.
Yes it’s true that I’ve been on the move lately
and have little time to talk.
What can I say
but that from this day forward,
I can only promise you vague dreams
and curious facts.
Yes, I keep moving, thats understood,
but please tell me something,
from which ocean did you arrive,
was it during summer?
or after a winters storm?                                                                                                                      Was the moon out that night?
My restless longing needs to know these things.
My thirst grows toward oblivion;
I need to feel the ocean move towards the shore.
I need to watch the stars so none go missing.
I need to keep learning about roses
and things until I know absolutely nothing at all. Really it’s true,
and it’s not my fault that I live without a compass
and that my love grows wildly in no particular direction.
Will you excuse me now, as I put distance
between you, me and this poem.

Black Allan, also known as Allan F-1 (1886–1910), was the father of the Tennessee Walking Horse. He was bred by a Morgan mare named Maggie Marshall and stood on Allendorf, a stallion related to Narragansett Pacer, Canadian Pacer, and Gaited Spanish Mustang imported from Texas. Black Allan was registered as No. 7623 by the American Trotting Registry. Despite being intended for racing, he preferred pacing and thus never competed. In addition to pacing, he exhibited a lateral ambling gait called the running walk. He was a black stallion measuring 5 feet tall. The breeders' association, which later became the Tennessee Walking Horse Breeders' and Exhibitors' Association, designated him as Allan F-1 in 1935. Throughout his life, Black Allan had several owners, but his final owners, James Brantley and Albert Dement, were the only ones who recognized his role as a breeding stallion. Black Allan produced 111 known offspring, including Roan Allen (F-38), Hunters Allen F-10, and Merry Legs F-4. He passed away on September 16, 1910, at the age of 29.

Richard Williams (born ca. 1971)  is a former American professional baseball executive and the former president of baseball operations of the Cincinnati Reds of Major League Baseball. Before his promotion, announced on December 27, 2016, he was the Reds' senior vice president and general manager. Williams is a graduate of the University of Virginia. He was an Echols Scholar at UVA, giving him priority to sign up for any class. He worked as an investment banker and from 2003–04 for the George W. Bush presidential re-election campaign.  He joined the Reds in 2006, upon their purchase by a group led by majority owner Robert Castellini, as director of baseball business operations. He later became vice president of baseball operations and then was named vp/assistant GM in November 2014. Twelve months later, he was promoted to general manager, working under Walt Jocketty, then president of baseball operations. Jocketty became an advisor to Castellini with Williams' December 2016 appointment.

Additive deformations of bialgebras in the sense of Wirth are deformations of
the multiplication map of the bialgebra fulfilling a compatibility condition
with the coalgebra structure and a continuity condition. Two problems
concerning additive deformations are considered. With a deformation theory a
cohomology theory should be developed. Here a variant of the Hochschild
cohomology is used. The main result in the first partad of this paper is the
characterization of the trivial deformations, i.e. deformations generated by a
coboundary. Starting with a Hopf algebra, one would expect the deformed
multiplications to have some analogue of the antipode, which we call deformed
antipodes. We prove, that deformed antipodes always exist, explore their
properties, give a formula to calculate them given the deformation and the
antipode of the original Hopf algebra and show in the cocommutative case, that
each deformation splits into a trivial part and into a part with constant
antipodes.

A former CIA agent, pursued by his own colleagues, reconnects with his old crew for a final mission. While the storyline isn't entirely original, blending elements from the Bourne series, The Expendibles, and The Losers, "RED" (short for "Retired, Extremely Dangerous") is the fourth film this year based on a graphic novel. It is also the fourth movie featuring individuals on a mission and the fifth with a CIA-related plot. I was initially doubtful, but upon reviewing the cast, I realized it was intended to be a comedy. As a result, I viewed the project differently. "RED" features John McClane, Cyrus the Virus, and The Queen working together to kill for entertainment. Clearly, the narrative and logic were secondary to the cast and their dynamic. 

Bruce Willis, known for his role in the "Die Hard" and "Sin City" series, has maintained a consistent character arc, albeit with little change. His performance in "RED" is recognizable, yet he remains consistently enjoyable. This time, he adds a layer of self-awareness, maintaining a carefree demeanor throughout the film, as if he's experienced this countless times and can now relax. Efforts to make him appear more relatable are somewhat amusing. The initial ten minutes depict him adjusting to retirement and wandering around his home in a dressing gown, reminiscent of Carl Fredricksen’s portrayal in "Up." However, deeper character development highlights his extreme oddity, offering a delightful glimpse into his actions. 

Helen Mirren, chosen to complement Willis's predictable casting, is well-suited for action roles. She embodies a flower-arranger on the outside and a formidable hitwoman on the inside, making her an unusual fit for the genre.

Liver lesion segmentation is a difficult yet critical task for medical image
analysis. Recently, deep learning based image segmentation methods have
achieved promising performance, which can be divided into three categories: 2D,
2.5D and 3D, based on the dimensionality of the models. However, 2.5D and 3D
methods can have very high complexity and 2D methods may not perform
satisfactorily. To obtain competitive performance with low complexity, in this
paper, we propose a Feature-fusion Encoder-Decoder Network (FED-Net) based 2D
segmentation model to tackle the challenging problem of liver lesion
segmentation from CT images. Our feature fusion method is based on the
attention mechanism, which fuses high-level features carrying semantic
information with low-level features having image details. Additionally, to
compensate for the information loss during the upsampling process, a dense
upsampling convolution and a residual convolutional structure are proposed. We
tested our method on the dataset of MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS)
Challenge and achieved competitive results compared with other state-of-the-art
methods.

You must hearken back to when real happiness was known
Remember its impact on your life

What you take as your life marches on day by day, an obligation to life.

The story is about a young boy named Johannes, who along with his family has to flee their home in Denmark after the German invasion. They leave behind almost everything they own, including Johannes' beloved pink rabbit toy. The family seeks refuge in England but faces many challenges on their journey. They have to rely on the kindness of strangers and often times find themselves living in difficult conditions. Along the way, Johannes struggles to come to terms with the loss of his toy and the upheaval in his life. As he grows older, he realizes that the war has forever changed him and those around him. Despite the hardships, the family remains resilient and ultimately finds hope in the aftermath of tragedy.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates for the third time this year, following a two-day meeting that ends on Wednesday.
The move, which would mark the third interest rate increase this year, is expected to be announced later in the day.
The rate hike is seen as a sign of a strong US economy, with low unemployment and steady economic growth.
However, some experts have warned that rising interest rates could lead to a slowdown in housing sales and construction, which could eventually dampen economic growth.
Analysts also say that the Fed's tightening of monetary policy could lead to higher borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, which could slow down spending and investment.
Despite these concerns, most economists expect the Fed to continue to gradually raise interest rates over the next few years as the economy continues to grow.

A Pan-Europan group known as Euronext is set to pursue a takeover of the London Stock Exchange (LSE), according to recent reports. Last week, the LSE declined a proposed acquisition by Germany's Deutsche Boerse, which offered 530 pence per share, valuing the exchange at approximately £1.35 billion. The LSE, which saw its stock increase by 25%, criticized the offer as undervaluing the company. Euronext, which emerged from the merger of exchanges in Brussels, Paris, and Amsterdam, is reportedly collaborating with three investment banks on a potential takeover offer. The LSE, Europe's largest stock market, holds significant value, with a total capitalization of £1.4 trillion.

Euronext already has a presence in London due to its 2001 acquisition of the London-based options and futures exchange, Liffe. Trading on the LSE is cleared through Clearnet, which Euronext owns a quarter of. Euronext, which also operates an exchange in Lisbon, recently appointed UBS and ABN Amro as additional advisors and is working with Morgan Stanley. Although the Deutsche Boerse bid was rejected, Werner Seifert, the CEO of the Frankfurt-based exchange, may present a revised proposal. The two exchanges have historically sought to merge but failed in 2000. In response to the LSE's rejection, Deutsche Boerse stated it believed its offer could provide benefits and expressed hope for a cash bid.

The LSE emphasized that the bid was undervalued and warned that there was no guarantee of success. However, it remains open to further discussions. Meanwhile, German publication Der Spiegel noted that part of Seifert's negotiations with the LSE focused on the location of the future board of a merged exchange. Seifert suggested the merged entity would operate from London, but the mayor of Frankfurt raised concerns that this could impact German employment. Analysts believe this situation presents a complex challenge.

I'm amazed by the streets of Chicago  
when winter clings to them with snow  
as if to pardon the city's errors  
and offer it a fresh, white, and clean surface—  
its limbs, the branches on all the trees  
tugging at the air that flows in from the lake.  
I've never lived near the lake's rhythm  
until I walked down the side of Chicago  
breathe in through the streets and out through the trees  
taking in the chill of the wet, numb snow.  
It makes my thoughts drift into believing it's clean  
as if to personally forgive my own errors.  
"But what have you done to forgive your mistakes?"  
Did I ask this? Or is that the lake's voice?  
Sometimes, it doesn't look clean, worn down by Chicago's presence.  
It scratches at the sky, asking for more snow  
to stick and freeze the tree trunks.  
If I were a branch unable to make a mistake,  
I'd reach out to the sky as it dispenses the snow  
and stretch my roots deep until they taste the lake.  
But I wouldn't bow to Chicago's relentless push  
to keep me from being clean.  
What does it mean to strive for cleanliness?  
I don't grasp the quiet of the trees  
under attack by Chicago's vastness  
as if to honor the city's flaws  
that shimmer like stars on the lake before freezing.  
Ah! How long has snow been here?  
How can something so ancient still feel so clean  
and move through the wind that sweeps in from the lake?  
Is it the gentle pressure from spiky branches  
that trust there'll be no more mistakes  
which makes these the sole pure thing in Chicago?  
Here comes the snow that finds the trees.  
Am I now clean? Where are my mistakes?  
Chicago belongs where it once lay with the lake.

There is a cemetery close to the White House where the Unknown Soldier rests, with flowers placed there by the tears of mothers. I visited this place not too long ago, bringing roses for the brave, and then I heard a voice speak from the grave: "I am the Unknown Soldier, the spirit voice began. 'And I think I have the right to ask some questions man to man.' 'Are my comrades cared for? Was their victory so sweet? Is that big reward you gave by selling pencils on the street? Did they truly win the freedom they fought for? Do you still respect that Croix de Guerre above that empty sleeve? Does a gold star in the window mean anything now? I wonder how my old girl feels when she hears a bugle call. 'And that baby who sang Hello, Central, give me no man can they replace her daddy with a military band?' 'I wonder if the profiteers have satisfied their greed? I wonder if a soldier's mother ever needs anything? 'I wonder if the kings, who planned it all, are really satisfied? They played their game of checkers and eleven million died. 'I am the Unknown Soldier, and maybe I died in vain, but if I were alive and my country called, I'd do it all over again.'"

Dark clouds assemble, a heavy cloak,
Promise of relief, thirst to revoke.
The air grows humid, pregnant with tears,
But nature’s sorrow, alas, disappears.

The grayish canvas, once thick and dire,
Scatters away, warming sun conspires.
Misled by whispers of skies torn apart,
I sought solace, but rain would not impart.

Soaked within, the earth pants for release,
A tango with showers, a fleeting tease.
Petrichor's fragrance, a nostalgic yearn,
Left unfulfilled, as the clouds adjourn.

The heavens toy, like a capricious friend,
A dance uncompleted, storms comprehend.
Whispers of thunder rumble in echos,
Only to fade, nature's wrath bestows.

Desire for droplets, my soul does seek,
To kiss my face, while sorrows I wreak.
But the sun prevails, sky painted in gold,
As aspirations of rainfall dissolve.

The barren ground aches for heaven's remorse,
Its thirst unquenched, a relentless force.

I was given an option by my roommate: he would either a) pay the bills and have the place to himself or b) I could stay and we would split everything. Being a recent graduate, I didn’t have much choice but to stay and split or live in my car. I picked door B.

I figured I could save money and eventually buy a house. I was already spending half of what I made on rent, but I made the best of a bad situation by splitting the rent. I was “stuck” spending almost as much as I did when it was just me and my roommate, which made saving difficult, but I managed. 

I lived with this guy for 3 years. The living situation got progressively worse as time went on. Picking teeth out of the bathroom sink, roommates bringing dates or new “best friends” home for the weekend, etc. After 3 years, my patience was wearing thin. I had already started looking for a new living arrangement when COVID-19 hit. Here I am, living in my car. 

I’m fortunate enough to live in Southern California, so the weather allows me to live in my car most of the year. It’s not ideal, and as a 6’4” male, it’s quite cramped, but it beats paying rent. I’ve basically been forced into an extreme form of saving money. I’ve got a freshwater shower at my gym, so showering is cost-effective and easy. I use the laundry mats, so laundry is cheap. I do all my “home” cooking in my car with a single burner induction cooktop. 

I’m able to save almost 70% of my monthly income, allowing me to place a generous offer on a house. If it weren’t for this unexpected turn of events, I would probably still be splitting rent, and not able to buy a house for another 1–2 years, if not more. It can be done, but it requires a disciplined lifestyle that not many people are willing to adopt. After experiencing this “lifestyle”, I don’t think I could go back to paying rent without putting most of my paycheck towards savings.

Recent semi-supervised instance segmentation methods mostly focus on modeling spectral or spatial relationships between pixels in different images through consistency and/or similarity learning. These methods either treat all pixels within an object as a unit or assign labels independently at each pixel without considering their spatial coherence, which limits their ability to capture complex object structures. In this paper, we propose a Mask-guided Sample Selection (MSS) approach for training a semi-supervised pixel-level classifier. Given a pixel of interest, our method selects its class-consistent neighboring pixels as semantic contextual samples through a learned mask. We pose the learning of the mask as a binary classification problem, where the mask is the decision boundary between the foreground (object) and background (rest of the image). Specifically, given an initial guess of the mask, we minimize the cross-entropy loss by iteratively refining the mask through gradient descent. We optimize the mask in a bottom-up fashion, starting from the pixels with the highest response and traversing the areas with the most uncertain labels. We evaluate MSS on four semi-supervised segmentation benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

Ron Williamson has returned to his hometown of Ada, Oklahoma after multiple failed attempts to play for various minor league baseball teams, including the Fort Lauderdale Yankees and two farm teams owned by the Oakland A's. An elbow injury inhibited his chances to progress. His big dreams were not enough to overcome the odds (less than 10 percent) of making it to a big league game. His failures lead to, or aggravate, his depression and problem drinking. Early in the morning of December 8, 1982, the body of Debra Sue Carter, a 21-year-old cocktail waitress, was found in the bedroom of her garage apartment in Ada. She had been beaten, raped and suffocated. After five years of false starts and shoddy police work by the Ada police department, Williamson—along with his "drinking buddy", Dennis Fritz--were charged, tried and convicted of the rape and murder charges in 1988. Williamson was sentenced to death. Fritz was given a life sentence. Fritz's wife had been murdered seven years earlier and he was raising their only daughter when he was arrested. Grisham's book describes the aggressive and misguided mission of the Ada police department and Pontotoc County District Attorney Bill Peterson to solve the mystery of Carter's murder. The police and prosecutor used forced "dream" confessions, unreliable witnesses, and flimsy evidence to convict Williamson and Fritz. Since a death penalty conviction automatically sets in motion a series of appeals, the Innocence Project aided Williamson's attorney, Mark Barrett, in exposing several glaring holes in the prosecution's case and the credibility of the prosecution's witnesses. Frank H. Seay, a U.S. District Court judge, ordered a retrial. After suffering through a conviction and eleven years on death row, Williamson and Fritz were exonerated by DNA evidence and released on April 15, 1999. Williamson was the 78th inmate released from death row since 1973. Williamson suffered deep and irreversible psychological damage during his incarceration and eventual stay on death row. For example, on September 22, 1994, he was five days away from being executed when his sentence was stayed by the court, following the filing of a habeas corpus petition. He was intermittently treated for manic depression, personality disorders, alcoholism and mild schizophrenia. It was later proven that he was indeed mentally ill and therefore was unfit to have been tried or sentenced to death in the first place. The State of Oklahoma, the city of Ada, and Pontotoc County officials never admitted any errors and threatened to re-arrest him. Another criminal from Ada, Glen Gore, was eventually convicted of the original crime on June 24, 2003. He was sentenced to death He was convicted at a second trial on June 21, 2006 and sentenced by Judge Landrith to life in prison without parole. This was required by law due to a jury deadlock on sentencing. Williamson and Fritz sued and won a settlement for wrongful conviction of $500,000 in 2003 from the City of Ada, and an out-of-court settlement with the State of Oklahoma for an undisclosed amount. By 2004, Williamson was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver and died on December 4, 2004 in a Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, nursing home. Fritz returned to Kansas City, where he lives with his daughter, Elizabeth . In 2006, Fritz published his own account of being wrongly convicted in his book titled Journey toward Justice. The book includes accounts (as subplots) of the false conviction, trial and sentencing of Tommy Ward and Karl Fontenot in the abduction, rape, and purported murder of Denice Haraway, as well as the false conviction of Greg Wilhoit in the rape and murder of his estranged wife, Kathy. At one time, all the men were incarcerated in the same death row. About two decades before Grisham's book, Ward and Fontenot's wrongful convictions were detailed in a book published in 1987 called The Dreams of Ada by Robert Mayer.

Adapromine is an antiviral drug of the adamantane group related to amantadine (1-aminoadamantane), rimantadine (1-(1-aminoethyl)adamantane), and memantine (1-amino-3,5-dimethyladamantane) that is marketed in Russia for the treatment and prevention of influenza. It is an alkyl analogue of rimantadine and is similar to rimantadine in its antiviral activity but possesses a broader spectrum of action, being effective against influenza viruses of both type A and B. Strains of type A influenza virus with resistance to adapromine and rimantadine and the related drug deitiforine were encountered in Mongolia and the Soviet Union in the 1980s. Electroencephalography (EEG) studies of animals suggest that adapromine and related adamantanes including amantadine, bromantane (1-amino-2-bromophenyladamantane), and memantine have psychostimulant-like and possibly antidepressant-like effects, and that these effects may be mediated via catecholaminergic processes. These psychostimulant effects differ qualitatively from those of conventional psychostimulants like amphetamine however, and the adamantane derivatives have been described contrarily as "adaptogens" and as "actoprotectors".

for yellow freestone peaches, downriver
wakened from a dream of work, Zug Island danced
into the bright day glad to be alive.
Full-figured women in their negligees
streamed into the streets from the dark doorways
to demand in Polish or Armenian
the ripened offerings of this new world.
Josef Prisckulnick out of Dubrovitsa
to Detroit by way of Ellis Island
raised himself regally to his full height
of five feet two and transacted until
the fruit was gone into those eager hands.
Thus would there be a letter sent across
an ocean and a continent, and thus
would Sadie waken to the news of wealth
without limit in the bright and distant land,
and thus bags were packed and she set sail
for America. Some of this is true.
The women were gaunt. All day the kids dug
in the back lots searching for anything.
The place was Russia with another name.
Joe was five feet two. Dubrovitsa burned
to gray ashes the west wind carried off,
then Rovno went, then the Dnieper turned to dust.
We sat around the table telling lies
while the late light filled an empty glass.
Bread, onions, the smell of burning butter,
small white potatoes we shared with no one
because the hour was wrong, the guest was late,
and this was Michigan in 1928.

Auroroborealia is a small bodied euichthyosaurian ichthyosaur discovered on the New Siberian Islands in the Russian Arctic. The animal was likely similar in size to Hudsonelpidia, around 1 to 1.5 meters in length. Although the fragmentary nature doesn't allow to determine its exact ontogenetic state, other remains from the area suggest that it was simply a small bodied taxon. It contains a single species, Auroroborealia incognita. Discovery and naming
The fossils of Auroroborealia were discovered by a joint expedition of the Geological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Trofimuk Institute of Petroleum Geology and Geophysics, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, during excavations in 2006 and 2009. These expeditions yielded a variety of ichthyosaurian remains from six stratigraphic levels ranging from the lower Carnian to middle Norian. Although most specimens were fragmentary, Zverkov et al. (2021) could nevertheless differentiate between a host of different ichthyosaurs. One fossil in particular, specimen ZIN PH 5/250, included cranial remains as well as anterior presacral vertebrae with associated neural arches and ribs. A bone fragment associated with the pectoral girdle is also part of this specimen. Based on this material Zverkov  et al. erected the species Aurororborealia incognita, while also describing a series of referred specimens (which however did not factor into the diagnosis of the genus).

Semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentations have been addressed using
different and specialized frameworks despite their underlying connections. This
paper presents a unified, simple, and effective framework for these essentially
similar tasks. The framework, named K-Net, segments both instances and semantic
categories consistently by a group of learnable kernels, where each kernel is
responsible for generating a mask for either a potential instance or a stuff
class. To remedy the difficulties of distinguishing various instances, we
propose a kernel update strategy that enables each kernel dynamic and
conditional on its meaningful group in the input image. K-Net can be trained in
an end-to-end manner with bipartite matching, and its training and inference
are naturally NMS-free and box-free. Without bells and whistles, K-Net
surpasses all previous state-of-the-art single-model results of panoptic
segmentation on MS COCO and semantic segmentation on ADE20K with 52.1% PQ and
54.3% mIoU, respectively. Its instance segmentation performance is also on par
with Cascade Mask R-CNNon MS COCO with 60%-90% faster inference speeds. Code
and models will be released at https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection.

A fallen angel longed for the earthly realm, reclining in the gleaming streets; his halo was crooked, and his lute lay silent at his feet. Thus, the Master intervened, granting him leave to descend to Earth for a lunar duration. He discarded his divine attire, barely pausing to adjust it, and bid farewell to Peter, who waited at the golden gate. The celestial musicians sang a tender goodbye, and the devils gazed upward as they trudged past the blazing flags of Hell. Never had an angel been seen—eyes of ethereal blue, features that defied Apollo, hair like gold; the women worshipped him; his lips mirrored Cupid’s curve. Yet he refused to touch them, and so they deemed him slow. Finally, a woman emerged, radiant and exquisite, who asked him, “Do you love me?” He replied, “Yes.” She urged him to embrace her, kiss her, and hold her, but he recoiled, declaring it inappropriate. She laughed at his hesitation, gently seducing him with her words: “You, who are truly man among men, speak as a child. We have surpassed the old rules; we have broken free from the rigid Puritan traditions of right and wrong.” The Master felt sorrow for his angel, calling him once more. Oh, how wondrous the woman was, and how trials were upon the angel! Deep within his torment, the Devil sang, echoing the strain of his own lament: “The ancient, outworn, Puritanic traditions of Right and Wrong.”

The effectiveness of advanced image segmentation techniques depends significantly on high-quality annotated datasets, which are often difficult to obtain, especially in medical contexts. To address this issue, this research introduces a weakly supervised image segmentation approach utilizing a deep geodesic prior. We believe that incorporating this prior can mitigate the negative impacts of weak labels on segmentation precision. The developed algorithm relies on prior knowledge derived from an auto-encoder, which learns to transform geometric maps into binary representations of objects. This information is integrated as an additional component in the segmenter's loss function. To demonstrate the viability of our approach, we tested it on segmentation tasks involving cardiac structures with clean and two types of noisy labels (L1, L2). Experimental results indicated that the proposed method improved the performance of standard deep learning-based segmentation by 4.4%, 4.6% (L1), and 6.3% (L2) in terms of dice scores. Additionally, the method demonstrated greater resilience to high-level noise owing to its incorporation of shape priors.

"The Double Life of Véronique" is a breathtaking and enigmatic film that weaves a complex narrative, blurring the lines between reality and imagination. Directed by Krzysztof Kieślowski, the film explores themes of identity, fate, and the interconnectedness of human lives.

The film centers around two women, Weronika in Poland and Véronique in France, who share an uncanny resemblance and a mysterious connection. We follow their parallel lives as they navigate personal struggles, passions, and opportunities. Kieślowski's masterful storytelling beautifully captures the intimacy and intricacies of their existence.

The cinematography is stunning and poetic, with every shot meticulously framed and lit. The use of colors and symbolism adds another layer of depth to the film, enhancing the overall visual experience. Zbigniew Preisner's hauntingly beautiful score perfectly complements the ethereal atmosphere, immersing the audience in the emotional journey of the characters.

The performances by Irène Jacob in the dual roles of Weronika and Véronique are mesmerizing. She effortlessly embodies each character, imbuing them with vulnerability, grace, and a sense of mystery. Jacob's subtle and nuanced acting adds to the enigmatic nature of the film, leaving the viewer captivated and intrigued.

"The Double Life of Véronique" is not a film that can be easily classified or dissected. Its open-ended narrative invites interpretation and reflection, and it skillfully challenges the audience's perception of reality. Kieślowski's ability to evoke emotion through visual storytelling is nothing short of genius, and this film is a testament to his talent.

This cinematic masterpiece offers a unique and thought-provoking viewing experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. It is a film that requires multiple viewings to fully appreciate its depth and nuances. "The Double Life of Véronique" is a true work of art, an exploration of the human condition that transcends boundaries and leaves a lasting impact.

The story concerns Bernice, a wealthy girl from Eau Claire, Wisconsin, who goes to visit her cousin Marjorie for the month of August. Marjorie feels that Bernice is a drag on her social life, and none of the boys want to dance with Bernice. Bernice overhears a conversation between Marjorie and Marjorie's mother where the younger girl complains that Bernice is socially hopeless. The next day, Bernice threatens to leave town, but when Marjorie is unfazed, Bernice relents and agrees to let Marjorie turn her into a society girl. Marjorie teaches Bernice how to hold interesting conversations, how to flirt with even unattractive or uninteresting boys to make herself seem more desirable, and how to dance. Bernice's best line is teasing the boys with the idea that she will soon bob her hair and they will get to watch. The new Bernice is a big hit with the boys in town with her new attitude, especially with Warren, a boy Marjorie keeps around as her own but neglects. When it becomes clear that Warren has shifted his interest from Marjorie to Bernice, Marjorie sets about humiliating Bernice, tricking her into going through with bobbing her hair. When Bernice comes out of the barbershop with the new hairdo, her hair is flat and strange. The boys suddenly lose interest in her, and Bernice realizes she's been tricked. Marjorie's mother points out that Bernice's haircut (which at the time was only seen on "liberated" women) would cause a scandal at an upcoming party held in her and Marjorie's honor. Bernice, deciding it would be best to leave the town before the party the next day, packs her trunk in the middle of the night and decides to leave on a train at 1 a.m. Before she goes, she sneaks into Marjorie's room and cuts off her cousin's two braids, taking them with her on her run to the station and throwing them onto Warren's front porch.

Organisers of the third Bangkok International Film Festival have been determined to carry on with this year's event despite the ravages of the Asian tsunami disaster.
The festivities have been scaled down, red carpets have been mothballed and profits from ticket sales are being donated to the tsunami relief fund. Apart from this, however, the festival has continued as originally planned. "When the disaster happened, we naturally asked ourselves if we should cancel," said the festival's executive director, Craig Prater. "The decision was made that we would continue, but that the focus would change.
"Our premieres became fundraisers, the opening night was visibly toned down and 10% of every ticket sold goes to the disaster fund," he continued. "But we feel like we've turned a page. We've acknowledged our position, and now it's business as usual."
Mr Prater's sentiments were echoed by Christine Rush, director of the festival's sister event, the Bangkok Film Market. "We have been careful to be respectful of the Thai nation's recovery from this terrible disaster," she said.
"However, the nation's recovery very much depends upon it continuing its economic life. "We are encouraging attendees to keep the victims in mind and aggressively support the aid organisations helping out," she added. Given the conspicuously low audience figures, that support may be more symbolic than significant. However, poor ticket sales have less to do with any fallout from the disaster and more to do with administrative and promotional difficulties.
The eclectic programme contains a wide range of titles, including such Oscar hopefuls as Ray Charles biopic Ray and Mike Leigh's abortion drama Vera Drake. That said, the absence of Thai subtitles on most film prints might have proved offputting to local cinemagoers.
On a more positive note, the celebrity guests attending the event have generated huge media interest in this busy capital city. Problems securing air transport, the clash with last Sunday's Golden Globes ceremony in Los Angeles and other factors have forced some big names to cancel.
But the festival has still attracted such Hollywood directors as Oliver Stone and Joel Schumacher, alongside such screen stars as Michael Douglas, Jeremy Irons and Jean-Claude Van Damme. Irons, whose film Being Julia is in competition for the festival's Golden Kinnaree awards, said he had wondered whether he should attend after December's catastrophe. "I questioned whether I should come when such a tragedy had happened," the British actor said. "I thought it might be in rather bad taste. But then I spoke to the organisers and I was encouraged to let life go on. "Now I've come here I'm very glad. What impresses me about Thai culture is they get over these things far quicker than we do in the West," he continued. "Basically I was invited here by Thailand. If they still want you to come, you should."
Now in its third year, Bangkok is a relatively recent addition to the hectic film festival calendar. And while it has yet to attain the stature of more established events held in Hong Kong, Tokyo and Pusan in South Korea, Mr Prater predicts it will soon become their equal. "It's grown awfully fast in three years - maybe too fast," he concedes. "We've had some bumps in the road, but that's only because the festival is still a baby. "I have no doubt in my mind that in five years, this will be the top Asian film festival in the world." The Golden Kinnarees will be awarded on Friday. The festival itself runs until 24 January.

Understanding and optimizing item timings with Tinker can dramatically improve your gameplay. Here are some tips you can utilize:

1. **Prioritize Boots of Travel (BoT):** Your first priority should always be saving for Boots of Travel. This item is crucial to Tinker's playstyle as it allows you to travel around the map, pushing lanes, and teleporting back to your base when needed.

2. **Farming Patterns:** Tinker is all about farming efficiently. Using March of the Machines, you can continually clear out waves of creeps. When farming the jungle, move strategically between camps to use March of the Machines to best effect.

3. **Stacking Neutral Creeps:** While farming waves with March, try to stack neutral camps whenever possible, this will allow for maximizing your gold and experience gain.

4. **Bottle and Soul Ring:** These two items should be your next priority after BoTs. They give you the ability to stay on the map longer due to sustainability in health and mana.

5. **Blink Dagger Timing:** Blink Dagger is another high priority item. Try to get it before the 20-minute mark. It offers a great deal of mobility and can save you from many sticky situations.

6. **Scythe of Vyse and Dagon:** These are your luxury items. The former is great for control and adding an extra layer of disable in team fights, whereas the latter will let you burst down enemies quickly. Their timings largely depend on how well you have farmed.

Remember that both your individual skill level and the state of your specific game can affect this schedule. Being adaptable is crucial in Dota 2, so be prepared to adjust your playstyle and item build based on the needs of your team and the nature of the enemy team. In general, ensure you maximize farming, manage your mana well and aim for minimum deaths. Good luck!

1/3 cup ranch dressing  
1 teaspoon hot chile paste (such as sambal oelek)  
4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1 inch pieces  
24 (1-inch) pieces red onion  
12 slices thick cut bacon  
salt and black pepper to taste  
12 (6 inch) bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 2 hours  

Whisk together ranch dressing and hot chile paste in a large bowl. Mix in chicken pieces and toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 to 3 hours. Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove chicken from the bag and transfer to a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Pat chicken pieces dry with more paper towels. Thread a piece of onion about 1 1/2 inches down the skewer. Thread the end portion of one strip of bacon onto skewer so the rest of the strip is hanging down. Skewer on a piece of chicken; thread on the next portion of the bacon. Turn the skewer so that the long end of the bacon is again hanging down. Repeat this process of skewering and turning until the entire strip of bacon is threaded, using 4 to 5 chicken pieces. Thread a second piece of onion onto the end of the skewer. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for all twelve skewers. Season chicken skewers with salt and pepper as desired. Cook the skewers on the preheated grill, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until nicely browned on all sides and the meat is no longer pink in the center, 12 to 16 minutes total per skewer. Serve with ranch dressing as a dipping sauce.
