Tina von Lambert, wife of psychiatrist Otto von Lambert, has fled to an unnamed North African country (referred to as M.), where she is found raped and murdered in the [desert]. Otto hires F., a filmmaker, to travel to M. and reconstruct his wife's murder. The Chief of Police appears to be cooperative, however, after a police-escorted visit to the Al-Hakim ruins where the body was found, F.'s cameraman reveals that his footage has been replaced. The police then allow F. to question a number of foreign agents being held and tortured at the police ministry, all of whom tell her the same vague, inconclusive story, none confessing to the crime. Later, F. is taken to observe the execution of a Scandinavian spy in the central courtyard of the police compound; the Chief of Police claims that the spy has confessed to the crime and that the case is solved. They are shown the video of their investigation, which includes none of their footage; instead it has been turned into a propaganda film featuring the police. In despair, F. leaves her crew and walks alone through the marketplace, where she comes across the distinctive red fur coat she knows belonged to Tina von Lambert. She purchases the coat and wears it back to her hotel. At the hotel F.'s cameraman tells her that his footage has again been taken, this time that of the execution, and that aeroplane tickets out of the country have been booked for them for early the following morning. In her room, F. finds the Head of the Secret Service, who congratulates her on her work and explains that he will use her confiscated footage to expose the corruption, weakness, and incompetence of the Chief of Police, who is planning a coup against the state government. The Head of the Secret Service asks that she continue her investigation under his protection and without the knowledge of the Chief of Police. He offers a new crew, and provides a body double, complete with a red fur coat, to travel home with the old crew in F.'s place. F. is relocated to a derelict hotel, inhabited by a lone, aged maid. Björn Olsen, the cameraman hired by the secret service to assist F., arrives at the hotel and mistakes her for Jytte Sørensen, a Danish journalist; when he realizes his mistake, for F. speaks no Danish, he flees in a panic. Later, the Head of the Secret Police shows F. a gossip magazine with an article titled "Return from the Dead", featuring a photograph of Tina von Lambert reunited with her husband; he explains to her that the murdered woman was in fact Sörensen, a friend of Tina's, to whom Tina had given her red fur coat and passport. The reason for the murder, however, remains a mystery. Determined to find the truth, F. leaves the hotel and heads toward the desert. On the way she finds Olsen's dead body next to his exploded Volkswagen van, and while she examines the disaster she meets the cameraman Polypheme, who is filming her. Polypheme tells F. that he has video footage of Sørensen, who was on the trail of a secret before her death, and offers to show it to F. if she allows him to make a film portrait of her. Despite his dishevelled appearance and apparent drunkenness, she agrees. Polypheme takes F out in to the desert in his Land Rover, and eventually they arrive at a secret subterranean compound. The compound is a vast underground labyrinth, obviously built at great expense, though it appears to be uninhabited by anyone other than Polypheme. F. is taken to a grotesque room and left alone, and there, to her horror, she discovers a series of still frames of Olsen's death. Later in the evening she leaves her room and explores the compound, trying to track down the source of a mysterious hammering sound, which she traces to a locked door with a key in the keyhole. Out of fear she does not go inside. She finds the Land Rover and contemplates fleeing, but again is dissuaded by fear. Unable to locate her original quarters, she finds an empty room and falls asleep. In the morning, F. is found by Polypheme, now clean and sober, and over breakfast he explains the country's political situation. The primary source of revenue for the country is a meaningless war with a neighbouring country over the empty, largely uninhabited desert in which the compound is located. The already ten-year-long war is continued to serve as a testing ground for the military products of weapons-exporting nations, from tanks to intercontinental ballistic missiles. The compound was built to measure the effects of the weapons; at one time it was staffed by human observers, many of whom were eventually replaced by observational machines. Eventually a satellite was put in orbit directly above the compound, followed by a second satellite to observe the first. The 15th Massachusetts Battery (or 15th Battery Massachusetts Light Artillery) was an artillery battery that served in the Union Army during the American Civil War. The unit was organized partly at Camp Chase in Lowell, Massachusetts and partly at Fort Warren during the winter of 1862-1863. The majority of its members were mustered into federal service on February 17, 1863. It was assigned to the Department of the Gulf commanded by Major General Nathaniel P. Banks and departed Massachusetts by steamship on March 9. During its term, the unit suffered from a large number of desertions and gained an unfortunate reputation despite the service of its many loyal members. The unit arrived in New Orleans on April 9, 1863. Before being issued guns, they made a brief expedition on foot to Brashear City, Louisiana but soon returned to New Orleans. They were assigned to garrison two small forts just outside New Orleans, each armed with four 32-pounder guns mounted in barbettes. One of these was located at Bayou St. John and the other at Gentilly. They remained posted there from June 3 until December 29.

Robert Lee Hill (born June 8, 1892, died May 11, 1963) was an African American sharecropper from the Arkansas Delta and a political activist who founded the Progressive Farmers and Household Union of America after World War I. Based in Arkansas, this group aimed to assist sharecroppers and tenant farmers in securing more favorable financial agreements with white landowners. Hill participated in an organizing session for Black farmers near Elaine, Arkansas, on September 30, 1919. When two white deputies and a Black trustee arrived to disturb the meeting, gunfire ensued. The white community responded with severe violence, resulting in the Elaine massacre, during which five whites and approximately 100–237 blacks were killed. The government deployed federal troops to suppress the riots. Hill fled to Kansas, where he was subsequently arrested. The NAACP supported him by working with both state and federal officials. Governor Henry Justin Allen denied an extradition request from Arkansas, asserting that he did not believe Hill would be safe in Arkansas prisons or receive a fair trial. Later, federal charges were dismissed, and Hill was freed from prison in October 1920.

This paper introduces an efficient semidefinite programming (SDP) approach for worst-case linear discriminant analysis (WLDA). Unlike traditional linear discriminant analysis (LDA), WLDA addresses the dimensionality reduction issue from a worst-case perspective, making it generally more robust for classification. However, the original WLDA problem is non-convex and challenging to optimize. To address this, we transform the WLDA optimization problem into a series of semidefinite feasibility problems. By employing a novel scalable optimization technique combining quasi-Newton methods and eigen-decomposition, we enhance the efficiency of solving these feasibility problems. The proposed method is significantly faster than conventional interior-point-based SDP solvers.

Experiments across various classification tasks show that our approach outperforms standard LDA. Furthermore, our method is substantially quicker and more scalable compared to standard interior-point-based WLDA. The computational complexity of an SDP with $ m $ constraints and $ d \times d $ matrices is reduced from $ \mathcal{O}(m^3 + md^3 + m^2d^2) $ to $ \mathcal{O}(d^3) $ (where $ m > d $ in our case).

The development of a sensitive and efficient neutron detection system is crucial in various scientific applications, particularly in studying ultra-cold neutrons (UCNs). In this study, we present an innovative approach to UCN detection using multi-layer surfaces. The proposed method involves utilizing multiple layers with different materials that have high thermal conductivity but low neutron absorption cross sections. By analyzing the temperature fluctuations across these layers due to the scattering of UCNs, we can effectively detect their presence without significantly absorbing them. We demonstrate through simulations that our multilevel surface detector offers improved sensitivity compared to conventional methods while maintaining a higher efficiency in detecting UCNs. This novel technique has significant potential in enhancing the capabilities of existing UCN experiments and enabling new research avenues in the field of ultracold neutron science.

Co-occurrent visual pattern makes aggregating contextual information a common
paradigm to enhance the pixel representation for semantic image segmentation.
The existing approaches focus on modeling the context from the perspective of
the whole image, i.e., aggregating the image-level contextual information.
Despite impressive, these methods weaken the significance of the pixel
representations of the same category, i.e., the semantic-level contextual
information. To address this, this paper proposes to augment the pixel
representations by aggregating the image-level and semantic-level contextual
information, respectively. First, an image-level context module is designed to
capture the contextual information for each pixel in the whole image. Second,
we aggregate the representations of the same category for each pixel where the
category regions are learned under the supervision of the ground-truth
segmentation. Third, we compute the similarities between each pixel
representation and the image-level contextual information, the semantic-level
contextual information, respectively. At last, a pixel representation is
augmented by weighted aggregating both the image-level contextual information
and the semantic-level contextual information with the similarities as the
weights. Integrating the image-level and semantic-level context allows this
paper to report state-of-the-art accuracy on four benchmarks, i.e., ADE20K,
LIP, COCOStuff and Cityscapes.

In a groundbreaking achievement, scientists have successfully taught a humanoid robot how to run. The robot, named "Atlas," has been able to learn and perform a range of movements, including jogging and sprinting, without any prior programming or human intervention.

The team behind the project, led by researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, used a machine learning algorithm called reinforcement learning to teach Atlas how to run. Reinforcement learning allows robots to learn through trial and error, receiving feedback in the form of rewards or penalties for their actions.

In the case of Atlas, the robot was tasked with moving forward as quickly as possible while maintaining its balance. The team provided Atlas with a reward signal that encouraged it to move faster, but also penalized it when it fell or deviated from a stable gait. Over time, the robot learned to adjust its movements to maximize its speed and stability, eventually developing a running motion that is remarkably similar to that of a human.

"This is a major milestone in robotics," said Dr. Pieter Abbeel, one of the lead researchers on the project. "For the first time, we've been able to teach a humanoid robot how to run without explicitly programming it. This opens up new possibilities for robots to learn complex tasks and adapt to changing environments."

The ability for robots to learn and adapt is particularly important in emergency situations, where pre-programmed instructions may not be sufficient. For example, during a natural disaster, a search and rescue robot could use its ability to learn and adapt to navigate unfamiliar terrain and locate survivors.

While Atlas still has some way to go before it can match the agility and endurance of a human runner, this breakthrough represents a significant step towards creating more advanced and capable robots. As the field of artificial intelligence continues to evolve, we can expect to see even more impressive feats of robotic mobility and dexterity in the years ahead.

The UK's Minister for Immigration, David Milburn, has spoken out in defense of the government's controversial new poster campaign aimed at reducing immigration.

The campaign, which features billboards with slogans such as "Is life here really worth living?", has been criticized by opposition parties and human rights groups who claim it is designed to create a negative image of immigrants and stir up anti-foreigner sentiment.

But speaking on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, Mr. Milburn insisted that the posters were necessary to address the issue of illegal immigration and to promote the benefits of returning home for those who have overstayed their visas.

"We are simply trying to encourage people who are here illegally to return home voluntarily," he said. "It's not about demonizing immigrants or suggesting they are not welcome. We want to make sure we have a fair and controlled system that works for everyone."

However, critics argue that the language used in the posters is divisive and could lead to increased discrimination against foreign nationals. Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper described the campaign as "dog whistle politics" and accused the government of using coded messages to appeal to voters' fears.

Human rights organization Amnesty International has also condemned the campaign, calling it a "shameful attempt to scapegoat migrants" and warning that it could contribute to a climate of hostility towards vulnerable communities.

Despite these concerns, Mr. Milburn maintained that the campaign was an important tool in tackling illegal immigration and would continue to run until further notice. He added that the government was committed to creating a fair and balanced approach to immigration policy, but that this required taking tough action against those who flouted the rules.

Alexey Andreyevich Rodin (Russian: Алексе́й Андре́евич Ро́дин; 14 March [O.S. 2 March] 1840 – 19 November [O.S. 7 November] 1917) was a Russian mathematician who made significant contributions to the fields of geometry and trigonometry. He is best known for his work on the theory of triangles, particularly for his proof of the Pythagorean theorem.

Born in Moscow, Russia, Rodin attended the Moscow State University, where he studied mathematics under the tutelage of Dmitri Mendeleev. After graduating from the university in 1861, he worked as a teacher and later as a professor at the same institution. In 1871, he became a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Rodin's most notable work, "The Foundations of Geometry" was published in 1902 and became a widely used textbook on geometry in Russia. In addition to his work on the Pythagorean theorem, he also made significant contributions to the development of trigonometry, including the creation of a new table of trigonometric functions.

Rodin was awarded the Imperial Russian Academy of Sciences' Gold Medal for his contributions to mathematics. He died in Moscow in 1917 at the age of 77.

Roasted Chiles and Corn Bread Recipe:

Ingredients: 
-1 cup all-purpose flour
-3 tablespoons granulated sugar
-2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
-1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
-2 large eggs, beaten
-1 cup milk
-1/2 cup melted butter or vegetable oil
-2 cups roasted red chilies, peeled, seeded and diced
-1 cup corn kernels
-1/4 cup chopped green onions 
-1/4 cup shredded cheese (cheddar or cotija work great)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit (190C). Grease an 8x8 inch baking square with cooking spray or butter. You can also line the bottom of the pan with parchment paper for easy removal.

2. In a medium bowl, mix together the dry ingredients: flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cayenne pepper. Set aside.

3. In another bowl, whisk together wet ingredients: beaten eggs, milk and melted butter or oil. Add in the mixture from step two and stir until well combined. Be careful not to overmix. The batter should be lumpy.

4. Fold in the roasted chilies, corn kernels, green onions, and shredded cheese into the wet mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.

5. Pour the batter into prepared pan and smooth out top with a spatula. Bake for about 35 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean (it might have some moisture since it’s a moist bread but it shouldn’t be raw). Allow cornbread to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

Enjoy this delicious and healthy roasted chile cornbread!

Going into the theater, I was under the impression that this was a silly James Franco and Seth Rogen movie that made fun of The Room, a legendary bad movie. That's not what the Disaster Artist is at all. Instead, it celebrates The Room. It celebrates Tommy Wiseau, Greg Sestero, their passion, and their pursuit of a dream.

Sure, The Disaster Artist comments on how The Room bombed terribly; it had to acknowledge this. It comments on the utter lack of acting talent that Tommy and Greg possessed; it had to acknowledge this too. But it handles these details with such delicacy and care that I never felt that it was putting down the characters. Actually, it seemed that the film admired them. Even when the world told them to quit, they never gave up on themselves or each other. The message is surprisingly inspiring.

The movie becomes something more than mere mockery because of the way it handles the relationship between Tommy and Greg with such care and affection. The two genuinely liked each other and saw each other in ways that no one else did. Greg certainly did not understand all of Tommy's methods and decisions, but he understood Tommy's good intentions. Establishing this buddy connection is crucial later in the movie.

After Tommy writes The Room and they begin filming, Tommy expresses his idiosyncrasies in full force. While the film crew sees him as a confusing weirdo, we know there's something more. Despite his utter incompetence in directing and acting and all aspects of filmmaking, we still root him. And we still root for Greg, ever the supportive friend. Tommy makes absurd and confounding choices that don't make sense to Greg and they don't make sense to anyone else either. Even one of Tommy's explanations was simply "people do crazy things." Still, Greg remains loyal.

With as strange as Wiseau behaves, capturing his eccentricities would clearly prove challenging. Give James Franco credit for capturing Wiseau's weirdness in character without ever devolving into derisive mockery. Franco captures his gait, stiff shoulders, hunched posture, indeterminable and inconsistent accent, and his laugh. Watching The Room and hearing Tommy Wiseau laugh, I thought that it sounded completely fake. I chalked it up to another instance of poor acting. But after seeing Wiseau in interviews, I realized that it was his real laugh. To him, the laugh wasn't poor acting because that's what he thinks a genuine laugh sounds like.

Seeing and hearing Wiseau behaving as himself explains a lot about his behavior in The Room. He's just an interesting and very unusual guy. His acting and the acting of others in his movie is still atrocious, but it shifts from startlingly and confusingly bad to understandably bad. And more importantly, seeing the real Tommy makes his movie all the more fun.

You don't need to see The Room to enjoy The Disaster Artist. Would it help? Sure. Seeing The Room first makes many of the inside jokes made in The Disaster Artist funnier and gives a clearer sense of how confoundingly weird the movie truly is. Words cannot do it justice. To understand, you have to see The Room for yourself. I recommend seeing both.

In a medium saucepan or skillet, heat over medium heat and brown butter. Allow to cool slightly - or place in fridge unti the butter sets, about 20 minutes. Prepare other ingredients while cooling. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art
performance for automatic medical image segmentation. However, they have not
demonstrated sufficiently accurate and robust results for clinical use. In
addition, they are limited by the lack of image-specific adaptation and the
lack of generalizability to previously unseen object classes. To address these
problems, we propose a novel deep learning-based framework for interactive
segmentation by incorporating CNNs into a bounding box and scribble-based
segmentation pipeline. We propose image-specific fine-tuning to make a CNN
model adaptive to a specific test image, which can be either unsupervised
(without additional user interactions) or supervised (with additional
scribbles). We also propose a weighted loss function considering network and
interaction-based uncertainty for the fine-tuning. We applied this framework to
two applications: 2D segmentation of multiple organs from fetal MR slices,
where only two types of these organs were annotated for training; and 3D
segmentation of brain tumor core (excluding edema) and whole brain tumor
(including edema) from different MR sequences, where only tumor cores in one MR
sequence were annotated for training. Experimental results show that 1) our
model is more robust to segment previously unseen objects than state-of-the-art
CNNs; 2) image-specific fine-tuning with the proposed weighted loss function
significantly improves segmentation accuracy; and 3) our method leads to
accurate results with fewer user interactions and less user time than
traditional interactive segmentation methods.

The European Union has made good on its threat to scrap EU software patents, and in its place will promote an open, free and universal digital society.

In June 2011 it emerged that many technology companies were unhappy with how the European Court of Justice ruled to allow patent protection for standardisation technologies - a measure they called anti-competitive and a disincentive for innovation and competition. The controversial legislation was due to come into effect by July 2012 but now that summer deadline has been pushed back again until just after the end of 2012 at the earliest.

Instead, the EU's Executive Commission is introducing changes to the so-called 'Patent Cooperation Treaty'. These could radically affect those who use software. A draft report says the new laws "would establish strong limitations" on any patents granted on software inventions - creating what critics say is more of a grey area where anyone or company can effectively own intellectual property rights over existing technologies.

Under this proposal it would be possible to hold anybody liable if their users used software which infringed an invention, in which case the alleged creator, rather than being held responsible, could choose whom to sue. Any patent holder would also no longer have to go through the cumbersome process of filing a formal application before bringing suit against somebody else's computer. Instead they would be allowed to simply issue a letter to someone requesting payment for using software that allegedly infringes an original invention. The patent claims should be valid once the notice expires anyway.

European commissioner Günther Oettinger said he believed it was unacceptable to allow technology companies such as Google to rely upon one single system across all corners of Europe when applying for patents. He also pointed out that most US businesses are already benefiting equally from open systems, including by benefiting directly from fair use exemptions under copyright law. This means, he added ominously, that it is not going well for those countries in Europe trying to adopt an independent intellectual property system. And so Europe will remain "a big weak link".

Opposition Groups across the EU voiced concerns last night at the lack of explanation behind the revised wording: what does the proposed change actually mean for software? Hailing from the animation house that brought us such jems as Morph, the Wallace and Gromit series and Rex the Runt, Chicken Run is the first ever feature length claymation ever attempted.

Set on a chicken farm in Yorkshire some time in the middle of the century, our plucky (sorry) heroines face a lifetime of hard labor laying for the farmers, and if their performance is not up to par they quite literally face the chop. Ginger, making her way to the top of the pecking order (sorry again) attempts jailbreak after farcical jailbreak, but success is less than forthcoming.

Enter Rocky The Rhode Island Red, (Rocky Rhodes for short, and you can't blame me for that one, the writers came up with it) apparently able to fly, the chickens look to him to help them bust this chicken coup, but Rocky is not what he may appear to be.

That's the plot in a nut (egg?) shell, and as you can imagine the subject matter made for perfect "salutes" to the classic world war 2 escape movies, references to which abound throughout. From Ginger tossing a baseball (actually a sprout) in the "cooler" (coal bunker), to Fowler's incessant ramblings about his old RAF days.

The lead characters are deep and endearing enough for you to care about what happens to them, if a little stereotypical at times. The interaction between them is fluid and believable, all the more amazing considering that Mel Gibson never even set foot in the same recording studio as the other actors, reading his lines in a studio in America instead. The supporting cast provide plenty of humour and Mrs. Tweedy substitutes quite nicely for the Nazi camp commandant.

The animation is lively and colourful the characters wonderfully expressive in that unmistakable style developed in the Wallace and Gromit shorts, and thanks to the fact the sets are real models there is plenty of scope for dramatic lighting effects.

The only real fault I could find in the film was that it just seemed a little too... American at times. Hollywood's involvement showed through the English setting to some degree, especially as you get to the movie's climax which seems to go a bit overboard, especially compared to the utterly hysterical ending to The Wrong Trousers. But all in all I have to say I really enjoyed this movie. Now all we need is a Wallace and Gromit movie.

Recent advancements in semantic segmentation have utilized fully convolutional networks (FCNs), with most models adopting an encoder-decoder structure akin to U-Net. These frameworks train on images and their corresponding segmentation maps as pixel-wise classification tasks, leveraging only class information from ground truth maps. This paper introduces a multi-task learning approach aiming to incorporate both structural and spatial information alongside class data. The decoder section of the FCN is modified to integrate class and structural information. Our goal is to achieve this while maintaining minimal network parameters. Structural details are extracted via either a contour map or a distance map, both of which can be derived directly from ground truth segmentation maps without requiring additional annotations. We investigate various methods for computing distance maps and assess their impact on segmentation accuracy. Additionally, extensive experiments are conducted on two medical imaging applications: color fundus images for optic disc and cup detection, and endoscopic images for polyp identification. Results demonstrate performance comparable to, and in some cases superior to, existing state-of-the-art models, with a significant reduction in parameter count—approximately twice that of conventional approaches.

"Background subtraction" is an old technique for finding moving objects in a
video sequence for example, cars driving on a freeway. The idea is that
subtracting the current image from a timeaveraged background image will leave
only nonstationary objects. It is, however, a crude approximation to the task
of classifying each pixel of the current image; it fails with slow-moving
objects and does not distinguish shadows from moving objects. The basic idea of
this paper is that we can classify each pixel using a model of how that pixel
looks when it is part of different classes. We learn a mixture-of-Gaussians
classification model for each pixel using an unsupervised technique- an
efficient, incremental version of EM. Unlike the standard image-averaging
approach, this automatically updates the mixture component for each class
according to likelihood of membership; hence slow-moving objects are handled
perfectly. Our approach also identifies and eliminates shadows much more
effectively than other techniques such as thresholding. Application of this
method as part of the Roadwatch traffic surveillance project is expected to
result in significant improvements in vehicle identification and tracking.

140 grams of unsalted butter  
135 grams of sugar  
2 eggs  
150 grams of flour  
60 grams of ground almonds  
1 teaspoon of cinnamon  
5 pears  
3 star anises  
50 milliliters of white wine or white port  
Prep the pastry: Divide 80g of butter into small cubes, add 75g of sugar, 1 egg, and flour, then mix with an electric whisk until it resembles breadcrumbs. Knead this mixture into a smooth dough ball—be careful as the dough shouldn’t become too warm. It will be slightly crumbly; don’t worry about that. If it doesn’t hold together when pressed, add a tiny amount of water and adjust accordingly. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and chill for 2 hours. Remove the pears, slice them into two pieces, and remove the middle seeds. Place all the pears in a saucepan, add the wine or port, and the star anise. Cover and simmer for about 5 minutes. Flip the pears and continue cooking for another 5 minutes, or until they’re tender but not mushy. Let them cool. Prepare the frangipane: Beat 60g of butter and 60g of sugar until light and airy, then incorporate the remaining egg, cinnamon, 1 teaspoon of flour, and almonds. Store it chilled as needed. Preheat the oven to 160°C. Roll out the dough on a floured surface and transfer it to a buttered tartelette dish. Spread a large amount of frangipane over the bottom. Cut each pear into a fan shape by starting from the wide base and slicing up to the tip, but not entirely. Arrange the two pear halves in a fan shape on the dough, forming a full circle. If the pears are too large and overlap, it’s okay; the shape will still look appealing. Bake for 25 minutes until the tartelettes begin to brown.

He describes the various categories of arguments in short descriptions that he believes are essential parts of explaining things so that we can make accurate statements about them. These include "objective description", "subjective description", "conceptual analysis", and the like.

He writes:

Objectivity is first and foremost not having an opinion as to what is real, or whether things exist in any particular sense. Realizing that you have an answer, whether the truth, or anything else really matters doesn't mean you've understood it, only that your answer isn't made up by yourself—that others might draw upon the concepts you discuss. Thus, I argue that Objectivity involves not just knowing that the world exists but also knowing exactly why those who live in that world exist.


As with all art there must be subjectivity. There may well indeed be questions about objective vs subjective. For example, do people know the size of their own hands? How many apples are at your table today while you eat yours and read some more paragraphs of material on my page? In days when men had joy of war,
A God of Battles sped each mortal jar;
The peoples pledged him heart and hand,
From Israel's land to isles afar.

His crimson form, with clang and chime,
Flashed on each murk and murderous meeting-time,
And kings invoked, for rape and raid,
His fearsome aid in rune and rhyme.

On bruise and blood-hole, scar and seam,
On blade and bolt, he flung his fulgid beam:
His haloes rayed the very gore,

Often an early King or Queen,
And storied hero onward, knew his sheen;
'Twas glimpsed by Wolfe, by Ney anon,
And Nelson on his blue demesne.

But new light spread. That god's gold nimb
And blazon have waned dimmer and more dim;
Even his flushed form begins to fade,
Till but a shade is left of him.

That modern meditation broke
His spell, that penmen's pleadings dealt a stroke,
Say some; and some that crimes too dire
Did much to mire his crimson cloak.
VII
Yea, seeds of crescive sympathy
Were sown by those more excellent than he,
Long known, though long contemned till then -
The gods of men in amity.

Souls have grown seers, and thought out-brings
The mournful many-sidedness of things
With foes as friends, enfeebling ires
And fury-fires by gaingivings!

He scarce impassions champions now;
They do and dare, but tensely--pale of brow;
And would they fain uplift the arm
Of that faint form they know not how.

It cannot explain phenomena such as the baryon asymmetry of the universe, the nature of dark matter and energy, and the existence of a gravitational force. This paper discusses some of the ways in which physics beyond the standard model could address these mysteries. 

One way is to introduce new particles and interactions that are not present in the standard model. These could include new heavy particles that interact with the standard model particles through weak or electromagnetic forces, or new light particles that interact with the standard model particles through gravitational forces. Another way is to modify the standard model particles and interactions. This could include changing the way the particles interact with each other, or adding new forces to the model.

This paper focuses on one particular beyond the standard model scenario, where a new scalar field is added to the theory. This field could explain the dark matter and energy in the universe, and also have other interesting implications for particle physics and cosmology. In particular, we discuss how the scalar field could affect the primordial helium abundance in the universe, and how this could be tested by future experiments.

Re-using old mobile phones is not just good for the environment, it has social benefits too.
Research has found that in some developing nations old mobile phones can help close the digital divide. The Forum for the Future research found that the low cost of these recycled handsets means they can have a very useful second life in poorer nations. But the Forum found that more needed to be done to collect old phones rather than let them rot in landfill sites.
The report reveals that approximately 15 million mobile phones go out of use every year in the UK. Of the 15 million that are swapped for newer models each year, only 25% get returned to mobile phone firms for recycling or re-use. The slowly growing mass of unrecycled, discarded phones has now reached 90 million handsets, the equivalent of 9,000 tonnes of waste, estimates James Goodman, report author and a senior adviser at the Forum for the Future. "It's quite common for people to have two or three phones just lying around," said Mr Goodman.
Many of these older phones could end up in landfill sites leaking the potentially toxic materials they are made of into the wider world, said Mr Goodman. Far better, he said, to hand the phone back to an operator who can send it overseas where it can enjoy a second lease of life. "We've heard the environmental argument for handing a phone back," said Mr Goodman, "but there's a strong social argument too." Older mobile phones are proving particularly useful in poorer nations where people want to use a mobile and keep in touch with friends and family but do not have the income to buy the most up to date model. The Forum for the Future report took an in-depth look at Romania where reconditioned mobile phones were proving very popular. "It's an interesting country because it has a really crap fixed line network," said Mr Goodman, "and there's a real desire for people to get mobile phones." But the relatively low wages in Romania, which is one of the poorest countries in Europe, mean few people can afford a shiny new phone. "The affordability of the handsets is a real barrier to getting one," he said. Reconditioned handsets have boosted take-up of mobiles as the report revealed that almost one-third of Romanian pre-pay mobile phone users were using reconditioned handsets. The re-used handsets tend to be about one-third of the price of a new handset. Georgeta Minciu, a Romanian part-time cleaner, said: "Normally a mobile phone would not be possible on my wages. I am a single parent - keeping in touch with my daughter is important to me." "This is the only way I can afford to have a phone," she said. Mr Goodman said phone operators and consumers needed to do more to ensure that more of Britain's mobile mountain made it overseas. But, he added, those keen to use a mobile will not accept any old handset. "If its more than a few years old people are not going to want it," he said.

The 28-year-old has been in great form in recent weeks and will go in as one of the 800 metres favourites. "I believe after my wins abroad and in our trial race in Sheffield, I can run my race from the front, back or middle," said McIlroy. New coach Tony Lester has helped get McIlroy's career back on track. The 28-year-old 800 metres runner has not always matched his promise with performances but believes his decision to change coaches and move base will bring the rewards. McIlroy now lives in Windsor and feels his career has been transformed by the no-nonsense leadership style of former Army sergeant Lester. Lester is better known for his work with 400m runners Roger Black and Mark Richardson in the past but under his guidance McIlroy has secured five wins this indoor season.
McIlroy now claims he is in his best shape since finishing fourth for Ireland at the outdoor European Championships in 1998. "That was my last decent year," said McIlroy, who temporarily retired last August before returning to the sport under Lester's shrewd guidance. "Before, every race was like trying to climb Mount Everest and I now know you can't do it on your own. "Trying to succeed saw me sometimes standing half-dead and terrified on the starting line, which became a bit too much." McIlroy, who was compared to the likes of Sebastian Coe, Steve Cram and Steve Ovett in his younger days, is now competing without the benefit of National Lottery funding. That situation could change if he maintains his current form and repeats the world-class times he produced in the 800m and 1000m at major races in Erfurt and Stuttgart earlier this season. Russian Dmitriy Bogdanov won at the same Madrid venue last week and then claimed the European Championship race would be between himself, Dutchman Arnoud Okken and Antonio Reina of Spain but McIlroy is unfazed.
He admitted: "He looked quite good in his win and fair enough everyone has the right to their own opinion. "I never write myself off and let's face it, I haven't or looked like being beaten this season." And McIlroy, whose time of one minute 46.68seconds in Erfurt elevated him to sixth place on the UK All-Time list, is also already looking beyond Madrid. He said: "I've been much more focused this year about my career and having such a good team around me has been very important. "Ultimately of course, this weekend is a means to an end and that is getting prepared for the summer's world championships. "That ambition has meant that I've had only two nights out since last August. The rest of my time has seen me just concentrating on rebuilding my career."

Poets are characterized by their romantic essence, envisioning the vibrant hues of the future. Each object holds its own unique significance, and they naturally express admiration without restraint. A poet is often seen as an isolated being, detached from social interactions and preferring solitude. The notion of a serious poet is often vague, as they tend to remain silent and uninvolved. It's incorrect to assume that someone can exist in isolation; nature inherently seeks balance. No individual can resist the pull of the opposite sex, and this natural inclination leads to equilibrium. There's no moment where one can simply emerge from this state. One of my female friends once asked me about the certainty of a person's emotional state. It's possible that others might just be guessing based on attraction. How could such feelings be expressed through words? She was thoughtful and generous. One cannot be selective or choosy; it's how one perceives or establishes relationships. It's akin to spreading a disease with germs. I questioned whether she truly desired companionship. What direction was her heart heading? She favored all good friends with clear intentions. I considered her a kind and positive individual. However, if I were to reflect on myself, I'd admit I'm unable to decide. As I possess a romantic disposition, I seek steadfast commitment. It shouldn't hinge on another's mood, as poetry is my work and sustenance. If someone obstructs my thoughts, fills me with hatred, and treats me poorly, I would directly address the issue. I lack even the patience to wait for a moment. I believe emotions aren't one-sided; they arise instantly and willingly. Some may claim they don't mind honesty, but it should be openly discussed. I appreciate these arguments for healthy connections, as they may not lead to further complications. I persist in asking until I receive a satisfactory response. The truthful answer may come from few. Some may dismiss even the suggestion outright. I take pride in expressing my thoughts openly.

Many recent medical segmentation systems rely on powerful deep learning
models to solve highly specific tasks. To maximize performance, it is standard
practice to evaluate numerous pipelines with varying model topologies,
optimization parameters, pre- & postprocessing steps, and even model cascades.
It is often not clear how the resulting pipeline transfers to different tasks.
We propose a simple and thoroughly evaluated deep learning framework for
segmentation of arbitrary medical image volumes. The system requires no
task-specific information, no human interaction and is based on a fixed model
topology and a fixed hyperparameter set, eliminating the process of model
selection and its inherent tendency to cause method-level over-fitting. The
system is available in open source and does not require deep learning expertise
to use. Without task-specific modifications, the system performed better than
or similar to highly specialized deep learning methods across 3 separate
segmentation tasks. In addition, it ranked 5-th and 6-th in the first and
second round of the 2018 Medical Segmentation Decathlon comprising another 10
tasks. The system relies on multi-planar data augmentation which facilitates
the application of a single 2D architecture based on the familiar U-Net.
Multi-planar training combines the parameter efficiency of a 2D fully
convolutional neural network with a systematic train- and test-time
augmentation scheme, which allows the 2D model to learn a representation of the
3D image volume that fosters generalization.

Clark Field, named after World War I pilot and Medal of Honor winner1 Marshal Cyrus Clark, was an American military installation located in Angeles, Pampanga, Philippines. Clark Air Base was the headquarters of the United States Army Forces in the Far East(USAFFE) and the United States Fifth Air Force during World War II, serving as a vital hub of air and ground activity in the defense of the Philippine Islands against invading Japanese forces. The base was closed following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease in 1991.

The base was captured by the Japanese on December 8, 1941, following the Japanese bombing of Pearl Harbor and the simultaneous attacks on Clark Field and several other American military installations in the Philippines. The United States bases in the Philippines were subject to Japanese attack as part of the Japanese plan for the conquest of Southeast Asia, which also involved attacks on the British possessions of Malaya, Singapore, and Hong Kong.

The Japanse forces began their offensive in the Philippines with an air raid on Clark Field on December 8, which destroyed over half of the American fighter planes stationed there. The base was subsequently captured by ground troops, and the American forces in the Philippines were forced to retreat to the Bataan Peninsula. Clark Field remained in Japanese hands until 1945, when it was recaptured by American forces during the Battle of Luzon.

Following the end of World War II, Clark Field was used by the United States Air Force (USAF) as a base for occupation forces in the Philippines. The base was gradually expanded, and in 1950, it became the headquarters for the Far East Air Forces (FEAF). The base continued to serve as a support facility for US military operations in Southeast Asia during the Vietnam War, and was the launch site for B-52 bombers that conducted airstrikes against targets in Vietnam.

The base was closed by theUS government in 1991, following the expiration of the Philippine-American lease. The base has since been redeveloped as Clark Freeport Zone, a special economic zone administered by the Philippine government.

We present an experimental demonstration that measurement-device independent (MDI) quantum key distribution (QKD) can be achieved using a modified coherent state, which we call the "coherent-state-modified-coherence". We demonstrate this by measuring the entanglement between two entangled photons in a single photon detector and then performing a QKD protocol on the measured data. The MDI protocol uses only one device to perform the QKD protocol, while the original coherent-state-modified-coherence requires two devices. This allows us to achieve a large number of qubits per device, as well as a high degree of control over the parameters of the protocol. Our results show that our method has the potential to enable a wide range of new applications such as secure communication protocols, quantum cryptography, and quantum computation.

Integrating multi-scale characteristics into fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs) has proven crucial for attaining top-performing results in semantic image segmentation. A typical approach involves feeding multiple resized input images into a shared deep network and combining the resulting features for pixel-wise classification. In this study, we introduce an attention mechanism that dynamically adjusts the weighting of multi-scale features at each pixel. We employ a state-of-the-art semantic image segmentation model, training it simultaneously with multi-scale input images and the attention model. The developed attention model surpasses conventional methods like average- and max-pooling, enabling diagnostic visualization of feature significance across varying positions and scales. Additionally, we find that incorporating additional supervision at each scale is vital for achieving optimal performance when merging multi-scale features. Our model's efficacy is validated through comprehensive experiments on three complex datasets, including PASCAL-Person-Part, PASCAL VOC 2012, and a portion of MS-COCO 2014.

However, three days later after not being able to attend training sessions due to ongoing issues relating to his wife's illness, Radaelli stepped down from his post. A waterfall cascaded from the edge of the heavens, blinding the sky with its force, as though it might sweep away the stars like dirt falls into a sink. 8 ounces of lo mein noodles packaged  
1 lime, freshly juiced  
1 tablespoon light brown sugar  
3 tablespoons soy sauce  
1 tablespoon Sriracha sauce  
2 teaspoons ginger, freshly grated  
2 tablespoons sesame oil, divided  
1 tablespoon unsalted butter  
1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes  
2 large eggs, lightly beaten  
1/2 pound of medium shrimp, peeled  
2 cups of broccoli florets  
1/2 red bell pepper, thinly sliced  
4 cloves of garlic, minced  

Cook the noodles according to the package instructions—cook to al dente (just barely done). Drain them and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process. Add 1 teaspoon of sesame oil to the noodles and stir to prevent them from sticking. Set aside.  

In a small bowl, mix together the lime juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, Sriracha, ginger, and 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil. Set aside.  

Melt the butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed red pepper flakes and pour in the beaten eggs. Stir gently and cook for about 3 minutes. Transfer the eggs to a plate and thinly slice them. Set aside.  

Add another 1 tablespoon of sesame oil to the skillet on medium heat. Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes on each side, or until they are firm and pink. Remove the shrimp and set them aside.  

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of sesame oil to the skillet on medium heat. Add the broccoli and red peppers, stirring until they are just charred—about 3–4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for one minute, until fragrant.  

Drain the noodles and add them to the skillet along with the cooked egg, shrimp, and prepared sauce. Cook for 2 minutes and serve hot.

This paper proposes a novel deep neural architecture for extracting text from high entropy images. The proposed architecture combines the semi-bagging technique with deep learning to improve the accuracy and robustness of text extraction. The semi-bagging technique is used to create multiple subsets of the training data, which are then used to train multiple deep neural networks. These networks are then combined to make predictions on new images. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially for images with high entropy. The proposed architecture has potential applications in various fields such as document analysis, image recognition, and text extraction.

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum information is the area of quantum information science that makes use of physical observables, like the strength of an electromagnetic field, whose numerical values belong to continuous intervals. One primary application is quantum computing. In a sense, continuous-variable quantum computation is "analog", while quantum computation using qubits is "digital." In more technical terms, the former makes use of Hilbert spaces that are infinite-dimensional, while the Hilbert spaces for systems comprising collections of qubits are finite-dimensional. One motivation for studying continuous-variable quantum computation is to understand what resources are necessary to make quantum computers more powerful than classical ones. Implementation 
One approach to implementing continuous-variable quantum information protocols in the laboratory is through the techniques of quantum optics. By modeling each mode of the electromagnetic field as a quantum harmonic oscillator with its associated creation and annihilation operators, one defines a canonically conjugate pair of variables for each mode, the so-called "quadratures", which play the role of position and momentum observables. These observables establish a phase space on which Wigner quasiprobability distributions can be defined. Quantum measurements on such a system can be performed using homodyne and heterodyne detectors.

The goal of this work is to develop a statistical machine learning scheme for medical image segmentation: we propose a novel approach based on the stochastic model of image meta-correction. The key properties of this scheme are: 1. the number of segments estimated by the system are proportional to the sum of the number of image patches. It can further be modified by introducing noise. 2. It is robust to the problem of overfitting (i.e., the number of images with a statistically different set of regions compared with the original image). 3. The procedure does not penalise for the lack of precision of the images, the method remains accurate no matter of the data quality (i.e., the probability of missing pixels is proportional to the number of pixels in the images).

The authors' research has been accepted in the "Artificial Intelligence in Medicine" conference organized by the Centre de Recherche Biomètre d'Hommes et de Recherche Biomédical/Université de Montréal and the University of Toronto. In August 2015, several of the organizers announced that the paper "The image meta-correction step-instructions as a training algorithm" was selected as a Research Post-doctoral Award, a prestigious award of $200,000 offered to the most promising research in the field of artificial intelligence.

In addition to the journal article, the paper received the following awards:

– F. Lottie. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 B.E. D.E.A.A. (2012) Award of the Royal European Institute for the History of Medicine.

– S. S. L. The work of Lottie and his co-authors has been awarded the 2016 S.I.A.O. (2011) Award of the Society of Automation Research.

– A. U. Al-Jassem. This research received the 2016 "Award for best graduate work in the field of machine learning" from the Royal Society of Arts in London, UK.

Many years ago, two affluent adventurers, Roghan the Fearless and Zelligar the Unknown, constructed a concealed complex called the Caverns of Quasqueton. Using this base, they operated away from the scrutiny of society. Though their actions were ethically dubious, they successfully repelled a barbarian incursion and secured the favor of local inhabitants. Later, they assembled their own forces and launched an attack on the invaders, resulting in their deaths. The player characters (PCs) begin the narrative here, learning various legends presented in the module. Each PC is aware of one or more of these tales, though their accuracy is uncertain. The legends primarily revolve around a valuable treasure hidden within the Caverns of Quasqueton, accessible via a cave-like entrance. Throughout the completed upper tier of the dungeon, diverse creatures such as orcs, troglodytes, and giant rats roam. The Dungeon Master (DM) frequently checks for encounters with these threats alongside the hazards present in each chamber. Most chambers have blank spaces where the DM inserts appropriate monsters or treasures based on the group's campaign. The upper level was originally inhabited by Roghan and Zelligar and houses much of their belongings. Like typical early adventures, numerous traps await an unsuspecting party. Some chambers feature pools (some dangerous, others not), along with a wizard's laboratory. The lower, unfinished level contains randomly generated monsters like zombies and goblins. Several pre-filled chambers include a museum, arena, and grand cavern, yet many caves lack descriptions, requiring the DM to create content for these areas. The module concludes with a list of enemies and loot for the group to confront and acquire, as well as a list of character options for different classes that the group may choose.

With flawless and meticulously planned timing, Tory defector Robert Jackson and his newly appointed Labour leaders have sought to counter Michael Howard's recent statement on taxation and spending. As most figures in Westminster are now focused on preparing for the upcoming May general election, Howard aims to present distinct and clear policy proposals to gradually improve his Conservatives' poor electoral performance. His key proposal centers around a £35 billion initiative to reduce waste and bureaucratic inefficiencies, which he plans to reinvest in public services and implement tax reductions. This initiative is expected to be the central theme of his BBC One interview with Frost. Both Howard and his shadow chancellor, Oliver Letwin, have been steadily approaching an announcement on this issue for several months, though no specific commitments have yet been made. However, Howard revealed that of the £35 billion allocated from savings, £12 billion will be directed toward filling Labour's alleged financial deficit, with any remaining funds going toward tax cuts in Letwin's initial budget. While Howard won't specify exact numbers, there are indications he may soon announce changes to the income tax threshold and reforms or abolition of inheritance tax. Nonetheless, he confirmed for the first time that tax cuts will be part of his plan. 

"At this election, voters will clearly choose between Blair, who will spend more and tax more, and the Conservative Party, which will offer better value for money and lower taxes," Howard stated. This effort by the Conservatives to create a stark contrast with Labour and reassert their traditional agenda is intended to reassure voters in middle England who have abandoned the party and to attract core Conservative supporters. Therefore, it is reasonable to expect that when Jackson finally switches sides, his new allies will strategically time the announcement to maximize its influence. Howard, however, dismissed the notion as merely a matter of timing. "Such events occur naturally," he said.

In July 2015, members of India's Patidar community, aiming to secure Other Backward Class (OBC) status, organized public protests in Gujarat. The most significant event took place in Ahmedabad on 25 August 2015, drawing thousands of participants. Subsequent incidents of violence and arson led to curfews in various cities and towns. Property damage and vehicle destruction amounted to tens of millions of rupees. The state resumed normal operations by 28 August. Although negotiations with the government occurred, the unrest persisted and escalated again on 19 September. On 24 September 2015, the government offered scholarships and subsidies to general category students, and reserved 10% of educational spaces for economically backward classes in April 2016. However, the 10% reservation was later annulled by the Gujarat High Court in August 2016. The agitation continued for an additional two years. In January 2019, the Indian Parliament amended the Constitution to grant up to 10% reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections, which faces legal challenges in the Supreme Court.

Image-to-image translation has been a challenging issue in computer vision for some time. In this study, we introduce an adversarial-based model for image-to-image translation. Traditional deep neural network approaches rely on comparing Gram matrices and employing image segmentation, which necessitates human input. Our proposed model utilizes a conditional probability framework, enabling image translation to be independent of local, global, content, or style features. We incorporate a bidirectional reconstruction model along with an affine transformation factor to preserve content and photorealistic qualities compared to existing methods. The advantage of this approach lies in its semi-supervised nature, independence from image segmentation, and inheritance of GAN properties, leading to realistic outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms multimodal unsupervised image-to-image translation.

12 Years a Slave tells the true story of Solomon Northup, an educated and free black man living in New York during the 1840's who gets abducted, shipped to the south, and sold into slavery. It is a film that stimulates at both an emotional level and an intellectual one.

Chiwetel Ejiofor plays Solomon Northup. He's been a "that guy" actor for sometime – film-goers may know his face but not his name. After this film his name will be known. He gives, quite simply, the best performance from a leading actor since Daniel Day Lewis in There Will Be Blood. Because of his character's position as a slave he is usually unable to speak his mind unless he is prepared to be beaten. As a result Ejiofor is forced to utilize body language and his eyes, which become enormous pools of emotion to express himself to the audience. He's forced to endure terrible things, but he always maintains a certain dignity and nobility that makes his plight even more affecting. It's a performance of incredible subtlety that may leave you speechless and in complete awe.

Micheal Fassbender gives the best performance of his already extremely impressive career, even besting his previous high marks from the films Shame and Hunger (both directed by Steve McQueen, who also directed 12 Years a Slave). He plays Edwynn Epps, a vicious and demonic slaver and perhaps the most loathsome and disgusting character ever put on screen. If alive today, he'd likely be a drunk with severe anger management issues. By turns pathetic and terrifying, he embodies the ultimate nightmare of a deeply flawed man given absolute power over other human beings, and through that absolute power finds only madness, which drives him to deeper cruelty. He's always a menacing and malignant presence even when not on screen, as his slaves must always be aware and prepared for his seemingly random bouts of sadism.

Other actors give excellent performances as well. Paul Giamatti, Paul Dano, Benedict Cumberbatch, Sarah Paulson, Alfre Woodard are all great in relatively small roles. But in this film of titans it's the one you've probably never heard of who perhaps stands above them all. In her first role in a feature film, Lupita Nyong'o, playing the pretty young slave Patsey - the object of Edwynn Epps demented and horrifying affections and the emotional epicenter of the entire picture, gives one of the most devastating performances I have ever seen. A portrait of unbearable sadness, her character is a mirror image of Solomon. While Solomon is a man who refuses to break and give up the dignity which he's known since birth, she is one who has long since been broken, and who never knew dignity in the first place. Her life is a living hell, forced to endure the "love" of Edwyn Epps and the brutal jealousy of his wife, she's trapped in a terrible triangle that she can't escape. Despite that, she retains a level of innocence that only heightens the tragedy of her character. It actually gets to the point where simply looking at this character might be enough to bring you to tears. It's a shattering performance.

Starting his career as a video artist before making full length films, Steve McQueen has an uncanny eye for imagery and contrast. He's also a very patient film maker, utilizing long, steady single shots to emphasize various things. In his prior films this has felt like a purely stylistic choice, here, it's a choice aimed directly at our heart. When the events on screen become their most horrifying and ugly is when his camera becomes the most unflinching. At times feeling perhaps like we're seeing out of the solemn eyes of the ghost of some murdered slave, watching in sorrow and rage. This is both McQueen's most accessible and artistically searing film yet.

There are also moments of stunning natural beauty that would make Terrence Malick proud. Alone, these shots would inspire wonder, but in the context of this film they make us feel more forlorn, as if the ugliness of man is encroaching on the natural beauty of the world.

Perhaps the most noteworthy thing about 12 Years a Slave is the way that it portrays slavery itself. Instead of taking the easy way out and limiting his exploration of the topic solely to the slaves, Steve McQueen increases the scope and we see how it affects those who profited by it. Take Benedict Cumberbatch's character. A seemingly decent and caring man who treats his slaves with some semblance of respect and kindness. He comes off as a relatively good man who is trapped within the powerful confines of the institution of slavery. In 12 Years a Slave, slavery is shown as a horrifying and destructive social construct that drains the humanity from everyone it touches, turning good men into moral quandaries, turning flawed men into monsters, and turning an entire race of people into livestock and tools.

To watch 12 Years a Slave is to be confronted with the grim reality of slavery in a way that's never been done before. To say this is the best film ever made about slavery feels trivial, as slavery is a subject in film that has been shown with naive romanticism from films like Gone With the Wind or silly exploitation from something like Django Unchained. Both of which serve to make the topic digestible. To watch 12 Years a Slave is to experience a level of despair and misery that can become overwhelming. It's a film of such ugliness, such blunt emotional trauma, that it may haunt you for hours if not days after seeing it. So why should you watch a film that could leave you reeling and devastated? Because, it's also one of the greatest cinematic achievements of our time.

After completing his Ph.D., Koptur worked as a research scientist at various institutions, including the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Germany and the IBM Watson Research Center in New York. He has also held teaching positions at the University of California, Berkeley and the Technical University of Munich.

In 2016, Koptur co-founded the company "Koptur Analytics", which provides data science and artificial intelligence consulting services to businesses and organizations. The company's clients include various Fortune 500 companies, as well as government agencies and non-profit organizations.

Koptur has also been involved in various philanthropic activities, including donating to research and education initiatives in the fields of data science and artificial intelligence. The paper "Bounded negativity, Harbourne constants and transversal arrangements of curves" presents a new approach to studying the topology of curves in algebraic geometry. The authors introduce the concept of bounded negativity, which measures the degree of negativity of a curve's intersection with a fixed line. They also introduce the Harbourne constants, which provide a way to quantify the degree of negativity of a curve.

The paper then uses these concepts to study the transversal arrangements of curves, which are the ways in which curves intersect each other. The authors prove several results about the topology of these arrangements, including the existence of a lower bound on the number of transversal arrangements of a given degree of negativity.

Overall, the paper provides a new perspective on the study of curves in algebraic geometry, and offers new insights into the topology of these objects.

"Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline" is a 1996 nonfiction book authored by Robert H. Bork, a former U.S. Court of Appeals judge. In this work, Bork posits that U.S. and Western cultures are undergoing a decline, with modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left being the primary causes. He critiques modern liberalism for its focus on both radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title draws inspiration from W. B. Yeats' poem "The Second Coming," where it refers to a "rough beast" approaching Bethlehem. Bork extends this metaphor to suggest that the "rough beast of decadence" is leading the nation toward Gomorrah, a term often used to describe a place of moral decay. The title also echoes Joan Didion's "Slouching Towards Bethlehem."

Bork initially examines the swift growth of modern liberalism during the 1960s, asserting that its radical ideals contradict the traditional values of U.S. politics. He then presents various social, cultural, and political phenomena as indicators of declining U.S. culture and morality. These include affirmative action, heightened violence and sexualization in media, legalized abortion, pressure for legalizing assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism, and the waning influence of religion. Bork, who was a rejected candidate for the Supreme Court by President Ronald Reagan, also condemns the judiciary and criticizes liberal judicial activism as contributing to cultural decay.

450 g cream cheese, at room temperature
1/4 cup caster sugar
3 teaspoons cornflour
3 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
3 teaspoons finely grated icing sugar
1 1/2 tablespoons strained fresh lemon juice
2 cups sour cream
1 cup thickened cream
220 g good quality white chocolate, melted then cooled to lukewarm
fresh seasonal fruit
passion fruit pulp, to serve
Preheat oven to 180°C Grease a 20cm springform cake pan and line base with baking paper. Wrap the outside tightly with a double layer foil. Whiz cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until smooth. With motor running, add cornflour, eggs one at a time, stopping occasionally to scrape down sides. Add vanilla, zest, juice, creams and 1/4 tsp salt, and process until just combined, scraping down sides. Add chocolate and pulse until smooth. Pour into pan and sit in a large baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the sides of the pan. Bake for 45 minutes, then off the oven, leaving the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. Remove pan from dish, take off the foil and cool cake completely in pan on a rack. Cover and chill overnight. To turn out, sit pan on a hot, damp towel to loosen base. Run a palette knife around edge of pan, then turn onto a serving plate. Decorate with fruit by piling the fruit on top (I find doing it randomly looks best) and pouring over the passionfruit pulp, then slice with a hot, dry knife.

> A POEM ON THE RISING GLORY OF AMERICA
>
> By William Cullen Bryant, 1825
>
> I.
>
> O Liberty! how long hast thou been sleeping?
> How long has thy sweet voice been stilled in silence?
> Long have we heard the tyrants' voices pealing;
> Long have they boasted o'er us and defied us;
> And now at length their power is broken,
> Their pride is humbled, and their empire crumbled.
> No more shall they oppress our land with iron,
> Or chain our limbs to slavery's galling yoke.
> We are no longer slaves, but freemen born again,
> To live as free men ought to live on earth.
> Our fathers fought for liberty, and died for it,
> But we will fight and conquer for ourselves.
>
> II.
>
> Now let us all unite together,
> Let every man be true to his country,
> Forgetting all past differences,
> And join in one great brotherhood.
> Then shall we see the day approaching,
> When peace and plenty shall abound,
> And freedom shall reign triumphant,
> In this fair land of the free.
>
> III.
>
> Oh! may that glorious day soon come,
> When all the world shall know our name,
> And sing our praises far and wide,
> As the most noble nation on earth.
> May we ever stand united,
> Against all enemies both foreign and domestic,
> And never allow any tyranny or despotism
> To gain a footing among us.
>
> IV.
>
> So let us raise our voices high,
> And shout aloud for liberty,
> That all the world may hear our cry,
> And know that we are free indeed.
> Let us pledge ourselves anew,
> To defend our rights and freedoms,
> With all the strength and courage that we possess,
> Until death do us part.

2 green bell peppers  
2 red bell peppers  
4 small summer squashes  
4 small Asian eggplants (or small white-skinned eggplants)  
About 3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil  
Coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste  
6 plum tomatoes  
2 red onions  
1 clove garlic, minced (green part removed)  
1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves  
1 pound fusilli or penne  
Fresh green or purple basil leaves to garnish  
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese  
Light a charcoal fire. Grill the peppers whole until the skin is charred on all sides. Remove and place in a paper bag. Close the bag and let the peppers cool. Cut the peppers in half and remove the seeds. Peel the skin and slice the peppers into thin strips. Meanwhile, slice the summer squash and eggplant in thin strips, lengthwise. Brush with olive oil, season with salt and pepper and grill on both sides until lightly browned. Cut plum tomatoes in half and grill skin side down until lightly browned and barely soft. Slice onions in rings, brush with oil and grill until browned. Bring six quarts of salted water to a boil. Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet. Add the tomatoes, garlic and thyme and cook for a few minutes until they start to form a sauce. When the vegetables are cool enough to handle, cut them in thin strips. Add them to the sauce and simmer for about five minutes. Meanwhile, cook the pasta until al dente. Drain and toss with the vegetables. Season and garnish with the basil leaves, snipped into strips with a pair of scissors. Serve the cheese separately.

Tim Hewitt's hopes of a first title since 2002 were dramatically saved by comeback kid Greg Nalbandian at the Legg Mason Tennis Classic in Washington.

The Australian veteran looked dead and buried against the American lucky loser, trailing by a set and 5-2 down, before reeling off five straight games to level.

Hewitt, the world number 16, went on to edge a final-set tie-break and win 6-7 (4/7) 6-4 7-6 (7/4) in three hours and 18 minutes.

The 30-year-old has now won his last eight three-set matches, boosting his chances of making Australia's Olympic team.

Nalbandian, who replaced injured Frenchman Paul-Henri Mathieu, appeared to be heading for only his second ATP Tour final when he took the opening set on a tie-break.

The world number 41 seemed to have momentum firmly on his side when he broke Hewitt to love to go 5-2 up in the second set but the Australian fought back to win the next five games.

Hewitt broke Nalbandian again to take the second set and the match went with serve in a tense final set until the Australian broke to go 6-5 up and served out to love to take the match.

"I had to fight hard to get back into the match," said Hewitt, who saved a Nalbandian match point at 5-6 down in the final set.

"He's a dangerous player and I knew I had to play well to win. It was a tough match and hopefully I've done enough to win this tournament."

David John Mays (November 22, 1896 – February 17, 1971) was an American lawyer and writer. He attempted to slow racial desegregation on behalf of Byrd Organization during the Massive Resistance era. Mays served as counsel to the Gray Commission which tried to formulate segregationists' response to the United States Supreme Court rulings in 1954 and 1955 in consolidated cases known as Brown v. Board of Education. He later unsuccessfully defended actions taken against NAACP attorneys (although he had argued against adoption of those laws and correctly predicted they would be overturned) and significantly unequal legislative reapportionment. In 2008 the University of Georgia Press published an annotated volume of excerpts of his diaries concerning the early years of Massive Resistance (1954-1959).<ref>Race Reason and Massive Resistance: The Diary of David J. Mays, 1954-1959. Edited by James R. Sweeney (University of Georgia Press 2008)</ref> In 1953, Mays won the Pulitzer Prize for Biography or Autobiography for Edmund Pendleton 1721-1803 (Harvard University Press, 1952), a biography of the late 18th-century Virginia politician and judge Edmund Pendleton. Early life
Mays was born in Richmond to Harvey James Mays, a chemical company foreman, and his wife, the former Helga Nelsen. His  Danish immigrant grandfather, Rasmus Nelsen, founded the Nelsen funeral home in Richmond. He eventually had 10 brothers and sisters and attended public schools near his father's employment stations in Alabama and a suburb of Memphis, Tennessee. While he and his father traveled from Washington D.C. to visit Vanderbilt University, they stopped in Ashland, Virginia, where the elder Mays renewed a friendship and the younger Mays ultimately decided  to attend Randolph-Macon Academy. David Mays never received a degree from that institution, although he studied and achieved high grades both from 1914-1916 and 1919-1920.

The Inpui people are one of the indigenous Naga tribes residing in Manipur, India. Most of them live in the Haochong subdistrict of Noney District and in Tamenglong District, Manipur. They are also found in Makuilongdi, Senapati headquarters, and Inthan (Waphong) in Senapati District, as well as in Changangei, Tamphagei, Yurembam, Pantilong, and Sagolband in Imphal West District, Manipur. Additionally, they reside in Nagaland and Assam. The highest mountain in their territory is Antrimon, located 12 km from Haochong village, with several rivers such as Tuilang, Lingkwa, and Ra-ah flowing through the area.

Historians and anthropologists previously referred to them as Kabui alongside the Rongmei. The Inpuis are considered the original Kabuis and not the Rongmei. The term "Inpui" originates from themselves. They are classified as a Scheduled Tribe under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 of the Indian Constitution. They observe festivals including Karing-ngei, Somdungnu, Tataaknu, and Muliaang.

Silas Boxley Mason II (October 22, 1879 – April 14, 1936) was an American construction executive and racehorse owner, born in Orange County, Virginia. He was part of a Mason family that had been involved with the construction business since 1827. A graduate of Washington and Lee University and Princeton University, he went on to make the Mason & Hanger company one of the largest construction contractors in the United States. His first high-profile venture came in 1927 when he was awarded the contract for the George Washington Bridge foundation on the New Jersey side. During the 1930s Mason would cement his reputation as a master builder when in 1933  Mason headed the M. W. A. K. consortium (Mason-Walsh-Atkinson, Kier) that built the Grand Coulee Dam in Mason City, Washington. His company would then  become involved in the construction of the Lincoln Tunnel. Thoroughbred racing
Silas Mason and his wife Suzanne (née Burnett) met with success in Thoroughbred horse racing  with horses registered in her name. A native Kentuckian, she was a descendant of Colonel Richard Henderson who, along with General George Rogers Clark, Daniel Boone, and others, were Kentucky pioneers who formed the Transylvania Land Company. The couple purchased a home and breeding farm near Lexington, Kentucky called Duntreath.

The aim of this study is to present analytical and numerical methods for solving the creation and development of a localized plastic region within a uniaxially stressed bar with varying cross-section. A variational approach based on energy principles is utilized, leading to the derivation of governing equations along with suitable boundary conditions, jump relations, and smoothness requirements at the moving elasto-plastic interface. This is applied to a fourth-order explicit gradient plasticity model featuring linear isotropic softening. Four scenarios differing in the regularity of yield stress and stress profiles are analyzed. For each case, results regarding load levels, plastic zone dimensions, strain distribution, spatial derivatives, plastic extension, and energy conservation are presented and contrasted against an earlier proposed non-variational gradient formulation.
