The time slipped by like a performance; I possessed the wisdom that love bestows, a portion of maternal insight, yet despite my words and her approval, a storm from the harsh north concealed Love's luminous moon. Believing each of my statements, I lauded her form and intellect until pride illuminated her gaze and pleasure reddened her cheeks, while vanity gave her steps a lightness. Yet, despite our praise, we found only darkness above. We sat in silence, aware, though she had not spoken, that even the finest love must fade, and had been cruelly shattered were it not for Love's sudden flight from the clouds, driven by the cry of a foolish little bird.  

Though crowds gathered when she appeared, even elder men's eyes softened, yet only this hand—like a final courtier at a gypsy camp—recalls what is lost. These features, shaped by laughter into sweetness, remain, but I note what is gone. A crowd will come, unaware it strolls the very street where once a fiery cloud moved.

1 tablespoon of sea salt  
1 pound of imported orecchiette pasta  
1 1/2 pounds of broccoli rabe, stems removed and chopped into 1-inch pieces  
3 tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil  
4 cloves of garlic, finely chopped  
2 fillets of imported salted anchovies, cleaned  
1 teaspoon of crushed red pepper  
12 ounces of Italian sausage, casing removed  
1/3 cup of coarsely shredded ricotta salata  

Bring a large pot of water to a boil on high heat. Once the water is boiling, add the salt and pasta, stirring constantly. Set the timer for half of the recommended cooking time. When the time is up, add the rabe and continue cooking according to the recommended time. For al dente consistency, reduce the total cooking time by 2 minutes.  

While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Once the oil shimmers, add the garlic, anchovies, and red pepper. Use a wooden spoon to mash them into a paste and cook for 1 minute, avoiding burning the garlic. Add the sausage meat to the skillet and break it into small pieces. Cover the skillet and lower the heat to medium-low, stirring frequently.  

Drain the pasta and rabe, keeping 1 cup of the water used to cook the pasta aside. Add the pasta and rabe to the skillet and cook an additional minute. If the pan is dry, add 1/4 cup of pasta water at a time. Turn off the heat and stir in half of the cheese, then set aside the remaining cheese for later use.

Germán García Durán is a Colombian civil and environmental engineer, having earned his degree from the University of Los Andes in Bogotá, Colombia, and the University of Notre Dame in South Bend, Indiana, USA. His career includes serving as a consultant in Colombia and the United States, as well as a university professor in Colombia. He has twice held the position of Ambassador of Colombia to Kenya. Prior to this role, García was the General Manager of the National Institute of Renewable Natural Resources and Environment. As Permanent Representative to the United Nations Office in Nairobi, he focused on global environmental policies, including those related to the United Nations Environment Programme and UN-HABITAT. He also served as Chairman of the Group of 77 and was the Vice President of the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer. Currently, he is the Executive President of Río Urbano, a member of the Waterkeeper Alliance, which aims to protect riverbeds in urban areas.

6 ounces feta cheese, crumbled
4 ounces cream cheese
1 egg, beaten
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
1 tablespoon chopped fresh dill or 1 teaspoon dried dill
8 sheets packaged phyllo dough
1/2 cup butter
Defrost the phyllo dough and return the remainder to the freezer. Butter a cookie sheet. Melt the butter and remove from the heat. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Mix the feta and cream cheese with the egg, parsley, and dill and set aside. Layout one sheet of phyllo dough on a counter. (Keep the remaining dough covered with a slightly damp towel to prevent its drying out.) Brush the sheet of dough with some melted butter. Cut it the short way into 5 strips, about 3x10 inches each. Place 1-1/2 teaspoons of the filling at one end of each strip. Roll the strips into cylinders about 1/2 inch in diameter. Continue until all of the dough has been cut, filled, and rolled. Arrange 2 to 3 cylinder per person on the cookie sheet and brush them with more butter. (Freeze the rest of the cylinders, unbaked, for use at another time.) Bake for about 10 minutes, or until the cylinders are well browned and very flaky. Bureks, frozen unbaked, can go directly from the freezer into a preheated 375-degree F oven to make an instant hors d'oeuvre.

2 pounds of beef, flank steak (London broil)  
1 each bay leaves  
1 small onion  
1 whole ripe tomato  
1 each celery stalks  
1 tablespoon salt  
1 1/4 cups olive oil  
1/2 each green bell pepper finely chopped  
2 each garlic clove minced  
1 each bay leaf  
1/2 teaspoon oregano  
1/4 teaspoon cumin  
10 1/2 ounces tomato sauce  
1/4 teaspoon sugar  
1 tablespoon white wine vinegar  
1/2 cup stock from cooked meat  
1 teaspoon salt  
1/4 cup wine Burgundy  

In a suitable soup kettle, place the meat, bay leaf, whole onion, tomato, celery rib cut in half, and the salt. Cover with cold water and bring to a rapid boil. Skim several times. Lower heat and cook until meat is tender (approximately 1 hour). Allow meat to cool in stock, then remove to platter and shred. Strain stock and reserve to be used in sauce and the rest for a hearty soup.  

TOMATO SAUCE FOR ROPA VIEJA: Heat oil in a large skillet. Add onion and green pepper and sauté until transparent. Add the garlic, bay leaf, oregano, cumin, and cook 5 minutes longer. Combine tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, stock, salt, and wine. Add to sauté. Stir to mix well and bring to a boil. Lower heat and cook for approximately 30 minutes, stirring at intervals. In a 2 1/2 quart casserole with cover, place the shredded meat. Pour sauce over the meat and mix well. Cover and simmer for another 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve over white rice accompanied by very ripe fried plantains, when available.

Laser-induced magnetization precession of a thick Pt/Co/Pt film with
perpendicular interface anisotropy was studied using time resolved
magneto-optical Kerr effect. Although the demagnetization energy dominates the
interface anisotropy for the Co thickness considered, and the Co layer can be
characterized by an effective easy-plane anisotropy, we found that an
additional $\pi$ shift in the initial phase for the magnetization precession is
needed to describe the measured data using only the effective easy-plane
anisotropy. The additional $\pi$ phase is rendered by the dependence on the
phonon temperature of the interface anisotropy, in contrast to the dependence
on the electron temperature of the demagnetization energy. Our observation that
the precession phase is affected by both the electron and phonon temperature
warrants a detailed knowledge about the forms of anisotropy present in the
system under investigation for a complete description of laser-induced
magnetization precession.

The challenge of image segmentation becomes more complex when objects of interest are partially obscured, there is background clutter, or significant noise is present. To address this issue, the current study presents a new approach that employs "weak" shape priors for segmentation. In the proposed method, an active contour is restricted to reach a configuration where its geometric parameters closely match the empirical probability densities of the corresponding model densities, which are derived from training samples. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the introduced shape modeling is considered "weak" because it has minimal impact on segmentation, allowing data-driven forces to dominate. Additionally, the priors offer adequate constraints to ensure stable segmentation convergence, with significantly fewer training datasets required compared to PCA-based regularization techniques. The key benefits of this approach are illustrated through various experimental comparisons with existing methods.

Black trees against an orange sky,
Trees that the wind shook terribly,
Like a harsh spume along the road,
Quavering up like withered arms,
Writhing like streams, like twisted charms
Of hot lead flung in snow. Below
The iron ice stung like a goad,
Slashing the torn shoes from my feet,
And all the air was bitter sleet.
And all the land was cramped with snow,
Steel-strong and fierce and glimmering wan,
Like pale plains of obsidian.
-- And yet I strove -- and I was fire
And ice -- and fire and ice were one
In one vast hunger of desire.
A dim desire, of pleasant places,
And lush fields in the summer sun,
And logs aflame, and walls, and faces,
-- And wine, and old ambrosial talk,
A golden ball in fountains dancing,
And unforgotten hands. (Ah, God,
I trod them down where I have trod,
And they remain, and they remain,
Etched in unutterable pain,
Loved lips and faces now apart,
That once were closer than my heart --
In agony, in agony,
And horribly a part of me. . . .
For Lethe is for no man set,
And in Hell may no man forget.)
And there were flowers, and jugs, bright-glancing,
And old Italian swords -- and looks,
A moment's glance of fire, of fire,
Spiring, leaping, flaming higher,
Into the intense, the cloudless blue,
Until two souls were one, and flame,
And very flesh, and yet the same!
As if all springs were crushed anew
Into one globed drop of dew!
But for the most I thought of heat,
Desiring greatly. . . . Hot white sand
The lazy body lies at rest in,
Or sun-dried, scented grass to nest in,
And fires, innumerable fires,
Great fagots hurling golden gyres
Of sparks far up, and the red heart
In sea-coals, crashing as they part
To tiny flares, and kindling snapping,
Bunched sticks that burst their string and wrapping
And fall like jackstraws; green and blue
The evil flames of driftwood too,
And heavy, sullen lumps of coke
With still, fierce heat and ugly smoke. . . .
. . . And then the vision of his face,
And theirs, all theirs, came like a sword,
Thrice, to the heart -- and as I fell
I thought I saw a light before.
I woke. My hands were blue and sore,
Torn on the ice. I scarcely felt
The frozen sleet begin to melt
Upon my face as I breathed deeper,
But lay there warmly, like a sleeper
Who shifts his arm once, and moans low,
And then sinks back to night. Slow, slow,
And still as Death, came Sleep and Death
And looked at me with quiet breath.
Unbending figures, black and stark
Against the intense deeps of the dark.
Tall and like trees. Like sweet and fire
Rest crept and crept along my veins,
Gently. And there were no more pains. . . .
Was it not better so to lie?
The fight was done. Even gods tire
Of fighting. . . . My way was the wrong.
Now I should drift and drift along
To endless quiet, golden peace . . .
And let the tortured body cease.
And then a light winked like an eye.
. . . And very many miles away
A girl stood at a warm, lit door,
Holding a lamp. Ray upon ray
It cloaked the snow with perfect light.
And where she was there was no night
Nor could be, ever. God is sure,
And in his hands are things secure.
It is not given me to trace
The lovely laughter of that face,
Like a clear brook most full of light,
Or olives swaying on a height,
So silver they have wings, almost;
Like a great word once known and lost
And meaning all things. Nor her voice
A happy sound where larks rejoice,
Her body, that great loveliness,
The tender fashion of her dress,
I may not paint them.
These I see,
Blazing through all eternity,
A fire-winged sign, a glorious tree!
She stood there, and at once I knew
The bitter thing that I must do.
There could be no surrender now;
Though Sleep and Death were whispering low.
My way was wrong. So. Would it mend
If I shrank back before the end?
And sank to death and cowardice?
No, the last lees must be drained up,
Base wine from an ignoble cup;
(Yet not so base as sleek content
When I had shrunk from punishment)
The wretched body strain anew!
Life was a storm to wander through.
I took the wrong way. Good and well,
At least my feet sought out not Hell!
Though night were one consuming flame
I must go on for my base aim,
And so, perhaps, make evil grow
To something clean by agony . . .
And reach that light upon the snow . . .
And touch her dress at last . . .
So, so,
I crawled. I could not speak or see
Save dimly. The ice glared like fire,
A long bright Hell of choking cold,
And each vein was a tautened wire,
Throbbing with torture -- and I crawled.
My hands were wounds.
So I attained
The second Hell. The snow was stained
I thought, and shook my head at it
How red it was! Black tree-roots clutched
And tore -- and soon the snow was smutched
Anew; and I lurched babbling on,
And then fell down to rest a bit,
And came upon another Hell . . .
Loose stones that ice made terrible,
That rolled and gashed men as they fell.
I stumbled, slipped . . . and all was gone
That I had gained. Once more I lay
Before the long bright Hell of ice.
And still the light was far away.
There was red mist before my eyes
Or I could tell you how I went
Across the swaying firmament,
A glittering torture of cold stars,
And how I fought in Titan wars . . .
And died . . . and lived again upon
The rack . . . and how the horses strain
When their red task is nearly done. . . .
I only know that there was Pain,
Infinite and eternal Pain.
And that I fell -- and rose again.
So she was walking in the road.
And I stood upright like a man,
Once, and fell blind, and heard her cry . . .
And then there came long agony.
There was no pain when I awoke,
No pain at all. Rest, like a goad,
Spurred my eyes open -- and light broke
Upon them like a million swords:
And she was there. There are no words.
Heaven is for a moment's span.
And ever.
So I spoke and said,
"My honor stands up unbetrayed,
And I have seen you. Dear . . ."
Sharp pain
Closed like a cloak. . . .
I moaned and died.
Here, even here, these things remain.
I shall draw nearer to her side.
Oh dear and laughing, lost to me,
Hidden in grey Eternity,
I shall attain, with burning feet,
To you and to the mercy-seat!
The ages crumble down like dust,
Dark roses, deviously thrust
And scattered in sweet wine -- but I,
I shall lift up to you my cry,
And kiss your wet lips presently
Beneath the ever-living Tree.
This in my heart I keep for goad!
Somewhere, in Heaven she walks that road.
Somewhere . . . in Heaven . . . she walks . . . that . . . road. . . .

Drang nach Osten (German for "drive to the east") was an ideology promoted by certain German and Austrian political and military figures in the 19th century, which emphasized Germany's need to expand its territory towards the east through military conquest. This concept became particularly influential under the Third Reich, leading to aggressive expansionist policies that ultimately led to World War II.

The term itself originated in the 1840s with the writings of German nationalist leader Fritz Müller, who argued for a united Germany to actively pursue territorial conquests in order to become a major world power. His ideas were echoed by others including Otto von Bismarck, Adolf Hitler, and other proponents of Nazi Germany's aggressive expansionist policies.

In the view of these individuals, German unification was not enough and the country needed more land and resources to become truly great. This drive for expansion culminated in the Anschluss of Austria into the Reich in 1938 and the subsequent invasion of Poland in September 1939, which marked the beginning of World War II.

The Drang nach Osten ideology has been widely criticized as it contributed to the persecution and holocaust of millions of people, particularly Jews and Slavs. It also continues to be a controversial subject in modern-day Germany, with debates about whether the nation should take responsibility for its past actions and acknowledge the ongoing impact of its history on Europe and beyond.

Constance Eaton Hamilton (1862–1945) was a British-Canadian government official and activist. After activism supporting refugees and women in Winnipeg, she moved to Toronto and continued to support causes such as women's suffrage, becoming president of the Equal Franchise League of Toronto. She was elected for a one-year term on the  Toronto City Council in the 1920 elections, becoming the first female member of Toronto City Council and the first woman in Ontario to hold elected office at either the federal, provincial, or municipal level. After two terms  she resigned to continue her work campaigning for immigrant settlement and refugee issues, and for equal rights. In 1979, the Toronto city council established the Constance E. Hamilton Award on the Status of Women. Early life and education
She was born in Yorkshire, England in 1862 to Dr George Fowler Bodington (1829-1902) and Caroline Mary Eaton (1825-1873). Early she studied with private tutors. Fluent in German, she attended the Conservatory of Music in Leipzig, Germany and became a skilled pianist. She also worked as a part-time farmer for parts of her early life.  Hamilton immigrated to Canada with her family in 1887 and settled in Vancouver. The following year she met and married Lauchlan Hamilton, an older businessman.

WIS was the fourth television station to sign on in South Carolina and the third in the Columbia market, joining just four months after WCOS-TV (channel 25), which closed in 1956, and two months before WNOK-TV (channel 67, now WLTX on channel 19), which moved in 1961. In this paper, our primary focus is on the stability of iterated polynomials and linear transformations that maintain the strong $q$-log-convexity of polynomials. Let $[T_{n,k}]_{n,k \geq 0}$ denote an array of nonnegative numbers. We establish certain conditions for the linear transformation  
$$ y_n(q) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} T_{n,k} x_k(q) $$  
to preserve the strong $q$-log-convexity (or log-convexity) of polynomials. As applications, we demonstrate that several linear transformations—such as the Stirling transformations of different types, the Jacobi-Stirling transformations of various kinds, the Legendre-Stirling transformations of multiple varieties, and others—preserve the strong $q$-log-convexity (or log-convexity) uniformly. Specifically, we verify a conjecture by Lin and Zeng, expand upon findings by Chen et al., and extend results by Zhu regarding strong $q$-log-convexity of polynomials, as well as those by Liu and Wang concerning transformations that preserve log-convexity.

The stability of iterated polynomials leads to $q$-log-convexity. By leveraging the zero-interlacing technique, we derive two criteria for the stability of iterated Sturm sequences and $q$-log-convexity of polynomials. These results yield the stabilities of iterated Eulerian polynomials of types $A$ and $B$, along with their $q$-analogues. Furthermore, we show that the generating functions of alternating runs of types $A$ and $B$, the longest alternating subsequence in permutations, and up-down runs of permutations form $q$-log-convex sequences, respectively.

The novel *The Remains of the Day* recounts the story of Stevens, an English butler whose entire life has been devoted to serving Lord Darlington, as depicted in increasingly detailed flashbacks. The narrative commences with Stevens receiving a letter from his former colleague, Miss Kenton, detailing her married life, which he interprets as suggesting an unhappy marriage. This letter occurs at a time when Stevens has the chance to reconnect with this past relationship, albeit through the lens of seeking re-employment. Stevens’s new employer, a wealthy American named Mr. Farraday, urges him to borrow his car for a much-needed vacation, a "motoring trip." During this journey, Stevens reflects on his unwavering loyalty to Lord Darlington, the significance of the word "dignity," and his personal connection with his late father. Ultimately, he must grapple with the authenticity of his relationship with Miss Kenton. As the plot unfolds, growing evidence reveals Miss Kenton's former affection for Stevens, as well as his own admiration for her. Despite their professional camaraderie, they never openly admitted their feelings. It is later revealed that Miss Kenton, now Mrs. Benn, has been married for over two decades and has come to cherish her husband, anticipating the arrival of their first child. Stevens contemplates missed chances, both with Miss Kenton and with Lord Darlington. By the conclusion of the novel, Stevens shifts his focus to the "remains of [his] day," symbolizing his future service with Mr. Farraday.

Chinese authorities will continue implementing measures to prevent the economy from overheating by restricting credit in 2005, according to state media reports. These restrictions were introduced earlier this year to mitigate the risks of excessive economic growth leading to price increases. There were also concerns about placing undue strain on the weak banking system. Despite a growth rate of 9.1% in China, corporate investments have been increasing at a rate of over 25% annually. The rapid pace of economic development has maintained growth above 9% for more than a year. The expansion of China's manufacturing industry has led to a significant increase in energy demands, contributing to sustained high global oil prices. While the government aims for a 7% growth target, it insists that exceeding this figure does not necessarily result in an unstable economy. A declining yuan, currently pegged at 8.28 to the dollar, makes Chinese exports competitive internationally. China has so far avoided breaking the currency linkage or shifting its peg. To some degree, these credit control policies appear to be working: industrial production rose 15.7% in the year up to October, compared to 23% in February, and inflation dropped to 4.3%, though retail sales remain strong.

The Conservative Party would decrease the number of Members of Parliament by approximately one-fifth if they were elected, according to Tory leader Michael Howard. This proposal is part of the party's "smaller government bill," which will be announced later this week. Howard stated that the party would also reduce the number of government special advisers and proposed holding a referendum in Wales to determine whether the Welsh Assembly should be abolished. He mentioned that these changes would occur within five years of the Conservatives securing a general election victory. The exact number of MPs to be reduced would depend on the outcome of the Welsh referendum, though it is likely to result in a decline of around 120 from the current total of 659. If Wales retains its assembly, it would face greater losses. Howard emphasized that both parties intend to cut civil servants at Whitehall, with Labour targeting a reduction of over 80,000 and the Conservatives planning for nearly 100,000. He argued that such cuts should apply equally to their own ranks. "It is good to talk about reducing government departments, but what about ministers, Parliament, and special advisers?" he asked. Shadow leader of the Commons, Oliver Heald, remarked that this initiative aligns with the goal of minimizing unnecessary and expensive state intervention in people's lives by shrinking the size and role of the state. Howard noted that the plan would also address the "great unfairness" of having proportionally more Scottish and Welsh MPs in Westminster compared to those from England. He cited the average size of English constituencies at 70,000 residents, slightly above 66,000 in Northern Ireland, 59,000 in Wales, and 53,000 in Scotland. If the Welsh assembly were abolished, the number of Welsh MPs would be set to ensure fairness in representation relative to the rest of the UK. Howard insisted the changes should be enacted swiftly, potentially even before the next election. "A big bang is necessary; we cannot proceed gradually."

We introduce a technique for classifying cardiac diseases using a new method to extract image-based features that describe the heart's shape and movement. A novel semi-supervised learning process is designed to utilize a vast number of unsegmented images alongside a limited number of manually segmented ones, enabling the creation of pixel-level flow information between two time points in a 2D+t cine MRI sequence. By merging these flow maps with cardiac segmentation masks, we derive local flow patterns representing the 2D motion of myocardium and ventricular chambers. This results in time series data capturing the radius and thickness of myocardial regions, serving as reliable and interpretable indicators of abnormal cardiac motion. These motion features are integrated with shape-related attributes to facilitate disease classification. The model employs only nine input feature values and offers an explainable, straightforward, and adaptable framework for pathology categorization. On the ACDC training and test datasets, it achieves 95% and 94% accuracy, respectively, demonstrating performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods. Comparative analysis with other models highlights some of the model's strengths.

The film's plot is similar to 'E.T.' - a young boy meets an alien robot from outer space, who is stranded on earth, and runs afoul of paranoid government agents. Not to knock the Spielberg film, but what makes 'The Iron Giant' the better film is that the young boy is the teacher. It is he who has to teach the Giant about the beauty of life, the difference between good and evil, and choices we have to make. The Iron Giant, it turns out, is a weapon, who has to struggle against his own nature. The film has an obvious (and timely) gun control message, but its real message is about the choice we make when dealing with other people. We can use our powers for good or lash out at everyone around us.

I dare not give away the climax. All I will say is that it features a sacrifice absolutely breaktaking and emotionally shattering (albeit somewhat blunted by the ending). The animation is gorgeous, Michael Kamen's score is perfect, and the film beautifully evokes the 1950s.

Sadly, poor marketing kept audiences away in droves. All I can say is, to heck with the box office gross. Despite Warner's appearant desire to pretend the film never existed, the word is getting around about what a magical film this is, and I have no doubt it will join 'It's a Wonderful Life' as a film which bombed in theatres but became a classic over the years. See it now, so you can say you discovered it before everyone else did.

Over the past few years it has been demonstrated that "coarse timesteppers"
establish a link between traditional numerical analysis and microscopic/
stochastic simulation. The underlying assumption of the associated
lift-run-restrict-estimate procedure is that macroscopic models exist and close
in terms of a few governing moments of microscopically evolving distributions,
but they are unavailable in closed form. This leads to a system identification
based computational approach that sidesteps the necessity of deriving explicit
closures. Two-level codes are constructed; the outer code performs macroscopic,
continuum level numerical tasks, while the inner code estimates -through
appropriately initialized bursts of microscopic simulation- the quantities
required for continuum numerics. Such quantities include residuals, time
derivatives, and the action of coarse slow Jacobians. We demonstrate how these
coarse timesteppers can be applied to perform equation-free computations of a
kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of E. coli chemotaxis. Coarse-grained
contraction mappings, system level stability analysis as well as acceleration
of the direct simulation, are enabled through this computational multiscale
enabling technology.

Liverpool and Millwall have been accused by the Football Association of causing disorder during their Carling Cup game on 26 October. Millwall, which lost the match 3-0, have also faced charges regarding alleged racist conduct by their supporters. During the match at Millwall’s new Den Stadium, seats were damaged and four individuals were removed from the field. A disabled spectator sustained an injury near the pitch, and riot police were deployed to manage the situation. Liverpool fans alleged that the unrest began due to chants referencing the Hillsborough tragedy, in which 96 supporters died in 1989. However, Lions chairman Theo Paphitis dismissed these claims, stating that CCTV footage revealed the trigger for the conflict was a Liverpool supporter attacking a Millwall fan in the west end. Millwall have been cited with two violations under FA rules: failure to monitor fans for racist or abusive behavior and failure to prevent spectators from hurling objects onto the pitch. Liverpool faced one violation for allowing their fans to exhibit threatening, violent, or provocative actions. Both teams must respond by 23 December.

12 ounces flank steak, trimmed of excess fat and sinew
1 tablespoon peeled, minced fresh ginger
1 1/2 teaspoons soy sauce
1 teaspoon cornstarch
1 teaspoon peanut or vegetable oil
1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons oyster sauce
2 tablespoons Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
2 tablespoons peanut or vegetable oil
1 1/2 cups sugar snap peas (about 7 ounces), strings removed
1 cup very thinly sliced carrots (about 2 small)
4 medium scallions, halved lengthwise and cut into 2-inch pieces
1/4 cup pickled ginger slices (about 1 ounce), coarsely chopped if large
Basic Steamed White Rice, for serving
Cut the flank steak with the grain into 2-inch-wide strips, then cut each strip against the grain into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Place the beef and the remaining ingredients in a medium bowl and stir to evenly coat the meat; set aside. Place the oyster sauce and Shaoxing wine or sherry in a small bowl and stir to combine; set aside. Heat a 14-inch flat-bottomed wok over high heat until a bead of water vaporizes when dropped in the pan. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of the oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the reserved beef in an even layer. Cook undisturbed until the beef begins to sear, about 1 minute. Then, using a metal spatula, stir-fry for 30 seconds until the beef is lightly browned but not cooked through. Transfer to a plate. Drizzle the remaining tablespoon of oil around the perimeter of the wok and add the sugar snaps and carrots. Stir-fry until just warmed through, about 1 minute. Return the beef and any accumulated juices to the wok along with the reserved oyster sauce mixture, green onions, and pickled ginger. Stir-fry until the beef is just cooked through and the pickled ginger is well distributed, about 30 to 60 seconds. Serve with steamed rice.

Dinosaurs. Amusement Park. Tourists. Disaster.

Jurassic World encompasses all of them.

Of course, I had to experience it.

The opening is filled with potential, and it sets high expectations for the impending disaster. When it occurs, there are impressive action scenes, particularly involving the glass ball containing a soft, chewy child center.

However, the conclusion spirals into sheer nonsense.

This leads us to the final act: shut down your mind before watching it begin.

Phases of matter are conventionally characterized by order parameters
describing the type and degree of order in a system. For example, crystals
consist of spatially ordered arrays of atoms, an order that is lost as the
crystal melts. Like- wise in ferromagnets, the magnetic moments of the
constituent particles align only below the Curie temperature, TC. These two
examples reflect two classes of phase transitions: the melting of a crystal is
a first-order phase transition (the crystalline order vanishes abruptly) and
the onset of magnetism is a second- order phase transition (the magnetization
increases continuously from zero as the temperature falls below TC). Such
magnetism is robust in systems with localized magnetic particles, and yet rare
in model itinerant systems where the particles are free to move about. Here for
the first time, we explore the itinerant magnetic phases present in a spin-1
spin-orbit coupled atomic Bose gas; in this system, itinerant ferromagnetic
order is stabilized by the spin-orbit coupling, vanishing in its absence. We
first located a second-order phase transition that continuously stiffens until,
at a tricritical point, it transforms into a first- order transition (with
observed width as small as h x 4 Hz). We then studied the long-lived metastable
states associated with the first-order transition. These measurements are all
in agreement with theory.

In his foul mind, slugs and mud stirred,  
A flickering flame danced in his bent gaze,  
His form held a rat where men nurtured hope.  
The world shimmered with green eyes of a cat,  
Bare of its former strength, faded and worn,  
Upon the frail and broken, the bruised and lame,  
He sprawled, a brute of steel, to tear them further.  
Yet when one dared to strike, with briny might,  
Cowering became the path to ease these blows,  
And he would bear the weight of those who came after.  
What glory lies in God’s hollow praise?  
Your riches are but his craft to make death cruel.  
Your strong limbs suffer more in their breaking.  
And he has sold your beauty too cheap, though you perish to be sold.  
He knows nothing of sleep, and when the cats emerge, the rats are wary.  
We are safe until he creeps in at dusk,  
But he has gnawed a root, and in the dawn, a spark fades.  
Not all things are strange, nor do strange things fade.  
Ah! if the day were dry, lost within us,  
Yet it is as our hair, and only in the stillness does it stir.  
In the light, doubt lifts and flees, yet unrest lingers over the lost paths.  
Fingers close on voices that pass by,  
Where silent farewells are embraced so freely...  
Ah! this rot of a god, this miasmic gloom!

British film director Sir Alan Parker has been made an officer in the Order of Arts and Letters, one of France's highest cultural honours.
Sir Alan received his decoration in Paris on Wednesday from French Culture Minister Renaud Donnedieu de Vabres. "You have explored the possibilities of film with an immense talent," Mr de Vabres said as he presented the award. Parker praised French films, saying: "Hollywood, which created modern cinema, uses it only as a commodity." He told the minister: "I am honoured to be thus distinguished by France, the flag carrier of cinema throughout the world." Sir Alan's films include Oscar-winning Fame plus Midnight Express and The Commitments.
A founding member of the Director's Guild of Great Britain, he is a former chairman of the UK Film Council and on the board of the British Film Institute. "Through your work and your campaigns, you have shown us how the artist occupies an essential place in our contemporary society," Mr de Vabres said. "Through your dreams which you show us, through the links that you weave, you question the world through the mirror of your work." He also cited the director's 2003 film The Life of David Gale, in which Kevin Spacey played a man on Death Row, as proof of his "veritable artistic commitment against the death sentence".

Men said at vespers: 'All is well!'
In one wild night the city fell;
Fell shrines of prayer and marts of gain
Before the fiery hurricane.
On threescore spires had sunset shone,
Where ghastly sunrise looked on none.
Men clasped each other's hands, and said
'The City of the West is dead!'
Brave hearts who fought, in slow retreat,
The fiends of fire from street to street,
Turned, powerless, to the blinding glare,
The dumb defiance of despair.
A sudden impulse thrilled each wire
That signalled round that sea of fire;
Swift words of cheer, warm heart-throbs came;
In tears of pity died the flame!
From East, from West, from South and North,
The messages of hope shot forth,
And, underneath the severing wave,
The world, full-handed, reached to save.
Fair seemed the old; but fairer still
The new, the dreary void shall fill
With dearer homes than those o'erthrown,
For love shall lay each corner-stone.
Rise, stricken city! from thee throw
The ashen sackcloth of thy woe;
And build, as to Amphion's strain,
To songs of cheer thy walls again!
How shrivelled in thy hot distress
The primal sin of selfishness!
How instant rose, to take thy part,
The angel in the human heart!
Ah! not in vain the flames that tossed
Above thy dreadful holocaust;
The Christ again has preached through thee
The Gospel of Humanity!
Then lift once more thy towers on high,
And fret with spires the western sky,
To tell that God is yet with us,
And love is still miraculous!

In biological cells and novel diagnostic devices biochemical receptors need
to be sensitive to extremely small concentration changes of signaling
molecules. The accuracy of such molecular signaling is ultimately limited by
the counting noise imposed by the thermal diffusion of molecules. Many
macromolecules and organelles transiently bind to molecular motors and are then
actively transported. We here show that a random albeit directed delivery of
signaling molecules to within a typical diffusion distance to the receptor
reduces the correlation time of the counting noise, effecting an improved
sensing precision. The conditions for this active focusing are indeed
compatible with observations in living cells. Our results are relevant for a
better understanding of molecular cellular signaling and the design of novel
diagnostic devices.

Constructing a connectome from electron microscopy data involves identifying neurons and determining synaptic connections between them. Due to the high workload involved in manually extracting this information, there has been significant interest in developing automated methods to segment neurons and guide manual tracing. However, relatively little research has focused on automatically detecting actual synapses between neurons. This gap may stem from factors such as the necessity of obtaining neuronal shapes as the initial step, the greater time required for manual tracing compared to synapse annotation, and the use of neuronal contact areas as a proxy for synapses in connectivity analysis.

Recent studies have shown that contact area alone is insufficient for predicting synaptic connections. Additionally, as segmentation becomes more accurate, the proportion of time spent on synapse annotation increases, leading to diminishing returns in speed improvements. To address this challenge, we develop algorithms that automatically detect pre-synaptic neurons and their corresponding post-synaptic partners. Specifically, pre-synaptic structures are identified using a Deep and Wide Multiscale Recursive Network, while post-synaptic partners are detected using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with features conditioned on local segmentation.

This work is innovative as it requires minimal training, utilizes advancements in image segmentation, and offers a comprehensive solution for polyadic synapse detection. We also introduce new metrics to assess our algorithm on large-scale connectomes, demonstrating that complete automation can accurately represent most connectivity patterns.

Even though the plot has a little too much room to move around, I wish they had played it out at a slower tempo.

Overall, I think the movie is a brilliant work that will keep audiences guessing throughout.

Ingredients:
- 1 block of firm tofu
- 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro
- 1/4 cup of chopped scallions
- 2 cloves of minced garlic
- 1 tablespoon of soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil
- 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon of sesame oil
- 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper
- 6 egg roll wrappers
- 1 avocado
- Salt

Instructions:
1. Drain the tofu and cut it into small cubes.
2. In a pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and add the minced garlic.
3. Once the garlic is fragrant, add the chopped scallions and black pepper.
4. Add the cubed tofu to the pan and cook for about 5 minutes until it is lightly browned.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and salt to taste.
6. Pour the sauce over the tofu and stir to coat.
7. Add the chopped cilantro and stir to combine.
8. Lay out the egg roll wrappers and place a spoonful of the tofu mixture in the center of each wrapper.
9. Slice the avocado and place a few slices on top of the tofu mixture.
10. Fold the wrapper over the tofu mixture and tuck in the sides.
11. Roll the egg roll tightly and seal the end with a little water.
12. Heat a pan with vegetable oil over medium heat and add the egg rolls.
13. Cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown.
14. Serve the egg rolls with your favorite dipping sauce and enjoy!

Let D be a bounded domain in n-dimensional Eucledian space with a smooth
boundary. We indicate appropriate Sobolev spaces of negative smoothness to
study the non-homogeneous Cauchy problem for an elliptic differential complex
{A_i} of first order operators. In particular, we describe traces on the
boundary of tangential part t_i (u) and normal part n_i(u) of a
(vector)-function u from the corresponding Sobolev space and give an adequate
formulation of the problem. If the Laplacians of the complex satisfy the
uniqueness condition in the small then we obtain necessary and sufficient
solvability conditions of the problem and produce formulae for its exact and
approximate solutions. For the Cauchy problem in the Lebesgue spaces L^2(D) we
construct the approximate and exact solutions to the Cauchy problem with
maximal possible regularity. Moreover, using Hilbert space methods, we
construct Carleman's formulae for a (vector-) function u from the Sobolev space
H^1(D) by its Cauchy data t_i (u) on a subset S on the boundary of the domain D
and the values of A_i u in D modulo the null-space of the Cauchy problem. Some
instructive examples for elliptic complexes of operators with constant
coefficients are considered.

In this study, we introduce a novel category of Dynamic Mixture Models (DAMMs) that can dynamically adjust their mixture components and composition based on data-derived information. This information-driven approach enables precise computation of the overall likelihood and eliminates the need for computationally demanding simulation methods. A comprehensive Monte Carlo analysis demonstrates that the newly introduced model effectively approximates complex stochastic dynamic mixture models, including various other types of models. The characteristics of the proposed model are analyzed within the paper, and an application in financial econometrics is presented.

4 ounces bittersweet (not unsweetened) or semisweet chocolate, chopped  
3/4 cup sugar  
6 tablespoons (3/4 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature  
1 teaspoon vanilla extract  
6 large eggs, separated  
1/2 cup poppy seeds, ground (about 3 1/4 ounces)  
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour  
Powdered sugar  
Whipped cream  
Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter and flour a 9-inch diameter spring-form pan with 2 3/4-inch high sides. Melt 4 ounces bittersweet chocolate in a double boiler set over simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and let cool for 10 minutes. In a large bowl, mix 3/4 cup sugar, unsalted butter, and vanilla extract. Add egg yolks one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Incorporate melted bittersweet chocolate, then add poppy seeds. Use an electric mixer with clean dry beaters to whip the egg whites until stiff but not dry. Fold half of the whipped egg whites into the chocolate mixture, then incorporate the remaining egg whites and flour. Combine everything and pour into the prepared pan. Smooth the top with a spatula. Bake for 45 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let it cool completely. (It can be made 1 day in advance. Wrap tightly and store at room temperature.) Cut around the sides of the pan to release the cake. Remove the sides. Dust the cake with powdered sugar and serve with whipped cream.

Andrea Arnold, an Oscar-winning filmmaker, has received congratulations from the UK Film Council, an organization that partially supported her project. Arnold’s film *Wasp* secured the best live-action short film award on Sunday. Chief executive officer John Woodward of the UK Film Council stated, “The organization invests millions in short filmmaking annually through lottery funds.” He noted that it is rewarding to see emerging filmmakers receive such esteemed recognition.

*Wasp*, which was produced with support from the Film Council and Channel 4, outperformed entries by other UK nominees, Gary McKendry and Ashvin Kumar, to win the prize. The film features actress Nathalie Press, who portrayed a single mother in *My Summer Of Love*, a Bafta-winning drama, who must take extreme measures after being invited to a date without a babysitter for her four children. The film has garnered over 30 international accolades, including the Sundance Short Film Prize. Arnold, based in Dartford, Kent, expressed that her win was “truly overwhelming,” stating, “I’m not used to this kind of achievement,” after receiving her Oscar from Jeremy Irons. She thanked those involved, saying the beers would be on her when they returned home. The director was one of only two British winners at the event, the other being Sandy Powell, who won the costume design Oscar for her work on *The Aviator*.

Draft Day is a riveting sports drama that takes viewers behind the scenes of one of the most intense and high-stakes events in American football - the NFL draft. The film follows the story of Sonny Weaver, the general manager of the Cleveland Browns, as he navigates through the complex web of trades, negotiations, and tough decisions that come with selecting the best young talent to join his team.

The cast is led by Kevin Costner, who delivers a powerful performance as Sonny. He captures the intensity and determination of a man who has dedicated his life to building a winning football team, while also showing the human side of someone who faces immense pressure and scrutiny. His chemistry with Jennifer Garner, who plays his daughter, is heartwarming and adds depth to the story.

Director Ivan Reitman does an excellent job of creating tension and suspense throughout the film. The pacing is just right, allowing for moments of quiet reflection and character development without losing the momentum of the story. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the energy and excitement of the draft room and the city of Cleveland.

One of the standout aspects of Draft Day is its portrayal of the relationships between the characters. From Sonny's strained relationship with his wife to the bond between him and his daughter, the film explores themes of family, loyalty, and sacrifice. These relationships add emotional depth to the story and make the stakes even higher.

Overall, Draft Day is a must-see for football fans and anyone who enjoys a well-crafted drama. It's a thrilling ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

For many, many days together
The wind blew steady from the East;
For many days hot grew the weather,
About the time of our Lady's Feast.
For many days we rode together,
Yet met we neither friend nor foe;
Hotter and clearer grew the weather,
Steadily did the East wind blow.
We saw the trees in the hot, bright weather,
Clear-cut, with shadows very black,
As freely we rode on together
With helms unlaced and bridles slack.
And often, as we rode together,
We, looking down the green-bank'd stream,
Saw flowers in the sunny weather,
And saw the bubble-making bream.
And in the night lay down together,
And hung above our heads the rood,
Or watch'd night-long in the dewy weather,
The while the moon did watch the wood.
Our spears stood bright and thick together,
Straight out the banners stream'd behind,
As we gallop'd on in the sunny weather,
With faces turn'd towards the wind.
Down sank our threescore spears together,
As thick we saw the pagans ride;
His eager face in the clear fresh weather,
Shone out that last time by my side.
Up the sweep of the bridge we dash'd together,
It rock'd to the crash of the meeting spears,
Down rain'd the buds of the dear spring weather,
The elm-tree flowers fell like tears.
There, as we roll'd and writhed together,
I threw my arms above my head,
For close by my side, in the lovely weather,
I saw him reel and fall back dead.
I and the slayer met together,
He waited the death-stroke there in his place,
With thoughts of death, in the lovely weather,
Gapingly mazed at my madden'd face.
Madly I fought as we fought together;
In vain: the little Christian band
The pagans drown'd, as in stormy weather
The river drowns low-lying land.
They bound my blood-stain'd hands together,
They bound his corpse to nod by my side:
Then on we rode, in the bright March weather,
With clash of cymbals did we ride.
We ride no more, no more together;
My prison-bars are thick and strong,
I take no heed of any weather,
The sweet Saints grant I live not long.

Marigold Lesley is a creative young girl whose father passed away before she was born. She lived at her grandfather's estate, Cloud of Spruce. Marigold's family consists of her affectionate yet authoritative mother, a strong-willed grandmother, a shrewd older grandmother, her uncle Klondike, a former sailor, and her aunt Marigold, a doctor who saved her life as a baby. Due to this, the Lesleys named Marigold after her aunt and uncle Klondike got married to her. These relationships brought Marigold a generally happy and carefree upbringing, though she still experienced various adventures, interests, and challenges tied to the unique setting she grew up in. The novel explores Marigold's persistent envy of her father's first wife, Clementine; a meeting with a Russian princess; multiple efforts to behave well; and an unexpected success in cooking. A significant part of Marigold's imagination was Sylvia, her idealized playmate she cherished deeply, who often replaced real friends in her life. However, as Marigold matured and faced difficulties with boys, she eventually had to let go of Sylvia and her youthful days.

I've had this experience before. For me it was sort of a psychological block on getting the music going in a direction that didn't fit the lyrics, so the music was locked into a certain rhythm/melody that I knew was "wrong" for the lyrics, but I couldn't break out of it... sometimes you just have to walk away for a while and come back to it later. Sometimes it means the melody/rhythm you're writing simply isn't right for the lyrics, and you have to scrap it and start over from scratch.

As others have said, it can be helpful to jam on the chords and see if anything new presents itself, or to start singing random notes or lyrics over the chords (exactly what you were doing), until something clicks.

For others, it can help to talk/sing the lyrics aloud as if you're having a conversation, and then sing/speak the tones/rhythms of your speech back into a melody.

Sometimes when I'm really stuck in this situation, I'll reduce the lyrics to just a few key words, or even a single word, and use that as the seed for the melody. I find that once I have a good melody, I can usually modify it to fit the actual lyrics, if I need to.

What more could be said about Raimi's iconic cult classic, which has already been thoroughly discussed, except perhaps nothing? I'll attempt to offer something new. Before Spider-Man and the many spin-offs of this film were developed or even imagined, Raimi and his team crafted a low-budget zombie movie purely for enjoyment, and remarkably, it has evolved into a standout example of horror excellence. A prime illustration of how to create an engaging film on a limited budget, The Evil Dead delivers on its promise—unparalleled in its relentless horror. Despite its modest budget and occasionally shaky performances, it mesmerizes viewers with its chilling ambiance and intense special effects. Those who find themselves overwhelmed may want to skip this one; after all, the sheer terror it evokes is worth the risk. In fact, if you're afraid of anything, just flee.

The film's success stems from multiple factors. Chief among them is Raimi's exceptional direction. By employing quick cuts and dynamic angles, he crafts an unsettling environment that, though often difficult to look at, is irresistible to watch. His unique style is instantly recognizable, particularly evident in the film's opening sequence, where the camera itself builds tension and suspense, making you anxious for what's next. At times, you might wish the scenes would end to avoid the relentless gore and violence, yet you can't help but enjoy the thrill. One of the most striking moments occurs when shadows from the trees begin chasing individuals, collapsing any object in their path. Truly remarkable technical execution.

TED also excels in pacing and atmosphere, enhancing the overall experience as the action unfolds. Some sequences stretch on for what feels like forever, offering both frustration and satisfaction. The film's most unforgettable shot involves darkness from the trees pursuing people, causing obstructions to fall. An awe-inspiring technique, executed with precision.

Families of steady states of the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system
are constructed, which are parametrized by the central redshift. It is shown
that as the central redshift tends to zero, the states in such a family are
well approximated by a steady state of the Vlasov-Poisson system, i.e., a
Newtonian limit is established where the speed of light is kept constant as it
should be and the limiting behavior is analyzed in terms of a parameter which
is tied to the physical properties of the individual solutions. This result is
then used to investigate the stability properties of the relativistic steady
states with small redshift parameter in the spirit of recent work by the same
authors, i.e., the second variation of the ADM mass about such a steady state
is shown to be positive definite on a suitable class of states.

1 kg beef brisket

2 tomatoes, cleaned, seeded, cut into ¾ inch pieces

1 onion, thinly sliced

1 celery stalk, cut into ¾ inch lengths

1 large carrot, peeled and cut into ¾ inch pieces

1 garlic clove, peeled and chopped

2 cups chopped, dried (about 1 lemon), red tomatoes

2 large red peppers (e.g. a red/kalamata), seeded and cut into ¾ inch pieces

1 tsp each of oregano, salt, pepper

2 tsp basil

3 tbsp olive oil

1 tbsp freshly ground black pepper

4 tbsp honey

1 cup low fat ricotta cheese (about 30 gms), divided

2 tbsp chopped fresh basil

1 tbsp chopped parsley (optional, add to taste)

fresh ground black pepper to taste

salt and pepper to taste

In a large frying pan, brown the beef brisket in the olive oil with the celery, onion, and garlic over a high heat for 4-5 minutes, removing most of the fat from the pan. Add the tomatoes, peppers, basil, oregano, salt, pepper and honey and toss to combine. Next add half the beef to the pan, cover with the remaining tomato mixture, turn the heat up to medium-high, then cook for another three minutes, or until the beef is cooked completely. In a large bowl, mix together the cheese and half the meat mixture, and then add the remaining meat mixture and half the cheese mixture. The Alden staRRcar, short for "Self-Transport Road and Rail Car", was a personal rapid transit (PRT) system designed by William Alden in the 1960s. It originally envisioned small electrically powered cars suitable for short distance trips at low speed within urban areas, which could optionally merge onto tracks that would provide power and guidance for high-speed travel over longer inter-city distances. It was one of the earliest dual-mode vehicles to be proposed, and one of the earliest to be actually built. Over its lifetime the design changed dramatically, originally a four-person vehicle with dual-mode operation but eventually emerging as a much larger people mover for 20 people. In this form, Boeing Vertol was awarded a construction contract in 1970 to build a demonstration system in Morgantown, West Virginia. A smaller system was also built by their licensee, Kobe Steel, and installed at the Expo '75 on Okinawa (as well as the more advanced CVS). The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system first opened for service in 1975, and with the exception of a closure for a major expansion, has remained in service since then.

This paper introduces Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRW-Net) for semantic image segmentation as a combination of convolutional neural networks, random walks on graphs and spectral graph theory. The basic idea is to extend the receptive field of a neural network's convolutional layer at a minimal cost. Given a CNN, CRW-Net extends the receptive field by one convolutional layer which has random connections to the original CNN's convolutional layers. The randomness comes from the random choice of edges in Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs). To solve the issue of overfitting in GCN-based models, We proposed a loss function called graph spectral loss. We empirically show that the proposed method can improve segmentation performance when it is combined with fully connected CRF on PASCAL VOC 2012 (segmentation accuracy 71.2\%), VOCS (segmentation accuracy 77.1\%) and COCO-Stuff (segmentation accuracy 51.2\%). Our proposed method achieved the state-of-the-art performance on COCO-Stuff, outperformed the previous best result by more than 3\%.

The above text was extracted from a page on the arxiv.org website (https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06107). I've seen researchers reference arxiv.org, but I've always wondered how people use this resource. Do the papers get cited on Google Scholar? If not, what is the primary use case for authors to release papers on arxiv.org?

A: ArXiv is not a publication venue; it is an archive.  They have an agreement that once an author publishes on the archive, he/she will not post the work elsewhere for at least a month, which is why you see one-month "first notice of use."  That protects the author in case somebody sees the work, then publishes something on it earlier.

A: The primary use of arxiv is to provide a quick way for researchers to distribute their work to a large audience before peer review. Once posted, the paper can be immediately cited, discussed, etc., while the researchers work on tweaking / fixing their paper.
For example, if an author finds a minor error in their arXiv posted paper, they can make the corrections and repost it

Over the last ten years, deep convolutional neural networks have been extensively used for medical image segmentation and demonstrated satisfactory results. However, these models suffer from an inability to capture long-range dependencies within the images due to their inherent inductive biases. Recent transformer-based architectures that utilize self-attention mechanisms can effectively handle long-range dependencies and learn highly expressive representations. This leads us to investigate the potential of employing transformer-based architectures for medical image segmentation tasks. Most existing transformer-based architectures for vision applications necessitate large datasets for proper training. In contrast, medical imaging datasets typically contain fewer data points, posing challenges in training transformers for such applications. To address this, we introduce a Gated Axial-Attention model that enhances existing architectures by incorporating an additional control element in the self-attention module. Additionally, we develop a Local-Global training strategy (LoGo) to improve model performance on medical images. Specifically, we process entire images and their patches separately to learn both global and local features. The proposed Medical Transformer (MedT) has been tested on three distinct medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional convolutional and related transformer-based architectures. Twenty-eight unshrouded young women were bathing by the shore or near a wooded lake's edge.  
Twenty-eight girls, all attractive, worthy of Mack Sennett's film and Florenz Ziegfield's Fool's Folly.  
They played and swam with the innocent joy of youth and beauty,  
Fully immersed in the purest spontaneity and vibrancy of summer awareness.  
Enhanced and deepened by the gentle touch of water,  
Their allure heightened by the softness and silkiness of the surface,  
Bathed in the energy ignited by their nudity,  
Elevated: revered: undeniable.  
A man of thirty gazed upon them from afar.  
He lived in the prison of ten million dollars.  
He was wealthy, handsome, and hollow, watching them from behind the curtain.  
Which girl does he find most appealing?  
All are equally beautiful and desirable from a distance.  
For if poverty dulls judgment and makes perception more acute,  
Then the gleam of wealth is also a kind of blindness.  
For has not a Frenchman said, "Though this is America...  
What he has said is not entirely relevant,  
That a naked woman is proof of God's existence?"  
Where is he heading?  
Will he join them in splashing and laughing?  
They did not notice him, though he noticed them and was among them.  
He saw them as he would not have seen them had they been aware of him or of men in complete degradation:  
This is his enchantment and impoverishment,  
As he possesses them only through gaze.  
He felt the wood's secrecy, knew the June warmth,  
The heat around him held by the mansard roof,  
He glimpsed the shadowy light on last year's brittle leaves,  
Looked over and overlooked, glimpsed by the fall of death,  
Winter's sorrow and May's renewal.

Fiat's board has approved a deal to give GM a $2.8bn (£1.7bn) stake in its auto business, clearing a major obstacle to a merger of the two carmakers.

The deal had been delayed as Fiat's board debated GM's offer and fought off a rival bid from Ford.

The merger will create the world's third-biggest carmaker by sales.

The combined company will be called Fiat-GM and be headed by Fiat's CEO, Sergio Marchionne.

The deal must still be approved by regulators and shareholders.

If it goes through, GM will get a 20% stake in Fiat, while Fiat will get a 1.5% stake in GM.

The companies said the deal would save them $2.8bn a year by 2015.

The merger has been approved by the boards of both companies but still needs the go-ahead from regulators and shareholders.

If the merger is approved, the new company would be worth about $140bn, based on the companies' current market values.

By comparison, Toyota is currently the world's biggest carmaker with sales of 10.2 million vehicles last year, followed by Volkswagen with 8.3 million.

Fiat-GM would sell about 8.6 million cars a year.

The merger deal comes as the auto industry struggles to recover from a sharp drop in sales in the US and Europe.

The combined company will have about $132bn in debt, ranking it as one of the most indebted companies in the world.

GM sold a record 4.7 million cars and trucks in 2010 but analysts say it needs to expand to survive as sales growth slows in its main markets.

Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornmeal
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 package (2 1/4 teaspoons) active dry yeast
- 1 cup warm water (110°F)
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 cup pizza sauce
- 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
- 1/2 cup sliced pepperoni
- 1/4 cup sliced black olives (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced green bell peppers (optional)
- 1/4 cup sliced red onions (optional)
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- Fresh basil leaves for garnish (optional)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, salt, and sugar. In a separate small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5 minutes until it becomes frothy.

2. Pour the yeast mixture and olive oil into the dry ingredients. Stir until a dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour. If it's too dry, add a little more water. Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.

3. Grease a deep-dish pizza pan or a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil. Press the dough into the pan, making sure to cover the bottom and sides evenly. Let the dough rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes until it doubles in size.

4. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Once the dough has risen, spread the pizza sauce evenly over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges. Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce.

5. Arrange the pepperoni slices on top of the cheese. If desired, add black olives, green bell peppers, and red onions as additional toppings. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the toppings.

6. Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is bubbly and slightly browned.

7. Remove the pizza from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh basil leaves if desired. Slice and serve hot.

Enjoy your delicious homemade Pepperoni Deep-Dish Pizza!

The KDB said the investment was aimed at helping Hanvit improve its financial structure and maintain its role as a leading credit card provider in the country. The fund will also provide Hanvit with a loan of up to 50 billion won to help the company stabilize its cash flow.

Hanvit's chief executive officer, Kim In-seok, welcomed the investment andsaid the company would use the funds to strengthen its internal management and diversify its business portfolio.

The rescue of Hanvit comes amid a wider government effort to shore up South Korea's troubled finance sector. Last month, the government injected $5.3 billion into troubled lender Shinhan Bank to prevent its collapse.

This approach directly yields the classical Maxwell equations but also extends their conceptual framework by incorporating charge density, mass density, and the four-velocity, which defines the motion of charges based on geometric principles. These geometric interpretations echo the concept of mass in General Relativity, where mass is associated with the scalar curvature $ R $. This suggests the potential development of gravity. Specific solutions from the proposed theory are analyzed to examine the unification of electromagnetic and gravitational effects, alongside their connection to analogous solutions derived from the classical Maxwell and Einstein field equations.

Deep learning techniques for 3D brain vessel image segmentation have not been
as successful as in the segmentation of other organs and tissues. This can be
explained by two factors. First, deep learning techniques tend to show poor
performances at the segmentation of relatively small objects compared to the
size of the full image. Second, due to the complexity of vascular trees and the
small size of vessels, it is challenging to obtain the amount of annotated
training data typically needed by deep learning methods. To address these
problems, we propose a novel annotation-efficient deep learning vessel
segmentation framework. The framework avoids pixel-wise annotations, only
requiring weak patch-level labels to discriminate between vessel and non-vessel
2D patches in the training set, in a setup similar to the CAPTCHAs used to
differentiate humans from bots in web applications. The user-provided weak
annotations are used for two tasks: 1) to synthesize pixel-wise pseudo-labels
for vessels and background in each patch, which are used to train a
segmentation network, and 2) to train a classifier network. The classifier
network allows to generate additional weak patch labels, further reducing the
annotation burden, and it acts as a noise filter for poor quality images. We
use this framework for the segmentation of the cerebrovascular tree in
Time-of-Flight angiography (TOF) and Susceptibility-Weighted Images (SWI). The
results show that the framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, while
reducing the annotation time by ~77% w.r.t. learning-based segmentation methods
using pixel-wise labels for training.

The legendary Dutch coach Rinus Michels, known as "the General," passed away at the age of 77. He is credited with creating "total football" and led the Dutch national team at the 1974 World Cup, where they reached the final but lost 2-1 to Germany. Later, he guided the team to win the 1988 European Championship with a 2-0 victory against the Soviet Union. Michels played for Ajax and coached the team to four national titles and a European Cup during the period 1965–71. His 1970s squad, centered around Johan Cruyff and Johan Neeskens, popularized "total football," emphasizing teamwork and individual creativity. Cruyff orchestrated the team’s play, allowing players to rotate in and out of defense and executing innovative attacking strategies. Michels had recently undergone heart surgery, and a spokesperson from the Dutch football federation stated that he was one of the best coaches in history. He also spent time at Barcelona, FC Cologne, and Bayer Leverkusen, taking them to league titles. In 1999, he was named the FIFA Coach of the Century, and he earned five caps for the Netherlands as a hard-driving center forward. Dutch sports minister Clemence Ross-van Dorp praised him as the man who, alongside Cruyff, helped make Dutch football prominent.

General Sir John Gordon Noel Wilton,  (22 November 1910 – 10 May 1981) was a senior commander in the Australian Army. He served as Chief of the General Staff (CGS), the Army's professional head, from 1963 until 1966, and as Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (CCOSC), forerunner of the role of Australia's Chief of the Defence Force, from 1966 until 1970. His eight-year tenure as senior officer of first the Army and then the Australian military spanned almost the entire period of the nation's involvement in the Vietnam War. Born in Sydney, Wilton entered the Royal Military College, Duntroon, in 1927. Owing to lack of opportunity in the Australian military at the time, he took a commission in the British Army following his graduation in 1930. He spent most of the remainder of the decade with the Royal Artillery in India. Wilton returned to Australia on the eve of World War II and was commissioned into the Royal Australian Artillery. He saw action with the 7th Division in Syria and the 3rd Division in New Guinea, earning a mention in despatches in the former campaign and the Distinguished Service Order in the latter.  Finishing the war a temporary colonel, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1947. Wilton was posted to Korea in 1953 to take command of the 28th Commonwealth Brigade, leading it in its final action of the war in July. He was raised to Commander of the Order of the British Empire and awarded the US Legion of Merit for his performance in Korea.

Bradley Sinopoli (born April 14, 1988) is a former Canadian football wide receiver who played for nine years in the Canadian Football League (CFL). He was originally a quarterback with the Calgary Stampeders before being converted to wide receiver in 2013. He then joined the Ottawa Redblacks where he was twice named the CFL's Most Outstanding Canadian, was named an East Division All-Star three times, and a CFL All-Star in 2018. He won two Grey Cup championships, after winning with the Stampeders in 2014 and with the Redblacks in 2016, the latter of which he was also named the game's Most Valuable Canadian. Sinopoli played CIS football for the Ottawa Gee-Gees from 2007 to 2010. In 2010, Sinopoli became the fourth Gee-Gee player to win the Hec Crighton Trophy after passing for a school record and CIS leading 2,756 passing yards and 22 touchdowns in eight games. Because of his strong season, he was one of only two quarterbacks invited to the CFL Evaluation Camp for players eligible in the 2011 CFL Draft.

Toronado, born on 20 February 2010, is an Irish-bred and British-trained Thoroughbred racehorse. In 2012, he was one of the top British two-year-olds, claiming three victories including the Champagne Stakes at Doncaster. On his three-year-old debut, he won the Craven Stakes and became a favorite for the 2000 Guineas and Epsom Derby. In 2013, he competed against Dawn Approach and won the Sussex Stakes, marking his most significant victory. In 2014, he triumphed in the Queen Anne Stakes but lost to Kingman in the Sussex Stakes and to Charm Spirit in the Prix du Moulin, finishing unplaced when favored for the Breeders' Cup Mile.

Toronado is a bay colt with a white blaze and white socks on his front legs, bred in Ireland by Paul Nataf. His father, High Chaparral, won The Derby in 2002 and the Breeders' Cup Turf in 2002 and 2003. As a stallion, he is renowned for siring So You Think. His mother, Wana Doo, is a Kentucky-bred mare who won two races in France. Wana Doo is a half-sister to Casamento, who won the Racing Post Trophy in 2010. She is a descendant of Regal Lady, a half-sister to the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner Vaguely Noble.

> We introduce VisDA, a new benchmark dataset and challenge to evaluate domain adaptation algorithms in visual recognition tasks. It consists of 152 classes with 300k images collected from ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) and Pascal VOC 2012 datasets. Each class has two domains: synthetic rendered images and real world photos. This setup allows us to study how well an algorithm can adapt between different rendering styles or between different sensors such as RGB cameras and depth sensors. In addition, we provide a set of evaluation protocols that are designed to be challenging but fair. Our goal is to encourage researchers to develop more robust models by evaluating them on this new benchmark.

We examine the lexicographically smallest infinite $ \frac{a}{b} $-power-free word over the set of non-negative integers. This word often serves as a fixed point of a uniform morphism or is closely related to one. For instance, the lexicographically smallest $ \frac{7}{4} $-power-free word is a fixed point of a $ 50847 $-uniform morphism. We determine the structural properties of the lexicographically smallest $ \frac{a}{b} $-power-free word for three classes of rational numbers $ \frac{a}{b} $, along with several sporadic rationals that do not fit into general categories. To achieve this, we create an automated method for verifying $ \frac{a}{b} $-power-freeness for morphisms of specific forms, including both explicit and symbolic rational numbers $ \frac{a}{b} $. Ultimately, we connect these results to words on a finite alphabet. Specifically, the lexicographically smallest $ \frac{27}{23} $-power-free word is indeed a word on the finite alphabet $ \{0, 1, 2\} $, and its sequence of letters follows a $ 353 $-automatic pattern.

In a major breakthrough for the fight against software piracy, four Americans have been convicted of engaging in widespread copyright infringement by operating a pirate website. After a seven-day trial, a federal jury in Texas found Denelle Dixon, David Bodher, Jeff Lundqvist, and Matthew Smith all guilty of conspiracy to commit copyright infringement. 

The four defendants were the masterminds behind a popular peer-to-peer file-sharing website called "MegaUpload," which allowed users to store and share files, including copyrighted content such as movies, TV shows, music, and software, without permission from the copyright holders. The site was shut down by the FBI in 2012 following an investigation that revealed the massive scale of copyright infringement taking place on the site. 

The jury found that the defendants were aware of the widespread copyright infringement taking place on MegaUpload but took no meaningful action to prevent it. In a statement, the U.S. Attorney's Office said that the defendants "made a profit by encouraging, promoting, and assisting the widespread distribution of copyrighted materials without the permission of the copyright owners." 

The four defendants face a maximum sentence of five years in prison and significant financial penalties for their role in operating MegaUpload. The sentencing hearing is scheduled for later this year.

The co-occurrence of visual patterns enables the aggregation of contextual information, which serves as a standard approach to improve pixel representations for semantic image segmentation. Current methodologies primarily focus on extracting context from the entire image, such as aggregating image-level contextual data. Although these methods show promise, they diminish the importance of pixel representations within the same category, referred to as semantic-level contextual information. To counteract this limitation, this study introduces a method that enhances pixel representations by incorporating both image-level and semantic-level contextual information. Initially, an image-level context module is developed to capture contextual information for each pixel in the overall image. Subsequently, for each pixel, the representations of the same category are aggregated, with the categories being learned through ground-truth segmentation supervision. Finally, the similarity between each pixel's representation and the respective image- and semantic-level contextual information is calculated. The resulting pixel representation is then augmented using the computed similarities as weights, combining both types of contextual information. By integrating image-level and semantic-level contexts, this paper achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmark datasets: ADE20K, LIP, COCOStuff, and Cityscapes.

The abstract of the paper "Higher Order Differentiation over Finite Fields with Applications to Generalising the Cube Attack" could look something like this:

In this paper, we explore the concept of higher order differentiation over finite fields and its applications in cryptography, specifically in the context of generalizing the cube attack. We introduce a new technique for computing higher order derivatives of functions over finite fields, which enables us to analyze and improve the security of cryptographic primitives.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique by applying it to several examples of cryptographic functions, including the S-box and the AES encryption algorithm. Our results show that higher order differentiation can be a powerful tool for analyzing and breaking cryptographic primitives, and that our technique provides a significant improvement over existing methods.

Furthermore, we use our technique to generalize the cube attack, a well-known attack on block ciphers, to a higher order attack that can break more rounds of the encryption algorithm. Our results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach, and highlight the importance of considering higher order differential properties in the design and analysis of cryptographic primitives.

Overall, our work provides a new perspective on the study of cryptographic functions and their differential properties, and demonstrates the potential of higher order differentiation as a tool for analyzing and improving the security of cryptographic primitives.
