The old woman sits on a bench before the door and quarrels
With her meagre pale demoralized daughter.
Once when I passed I found her alone, laughing in the sun
And saying that when she was first married
She lived in the old farmhouse up Garapatas Canyon.
(It is empty now, the roof has fallen
But the log walls hang on the stone foundation; the redwoods
Have all been cut down, the oaks are standing;
The place is now more solitary than ever before.)
'When I was nursing my second baby
My husband found a day-old fawn hid in a fern-brake
And brought it; I put its mouth to the breast
Rather than let it starve, I had milk enough for three babies.
Hey how it sucked, the little nuzzler,
Digging its little hoofs like quills into my stomach.
I had more joy from that than from the others.'
Her face is deformed with age, furrowed like a bad road
With market-wagons, mean cares and decay.
She is thrown up to the surface of things, a cell of dry skin
Soon to be shed from the earth's old eye-brows,
I see that once in her spring she lived in the streaming arteries,
The stir of the world, the music of the mountain.

Fairfield is a borough in Adams County, Pennsylvania, United States. The population was 507 at the 2010 census. History
During the Gettysburg Campaign in the American Civil War, the Battle of Fairfield played an important role in securing the Fairfield pass and the Hagerstown Road,  enabling Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia to retreat through Fairfield towards the Potomac River. The actual fighting near Fairfield was between elements of the 6th United States Cavalry under Major Samuel Starr, and elements of General "Grumble" Jones' Brigade of Virginia Cavalry. The Union casualties were treated in the town of Fairfield, specifically in the homes of Mrs. Sarah Amanda Blythe, Rufus Christian Swope, and in what is now St. John's Lutheran Church. For more information on the town of Fairfield, see Fairfield In the Civil War, by Sarah Sites Thomas, Tim Smith, Gary Kross, and Dean S. Thomas.
The Fairfield Historic District and Fairfield Inn are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Mobile phone users who subscribe to T-Mobile's HotSpot service will be able to make free internet telephone calls, it has been announced.

The firm said that its customers would now be able to use Skype software on their phones for free when connected to one of its 10,000 WiFi hotspots in the UK and Ireland.

Skype allows people with broadband connections to talk over the internet using voice or video technology.

T-Mobile said it was the first mobile operator to offer such a deal.

It said that by combining its HotSpot service - which offers access to wireless networks at airports, hotels and cafes - with Skype, it could provide an alternative to traditional fixed line telephony services.

Users can download the Skype application onto their handsets via the web and then connect to any of T-Mobile's hotspots to start making calls.

They are also able to receive incoming calls while they are away from home or work.

Callers do not need to have Skype installed on their own computers but must have a microphone attached to their PC.

A spokesman for T-Mobile said that the company had already seen a surge in demand for its HotSpot service since announcing the new partnership last week.

Remember him, whom passion's force  
Deeply and vainly severed:  
Recall the perilous hour,  
When neither fell, though both were loved.  
That yielding chest, that melting gaze,  
Too eager to be blessed:  
That gentle prayer, that pleading sigh,  
The wilder wish rebuked, restrained.  

Oh! let me feel that all I lost  
Saved thee what conscience fears;  
And blush for every pain it cost  
To spare the empty regret of years.  

Yet think of this when many a voice,  
Whose loud words cast blame on you,  
Would hurt the heart that loved you wrongly,  
And tarnish a near-forgotten name.  

Think that, no matter what others face,  
You have subdued each selfish thought:  
I bless your purer soul now,  
Now, in quiet solitude.  

Oh, God! that we had met in time,  
Our hearts as deep, thy hand more free;  
When thou hadst loved without a sin,  
And I been less unworthy thee!  

Far may thy days, as before,  
Be free from this gaudy world!  
And that bitter moment o'er,  
Oh! may such trial be thy last.  

This heart, alas! long corrupted,  
Could destroy itself, yet still desire to meet thee in the crowd,  
Where presumption hopes for joy.  

Then to the things whose bliss or sorrow,  
Like mine, is wild and worthless,  
That world resigns, such scenes forsake,  
Where those who feel must surely fall.  

Thy youth, thy beauty, thy tender care,  
Your soul from long isolation pure;  
From what even here has passed, may guess  
What there your bosom must endure.  

Oh! forgive that crying eye,  
Not by virtue shed in vain;  
My fury drew from eyes so dear;  
For me they shall not weep again.  

Though long and mournful must it be,  
The thought that we no longer meet;  
Yet I deserve the stern decree,  
And almost deem the sentence sweet.  

Still—had I loved thee less—my heart  
Had then less sacrificed to thine;  
It felt not half so much to part  
As if its guilt had made thee mine.

Ingredients:
2 lbs mirabelle plums (about 20-25 plums)
2 cups sugar
1/2 cup fresh rosemary leaves
1/4 tsp kosher salt

Instructions:
1. Rinse the mirabelle plums and pat them dry with a paper towel. Remove the stems and cut the plums in half. Remove the pits.
2. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, combine the sugar, rosemary, and salt. Add the plums and stir to combine.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture has thickened and the plums have broken down, about 30-45 minutes.
4. Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture cool for 5 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
5. Transfer the jam to a clean jar and let it cool to room temperature. Cover and refrigerate for up to 1 month.

Sir Anthony Meyer, a Conservative backbencher who contested Margaret Thatcher for the party leadership in 1989, has passed away. He was 84, had been battling cancer for several months, and died at his London residence. This unsuccessful leadership challenge facilitated Michael Heseltine's subsequent bid, which ultimately enabled John Major to become Prime Minister after the second vote. Meyer's local party, Clwyd North West, voted against him due to this challenge. Born on 27 October 1920, Meyer attended Eton and New College, Oxford. He served in the Scots Guards during World War II, sustaining injuries in Normandy. He worked under Edward Heath on European affairs at the Foreign Office and later secured the Eton and Slough seats for the Conservatives in 1964, winning by 11 votes. Labour reclaimed the seat two years later, and Meyer did not return to Parliament until 1970. His chances of securing a parliamentary position were limited due to his tendency to oppose party directives.

Recent developments in generative models and adversarial learning have spurred growth in the field of image-to-image (I2I) translation. Current I2I methods typically rely on either fully paired (supervised) or fully unpaired (unsupervised) datasets. However, obtaining large-scale paired data is often expensive and time-consuming. As a result, many studies prefer unsupervised approaches, which are less accurate but more practical. This paper seeks to connect supervised and unsupervised I2I translation, particularly for semantic image segmentation. We utilize pix2pix and CycleGAN, leading-edge I2I techniques. We introduce a strategy to choose a minimal number of paired samples, significantly enhancing performance in both supervised and unsupervised settings compared to random selection. Additionally, we incorporate both selected paired and unpaired samples into the training process. Experimental results demonstrate that a highly weak supervised I2I solution based on just one paired sample achieves performance surpassing the unsupervised CycleGAN model and rivaling the supervised pix2pix model trained on thousands of pairs.

The exceptional Lie algebra E_7(-25), a crucial element in understanding supersymmetric gauge theories, is explored in this research. The study focuses on its representation theory, specifically addressing multiplets and invariant differential operators associated with it. By analyzing these elements of E_7(-25), an extensive overview of their properties contributes to enhancing our comprehension of related mathematical structures while providing valuable insights into applications within physics.

Semantic segmentation models trained on public datasets have achieved great
success in recent years. However, these models didn't consider the
personalization issue of segmentation though it is important in practice. In
this paper, we address the problem of personalized image segmentation. The
objective is to generate more accurate segmentation results on unlabeled
personalized images by investigating the data's personalized traits. To open up
future research in this area, we collect a large dataset containing various
users' personalized images called PIS (Personalized Image Semantic
Segmentation). We also survey some recent researches related to this problem
and report their performance on our dataset. Furthermore, by observing the
correlation among a user's personalized images, we propose a baseline method
that incorporates the inter-image context when segmenting certain images.
Extensive experiments show that our method outperforms the existing methods on
the proposed dataset. The code and the PIS dataset will be made publicly
available.

Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas has stated he will not condone attacks like the one that occurred in Tel Aviv last Friday, which involved a suicide bomber. In an interview prior to a meeting in London aimed at discussing Palestinian reforms, Abbas emphasized that these attacks undermine Palestinian interests. He noted that the Palestinian Authority (PA) is fully committed to eliminating the violence. The attack, which resulted in five fatalities, marked the first of its kind since Abbas took office. Abbas confirmed that Israel provided information to the PA regarding the attackers. The Israeli government disputes Syria's claims of involvement in the nightclub bombing, and Israeli officials briefed foreign diplomats on Monday about Syria's alleged role. British Foreign Minister Jack Straw indicated that there has been a sustained flow of information indicating that Palestinian militant groups operate within Syria.

In an email interview with the British newspaper *The Independent*, Abbas asserted that peace is achievable and that negotiations with Israel are necessary to achieve a just and internationally recognized peace. He stressed that it would be unwise for Israelis or the global community to let this opportunity slip away. The meeting on Palestinian reforms, organized by British Prime Minister Tony Blair, will also include U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan, World Bank representatives, and foreign ministers from 23 European and Arab nations. Straw described the event as a critical step in revitalizing the peace process, highlighting the high level of participation as a reflection of the momentum and opportunities generated by recent developments. A spokesperson for Blair mentioned that the Prime Minister anticipated discussions on a thorough, coordinated, and practical plan for both the Palestinian Authority and the international community.

I've always been very emotional. Even small events can impact my day. The problem is, when something feels significant to me, others often dismiss it as unimportant, making me feel ignored. To cope, I add details to the situation to make it more dramatic, so I don’t come off as overly sensitive. For instance, if I spill coffee on the table and it’s nearly empty, I’ll exaggerate it as being half-full, hot, and messy. It's hard to control this behavior—it's both silly and compulsive. 

Let me share another example. When my friend lost $10,000 in investments overnight, I told my boyfriend about it, but I mentioned he lost $100,000 instead. I didn’t think twice about it—maybe it just came out of nowhere. Now I stick to this lie, and I start believing it myself. It’s gotten so confusing that I can’t tell which parts of my past are real and which are fabricated.

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs pork belly
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup wild huckleberries
- 1/4 cup honey
- 1/4 cup white wine vinegar
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 1 tbsp cornstarch

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 325°F.

2. Season the pork belly with salt and black pepper.

3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork belly and sear on all sides until browned.

4. Transfer the pork belly to a baking dish and place it in the oven. Bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until the pork is tender and the skin is crispy.

5. While the pork belly is cooking, prepare the wild huckleberry sauce. In a small saucepan, combine the huckleberries, honey, white wine vinegar, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.

6. In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp of water until smooth. Add the cornstarch mixture to the huckleberry sauce and stir until thickened.

7. Remove the pork belly from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing it. Serve with the wild huckleberry sauce.

Now that a critical mass of people have embraced digital TV, DVDs, and digital video recorders, the next revolution for TV is being prepared for our sets.
In most corners of TV and technology industries, high-definition (HDTV) is being heralded as the biggest thing to happen to the television since colour. HD essentially makes TV picture quality at least four times better than now. But there is real concern that people are not getting the right information about HD on the High Street. Thousands of flat panel screens - LCDs (liquid crystal displays), plasma screens, and DLP rear-projection TV sets - have already been sold as "HD", but are in fact not able to display HD.
"The UK is the largest display market in Europe," according to John Binks, director of GfK, which monitors global consumer markets.
But, he added: "Of all the flat panel screens sold, just 1.3% in the UK are capable of getting high-definition." There are 74 different devices that are being sold as HD but are not HD-ready, according to Alexander Oudendijk, senior vice president of marketing for satellite giant Astra. They may be fantastic quality TVs, but many do not have adaptors in them - called DVI or HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) connectors - which let the set handle the higher resolution digital images. Part of this is down to lack of understanding and training on the High Street, say industry experts, who gathered at Bafta in London for the 2nd European HDTV Summit last week. "We have to be careful about consumer confusion. There is a massive education process to go through," said Mr Binks. The industry already recognised that it would be a challenge to get the right information about it across to those of us who will be watching it. Eventually, that will be everyone. The BBC is currently developing plans to produce all its TV output to meet HDTV standards by 2010.
Preparations for the analogue switch-off are already underway in some areas, and programmes are being filmed with HD cameras. BSkyB plans to ship its first generation set-top boxes, to receive HDTV broadcasts, in time for Christmas. Like its Sky+ boxes, they will also be personal video recorders (PVRs). The company will start broadcasts of HDTV programmes, offering them as "premium channel packages", concentrating, to start with, on sports, big events, and films, in early 2006. But the set-top box which receives HDTV broadcasts has to plug into a display - TV set - that can show the images at the much higher resolution that HD demands, if HDTV is to be "real". By 2010, 20% of homes in the UK will have some sort of TV set or display that can show HD in its full glory.
But it is all getting rather confusing for people who have only just taken to "being digital". As a result, all the key players, those who make flat panel displays, as well as the satellite companies and broadcasters, formed a HD forum in 2004 to make sure they were all talking to each other. Part of the forum has been concerned with issues like industry standards and content protection. But it has also been preoccupied with how to help the paying public know exactly what they are paying for.
From next month, all devices that have the right connectors and resolution required will carry a "HD-Ready" sticker. This also means they are equipped to cope with both analogue and HDTV signals, and so comply with the minimum specification set out by the industry. "The logo is absolutely the way forward," said David Mercer, analysts with Strategy Analytics. "But it is still not appearing on many retail products." The industry is upbeat that the sticker will help, but it is only a start. "We can only do so much with the position we are in today with manufacturers," said Mr Oudendijk. "There may well be a number of dissatisfied customers in the next few months." The European Broadcast Union (EBU) is testing different flavours of HD formats to prepare for even better HDTV further down the line. It is similarly concerned that people get the right information on HDTV formats, as well as which devices will support the formats. "We believe consumers buying expensive displays need to ensure their investment is worthwhile," said Phil Laven, technical director for the EBU. The TV display manufacturers want us to watch HD on screens that are at least 42in (106cm), to get the "true impact" of HD, they say, although smaller displays suffice. What may convince people to spend money on HD-ready devices is the falling prices, which continue to tumble across Europe. The prices are dropping an average of 20% every year, according to analysts. LCD prices dropped by 43% in Europe as a whole last year, according to Mr Oudendijk.

Lawrence Sidney Eagleburger, born on August 1, 1930, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, was an American politician and diplomat who held a brief position as Secretary of State under President George H. W. Bush from 1992 to 1993, which was one of the shortest in modern history. Before that, he held various roles under Presidents Richard Nixon, Jimmy Carter, and Ronald Reagan, as well as serving as Deputy Secretary of State under James Baker during George H. W. Bush's administration. Eagleburger is the sole career Foreign Service officer to have served as Secretary of State. 

Eagleburger was the son of Helen Van Ornum, an elementary school teacher, and Leon Sidney Eagleburger, a physician. He graduated from Jacobs High School in Stevens Point, Wisconsin, then studied at Stevens Point State College (now the University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point), earning his bachelor’s and master’s degrees from the university. During his time at Wisconsin, he joined the Alpha Sigma Phi fraternity.

Mussa Moloh, born around the mid-to-late 1800s, is considered the last ruler of the Fuladu kingdom in the Senegambian region of Africa. He collaborated with colonial authorities to maintain control and suppress uprisings, which eventually contributed to his demise. The Fulbe Empire originated from a rebellion led by Mussa Moloh's father, Moloh Eggue, also called Alfa Moloh, against the Mandinka who previously governed the Gambian area. After the Mandinka rulers left, the territory they once controlled became part of the Fulbe state. This empire had a broad and varied population, although the Fulbe were typically seen as a unified group. Their diversity led to cultural conflicts, prompting Alfa Moloh to dispute with certain factions, which caused those groups to depart from the Fulbe state. The main supporters of Alfa were the Fulbe Firdu, comprising approximately 30,000 people, who relocated north to establish permanent settlements in Tomari and Jimana, both of which were former Mandinka kingdoms in the Gambian valley. Over time, the Fulbe empire evolved into a state formed through the efforts of Alfa's son, Mussa Moloh.

Quasi-power law ensembles are discussed from the perspective of nonextensive
Tsallis distributions characterized by a nonextensive parameter $q$. A number
of possible sources of such distributions are presented in more detail. It is
further demonstrated that data suggest that nonextensive parameters deduced
from Tsallis distributions functions $f\left(p_T\right)$, $q_1$, and from
multiplicity distributions (connected with Tsallis entropy), $q_2$, are not
identical and that they are connected via $q_1 + q_2 = 2$. It is also shown
that Tsallis distributions can be obtained directly from Shannon information
entropy, provided some special constraints are imposed. They are connected with
the type of dynamical processes under consideration (additive or
multiplicative). Finally, it is shown how a Tsallis distribution can
accommodate the log-oscillating behavior apparently seen in some multiparticle
data.

1 Tablespoon Butter, Melted
1 pinch Cayenne Pepper
1 pinch Freshly Ground Pepper
1 pinch Coarse Salt
1/2 cups Hot Pepper Sauce, Divided (I Used Frank's)
1 pound Chicken Tenders
1/4 cups Ranch Dressing
1/2 cups Crumbled Blue Cheese, Divided
4 whole Large Jalapeno Cheddar Tortillas
4 slices Bacon, Cooked And Coarsely Chopped
2 whole Eggs, Hardboiled And Roughly Chopped
2 cups Shredded Romaine Lettuce
1 cup Shredded Cheddar Cheese
1 whole Roma Tomato, Diced
Combine the butter, cayenne pepper, black pepper, salt and 1/4 cup of the hot pepper sauce in a bowl. Whisk to combine. Add the chicken and toss to coat. Cover the bowl and marinate the chicken in the refrigerator for however long you want to. An hour or more. Heat an indoor grill (or outdoor, whatevs) over medium-high and coat the grates with cooking spray. Add the chicken tenders and grill until cooked through with nice grill marks on both sides, about 8 minutes total. Remove chicken from the grill and roughly chop it. In a small bowl, whisk the ranch dressing with 1/4 cup of the blue cheese crumbles. Or buy blue cheese dressing. Heat up the tortillas in the oven or microwave and start crafting your wraps. Layer some chicken in the center of a tortilla, followed by bacon, eggs, romaine, tomatoes, blue cheese crumbles, cheddar, the dressing and a few more good glugs of hot pepper sauce. With your fingers, mix up the filling so the dressing evenly coats all of the ingredients. Roll up the burrito and tuck in the corners. You can throw it back on the grill if you want, or if youre a ravenous freak, go ahead and slice it in half and demolish. OMG.

10 ounces of bacon slab, sliced into lardons  
olive oil  
1 1/2 heads of cauliflower, trimmed and chopped into small florets  
1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped  
1 stalk of celery, chopped  
2 medium potatoes, peeled and chopped  
1 bay leaf  
4–5 cups of chicken broth  
1 cup of heavy cream  
1 cup of crème fraîche  
salt and freshly ground black pepper  
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Take about 1 cup of the cauliflower florets, season with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and arrange them on a baking sheet. Roast until golden and crispy, approximately 30 minutes. Set aside. In a large soup pot, sauté the lardons until they become crisp, then transfer them to the pot, retaining the fat. Add the chopped onion, celery, and garlic to the pot, stir to combine, and cook for about 2 minutes until the onion softens. Add the bay leaf, potato pieces, and the remaining cauliflower, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, for about 5–7 minutes. Pour in 4 cups of chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook, covered, for about 20 minutes until the cauliflower and potatoes are tender. Remove the bay leaf and stir in the cream. Use a handheld blender or blend in batches to puree the soup until it's smooth and creamy. Return to the heat for an additional 5–6 minutes until fully cooked. If desired, add more broth or cream to thin the soup. Season with salt and pepper as needed. Just before serving, mix in the crème fraîche. Serve the soup in individual bowls, topping each with slices of roasted cauliflower and crispy lardons.

The LBNF/DUNE CDR describes the proposed physics program and experimental
design at the conceptual design phase. Volume 2, entitled The Physics Program
for DUNE at LBNF, outlines the scientific objectives and describes the physics
studies that the DUNE collaboration will perform to address these objectives.
The long-baseline physics sensitivity calculations presented in the DUNE CDR
rely upon simulation of the neutrino beam line, simulation of neutrino
interactions in the far detector, and a parameterized analysis of detector
performance and systematic uncertainty. The purpose of this posting is to
provide the results of these simulations to the community to facilitate
phenomenological studies of long-baseline oscillation at LBNF/DUNE.
Additionally, this posting includes GDML of the DUNE single-phase far detector
for use in simulations. DUNE welcomes those interested in performing this work
as members of the collaboration, but also recognizes the benefit of making
these configurations readily available to the wider community.

FANet: A Feedback Attention Network for Improved Biomedical Image Segmentation

Background:
Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications, including disease diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep learning techniques have shown promising results in image segmentation tasks; however, their performance can be limited by the gap between the training data distribution and real-world scenarios. Moreover, the lack of interpretability in deep models hinders understanding the reasoning behind their predictions.

Objective:
To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework called FANet (Feedback Attention Network), which incorporates feedback attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and interpretability of biomedical image segmentation.

Methodology:
FANet consists of two main components: an encoder network and a feedback attention module. The encoder network follows a U-Net architecture with skip connections, designed to capture multi-scale contextual information. The feedback attention module is applied on top of the encoder network, consisting of multiple attention layers that focus on different aspects of the input image. Each attention layer computes spatial attention maps to highlight relevant regions, allowing the model to refine its predictions based on the feedback received from previously generated outputs. We implement a self-gated mechanism that adaptively weights the importance of the attention signals, enabling the model to balance between local and global dependencies. Additionally, we introduce a routing strategy that directs the information flow across different attention layers, facilitating better feature representation and exchange.

Results:

Actor Daniel Day-Lewis is to be presented with an award for his career in film at the Berlin Film Festival.
The 47-year-old, whose credits include his Oscar-winning performance in My Left Foot, will be presented with the Berlinale Camera award on 15 February. The honour, awarded since 1986, honours figures in cinema that the festival feels "particularly indebted to". Man to Man, a historical epic starring Kristin Scott Thomas, opens the German festival on 10 February. A candid documentary about the life and career of singer George Michael, A Different Story will also be screened at the 10-day event. '
Day-Lewis has competed four times at the Berlin Film Festival, with films In The Name Of The Father (1994), The Crucible (1997), The Boxer (1998) and Martin Scorsese's Gangs Of New York (2003). The festival praises him for his "sensational start" with roles in My Beautiful Launderette and costume classic A Room With A View, and a "great number of celebrated roles" in subsequent productions. Japan's oldest film studio will also be honoured along with Day-Lewis. Shochiku film studios, which was founded 110 years ago, will become the first cinematic institution to receive the Berlinale Camera award. Famous Japanese directors including Akira Kurosawa have had films produced at the studio.

This seems to be Miyazake's most personal work, clearly a serious design. It is set in an imaginary time which blends the time of the ancient gods (Shinto style, gods of place and nature) with the settlement of humans and the coming of metalworking and war. The world is not in balance, and a distant conflict between industry and nature has wounded one of the gods of the forest, which is then killed by a sentry boy as it rampages into farmland he guards. The evil controlling it transfers to him, beginning a slow takeover, and he must journey to the origin of the conflict to find a way to cure himself and incidentally, as he will learn, to try to restore balance. But this is not a simplistic tale, he finds there are other characters in play, and there is good and evil in everyone, and no easy balance. The Princess (Hime) of the story is a mysterious human who has been raised by wolves (which are themselves powerful forest gods, a little reminiscent of the Amerindian Coyote myth), who becomes both his ally and his enemy. The story is not easy to understand. It has many Japanese mythic elements but even then, it is a work of Miyazake's unique imagination, and is not intended to be simple or to have a clean resolution.

The animation is spectacular, and unusual, with new elements even for Miyazake and marks a new departure for style which you can see continued in his next film, Sen to Chihiro - more nature, more wild, more jamming on elements from Japanese myth and folklore. And, continuing the trend to be more personal, concerned with ethics and character, and less sci-fi. There are at least half a dozen well developed characters threaded through the story, and their animation is wonderful in displaying subtle character.

The original Japanese soundtrack has some amazing singing and draws upon some of the best talent available for voices - in Japan, Miyazake is universally known and this was a masterpiece carefully crafted. Japanese television documented a lot of the production. The English translation drew on some good talent but they seem not to have "gotten it" quite so intensely as the Japanese crew.

If you haven't seen Miyazake, give it a try (but maybe look at Sen to Chihiro first, or even Laputa or Kiki's Delivery Service, for easier and lighter introduction to his work). Some say he is the Japanese Disney, but I don't like that. His work has a depth and sophistication that goes beyond Disney cute. There is no other animation like it. This is truly an adult work: children might like some of the visuals, but I doubt that many kids below teen age will have any idea what it is all about, and even adults will get more out of this each time you see it again.

Georgia E. Engelhard Cromwell (born November 19, 1906; died September 14, 1986) was an American mountaineer who explored the Canadian Rockies and the Selkirk and Purcell ranges. She was the first woman to climb many of the Rockies' peaks and the leading female amateur climber of her era. She was also known for her skills as a painter and photographer. 

Engelhard was born in Manhattan on November 19, 1906, the eldest child of George Engelhard, a lawyer, and Agnes Stieglitz. She was the niece of Alfred Stieglitz, an American photographer and advocate for modern art, and his wife, Georgia O'Keeffe, a renowned artist often called the "Mother of American Modernism." To prevent name confusion between the two Georgias, she was commonly addressed as "The Kid" or "Georgia Minor." She occasionally posed for photographs with Stieglitz, including nude portraits. Stieglitz was a close friend and mentor to Engelhard, and they maintained correspondence from the time she was twelve until her early twenties.

Pelagius resided at Kardanoel and taught a doctrine there, asserting that whether one went to heaven or hell was solely their own choice, unrelated to the Church. He rejected the concept of Adam and Eve, disbelieving in original sin. His doubts arose after the fall of man, and he mocked original sin. He ridiculed the idea with phrases like "row-ti-tow" and "ti-oodly-ow." Later, the bishop Germanus, known for his stern demeanor, confronted Pelagius, leading to harsh treatment of the heretics. Germanus used his powerful staff to beat and bang the heretics repeatedly, causing them to shout in unison. The heretics were severely punished, often being hanged. Germanus's actions were intense, hitting them hard and pounding them for long periods on various occasions, making them cry out in agreement. The faithful then turned to the Church for guidance, as the times became increasingly uncertain. Though the world has become more doubtful, those who remain steadfast in their faith continue to embrace the truth, trusting in divine providence. They celebrate the Lord’s gifts, including the temporal sword and the heretics’ fervor, and find solace in the blessings of Christendom, particularly in the rich beer made from barley.

> Kennekuk was a Native American chief who lived in Illinois during the 18th century, and whose name has been given to several places throughout central Illinois. He was born around 1720 near present-day Peoria, Illinois, and died sometime after 1795. His father's name was Kishkequa (or Keeshkequa), which means "the one with the long hair." His mother's name was Wahpeekanaka ("she who weeps").
>
> In his youth he became known as a great warrior, but later turned away from warfare and devoted himself to peacemaking. He married a woman named Pawheecheka ("she who laughs"), and they had two sons, Tapouyee ("little bear") and Chicagou ("big river").
>
> During the French and Indian War, Kennekuk fought on the side of the British against the French. After the war ended, he helped negotiate peace between the various tribes living in what would become Illinois. He also worked to establish good relations with white settlers moving into the area.
>
> One of Kennekuk's most important contributions was his role in establishing Fort Clark at the confluence of the Sangamon River and the Illinois River. This fort served as a key trading post for many years, and played an important part in opening up central Illinois to settlement by whites.
>
> Kennekuk continued to work for peace until his death sometime after 1795. He is buried on a hill overlooking the site where Fort Clark once stood. A monument marks his grave today.

U.S. Open winner Svetlana Kuznetsova has tested positive for a prohibited substance, as reported by Belgian officials. According to Belgian sports minister Claude Eerdekens, the Russian world number five tested positive for the stimulant ephedrine on December 19. Kuznetsova was participating in an exhibition match in Charleroi at the time. Eerdekens stated, "There is a problem. Ephedrine was detected. She remains innocent until proven guilty. She may request a retest." The situation remains uncertain since the tournament was not organized by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), the International Tennis Federation (ITF), or the Women's Tennis Association (WTA). The test was conducted by regional Belgian authorities, and Kuznetsova has not yet received results from a second sample.

At the Australian Open, prior to Eerdekens revealing the result, Kuznetsova mentioned, "I am not worried. I am not using anything to enhance my performance. I have not been informed of any positive tests, and I believe it is unjust that the result came out this way." Eerdekens confirmed that the findings were sent to the player’s Spanish address, along with the Belgian prosecutors’ office and the Belgian and Russian tennis federations. He admitted that Kuznetsova may have used a medication containing the banned substance. "We have simply stated a fact," he said. "The relevant federation will determine the disciplinary actions after a proper process respecting the defense."

Tarpishchev criticized Kuznetsova's naming, stating, "Firstly, this Belgian sports minister has violated every ethical guideline by identifying a player without evidence of wrongdoing or basic proof. We all understand the fundamental principles in doping cases. If there is a positive sample, they should inform the relevant parties immediately."

2 medium lemons
2 cups unbleached all-purpose flour
1 3/4 cups sugar
1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt
1/2 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1 1/3 cups extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/4 cups 2% milk
3 large eggs
1/4 cup limoncello
butter for the pan
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Put out the milk, eggs and limoncello to warm up somewhat (room temperature is ideal) while you prepare the lemons and while the oven preheats. Zest the two lemons; you should end up with about 1 1/2 tablespoons of zest. Then juice one of the lemons which should yield approximately 1/4 of juice. Set aside. Prepare the cake pan: butter it, cover the bottom with parchment paper, and butter the paper also. You will be baking a relatively liquid batter so you want a pan that's at least 2" high. I used a spring-form pan which worked well. In a medium bowl whisk together the dry ingredients -- the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Using a stand mixer with the whisk attached, mix together the wet ingredients: the lemon zest and juice, the olive oil, limoncello, eggs and milk. With the whisk running on slow speed, add your dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in a slow but steady stream until just combined. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and bake for an hour, or until done. When done the cake with have a golden honey brown top in its center, and a cake tester inserted in the middle of the cake will come out clean. Place the cake on a wire rack for 30 minutes. At the end of that time, run a thin knife around the edge of the cake to ensure that it will come out cleanly, and invert on to another wire rack. Now remove the parchment paper from the bottom of the cake, and using another wire rack, turn the cake upside down so that it is again top-side up and let it cool completely, which will take about 2 hours. Once completely cool, the cake is ready to be iced or frosted, as you wish, or served plain as is. My family likes it served just with fresh berries (blueberries and raspberries in particular) and a dollop of whipped cream. This moist cake keeps well for several days when wrapped up and stored at room temperature.

This paper investigates the generation of linear and non-linear Alfvén waves in the coronal funnels through impulsive energy release processes. The authors conducted numerical simulations to study the dynamics and characteristics of these waves, focusing on how they interact and propagate in the coronal structures. It was found that impulsive events can generate both linear and non-linear Alfvén waves, with the latter exhibiting strong nonlinearities and wave steepening effects. The simulations also revealed that the generated waves can transport energy and momentum from the energy release site to distant regions of the funnel, which could have significant implications for coronal heating and solar wind acceleration. These findings provide new insights into the complex wave dynamics in the solar corona and can contribute to our understanding of fundamental physical processes occurring in this highly dynamic environment.

Recent decades have seen the discovery of numerous complex materials. At the
root of the complexity underlying many of these materials lies a large number
of possible contending atomic- and larger-scale configurations and the
intricate correlations between their constituents. For a detailed
understanding, there is a need for tools that enable the detection of pertinent
structures on all spatial and temporal scales. Towards this end, we suggest a
new method by invoking ideas from network analysis and information theory. Our
method efficiently identifies basic unit cells and topological defects in
systems with low disorder and may analyze general amorphous structures to
identify candidate natural structures where a clear definition of order is
lacking. This general unbiased detection of physical structure does not require
a guess as to which of the system properties should be deemed as important and
may constitute a natural point of departure for further analysis. The method
applies to both static and dynamic systems.

Blueberry Muffins Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 cup buttermilk
- 1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a muffin tin with paper liners or grease it lightly with cooking spray.
2. In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
3. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
4. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.
5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, alternating with the buttermilk. Begin and end with the dry ingredients, mixing just until incorporated.
6. Gently fold in the fresh blueberries, being careful not to crush them.
7. Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, filling each cup about 2/3 full.
8. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
9. Remove the muffins from the oven and allow them to cool in the tin for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
10. Enjoy your homemade blueberry muffins plain, or you can top them with a sprinkle of powdered sugar, a drizzle of glaze, or a dollop of whipped cream. Serve and enjoy with a hot cup of coffee or tea!

In biological cells and new diagnostic tools, biochemical receptors must be able to detect minute variations in the concentrations of signaling molecules. The precision of these molecular signals is constrained by the noise generated through thermal diffusion. Many large molecules and organelles temporarily attach to molecular motors and are subsequently moved actively. Here, we demonstrate that a random yet directed delivery of signaling molecules within the typical diffusion range to the receptor decreases the correlation time of the counting noise, thereby enhancing sensing accuracy. These conditions align with findings observed in living cells. Our conclusions are significant for advancing knowledge about molecular cell signaling and the development of innovative diagnostic systems.

The Lennox Bridge, situated in Glenbrook, is a heritage-listed road bridge that spans Brookside Creek (also called Lapstone Creek) and connects to the City of Blue Mountains in New South Wales, Australia. Built in 1832-1833, it was constructed by James Randall and other convicts, and designed by David Lennox. The bridge is alternatively referred to as Lennox Bridge or The Horseshoe Bridge. It is currently owned by the Blue Mountains City Council and was listed in the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999. The structure features a single-span stone arch bridge above water level with a road width of . The initial road along the eastern slopes of the Blue Mountains, constructed by William Cox (1814–15), was described by Governor Macquarie as "pretty steep and sharp" and was deemed hazardous due to severe washways. This road was replaced in 1824 by the Bathurst Road (now Old Bathurst Road), which avoided watercourses but had an extremely steep gradient, making it dangerous for travelers. When Major Thomas Mitchell became Surveyor General in 1828, he prioritized improving the Great Western Road. He focused on creating a more direct and easier-to-grade route for the Great Western Road, recommending the construction of a road along this path midway between the existing roads, rather than establishing a permanent repair team on the Old Bathurst Road.

Automatic Spine Segmentation using Convolutional Neural Network via Redundant Generation of Class Labels for 3D Spine Modeling

We present a novel approach to segment the spine of a 3D model using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a novel classifier. We use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate a set of class labels for each segment of the spine. We then use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to segment the segmented spine into the segments that are labeled by the class labels. We show that the segmented spine can be automatically segmented using the segmented spine classifier. We also show that the segmented spine classifier can be used to automatically segment the spine of a 3D model.

Min-cut clustering, based on minimizing one of two heuristic cost-functions
proposed by Shi and Malik, has spawned tremendous research, both analytic and
algorithmic, in the graph partitioning and image segmentation communities over
the last decade. It is however unclear if these heuristics can be derived from
a more general principle facilitating generalization to new problem settings.
Motivated by an existing graph partitioning framework, we derive relationships
between optimizing relevance information, as defined in the Information
Bottleneck method, and the regularized cut in a K-partitioned graph. For fast
mixing graphs, we show that the cost functions introduced by Shi and Malik can
be well approximated as the rate of loss of predictive information about the
location of random walkers on the graph. For graphs generated from a stochastic
algorithm designed to model community structure, the optimal information
theoretic partition and the optimal min-cut partition are shown to be the same
with high probability.

Two whole English muffins, halved  
Softened butter  
Thinly sliced smoked salmon  
Four whole eggs  
Three whole egg yolks  
One and one-half sticks of butter  
One whole lemon, juiced  
Cayenne pepper to taste  
Black pepper to taste  
(This plate from Pastis restaurant in New York City.) First, bring a pot of water to a boil. While the water is heating, place a few English muffin halves on a baking sheet. Lightly grease the muffins and place them under the broiler for just a few minutes, or until they are slightly golden. Next, cook the eggs. Using a spoon, swirl the boiling water in a large circular motion. When the water is spinning rapidly, crack an egg into it. Add one, two, or three eggs. The purpose of the swirling is to help the egg encircle itself as it cooks, keeping it intact. Cook for approximately 2 1/2 to 3 minutes. In a small saucepan, melt 1 1/2 sticks of butter until it starts to bubble. Transfer the egg yolks into a blender. Operate the blender on low speed to mix the yolks, then gradually add the very hot butter in a slow stream. Continue adding butter until it's fully incorporated. Immediately start adding lemon juice to the blender. Add cayenne pepper. Place the English muffins on the plate, facing upwards. Then, place a slice of smoked salmon on each half. Place an egg on top of the salmon and cover it with a generous amount of hollandaise sauce, followed by a sprinkle of black pepper. Note: To ensure everything is hot when it's ready to serve, immerse the poached eggs in the hot water just before serving, and prepare the hollandaise sauce at the very end.

British Airways has decided to stop flights from London Heathrow to Jeddah and Riyadh in Saudi Arabia starting on 27 March. The airline stated that the decision is based on lower passenger demand for these services. Currently, British Airways operates four flights per week to Jeddah and three weekly trips to Riyadh. In 2003, the company temporarily halted flights to Saudi Arabia for three weeks following a government alert regarding a potential threat to UK aviation interests in Saudi Arabia. British Airways will now suspend these flights, which it claims will continue to be reviewed. The decision, made by BA's commercial planning director, Robert Boyle, was described as challenging due to the long-standing relationship between the two countries. However, the routes do not currently generate sufficient profit to maintain operations. Passengers with bookings after the suspension date will be informed by British Airways for alternative travel arrangements.

The rising popularity of online gaming may pose challenges for internet service providers, according to network monitoring company Sandvine. The firm highlighted this concern after analyzing data showing that traffic on the Xbox game network surged fourfold on the release day of Halo 2. This spike continued into December, prompting Sandvine to urge service providers to ensure their infrastructure can handle growing bandwidth demands. Halo 2, a widely played single-player game, can be integrated with Microsoft’s Xbox Live subscription service. Players can form clans or teams to compete against others.  

However, the increase in user numbers and bandwidth requirements should serve as a reminder for the industry to upgrade its networks to accommodate higher traffic volumes, stated Sandvine’s chief technology officer, Marc Morin. To address congestion, providers are adopting more intelligent networks that track bandwidth usage. It may soon become standard to charge users based on the amount of bandwidth they consume. "The dramatic rise in Xbox Live traffic linked to Halo 2 underscores the importance of action," Morin emphasized. "Internet service providers must prioritize or reserve bandwidth for gaming to enhance the experience for high-end users."  

A key issue in online gaming is "lag," which refers to the delay between a player’s actions and the corresponding response in the game. Gamers often prefer connections with minimal lag. As traffic analysis becomes crucial for maintaining bandwidth-heavy users, analysts like Lindsay Schroth from The Yankee Group note that operators must differentiate themselves in a competitive broadband market. She stressed the need for improved network performance to retain gamers.

Recent advances in deep learning based image segmentation methods have
enabled real-time performance with human-level accuracy. However, occasionally
even the best method fails due to low image quality, artifacts or unexpected
behaviour of black box algorithms. Being able to predict segmentation quality
in the absence of ground truth is of paramount importance in clinical practice,
but also in large-scale studies to avoid the inclusion of invalid data in
subsequent analysis.
  In this work, we propose two approaches of real-time automated quality
control for cardiovascular MR segmentations using deep learning. First, we
train a neural network on 12,880 samples to predict Dice Similarity
Coefficients (DSC) on a per-case basis. We report a mean average error (MAE) of
0.03 on 1,610 test samples and 97% binary classification accuracy for
separating low and high quality segmentations. Secondly, in the scenario where
no manually annotated data is available, we train a network to predict DSC
scores from estimated quality obtained via a reverse testing strategy. We
report an MAE=0.14 and 91% binary classification accuracy for this case.
Predictions are obtained in real-time which, when combined with real-time
segmentation methods, enables instant feedback on whether an acquired scan is
analysable while the patient is still in the scanner. This further enables new
applications of optimising image acquisition towards best possible analysis
results.

1.5 cups sugar  
1 cup cranberry juice drink  
4 cups fresh cranberries (16 ounces)  
0.5 cup chopped walnuts  
0.5 cup currants  
0.25 cup fresh orange juice  
2 tablespoons cider vinegar  
0.5 teaspoon ground ginger  
2 cloves garlic, minced  
6 sheets frozen phyllo pastry, thawed  
0.5 cup unsalted butter, melted  
8 ounces Brie, cut into 1/4-inch pieces  
Combine sugar and juice drink in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add cranberries and next 6 ingredients; return to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes or until thickened, stirring often. Cool completely (mixture will thicken as it cools). Place 1 sheet phyllo on a damp towel; brush with butter. Layer a second and third sheet on top of the first, brushing each with butter. (Set remaining 3 sheets aside, covering with a damp towel to prevent drying out.) Cut phyllo in half lengthwise; cut each half crosswise into thirds, forming 6 squares. Place 2 pieces of Brie in center of each square. Gather corners of phyllo squares over Brie, and twist gently, forming a bundle. Place bundles on a lightly greased baking sheet. Repeat procedure with remaining phyllo, butter, and Brie. Bake at 375° for 13 minutes or until golden. Place 2 bundles on each of 6 individual serving plates, and serve hot with cranberry chutney. Note: Serve leftover chutney with roast chicken, pork, or ham.

We derive the general 5-dimension metric structure of the $Dp-Dq$ system in
type II superstring theory, and demonstrate the physical meaning of the
parameters characterizing the 5-dimension metric structure of the
\textit{holographic} QCD model by relating them to the parameters describing
Regge trajectories. By matching the spectra of vector mesons $\rho_1$ with
deformed $Dp-Dq$ soft-wall model, we find that the spectra of vector mesons
$\rho_1$ can be described very well in the soft-wall $D3-Dq$ model, i.e,
$AdS_5$ soft-wall model. We then investigate how well the $AdS_5$ soft-wall
model can describe the Regge trajectory of axial-vector mesons $a_1$. We find
that the constant component of the 5-dimension mass square of axial-vector
mesons plays an efficient role to realize the chiral symmetry breaking in the
vacuum, and a small negative $z^4$ correction in the 5-dimension mass square is
helpful to realize the chiral symmetry restoration in high excitation states.

The Sunspot number series is affected by several uncertainties, which remain poorly understood. Recent developments have emphasized the importance of improving our understanding of these uncertainties, particularly due to a significant revision of the international Sunspot Number [Clette et al., Space Science Reviews, 2014]. We offer the first comprehensive assessment of these uncertainties, which follow a Poisson-like distribution with a multiplicative factor that varies with both time and observatory conditions. We derive a straightforward formula for these uncertainties and demonstrate how their temporal evolution aligns with changes in observational data and data processing. Accurate knowledge of these uncertainties is crucial for effectively combining multiple observations into composite images and maintaining the consistency of these composites over time.

Abstract:

Unsupervised pathology image segmentation is a challenging task that requires identifying regions of interest in medical images without the need for manual labeling or prior knowledge of the disease being present. Representation learning, which has emerged as a powerful tool in deep learning, has shown promising results in this domain by learning a low-dimensional representation of the input images that can be used for clustering and classification. In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised approach to pathology image segmentation using representation learning with spherical k-means clustering. Our approach is based on training a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn a representation of the input images by training the network in a self-supervised manner. We then use the learned representation to cluster the images into regions of interest using spherical k-means clustering. The performance of our approach is evaluated on a benchmark dataset of lung tissue specimens and shows significant improvement over state-of-the-art methods. Our work contributes to existing research on unsupervised pathology image segmentation by providing a novel approach that leverages the strengths of representation learning and clustering techniques for accurate and efficient segmentation.

Like the wild green hills of Wyre,  
The train moved, shifting sky and shire,  
And far back, a fading peak,  
Low in the forsaken west,  
Shrank the high-reared head of Clee,  
My hand remained empty on my knee.  
Aching on my knee it stayed:  
That morning half a shire away,  
So many an honest man’s fist  
Had nearly torn it from the wrist.  
Hand, I said, since now we must go,  
From fields and men we’ve known by heart,  
To strangers’ faces and lands—  
Hand, you have held true to men.  
Let it be clean, let it rot before you do  
What they won’t believe of you.  
You and I must not be ashamed  
In London streets where Shropshire names are spoken;  
On banks of Thames they’ll not say  
Severn produces worse men than they;  
And friends abroad must remember  
Friends left behind at home.  
Oh, I will be stiff and cold  
If I forget you, hearts of gold;  
The land where I will never mind you is  
The land where all is forgotten.  
And if my foot never returns  
To Teme or Corve or Severn shore,  
May luck be with you still—  
By falling stream and rising hill,  
By chiming tower and whispering tree,  
Men who made a man of me.  
Your work in town and farm  
Will still keep my head safe,  
Your hands that gave me grip  
To friend me to the grave.

You have never experienced a distant land;

You have not traveled through Indian waters,

For miles, as far as the gaze can reach;  
You have not seen a summer night  
When girls could sew by a worm’s light;  
Nor have you seen the North Sea in spring  
Send out bright colors that seem to flutter  
Like birds in solid white ice—  
Lovely home, lovely contented one,  
You have not seen black hands pick  
Cotton when the blossoms are dense;  
You have not heard black voices in harmony;  
You have not sat upon flat stones  
That once rose to hide proud rulers from sight.  
You have not seen fields bursting with color  
Where green plants had so little space  
That they pleased the eye like brighter flowers—  
Lovely home, all these long hours.

Simple maid, bless thy dear face;  
For thou hast created more beautiful fabric  
To nurture thy gentle soul;  
I love thee for a heart that is kind —

If someone had nudged me about 15 minutes into 'Ray' and asked what I thought of Jamie Foxx in the title role, it would have been time for a blank stare. After all, what is this (fictitious) person talking' about? That wasn't Jamie Foxx up on the big screen. That was Ray Charles. This is one of the best performances by anybody in recent years. Like the soundtrack, Jamie as Ray is flat-out brilliant.

The blind Genius of Soul (who took a revolutionary step of mixing gospel with R&B) died during production. The movie about his troubled life is good, not great. Taylor Hackford's direction and James L. White's script follow the well-worn biopic outline. Super-talented youngster battles adversity, achieves greatness while also self-destructing, then picks himself up out of the gutter for a happy ending. The film shows Charles' flaws (heroin abuse, chronic womanizing, persistent bastard-fathering) even as it sucks you in with his beautiful music.

Kerry Washington and Regina King play the main women in Ray's life, one his long-suffering wife and the other his longtime mistress. Both actresses match Foxx stride for stride. What takes him to a different level, though, is his deep understanding and uncanny impersonation of the great musician. The entire cast is effective, especially Sharon Warren as his headstrong mother and Curtis Armstrong as a music exec. Hackford's stars are likely to be rewarded with trophies and---better yet---more starring roles.

I was not a Ray Charles aficionado before 'Ray'. Apparently, the film has left out a lot (as do all biopics), but this picture functions as both an old-fashioned crowd pleaser AND a dark investigation of a brilliant/troubled man. For those who whine that Foxx doesn't actually sing (as if that somehow diminishes his performance), take a hike. No mere actor can sing like Mr. Charles anyway. You can't have everything. What the talented star does in this picture is about as close to "everything" as we'll probably see for a while.

Color and brightness are crucial elements in an image. Typically, clusters of image pixels with similar color or brightness form a meaningful representation of an object. These clusters are well-suited for computer vision tasks like saliency detection and object proposal generation. However, pixels that share a similar real-world color can differ significantly due to intensity variations. In this paper, we revisit the affinity matrices used in image segmentation techniques based on spectral clustering. A new affinity matrix, designed to be resilient to color distortions, is introduced for identifying objects. Additionally, a cohesion measurement (CM) for object regions is developed using the newly defined affinity matrix. By employing the new CM, a novel object discovery approach is proposed to uncover hidden objects within an image by leveraging the eigenvectors of the affinity matrix. The method is then applied to both saliency detection and object proposal generation. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets show that the proposed CM-based method achieves favorable performance for these tasks.

1 medium, firm eggplant
1 clove garlic, cracked away from the skin
2 pinches ground allspice
Coarse salt and black pepper
1 handful flat-leaf parsley tops
A drizzle extra-virgin olive oil
1 whole grain baguette or other long crusty bread, sliced at bread counter
Preheat oven to highest setting, at least 500 degrees F. Cut 2 or 3 slits into whole eggplant. Place eggplant directly on the oven rack in the middle of the oven and roast the eggplant until it is tender, about 20 minutes. Keep the slits facing up so that the eggplant does not loose liquids as it roasts. The roasted eggplant will look like a flat tire when you remove it from the oven. Using a sharp utility knife, carefully peel skin away from eggplant flesh. Add cooked eggplant flesh and juice to food processor and combine with garlic, allspice, salt, and pepper and parsley. Pulse grind the eggplant into a paste, add a drizzle of olive oil. Transfer to a serving dish. The seeds of the eggplant will make the spread resemble caviar eggs, and so the name: poor man's caviar. To serve, surround a bowlful of spread with crusty bread rounds. Tidbit: Mixed olives and selections of Italian sheep's milk cheeses are suggested accompaniments to this menu to round out your buffet. They require no recipe or preparation and add something to the offering overall. Place them on the buffet near the eggplant caviar and bread.

The novel follows a young boy named Nils Holgersson, whose primary joy lies in eating and sleeping, and who particularly enjoys causing trouble. He delights in tormenting the animals on his family’s farm. One day, Nils catches a tomte in a net during a church service and leaves him at home to study Bible passages. The tomte offers Nils a large gold coin in exchange for freeing him, but Nils refuses, leading the tomte to transform Nils into a small tomte, making him unable to speak human language and capable of communicating with animals. This transformation makes the animals happy to see the boy reduced in size and angry and hungry for vengeance. 

Meanwhile, wild geese migrate over the farm, and a white farm goose tries to join them. To prevent his family from returning, Nils clutches the bird’s neck as it flies away and joins the wild geese. The geese, displeased with the boy and the domestic goose, take him on an adventure through all the historical provinces of Sweden, observing their natural features and economic resources. During the journey, Nils faces challenges that force him to grow up: the domestic goose must demonstrate its flying skills, and Nils must convince the geese he can be a valuable companion despite their initial doubts. 

The story also contains several side plots involving individuals affected by Nils and the geese. For instance, a young provincial man in Stockholm feels isolated and isfriend by an elderly gentleman who shares the city’s history. Later, the man discovers that the gentleman was actually the King of Sweden.

Wife Swap makers sue US 'copycat'

The makers of the hit UK reality TV show Wife Swap are suing an American company, claiming it copied their idea.

RDF Media, which makes Wife Swap for Channel 4, says ABC's Wife Swap "brazenly copied" the programme.

It says the US version, which started in 2004, is "strikingly similar" to Wife Swap and is seeking unspecified damages.

ABC has not yet commented on the lawsuit, filed in a federal court in Los Angeles.

The British version of Wife Swap was first broadcast in 2003 and sees two mothers swap lives for two weeks.

'Substantial copying'

RDF says the US programme - which has similar rules and is shot in a similar style - breaches copyright and trade mark law.

"The blatant and substantial copying of the format of Wife Swap is an outrageous infringement of RDF's intellectual property rights," said RDF's chief executive David Frank.

"It is deeply disappointing that ABC has chosen to copy our highly original and successful show rather than come up with its own format."

The lawsuit says the UK show has been sold to broadcasters in more than 50 countries and has been a "tremendous success".

It says RDF has spent millions of pounds promoting Wife Swap and that the US show has caused it "significant damage".

1 1/2 lb uncooked boneless skinless chicken breast - 3/4" cubed
1 1/2 cup 1/2" diced potato
1 cup 1/4" sliced carrots
1 cup frozen peas
1/3 cup + 2 tsp unsalted butter
1/3 cup chopped yellow onion
1/3 cup all-purpose flour
1 tsp sea salt
1/4 tsp black pepper
1/4 tsp celery seed
1/4 tsp dried thyme
1 1/2 cup unsalted chicken broth
2/3 cup milk (I use 1%)
2 refrigerated pie crusts (9in)
In a medium sauce pan combine raw cubed chicken, carrots, peas and potatoes. Add just enough water to cover And a pinch of salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer for 10 - 15 minutes, or until carrots and potatoes are just fork tender. When done drain in colander and set aside. Preheat oven to 425F. Grease a square 2 quart casserole dish all over with 2 tsp butter. Unroll one pie crust and press into dish, forming and pressing from center out to fit and stretch up sides of dish, almost to top edge. If you get any tears just pinch 'em back together. Set aside. In same sauce pan used for chicken mix, melt butter over medium heat. When melted add onions and cook until translucent, Stirring frequently. About 3 minutes. Whisk in flour, salt, pepper, celery seed and thyme to make a roux. Cook until roux is golden, whisking frequently. About 2 minutes more. Slowly add chicken broth and milk, whisking constantly to prevent clumping and sticking to bottom. Bring to a simmer until thickened, stirring constantly. About 5 minutes. Turn off heat. Gently fold chicken and veg mixture into sauce. Pour filling into bottom pie crust, spreading out evenly. Unroll and add top crust, pinching to seal edges (use the tines of a fork for best seal). Cut a few slits for steam vents in top. Pop it in the oven and bake 30-35 minutes or until top is golden brown. When done remove from oven, spread an additional tablespoon of butter over top to melt into crust if desired. Allow to cool 10 minutes, dish up and enjoy!

Ingredients:

* 1 cup stone-ground grits
* 4 cups water
* 1/2 cup grated cheddar cheese
* 1/2 cup diced ham
* 1/4 cup chopped scallions
* 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
* 1/4 cup chopped fresh chives
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* Salt and pepper to taste
* 1/4 cup crumbled bacon (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (180°C).
2. In a medium saucepan, bring the water to a boil. Gradually whisk in the grits and reduce heat to low. Cook for about 5-7 minutes or until the grits are tender, stirring occasionally.
3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked grits, cheddar cheese, diced ham, chopped scallions, chopped parsley, and chopped chives.
4. In a separate bowl, mix together the olive oil, salt, and pepper. Pour the mixture over the grits mixture and stir until everything is well combined.
5. Pour the grits mixture into a 9x13 inch baking dish and top with crumbled bacon (if using).
6. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until the top is golden brown and the grits are heated through.
7. Serve hot and enjoy!

Note: You can also add some diced tomatoes, bell peppers, or jalapenos to the grits mixture for extra flavor. Additionally, you can substitute the cheddar cheese with other types of cheese like parmesan, gouda, or mozzarella.

Crust:
- 1/2 cup butter
- 1/2 cup white sugar
- 5 tablespoons cocoa powder
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 egg, lightly beaten
- 1 1/2 cups graham cracker crumbs
- 1 cup chopped walnuts

Filling:
- 2 cups confectioners' sugar
- 1/2 cup butter, softened
- 3 tablespoons instant French vanilla pudding mix
- 3 tablespoons milk

Topping:
- 4 ounces semisweet chocolate
- 2 tablespoons butter

Prep the crust by placing 1/2 cup of butter in a large saucepan and melting it over low heat. Add the sugar, cocoa powder, and vanilla extract, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Remove from heat, mix in the egg until combined, then incorporate the graham cracker crumbs and walnuts. Fill the bottom of the prepared 9x13-inch dish with this mixture, pressing it down evenly, and let it cool in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

Make the filling by beating confectioners' sugar, softened butter, pudding mix, and milk until the mixture is smooth and fluffy. Spread this over the cooled crust and refrigerate for another 30 minutes.

For the topping, melt chocolate with 2 tablespoons of butter over very low heat, stirring until the mixture is warm but not hot and pourable. Pour the topping over the filled crust, using an offset spatula or knife to spread it evenly. Place the dish back in the refrigerator to cool the topping for about 15 minutes. Once the topping is cool but not firm, cut into squares and return to the refrigerator to finish chilling.

In the previews, "The 40 Year-Old Virgin" boasts the image of another immature sex romp about a 40-ish Lonely Guy who suddenly feels the urge to do the deed simply because he hasn't. Too many past bad experiences have dampened his enthusiasm to the point that he avoids women completely. And then the unexpected happens: he falls in love. What's more, there's a movie out about it, and it's called "The 40 Year-old Virgin."

The virgin of the title is Andy Stitzer (Steve Carell), who is indeed 40, works as an employee at an electronics store and collects vintage action figures, which are displayed all throughout his nice bachelor pad for all to see. He has a lovely home theater system and watches "Survivor" with his two kind elderly neighbors. He's a pretty picturesque definition of the Lonely Guy who needs to go out more and talk to more women.

Now here's the real novelty with this picture: it does the impossible task of actually dealing with its subject matter in a cute, mature fashion. This is a movie that could very easily have turned out a lot differently in the hands of a more transparent team of filmmakers. It could have descended into endless sex gags and jokes but thankfully this picture never stoops that low. Sure there are sex jokes here and there and even a few prods are aimed at the gay community (which are, in no way, meant to be taken as gay-bashing), as two of the characters exchange insults towards each other while playing a video game ("Mortal Kombat: Deception," no less - the ultimate testosterone-driven fightfest for guys).

As someone who is rapidly approaching 20, collects McFarlane Toys action figures AND has himself never done the deed, I found this film amusing and touching in a way that a similar-themed movie could never have been. I was able to relate to the character of Andy Stitzer more than anyone in the theater because I was the only teenager present at this showing; everyone else looked like they were all past 40. A bit arrogant, I know, but would you ("you" is italicized) still be able to relate if you were the only teen present at an afternoon screening of "The 40 Year-Old Virgin"?

Of course Andy has never had sex and wakes up everyday with "morning rise" (don't ask), and he's pressured by his buddies to try outlandish methods of gaining the attention of the opposite sex. When it's first discovered Andy is a virgin, at 40, his three buddies and fellow electronics store coworkers David (Paul Rudd), Jay (Romany Malco) and Cal (Seth Rogen) all at first assume he's gay because he's never been with a woman, which couldn't be any further from the truth. The truth is, Andy loves women, but past traumatic experiences (revealed hilariously one after the other in a flashback sequence) have put him on the sidelines for good.

David, Jay, and Cal each embark on a mission to get Andy laid, so help them all. But you know that such escapades will only end in disaster, as proved by one date with Nicky (Leslie Mann), who puts Andy through the worst drunk-driving experience I think anyone would not want to go through and he has a rather creepy encounter with Beth (Elizabeth Banks), the pretty girl who works in the bookstore and is eventually revealed to be a total sex fiend.

Things brighten up for Andy when he meets Trish (Catherine Keener), the friendly woman who works at a store across the street that sells stuff on eBay for people. Hmmm. And with that nice-looking collection of action figures, you can go figure that in the end a large financial payoff awaits him, that is if he can ever "do the deed."

At last, this is the sex romp we've been waiting for. It deals with a very real issue a lot of Lonely Guys probably go through, not that anything is wrong with being a virgin but let's look at the big picture: How many of us "Lonely Guys" want to be a lonely guy forever? The important thing we're taught in this picture is that Lonely Guy must be himself. I don't think he needs to go through body waxing like Andy does (which is side-splitting to be honest, and according to this website and various other news articles, was in fact real, and so was the blood on Carell's shirt afterward).

"The 40 Year-Old Virgin" was directed by Judd Apatow and co-written by himself and Carell, which originated as a skit that starred Carell. Carell is sweet and human, as his character is not some layabout who approaches this thing with his eyes shut. This is probably one of the most intelligent romps I've ever seen and is not offensive (a whole lot) because its characters are treated with dignity and respect. Even Carell's buddies, who pass off bad advice to cover up their own relationship insecurities, can be related to on a fundamental level.

The way "The 40 Year-Old Virgin" plays out is indeed funny in the end, but I'll leave that up to you, the viewer, to observe. Surely, if anyone can go through the things Andy does and still have the strength to attract a woman as sexy as Catherine Keener, then it's true: It is never too late!

Moskvitch 2140 series is large family car produced by Soviet automotive maker AZLK from January 1976 to 1988. It started first as Moskvitch 2138 and Moskvitch 2140 on a modified 412 platform. Pre-production models were shown during 1975. Starting in 1981, the modernised modification of the M-2140 export/luxury model was also designed and branded "2140 SL" in the Eastern Bloc countries and "1500 SL" outside. The most notable differences between the two models were redesigned dashboard and front seat headrests in the M-2140. Starting in 1982, the M-2138 models were discontinued and the M-2140 became the only Moskvitch cars available in all markets. Researchers are exploring methods to ensure laptops remain powered throughout an entire workday. Using novel chemical combinations to build batteries may enhance power output, according to industry professionals. These advancements encompass various aspects, including how laptop chips are manufactured and strategies to minimize display power usage. Since laptops became popular, the duration between charges has consistently been a concern for users.

A 2000 study by Forrester Research revealed that battery life was the primary issue reported by laptop users. "At that time, the emphasis was more on performance and functionality," stated Mike Trainor, Intel's chief mobile technology evangelist. "Battery life was limited to two to 2.5 hours during the 1990s." However, today's laptops offer significantly longer battery life. While improvements in lithium-ion battery efficiency were achieved, additional modifications are necessary to achieve an eight-hour battery life before recharging. "Lithium-ion will never reach this goal alone," Trainor explained. "The industry has maximized energy storage from this technology."

Some new battery chemistries promise greater capacity in smaller spaces, but further development is required to transition these innovations from laboratories to mass production. Trainor expressed doubt about the rapid adoption of fuel cells, which have the potential to generate up to three times more energy than lithium-ion batteries. "Fuel cells require pumps, separators, and evaporators," he noted. "They are essentially mini-energy plants that must be reduced in size continually."

Intel collaborates with component manufacturers to assess power consumption across all laptop components and identify opportunities to reduce energy use. This effort has contributed to the development of the Mobile PC Extended Battery Li.

We introduce a new image segmentation task, termed Entity Segmentation (ES)
with the aim to segment all visual entities in an image without considering
semantic category labels. It has many practical applications in image
manipulation/editing where the segmentation mask quality is typically crucial
but category labels are less important. In this setting, all
semantically-meaningful segments are equally treated as categoryless entities
and there is no thing-stuff distinction. Based on our unified entity
representation, we propose a center-based entity segmentation framework with
two novel modules to improve mask quality. Experimentally, both our new task
and framework demonstrate superior advantages as against existing work. In
particular, ES enables the following: (1) merging multiple datasets to form a
large training set without the need to resolve label conflicts; (2) any model
trained on one dataset can generalize exceptionally well to other datasets with
unseen domains. Our code is made publicly available at
https://github.com/dvlab-research/Entity.
