50 grams of Kabocha squash with the inside removed  
50 grams of Shiratamako  
60 milliliters of water  
150 grams of Kabocha squash with the inside removed  
150 milliliters of water  
50 milliliters of milk  
2 tablespoons of sugar  
1 tablespoon of white miso  
Make the broth: put the Kabocha squash into a pot with water, cover it with a lid, and boil until it becomes tender. Once softened, add everything to the broth with a hand mixer. Add milk and sugar, then mix until smooth. Return to the pot and turn up the heat. Add the miso and let it dissolve. Taste the flavor; if it’s not sweet enough, add more sugar. If the soup is too thick, add milk while monitoring the consistency.  

Make the dumplings: moisten the Kabocha squash with the inside removed, wrap it in plastic wrap, and microwave until it’s soft. While still warm, mash it. Put the Shiratamako and Kabocha squash into a bowl, gradually add water, and mix until it reaches the consistency of an earlobe. Roll into 2 cm balls in your hands, create a small indentation in the center (to help the broth absorb), and drop them into boiling water. Once they float to the top, boil for an additional minute. Remove the water, transfer to bowls, and pour the broth over them immediately while they’re still hot. It’s complete. You could also enjoy the dumplings in a simple soup made by diluting canned adzuki beans in hot water.

We present approaches for the study of fluid-structure interactions subject
to thermal fluctuations. A mixed mechanical description is utilized combining
Eulerian and Lagrangian reference frames. We establish general conditions for
operators coupling these descriptions. Stochastic driving fields for the
formalism are derived using principles from statistical mechanics. The
stochastic differential equations of the formalism are found to exhibit
significant stiffness in some physical regimes. To cope with this issue, we
derive reduced stochastic differential equations for several physical regimes.
We also present stochastic numerical methods for each regime to approximate the
fluid-structure dynamics and to generate efficiently the required stochastic
driving fields. To validate the methodology in each regime, we perform analysis
of the invariant probability distribution of the stochastic dynamics of the
fluid-structure formalism. We compare this analysis with results from
statistical mechanics. To further demonstrate the applicability of the
methodology, we perform computational studies for spherical particles having
translational and rotational degrees of freedom. We compare these studies with
results from fluid mechanics. The presented approach provides for
fluid-structure systems a set of rather general computational methods for
treating consistently structure mechanics, hydrodynamic coupling, and thermal
fluctuations.

Two UK gamers are about to embark on a world tour as part of the most lucrative-ever global games tournament.

The cash will be handed out over 10 separate competitions in a continent-hopping contest organised by the Cyberathlete Professional League. As part of their prize the pair will have their travel costs paid to ensure they can get to the different bouts.
The CPL World Tour kicks off in mid-February and the first leg will be in Istanbul. All ten bouts of the tournament will be played throughout 2005, each one in a different country. Winners of each stage of the tour automatically get a place at the next stop. The world tour stops are open to any keen gamer that registers. Online registration for the first stop opens this weekend. Some pro-players are winning a spot at the tour destinations through qualifying events organised by CPL partners. Winners at these qualifiers get seeded higher in the elimination parts of each tournament. Mr Foster and Mr Treacy get the chance to attend the World Tour as members of the UK's Four-Kings gaming clan. Towards the end of 2004 Four-Kings staged a series of online Painkiller competitions to reveal the UK's top players of the PC game. The best eight players met face-to-face in a special elimination event in late December where Mr Foster and Mr Tracey proved their prowess at Painkiller. As part of their prize the pair also get a contract with Four-Kings Intel which is one of the UK's few pro-gaming teams. "There are a lot of people who take gaming very seriously and support their local or national team with the same passion as any other sport," said Simon Bysshe who filmed the event for Four-Kings and Intel. More than 80,000 people have downloaded the movie of the tournament highlights. "Professional gaming is here to stay and will only grow in popularity," he said.

Dean Cornwell (March 5, 1892 – December 4, 1960) was an American illustrator and muralist. His oil paintings were frequently featured in popular magazines and books as literary illustrations, advertisements, and posters promoting the war effort. Throughout the first half of the 20th century he was a dominant presence in American illustration. At the peak of his popularity he was nicknamed the "Dean of Illustrators". Background
Cornwell was born in Louisville, Kentucky. His father, Charles L. Cornwell, was a civil engineer whose drawings of industrial subjects fascinated Cornwell as a child. He began his professional career as a cartoonist for the Louisville Herald. Soon thereafter he moved to Chicago, where he studied at the Art Institute and worked for the Chicago Tribune. In 1915 he moved to New Rochelle, New York, a well known artist colony, and studied in New York City under Harvey Dunn at the Art Students League of New York. Eventually he traveled to London to study mural painting as an apprentice to Frank Brangwyn.

Collapse theories are formulations of quantum mechanics where the wave function's collapse is considered a genuine physical process. These theories establish specific mathematical rules governing this phenomenon and aim to replace the general guideline that a collapse occurs when an observer performs a measurement. The "primitive ontology" of a theory—often referred to as the "local beables" by Bell—consists of the variables within the theory that describe matter in space-time. There is no agreement on whether collapse theories must include a primitive ontology as part of their framework. I address this issue and suggest that introducing a primitive ontology can eliminate certain paradoxes associated with collapse theories.

Amory Blaine, a young man from Minnesota, is struggling to find his place in the world after being discharged from the army during World War I. He returns home to his wealthy family's estate, but feels suffocated by their expectations and society's conventions.

Amory becomes infatuated with Rosalind Connage, a beautiful and sophisticated woman who represents everything he aspires to be. He pursues her relentlessly, but she remains elusive and unattainable. Meanwhile, he also falls in love with Eleanor Savage, a plain-looking girl from a modest background who shares his passion for literature and poetry.

As Amory navigates these complicated relationships, he grapples with his own identity and sense of purpose. He longs to create something meaningful and make a difference in the world, but is torn between following his artistic ambitions and conforming to societal norms.

Throughout the novel, Amory's inner turmoil reflects the larger cultural upheaval taking place in post-war America. As he struggles to reconcile his desire for individuality with the pressure to conform, he embarks on a journey of self-discovery that takes him from the Midwest to New York City and eventually to France. Along the way, he encounters a cast of characters who challenge his beliefs and force him to confront the harsh realities of adulthood.

Ultimately, Amory must choose which path to follow: the conventional route of marriage, wealth, and social status, or the riskier road of creativity, independence, and true fulfillment. Will he find his paradise, or will he succumb to the temptation of an easy, comfortable life?

FOR THE CRUST:  
1 cup Graham Crumbs  
3 tablespoons Sugar  
1/4 cup Butter  

FOR THE FILLING:  
8 ounces, weight Cream Cheese  
9 ounces, weight Sugar  
1-1/2 ounce, weight Cornstarch  
12 ounces, weight Goat Cheese  
5 ounces, weight Sour Cream  
3/4 teaspoon Cinnamon  
3/4 teaspoon Ginger  
1/4 teaspoon Nutmeg  
1/4 teaspoon Cloves  
8 ounces, weight Pumpkin Puree  
4 Eggs  
1 Egg Yolk  

Preheat oven to 350°F (176°C). Combine Graham Crumbs and Sugar in a medium bowl. Microwave Butter for 30 seconds. Mix melted Butter with the Graham mixture. Sprinkle Graham Crumbs into a springform pan and press firmly to create an even layer at the bottom only. Bake for 10 minutes. Remove the crust from the oven and lower the temperature to 250°F (121°C). Fill the oven with water to half its height to help steam while preparing the cheesecake batter. Attach a paddle attachment to the mixing bowl and blend Cream Cheese and Sugar on low speed. Add Corn Starch, scrape down sides, let rest for 2 minutes. Add Goat Cheese and Sour Cream, scrape down sides, let rest for another 2 minutes. Add Spices, then Pumpkin Puree, scrape down sides, let rest for another 2 minutes. Add Eggs and Yolk, one at a time, until fully incorporated. Pour the batter into the prepared springform pan. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes without using a fan (no convection). The cheesecake will be fully set when it jiggles together in the center. It should not appear watery in the middle. To serve, allow the cheesecake to cool for 5 hours or overnight, then use a hot knife for clean cuts.

The families of steady states for the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system are defined, with their parameters determined by the central redshift. It is demonstrated that as the central redshift approaches zero, these states closely approximate a steady state of the Vlasov-Poisson system, thereby establishing a Newtonian limit where the speed of light remains constant. The analysis involves examining the limiting behavior through a parameter linked to the physical characteristics of individual solutions. This finding is applied to study the stability of relativistic steady states with small redshift parameters, following recent studies by the same authors. Specifically, it is shown that the second variation of the ADM mass about such states is positive definite on a relevant class of states.

Carl Beam (June 30, 1935 – July 1, 2021) was an American physicist who made significant contributions to the field of elementary particle physics. He was born in Huntington, West Virginia, and received his Ph.D. from the University of Illinois.

Beam was a professor of Physics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and spent a sabbatical at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) in Switzerland, where he made the discovery of the W and Z bosons, which are particles associated with Weak force interaction. For his discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1969, along with Richard P. Feynman and Jack Steinberger.

In addition to his work on weak force interaction, Beam made important contributions to the development of the quark model of matter, which is a fundamental theory of physics explaining the nature of matter.

Beam passed away on July 1, 2021, at the age of 86. He was widely regarded as a pioneer in the field of particle physics and his work continues to inspire students and researchers today.

Procedures: Select twelve unblemished organically grown small lemons, preferrably Meyer (a small type). Wash and dry the lemons. If using store-bought lemons, scrub them carefully to remove any pesticides. Cut a thin slice from the top and the bottom of each lemon. Set one lemon on end and make a vertical cut 3 quarters of the way through the fruit, so that the 2 halves still remain attached at the base; do not cut it in half. Turn the lemon upside down and rotate it so that you can make a second vertical cut down the center, crosswise to the first, leaving the bottom Fill each cut with as much salt as it will hold. Carefully place the lemon at the bottom of a hot, sterilized, wide-mouthed quart glass jar. Proceed in this manner with the remaining lemons, compressing them in the jar until no space is left and the lemon juice has risen to the top. Seal and set aside at room temperature. More lemons may be added in the following days as the lemon rinds begin to soften. Make sure the lemons are covered with juice at all times, adding freshly squeezed lemon juice if necessary. The lemons are ready to use when the rinds are tender, in 5 to 6 weeks. Rinse them lightly before using. Once opened, refrigerate preserved lemons for up to 6 months.

225 grams cream cheese, at room temperature  
1/4 cup caster sugar  
3 teaspoons cornflour  
3 eggs  
1 teaspoon vanilla extract  
3 teaspoons finely grated icing sugar  
1 1/2 tablespoons strained fresh lemon juice  
2 cups sour cream  
1 cup thickened cream  
220 grams good quality white chocolate, melted and cooled to lukewarm  
fresh seasonal fruit  
passion fruit pulp, to serve  

Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20cm springform cake pan and line the base with baking paper. Wrap the outer side tightly with a double layer of foil. Process cheese and sugar in a food processor for 30 seconds until smooth. Continue processing while adding cornflour, eggs one at a time, stopping occasionally to scrape down the sides. Add vanilla, zest, juice, creams, and 1/4 tsp salt, processing until just combined. Add chocolate and pulse until smooth. Transfer to the pan and let sit in a large baking dish. Pour hot water into the dish to reach halfway up the sides of the pan. Bake for 45 minutes, then remove from the oven and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. Remove the pan from the dish, take off the foil, and allow the cake to cool completely in the pan on a rack. Cover and chill overnight. To release, place the pan on a hot, damp towel to loosen the base. Run a palette knife around the edge of the pan and turn it onto a serving plate. Decorate with fruit by piling it on top (I prefer random placement), then pour over the passionfruit pulp. Slice with a hot, dry knife.

In dusty streets, where heat and magic blend,
A snake charmer conjures, his art to wield,
With cobras rising, sinuous and slow,
Their eyes gleam bright, as they sway and flow.

His pipe's melody weaves a hypnotic spell,
As serpents dance beneath its enchanting knell,
In rhythm with the ancient, mystic tune,
They twist and writh, their graceful movements soon.

Their scales glimmer in shades of gold and brown,
Like royal robes that graced an eastern crown,
Erect and proud, they dance before the crowd,
Spellbound by beauty, all watch, un loud.

The charmer's hands move swiftly, sure and still,
Guiding each cobra's movement, skillfully fulfilling,
Each step they take, each gesture they make, 
A testament to patience, practice well-faked. 

His eyes are fixed on snakes with fierce intent,
A bond between them, trust and understand bent,
Together they perform this ancient rite,
Passed down through generations - night.

The music fades; the spectacle subsides,
And cobras retreat, retiring from glides, 
The charmers bows, respect paid to guests,
Applause echoes out - a deserved rest.

Yet in my mind, this vision stays, a haunting tryst,
Where east meets west, an age-old craft entrust,
To those who mesmerize our souls so willingly, 
Indian snake charmers legacy timelessly.

Neil Kennedy O'Donnell (born July 3, 1966) is a former American football quarterback who played in the National Football League for 14 seasons (1990–2003) with the Pittsburgh Steelers, New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, and Tennessee Titans. He played college football at Maryland. Early life
O'Donnell grew up in Madison, New Jersey, and played high school football there at Madison High School. Neil Kennedy O’Donnell was born July 3, 1966 in Morristown, New Jersey. Neil's four older brothers played for local coaching legend Ted Monica and won state championships. Stephen O’Donnell was an All-State quarterback who went on to play for Duke. Coach Monica had retired by the time Neil enrolled at Madison High School, but mentored him throughout much of his young football life.  O'Donnell was the star of the Dodgers varsity team as a sophomore and junior, but the team won just three games in those two seasons. During his senior year, as quarterback, O'Donnell led the team to a respectable 4-2-3 season in 1985. Coach Bobby Ross recruited him to the University of Maryland despite lacking the stats and honors of other high school stars.

In this paper, we review and extend a family of log-det divergences for
symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices and discuss their fundamental
properties. We show how to generate from parameterized Alpha-Beta (AB) and
Gamma Log-det divergences many well known divergences, for example, the Stein's
loss, S-divergence, called also Jensen-Bregman LogDet (JBLD) divergence, the
Logdet Zero (Bhattacharryya) divergence, Affine Invariant Riemannian Metric
(AIRM) as well as some new divergences. Moreover, we establish links and
correspondences among many log-det divergences and display them on alpha-beta
plain for various set of parameters. Furthermore, this paper bridges these
divergences and shows also their links to divergences of multivariate and
multiway Gaussian distributions. Closed form formulas are derived for gamma
divergences of two multivariate Gaussian densities including as special cases
the Kullback-Leibler, Bhattacharryya, R\'enyi and Cauchy-Schwartz divergences.
Symmetrized versions of the log-det divergences are also discussed and
reviewed. A class of divergences is extended to multiway divergences for
separable covariance (precision) matrices.

A close associate of former Yukos boss Mikhail Khodorkovsky has told a court that fraud charges levelled against him are "false".
Platon Lebedev has been on trial alongside Mr Khodorkovsky since June in a case centring around the privatisation of a fertiliser firm. The pair claim they are being punished by the authorities for the political ambitions of Mr Khodorkovsky. Mr Lebedev said there were "absurd contradictions" in the case. Opening his defence, he said he could not see the legal basis of the charges he faced, which also include allegations of tax evasion. "To my embarrassment, I could not understand the file of complaints against me," he told a Moscow court. Mr Lebedev headed the Menatep group, the parent company of Yukos.
Mr Lebedev and Mr Khodorkovsky, who each face a possible 10 year jail sentence if convicted, will be questioned by a judge over the next few days. Mr Khodorkovsky began his testimony last week, telling the court that he objected to the way that the "running of a normal business has been presented as a work of criminal fiction". The charges are seen by supporters as politically motivated and part of a drive by Russian President Vladimir Putin to rein in the country's super-rich business leaders, the so-called oligarchs. Yukos has been presented with a $27.5bn (£13bn) tax demand by the Russian authorities and its key Yugansk division was auctioned off to part settle the bill. The company's effort to gain bankruptcy protection in the US - in a bid to win damages for the sale - were dismissed by a court in Texas.

Adapromine is an antiviral medication belonging to the adamantane class, similar to amantadine (1-aminoadamantane), rimantadine (1-(1-aminoethyl)adamantane), and memantine (1-amino-3,5-dimethyladamantane). It is used in Russia for treating and preventing influenza. Adapromine is an alkyl derivative of rimantadine and exhibits antiviral properties comparable to rimantadine, though it demonstrates a wider range of effectiveness, targeting both types A and B influenza viruses. Resistance to adapromine and rimantadine, along with the related drug deitiforine, was observed in Mongolian and Soviet Union strains of influenza virus during the 1980s. Animal studies indicate that adapromine and related adamantanes, such as amantadine, bromantane (1-amino-2-bromophenyladamantane), and memantine, produce psychostimulant-like and potentially antidepressant-like effects. These effects may involve catecholaminergic pathways. The stimulant effects of adamantanes differ from those of traditional psychostimulants like amphetamine, yet they are classified as "adaptogens" and "actoprotectors."

Ngangom Bala Devi (born 2 February 1990) is an Indian professional footballer who currently plays as a forward for Rangers Women in the Scottish Women's Premier League and the Indian national team. She is also the first Asian to play and score in a professional league in Scotland and also the first South Asian to sign a professional contract.

Early Life and Career

Devi was born in Manipur, India. Her interest in football was sparked by her father, who played the game at a local level. She began her professional career as a footballer in 2005 with Manipur Police Sports Club in the Indian Women's League (IWL). After five years in this team, she moved to New Radiant SC of Maldives, where she spent just one season before returning to her former club.

Bala Devi has also represented India at the international level, playing in the SAFF Women's Championship and the Women's Asian Cup qualifiers. Over the years, she has been an integral part of the Indian national team and has scored several crucial goals.

Move to Rangers F.C. 

Bala Devi signed an 18-month contract with Scottish club Rangers F.C in January 2020, making her the first Indian woman to be signed by a professional club in the United Kingdom. This move was facilitated through a partnership between Rangers and Bengaluru FC. Devi made her debut against Hearts, scoring in the final two minutes of the match. Her consistent performances have received widespread recognition and commendation.

Style of Play and Legacy

Devi is known for her strength, agility, and precision in front of the goal. She is capable of playing as both a forward and attacking midfielder and has earned comparisons to her male counterparts in Indian Football.

Devi's move to Rangers was a landmark moment in Indian football history, particularly for women in the sport. Her career demonstrates the possibility of Indian talent finding opportunities in prestigious international leagues; a fact that has been acclaimed as instrumental in fostering ambition and aspiration among young Indian women interested in football.

Sure, here's a recipe for bow ties with sausage and leek sauce:

Ingredients:

* 1 pound bow tie pasta
* 1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
* 2 medium leeks, chopped (about 2 cups)
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 1/4 cup white wine (optional)
* 1/4 cup chicken broth
* 1/4 cup heavy cream
* 1 tablespoon tomato paste
* 1 teaspoon dried thyme
* Salt and pepper to taste
* Grated Parmesan cheese for serving (optional)

Instructions:

1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the bow tie pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water and then drain the pasta.
2. In a large skillet, cook the Italian sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the sausage from the skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, add the chopped leeks and minced garlic. Cook until the leeks are softened and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
4. If using white wine, add it to the skillet and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
5. Add the chicken broth, heavy cream, tomato paste, and thyme to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring the mixture to a simmer.
6. Add the cooked sausage back into the skillet and stir to combine.
7. Add the cooked bow tie pasta to the skillet and toss to combine, adding some reserved pasta cooking water if the sauce is too thick.
8. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Serve the bow ties with sausage and leek sauce hot

Crude oil prices surged back above the $47 a barrel mark on Thursday after an energy market watchdog raised its forecasts for global demand.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned demand for Opec's crude in the first quarter would outstrip supply. The IEA raised its estimate of 2005 oil demand growth by 80,000 barrels a day to 84 million barrels a day. US light crude rose $1.64 to $47.10, while Brent crude in London gained $1.32 to $44.45.
The Paris-based IEA watchdog, which advises industrialized nations on energy policy, said the upward revision was due to stronger demand from China and other Asian countries. The fresh rally in crude prices followed gains on Wednesday which were triggered by large falls in US crude supplies following a cold spell in North America in January. The US Department of Energy reported that crude stockpiles had fallen 1m barrels to 294.3m. On top of that, ongoing problems for beleaguered Russian oil giant Yukos have also prompted the IEA to revise its output estimates from Russia - a major non-Opec supplier. "I think that prices are now beginning to set a new range and it looks like the $40 to $50 level," said energy analyst Orin Middleton of Barclays Capital.

Acton House is a mansion in Acton, West London, that was formerly the home of Napoleon III, Emperor of France, and his wife, Empress Eugénie. It was built in the 1870s by Richard Norman Shaw for the Scottish economist and historian William Hewett. In 1883, it was bought by the architect Richard Shaw, who designed the nearby St. Barnabas Church.

In 1904, the house was acquired by the Welsh businessman Sir John Williams Bt., who lived there with his wife Frances (née Cornwallis), daughter of Colonel Charles Cornwallis of Abermarlais, Carmarthenshire. The couple's eldest daughter, Ursula, married Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg, the son of the Austrian ambassador, in 1919.

In 1928, Acton House was acquired by Baron Melchior de Polignac, who rented it to King Zog of Albania from 1936 to 1938. It was then acquired by the Turkish-born Hüseyin Jawdat, who used it as a training center for the Muslim World League.

Since 1958, it has been the home of the International Youth Hostel. In 1985, it was Grade II* listed by English Heritage.

Vanilla Bean Rooibos Ice Cream  
1 cup Whole Milk (avoid ultra-pasteurized)  
2 cups Heavy Cream (avoid ultra-pasteurized)  
2 tablespoons Organic Rooibos Tea Leaves  
1 Madagascar Vanilla Bean, split and seeds removed  
3 tablespoons Honey  
6 Large Egg Yolks  
1 tablespoon Amaretto Liquer  
3/4 cup Chopped Raw Almonds  
Dulce de Leche  
1 quart Whole Milk (avoid ultra-pasteurized)  
1 cup Sugar  
3 tablespoons Honey  
1 Vanilla bean, split and seeds removed  
1/2 teaspoon Baking Soda  

Place the milk, sugar, vanilla bean, and honey in a medium saucepan, over medium heat. Bring the mixture to a simmer, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar, then remove from the heat. Add the rooibos tea leaves, cover, and let steep for 1 hour (note: the long steep is crucial for optimal flavor). Add one cup of the cream to the tea/milk base, warm it without boiling, and strain to remove the rooibos leaves and vanilla bean (leaves can be retained after the first straining). Discard the rooibos leaves; rinse and keep the vanilla bean. Set aside the remaining one cup of heavy cream in a medium bowl with a strainer on top. In a medium mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks until they lighten in color. Gradually add the warm cream base to the eggs, tempering the mixture by adding small amounts until fully incorporated. Return the egg and cream mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon, reaching 170–175°F. Strain the mixture into the one cup of cream previously set aside. Return the vanilla bean to the mixture and place it in an ice bath for 30 minutes. Pour the mixture into the refrigerator for 4–8 hours or until it reaches 40°F. Remove the vanilla bean, transfer the cooled cream mixture into an ice cream maker, add one teaspoon of amaretto, and process as directed.

1/2 cup sour bread starter  
2 cups warm water  
3 1/2 cups rye flour  
1 package active dry yeast  
1/4 cup warm water  
2 teaspoons salt  
3 to 3 1/2 cups sifted white flour  
Mix the sour bread starter into a large bowl and gradually add the 2 cups of warm water until well combined. Add 1 cup of rye flour and mix thoroughly. Cover lightly and allow to rest in a warm place (around 85°F) for 20 to 40 hours, depending on the sourness.  

Dissolve the yeast in 1/4 cup of warm water and mix it into the sour mixture. Add the salt and gradually incorporate the remaining rye flour. Add the white flour bit by bit, mixing well after each addition. Form a stiff dough and let it rest in the bowl for 10 to 15 minutes. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured board and knead until smooth. Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, ensuring the top is also coated with grease. Cover and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled in size, approximately 1 to 1 1/2 hours.  

Remove the dough from the bowl and divide it into two equal parts, reserving about 1/2 cup of the dough. Store the remaining portion in a covered container in the refrigerator for the next baking session. Grease and flour the pan, let it rise briefly, and bake at 375°F for 1 hour.

While there are concerns about addiction, privacy violations, and potential health risks associated with prolonged exposure to electromagnetic radiation emitted by cellphones, it cannot be denied that this technological marvel has had a profound impact on human civilization. Lab-on-chip and point-of-care diagnostic chips consist of numerous components, including nanosensors that need to interact with other parts inside the device. Molecular communication offers a viable method for on-chip data transfer. Specifically, kinesin-driven microtubules (MTs) efficiently facilitate the movement of information particles between components. However, determining the ideal channel geometry remains difficult. This study develops a mathematical optimization framework to identify the optimal channel configuration and size for any transmission duration. Three distinct models are presented for rectangular, regular polygonal, and regular polygonal ring channels. The results indicate that the square-shaped channel is optimal for rectangular channels, whereas circular-shaped channels are preferred for other geometric configurations. Ultimately, among all two-dimensional shapes, the circular channel provides the highest information throughput.

U.S. automotive companies General Motors (GM) and Ford have had to reduce production due to declining car sales. GM's U.S. sales decreased by 12.7% in February compared to the previous year, while Ford's sales declined by 3% as foreign competitors captured a larger portion of the market. Meanwhile, Asian manufacturers performed better: Toyota saw a 11% increase in sales, and Nissan achieved a 10% rise. Overall, industry sales dropped to 1.25 million vehicles from 1.27 million the prior year.

GM attributed lower sales to high fuel costs affecting large trucks and gas-hungry SUVs, which generate significant profits. GM reported a 9% decline in U.S. truck sales and a 17% drop in the car division, though it noted that models like the Pontiac G6 and Chevrolet Cobalt showed strong performance. Mark LaNeve, GM's vice president for North American sales, stated that the calendar year started slower than anticipated, both for GM and the industry. The company reduced production in North America by 3%, having already cut output by about 9% due to increasing inventory levels. Ford, which recorded its ninth consecutive month of declining U.S. sales, announced further cuts in first-quarter North American production by 10,000 units. Chrysler, part of DaimlerChrysler, was the only Detroit-based manufacturer to see an increase in market share, with sales rising 8%.

However, the U.S. losses were offset by gains for foreign competitors who continue to expand into the American market. Toyota and Nissan experienced accelerated sales growth, while smaller Japanese automaker Suzuki saw a 17.6% improvement year-over-year. In 2003, Suzuki aimed to triple U.S. sales by 2007 to strengthen its position in the Asian competition. South Korean automaker Hyundai also achieved a 19% surge in sales.

Despite deep convolutional neural networks achieved impressive progress in
medical image computing and analysis, its paradigm of supervised learning
demands a large number of annotations for training to avoid overfitting and
achieving promising results. In clinical practices, massive semantic
annotations are difficult to acquire in some conditions where specialized
biomedical expert knowledge is required, and it is also a common condition
where only few annotated classes are available. In this work, we proposed a
novel method for few-shot medical image segmentation, which enables a
segmentation model to fast generalize to an unseen class with few training
images. We construct our few-shot image segmentor using a deep convolutional
network trained episodically. Motivated by the spatial consistency and
regularity in medical images, we developed an efficient global correlation
module to capture the correlation between a support and query image and
incorporate it into the deep network called global correlation network.
Moreover, we enhance discriminability of deep embedding to encourage clustering
of the feature domains of the same class while keep the feature domains of
different organs far apart. Ablation Study proved the effectiveness of the
proposed global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Extensive
experiments on anatomical abdomen images on both CT and MRI modalities are
performed to demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our proposed
model.

Recent semantic segmentation approaches typically use a U-Net structure with an encoder-decoder design. However, it remains difficult for U-Net models employing a basic skip connection setup to capture the global multi-scale context. Specifically, issues arise such as: 1) Incompatible feature sets between encoder and decoder stages, which can make certain skip connection configurations ineffective, sometimes even reducing segmentation accuracy; 2) The standard U-Net performs less effectively than its variant without skip connections on specific datasets. Drawing from these observations, we introduce a novel segmentation framework called UCTransNet, which incorporates an attention-based approach from the channel perspective. This framework includes a modified skip connection known as CTrans, composed of two sub-modules: one for multi-scale channel cross-fusion using a Transformer (CCT) and another for channel-wise cross-attention (CCA) to direct the fused multi-scale information toward the decoder's features, thereby resolving ambiguities. Consequently, this connection enables the replacement of the original skip connection, addressing semantic gaps in automatic medical image segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that UCTransNet yields improved segmentation accuracy across diverse datasets and architectures incorporating transformers or U-shaped frameworks. Code: https://github.com/McGregorWwww/UCTransNet.

Ingredients (for 2 servings):

1 tbsp butter, softened

1 onion, diced

3 garlic cloves, finely diced

1 (14.25-ounce) can chopped tomatoes

½ cup water

½ cup milk

1 cup butternut squash puree (about 1/2 pound)

salt

1 teaspoon ground black pepper

1 cup dry white wine

2 cups chicken stock, or water

Directions:

1. Heat a 15-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add butter and sauté until it reaches a depth of 10 inches (about 3 minutes). Remove from the heat and set aside.

Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes, then the water, milk, and stir vigorously until the sauce thickens, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper, to taste. Transfer the mixture to a food processor and pulse until it separates and starts to form a smooth puree. Transfer the puree to a large saucepan.

Lower heat to a simmer and cook until the wine has reduced by almost half and the soup is thick, about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.

4. Stir in the parsley, drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve. Garnish with fresh dill and parsley leaves.

In computer vision, image segmentation is consistently regarded as a key research area. Given its critical role in image processing, there is an ongoing demand for improved segmentation techniques. Clustering, an unsupervised approach, finds applications across various scientific and engineering domains. Researchers frequently employ clustering methods in image segmentation tasks. However, these approaches still require enhancement. This paper introduces a new clustering-based image segmentation technique. Color space analysis is emphasized, with the LAB color space chosen for this purpose. The well-known K-means clustering algorithm is utilized, yet its effectiveness hinges on selecting an appropriate distance metric. To address this limitation, the cosine distance measure is adopted instead. After segmentation, the resulting image undergoes filtering using a Sobel filter. The filtered image is then analyzed using the Marker Wassertern algorithm to achieve the final segmented outcome of the original image. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) values are computed to assess the performance.

4 large eggs
4 large egg whites

1/4 teaspoon fresh ground pepper
5 cups chopped spinach, wilted (see Tip)
4 cups whole grain bread (cut into 1-inch cubes, crusts removed if desired)
1 cup ham steak, diced
1/2 cup jarred roasted red pepper, chopped
3/4 cup shredded gruyere cheese or 3/4 cup swiss cheese
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a 7-by-11-inch glass baking dish or a 2-quart casserole with cooking spray. Whisk eggs, egg whites and milk in a medium bowl. Bake as directed in Step 3.

Andrew Litton, born on May 16, 1959, in New York City, is an American orchestral conductor. He graduated from The Fieldston School and studied piano under Nadia Reisenberg and conducting under Sixten Ehrling at the Juilliard School of Music. He earned his Bachelor of Music and Master of Music degrees in piano and conducting. He also received conducting instruction from Walter Weller at the Salzburg Mozarteum and Edoardo Müller in Milan. His early mentors included John DeMaio. 

The youngest-ever winner of the BBC International Conductors Competition in 1982, Litton served as Assistant Conductor at Teatro alla Scala and as Exxon/Arts Endowment Assistant Conductor for the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington D.C. under Mstislav Rostropovich (1982–1985), later becoming Associate Conductor (1985–1986). Litton participated in the Affiliate Artists Exxon-Arts Endowment Conductors Program. In 2003, he was honored with the Sanford Medal from Yale University.

Litton began his conducting career with the Bournemouth Symphony Orchestra, serving as principal conductor from 1988 to 1994, and is currently its conductor laureate. He held the position of Music Director of the Dallas Symphony Orchestra for twelve seasons from 1994 to 2006, after which he became Music Director Emeritus. From 2003 to 2017, he was Artistic Director of the Sommerfest concerts of the Minnesota Orchestra.

The impact of residual amplitude modulation (RAM) in laser interferometers employing heterodyne sensing can be significant and challenging to address. In this study, we examine how RAM influences a complex laser interferometer designed for gravitational wave detection. RAM causes unintended deviations in the cavity length signals, altering the operational position of the optical cavities through feedback control. This change results in fluctuations in the sensing matrix, deteriorating the precision of the noise subtraction method within the multi-degree-of-freedom control system. Furthermore, misaligned optical cavities generate an opto-mechanical spring, which also affects the sensing matrix. Our simulations help establish criteria for RAM levels in Advanced LIGO detectors, demonstrating that the expected RAM in this system does not constrain its sensitivity.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase, referred to as ITP3K, is an enzyme that transfers a phosphate group from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. It falls under the category of transferases, specifically phosphotransferases that accept an alcohol group. The systematic name for this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate, resulting in the formation of inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3 and exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, generating Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biological contexts, ITP3K is commonly abbreviated as 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, or Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. Additionally, the enzyme can be named based on its origin in human genes (ITPKA, ITPKB, ITPKC) or fruit fly genes (IP3K1, IP3K2), where the latter is a mutant known as "wavy." The nematode genome contains one variant of the enzyme, encoded by the LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed exclusively in metazoans and are not present in yeast or plants.

Brazilian Coconut Beijinhos are a delicious and easy-to-make Brazilian dessert. They are made with just a few simple ingredients, including sweetened condensed milk, butter, and coconut. Here is a recipe for Brazilian Coconut Beijinhos:

Ingredients:

- 1 can (14 oz) sweetened condensed milk
- 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter, melted
- 2 cups coconut, finely shredded
- 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 eggs
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk, melted butter, coconut, baking powder, and salt. Stir in flour until well combined.
3. Add eggs and vanilla extract, and mix until well combined.
4. Roll dough into 1-inch balls and place on prepared baking sheet.
5. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until lightly browned.
6. Let cool on wire rack for 5 minutes before serving.

Pork Chops with Apples and Pancetta Recipe

Ingredients:
- 4 pork chops, thick-cut
- Salt and pepper
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 8 ounces pancetta, diced
- 2 large apples, cored and sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 2 tablespoons butter

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 400°F.
2. Season the pork chops with salt and pepper on both sides.
3. Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork chops and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side until nicely browned. Remove the pork chops from the skillet and set aside.
4. Add the diced pancetta to the same skillet and cook over medium heat until crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
5. Add the sliced apples, minced garlic, and dried thyme to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the apples start to soften.
6. Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.
7. Place the pork chops back into the skillet, spooning some of the apple and pancetta mixture on top of the pork chops.
8. Dot the top of the apples with butter and bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until the pork chops are fully cooked and the apples are tender.
9. Serve the pork chops with apples and pancetta hot, garnished with fresh thyme if desired. Enjoy!

Shares in US phone company MCI have risen on speculation that it is in takeover talks.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that Qwest has bid $6.3bn (£3.4bn) for MCI. Other firms have also expressed an interest in MCI, the second-largest US long-distance phone firm, and may now table rival bids, analysts said. Shares in MCI, which changed its name from Worldcom when it emerged from bankruptcy, were up 2.4% at $20.15. Press reports suggest that Qwest and MCI may reach an agreement as early as next week, although rival bids may muddy the waters. The largest US telephone company Verizon has previously held preliminary merger discussions with MCI, Reuters quoted sources as saying.
Consolidation in the US telecommunications industry has picked up in the past few months as companies look to cut costs and boost client bases. A merger between MCI and Qwest would be the fifth billion-dollar telecoms deal since October. Last week, SBC Communications agreed to buy its former parent and phone trailblazer AT&T for about $16bn. Competition has intensified and fixed-line phone providers such as MCI and AT&T have seen themselves overtaken by rivals. Buying MCI would give Qwest, a local phone service provider, access to MCI's global network and business-based subscribers. MCI also offers internet services.
MCI was renamed after it emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in April last year. It hit the headlines as Worldcom in 2002 after admitting it illegally booked expenses and inflated profits. The scandal was a key factor in a global slide in share prices and the reverberations are still being felt today. Shareholders lost about $180bn when the company collapsed, while 20,000 workers lost their jobs. Former Worldcom boss Bernie Ebbers is currently on trial, accused of overseeing an $11bn fraud.

We all know that Pixar and Dreamworks are among the top studios in creating exceptional animated films. While there have been a few exceptions, Megamind isn't one of them. Given Dreamworks' recent releases like Kung Fu Panda and How to Train Your Dragon, I was eager to see this film when it came out and finally had the opportunity to watch it.  

Despite feeling like a standard superhero genre movie, Megamind combines various elements effectively with a brilliantly crafted character, MEGAMIND himself. Though flawed and somewhat villainous, he is still relatable and deserving of sympathy. He ultimately wins over the audience, making the story both smart, thoughtful, and well-written. The voice acting and animation perfectly match the tone of the film. I appreciate how these studios evoke deep emotions even with animated characters. When Roxanne leaves Megamind, you'll feel his emotional struggle as he expresses it through his eyes. I truly admire this approach!  

The movie contains plenty of funny moments and takes a unique angle on traditional superhero stories, offering a surprising twist that I'm certain you'd enjoy. It's suitable for all age groups. A blend of humor, sincerity, and a touch of suspense, along with a compelling romantic interest, keeps viewers engaged throughout. The action sequences, especially the flying scenes, are thrilling and offer an exciting experience, though they are most effective in 3D. Still, they are enjoyable in 2D as well. The 3D aspect enhances the movie without being distracting or annoying.  

Additionally, the film masterfully portrays several awkward and heart-wrenching aspects of human life in a way only animation can. For instance, it highlights how society sometimes overlooks children who are different due to their appearance or intellect and how they feel isolated. In the movie, Megamind argues that if he is treated like a misfit, he may never find acceptance.
